jobs.title: Superintendent
jobs.industry: Management, Mining, Oil and Gas, Occupational Health and Safety, Operations Support, Other, Professional Services, Project Management, Quality, Research, Scientific, Training
jobs.employer_address: P.O Box 484, Mt. Hagen, WHP
jobs.description:
Superintendent – Metallurgy
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Metallurgy-Processing Department as a
Superintendent – Metallurgy.
Superintendent – Metallurgy (239661)
We seek to appoint an experienced Metallurgy Superintendent to join the Porgera team to lead metallurgical accounting and drive strategies that optimise plant performance and maximise gold recovery. This role has a strong development focus, with responsibility for knowledge sharing and future-proofing the metallurgy team in line with global best practice. It presents a unique opportunity to contribute to plant optimisation and improvements within an operation that values safety, visible leadership and operational excellence:
Duties and Responsibilities:
Leadership of the Metallurgy team to ensure safe, cost efficient, operation (daily to life-of-mine) is achieved through control and optimisation of the processing plant which includes Crushing, Grinding, Flotation, Pressure Oxidation autoclaves, Oxygen Plants, Lime Kilns, Tailings Detoxification, gold leach / CIP and gold room.
Accountable for high quality reporting of production, improvement and metallurgical reporting.  Including Metallurgical Accounting improvements.
Strengthen and enhance Metallurgy team performance and capability through focused training/coaching and feedback, employee development and talent identification / retention.
Hands on training, coaching and improvement of Metallurgical team members to ensure they understand the requirements of their roles, have strong analytical and reporting capabilities and they focus on transferring knowledge to operators to run the plant.
Establish and implement well-defined accountabilities for Metallurgy team interaction, reporting and support to process operations, assay laboratory, maintenance, mining, finance & product security teams.
Develop and manage systems to ensure training/employee development, statutory compliance and change management systems.
Manage and provide leadership of Project Management and Change Management processes to deliver capital and business improvement / continuous improvement projects to achieve business results, cost, quality, quantity and schedule.
Develop and manage processes for metallurgical assessment of future ore sources, improvements to process plant efficiency and reduction to operational risks.
Develop and manage systems to collect and analyse information to assess performance statistics, statutory requirements, systems efficiencies and business improvement initiatives, and provide timely recommendations for implementation in the operation.
To be suitable for this role, you will possess the following:
Tertiary Qualifications in Metallurgical or Chemical Engineering including at least 15 years’ experience in Minerals processing operations , including several years in Superintendent or senior metallurgist roles in the gold and / or base metals industry.
Demonstrated ability to identify, coach and mentor team members for their professional development and strengthen overall team capabilities in developing countries.
Demonstrated ability to lead a team safely and improve team safety awareness.
Demonstrated experience in management of metallurgical databases and accounting systems.
Demonstrated experience in project management, change management and business improvement systems to deliver results and act as a change agent
Experience in managing costs and budgeting
First aid certification or ability to obtain certification.
Certificate IV Training and Assessment (preferable).
Current Drivers Licence.
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures
Mobilisation Requirement
This is a PNG Citizen position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG citizens and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Superintendent – Metallurgy
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a
Superintendent – Metallurgy
. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.
Note:
This advert will be open until
19
th
April,2026
. If you do not hear from NPL within next two (2) weeks following the closing date, please consider your application unsuccessful for this opportunity.

Ensure compliance with all applicable safety regulations and standards.
Communicate safety concerns and recommendations to management.
Participate in the development and implementation of emergency preparedness plans.

jobs.title: Labour Mobility Reintegration Technical Consultant
jobs.description:
Labour Mobility Reintegration Technical Consultant
Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Job Description
Established in 1951, IOM is a Relate
Introduction
d Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is committed to ensuring a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally, while working towards harnessing the full potential of migration. Read more about IOM's workplace culture at
IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration
Nature of the consultancy: Advisory and technical services (Type A), subject to confirmation of funding and formal agreement with the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) of the Department of Treasury, providing strategic, analytical, and technical support to inform the design and potential operationalization of labour mobility reintegration systems, policies, and pilot programming in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
Project Context and Scope:
PNG has identified overseas labour mobility as a strategic pathway to expand employment opportunities, strengthen skills development, increase foreign exchange earnings, and improve household income and wellbeing. Labour mobility is coordinated by the LMU within the Department of Treasury, which oversees recruitment, deployment, worker welfare, return, and reintegration of PNG citizens under schemes such as the Pacific Australia Labour Mobility (PALM) and Recognised Seasonal Employer (RSE) programmes.
As PNG’s participation in regional labour mobility schemes expands, the scale and complexity of return and reintegration have increased. Returned workers and their families experience interconnected economic, social, and psychosocial reintegration challenges, particularly in contexts of circular migration, family separation, limited job matching, financial pressures, and community expectations. Strengthening reintegration systems is therefore critical to ensuring that skills, savings, and overseas experience translate into sustained household resilience and national development gains.
Subject to confirmation of funding and a formal agreement with the LMU, this consultancy will support the proposed project “Supporting the Reintegration of Migrant Workers in Papua New Guinea,” to be implemented by IOM in alignment with, and complementary to, the Government-led Enhancing Labor Mobility from Papua New Guinea Project (ELMP) supported by the World Bank. The Consultant will provide technical and operational leadership for the design and implementation of reintegration components under this framework.
Organizational Department / Unit and Reporting
Organizational Department / Unit to which the Consultant is contributing:
IOM Labour Mobility and Social Inclusion Unit, working in close coordination with the LMU, Department of Treasury, and the World Bank.
The Consultant will work under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission, IOM Papua New Guinea, with technical guidance from IOM Labour Mobility (Canberra) and the Regional Labour Mobility Specialist, IOM Regional Office in Bangkok. The Consultant will maintain close technical coordination with the LMU, Department of Treasury, and engage with the World Bank and other relevant partners, while collaborating with Regional Recruitment Hubs (RRHs), field teams, and subnational government counterparts to support coherent, government‑led implementation of labour mobility reintegration activities.
Responsibilities
Category A Consultants: Tasks to be Performed under this Contract
This is a Category A (Type A) consultancy providing senior technical and operational leadership to support implementation of labour mobility reintegration activities, in alignment with ELMP reintegration outputs and agreed delivery arrangements.
Reintegration Systems Design and Implementation Leadership
Lead the design, operationalisation, and technical oversight of labour mobility reintegration systems and programme components, aligned with ELMP reintegration objectives and national policy frameworks.
Provide technical and operational leadership to guide implementation of evidence‑based, family‑centred reintegration approaches through LMU and RRHs.
Support integration of reintegration considerations across the labour mobility cycle, including pre‑departure, overseas employment (including circular migration), and return.
Ensure safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, and psychosocial wellbeing considerations are embedded across reintegration systems and delivery modalities.
Evidence Generation, Monitoring and Learning
Lead reintegration evidence generation activities, including contextual analysis and validation exercises to inform implementation.
Support development and application of monitoring and learning frameworks for reintegration interventions, aligned with ELMP requirements.
Document implementation experiences, lessons learned, and good practices to inform adaptive management and future scale‑up.
Strategy, Programme and Systems Development
Provide technical leadership for the development and operationalisation of a nationally aligned Reintegration Strategy and Implementation Action Plan.
Translate strategic priorities into pilot‑ready programme designs suitable for decentralised delivery through RRHs.
Provide technical input into reintegration data management, referral, coordination, and tracking approaches between LMU and RRHs.
Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support
Design and deliver capacity‑building support for LMU and RRHs on reintegration case management, coordination, referrals, safeguarding, and engagement with returned workers and families.
Develop and contextualise a PNG‑specific reintegration training package drawing on regional and global good practices.
Provide on‑the‑job mentoring and technical backstopping to support consistent, government‑led reintegration implementation.
Coordination, Partnerships and Representation
Support coordination with government counterparts, development partners, and relevant stakeholders involved in labour mobility and reintegration.
Contribute technical inputs to inter‑agency discussions, workshops, and coordination fora related to labour mobility reintegration.
Support alignment between reintegration activities and broader ELMP implementation processes.
Reporting and Compliance
Provide technical inputs to inception, progress, and final reports related to reintegration implementation.
Ensure activities comply with IOM policies, safeguarding and data protection standards, and applicable environmental and social requirements.
4. Performance Indicators for the Evaluation of Results
Reintegration systems, tools, and programme components designed and operationalised in line with ELMP reintegration outputs.
Quality and timeliness of evidence products, strategy documents, and programme designs.
Strengthened institutional capacity of LMU and RRHs to lead reintegration implementation.
Documented lessons learned informing programme adaptation and scale‑up.
Timely and compliant technical contributions to project reporting.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications and Experience
Education
Master’s degree in Migration Studies, Development Studies, Economics, Public Policy, Social Sciences, or a related field; or
Bachelor’s degree with additional relevant professional experience.
Experience and Skills
Minimum five (5) years of progressive professional experience in labour mobility, migration governance, reintegration, or related programming.
Demonstrated experience providing technical and operational leadership for programme implementation.
Experience in evidence generation, strategy development, programme design, and capacity strengthening.
Experience working with government counterparts, UN agencies, and development partners.
Strong analytical, coordination, facilitation, and communication skills.
Experience in Papua New Guinea or comparable Pacific contexts is an asset.
Travel Required
- Travel within Papua New Guinea and, where required, within the Asia–Pacific region, including to remote and hardship locations.
Languages

jobs.title: Senior Project Associate-Labour Mobility Reintegration
jobs.description:
Senior Project Associate-Labour Mobility Reintegration
Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Job Description
Introduction
Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is committed to ensuring a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally, while working towards harnessing the full potential of migration. Read more about IOM's workplace culture at
IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration
Internal and external candidates will be considered for this vacancy. For the purposes of this vacancy, internal candidates are defined as staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded or ungraded contract, including Junior Professional Officers (JPOs), staff on Special Leave Without Pay (SLWOP), UN Volunteers with at least twelve (12) months of continuous service in IOM, and staff members on secondment/loan released by the Organization, unless otherwise specified in their contract. Staff members holding a regular, fixed-term or short-term graded contract will not retain their contract type if appointed to an ungraded position.
Organizational Context and Scope
Papua New Guinea (PNG) has identified overseas labour mobility as a key pathway to expand employment opportunities, strengthen skills development, and improve household incomes. Labour mobility is coordinated by the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) within the Department of Treasury and implemented through a decentralised system of Regional Recruitment Hubs. Strengthening systems that support safe, well-managed migration across the full mobility cycle,  including preparedness, worker welfare, and sustainable reintegrationm remains a key Government priority, led by the Labour Mobility Unit (LMU) in coordination with national stakeholders and partners.
In this context, IOM provides technical assistance, capacity strengthening, and operational support to Government counterparts to advance labour mobility initiatives in Papua New Guinea. This includes support to institutional coordination under the leadership of the LMU, reintegration analysis and planning, development of training approaches, and strengthening systems that promote sustainable outcomes for returning workers and their families.
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission, and in close coordination with national counterparts, the incumbent will provide administrative, coordination, and operational support to IOM’s labour mobility and reintegration programming, contributing to effective implementation of activities, strengthened collaboration with the LMU and partners, and alignment with national priorities and evolving labour mobility initiatives.
Responsibilities
Support day-to-day implementation of labour mobility and reintegration activities in line with approved work plans;
Track activity timelines, deliverables, and action points and flag delays, implementation issues, challenges and opportunities to advance labour mobility efforts to supervisor;
Provide logistical and administrative support for consultations with returned workers, families, Regional Recruitment Hubs, service providers, government counterparts and other stakeholders as needed;
Support routine coordination with the LMU and relevant partners, including meeting scheduling and follow-up on agreed actions and serve as the operational focal point for communication between IOM, LMU and field level stakeholders as required;
Assist with scheduling meetings, preparing participant lists, and compiling consultation documentation as required;
Maintain organized project files (physical and electronic), including high quality activity records, consultation notes, and training materials.
Support basic data cleaning, organization, and entry related to consultation findings, as required.
Support organization of training workshops for LMU staff, Regional Recruitment Hubs and other entities or individuals as needed.
Assist with coordination of translation, printing, and adaptation of training materials (e.g., Tok Pisin versions);
Support compilation of training reports, participant feedback, and post-training documentation.
Assist with coordination with partners, consultants, and service providers engaged under the project;
Support preparation of inputs to inception, progress, and final reports, including activity summaries, participant data, and annexes;
Compile and maintain databases, contact lists, and service provider directories developed under the project;
Assist with documentation of lessons learned, good practices, project monitoring reports, field reports, photographs and/or records for internal reporting purposes.
Support administrative and procurement processes in line with IOM procedures (e.g., travel requests, workshop costs, consultant support);
Assist with tracking of expenditures against planned activities, in coordination with programme and resources management staff;
Undertake other programme support tasks as requested by the supervisor.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications and Experience
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Administration, Business Administration, or a related field with 4 years of relevant experience;
Relevant administrative or programme support certifications are an asset.
Accredited Universities are those listed in the
UNESCO World Higher Education Database.
Experience
Minimum four (4) years of relevant experience in programme support, administration, or project coordination;
Experience supporting training workshops, consultations, or field-based activities is an advantage;
Experience working with government counterparts or development partners is desirable.
Skills
Strong organizational, coordination, and administrative skills;
Ability to manage multiple tasks and meet deadlines;
Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and basic data management tools;
Languages
All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).
For this position, fluency in English and Tok Pisin is required.
Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.
Required Competencies
IOM’s competency framework can be found at this
link
. Competencies will be assessed during the selection process.
Values
- all IOM staff members must abide by and demonstrate these five values:
Inclusion and respect for diversity
: Respects and promotes individual and cultural differences. Encourages diversity and inclusion.
Integrity and transparency
: Maintains high ethical standards and acts in a manner consistent with organizational principles/rules and standards of conduct.
Professionalism
: Demonstrates ability to work in a composed, competent and committed manner and exercises careful judgment in meeting day-to-day challenges.
Courage
: Demonstrates willingness to take a stand on issues of importance.
Empathy
: Shows compassion for others, makes people feel safe, respected and fairly treated.

: Develops and promotes effective collaboration within and across units to achieve shared goals and optimize results.
Delivering results
: Produces and delivers quality results in a service-oriented and timely manner. Is action oriented and committed to achieving agreed outcomes.
Managing and sharing knowledge
: Continuously seeks to learn, share knowledge and innovate.
Accountability
: Takes ownership for achieving the Organization’s priorities and assumes responsibility for own actions and delegated work.
Communication
: Encourages and contributes to clear and open communication. Explains complex matters in an informative, inspiring and motivational way.

– behavioural indicators (applicable only if with direct reports)
Leadership
: Provides a clear sense of direction, leads by example and demonstrates the ability to carry out the Organization’s vision. Assists others to realize and develop their leadership and professional potential.
Empowering others
: Creates an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential.
Building Trust
: Promotes shared values and creates an atmosphere of trust and honesty.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will direct, manage and ensure that mobile equipment repair is carried out in a productive and cost-effective manner to optimize mobile machinery availability and facilitate the delivery of Mining Services underground so productions targets can be met. You will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department, and this rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Supervise all maintenance Personnel in the workshop, including recruitment and termination of personnel.
Liaise closely with the Production Superintendent in respect of equipment servicing and preventive maintenance scheduling and required equipment availability.
Supervise and control any sub-contractor activity at the workshop.
Supervise all workshop apprentices under the guidance of the Apprenticeship Co-ordinator.
Prepare estimates and quotes on repairs for work to be carried out in the workshop where applicable
Regularly assess and determine if upgrades are required and check designs of buckets booms and GET meet site and manufacturer’s specification in conjunction with HOD Mining.
Provide support to the Mine Superintendent to optimize efficiencies in the underground mine to achieve the Weekly Plan.
Work closely with the Mine Superintendent and Shift Supervisors to improve mining standards, assess operator performance and identify improvement projects to maximize results, reduce risk and implement cost management initiatives.
Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to strive for a high level of performance by rewarding and recognizing high performance.
Ensure effective processes for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members are in place.
Continuously mentor and coach operators on acceptable mining standards and effective techniques on machinery to achieve these standards.
Identify skills gaps and training requirements and assist in developing training packages as required to close the skills gap.
Coordinate and assist with the delivery of training to employees.
Actively review the work performance of technicians and provide feedback to the area supervisors including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Ensure general housekeeping within the mine is of a high standard.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation
5+ years plus of underground mining experience (Essential)
2+ years Shift Supervisor experience (Essential)
Organizational skills – Good time management skills.
Good communication and interpersonal skills – Be an effective communicator and listener.
Extensive knowledge of SHE Management System relevant to K92 i.e. Policy and Procedures.
Supervisory skills – Be a good leader, motivator and teacher.
Good command of the English Language (oral & written).
Knowledge of various heavy earthmoving machinery components.
Knowledge and understanding of the Duty of Care standards, occupational Health & Safety Act & Regulations, Mining Inspection Act & Regulations.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Position Title:
Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer
Location: Port Moresby, National Capital District
Type: Full-time
Employing agency: Clinton Health Access Initiative Inc
Point of Hire: Port Moresby, National Capital District
BACKGROUND
The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skillsets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:
http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
.
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.
Malnutrition remains a critical public health challenge in Papua New Guinea with severe malnutrition accounting for 10% of Paediatric hospital admissions and a case fatality rate of 12.4%
[1]
. Exclusive breastfeeding for the first six months of life is a proven, cost effective and safe intervention to prevent malnutrition and its adverse effects. However, despite national efforts, the 2018 Demographic and Health Survey indicates that only 62% of children under six months in PNG are exclusively breastfed, highlighting gaps in early childhood nutrition practices
[2]
.
Madang District in Madang Province has been identified as a key project site for the Child Nutrition and Social Protection (CNSP) project due to its high rate of childhood malnutrition and limited access to essential health services. According to the Papua New Guinea Electronic Health Information System (eNHIS), the national target for moderate-to-severe malnutrition in children under five was set at less than 15% in 2023
[3]
.
However, Madang District reported a significantly higher malnutrition rate of 18.5 % in 2024, mirroring similar trends across Madang Province. The high burden of malnutrition stems from multiple interrelated factors, primarily the inability of families to provide adequate nutrition and the health system’s challenges in effectively engaging with communities on essential nutrition and child health interventions.
The inadequacy of health service delivery in Madang Province further exacerbates the malnutrition crisis. Outreach services remain low, with only seven integrated outreach sessions per 1,000 children under five years, limiting access to critical services such as immunization, growth monitoring, and nutrition counselling. Immunization coverage is alarmingly low at 21%, directly affecting vitamin A supplementation, which is essential for child growth and immunity. In addition, low antenatal care attendance of 47% for first visits and a facility-based delivery rate of only 32.1% further reduce opportunities for micronutrient supplementation during pregnancy, which is crucial for preventing maternal and child malnutrition. Addressing these service delivery gaps through targeted interventions will be key to improving child nutrition and overall health outcomes in Madang District.
Position Overview
The M&E Officer will lead the monitoring, evaluation, and learning efforts of the CNSP Project in Madang Province. This position plays a central role in tracking program performance, ensuring data-driven decision-making, and fostering accountability at all levels. The M&E Officer will be based in Port Moresby and report to the Special Advisor, Program Manager.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Design and implement a comprehensive M&E framework aligned with project objectives, CHAI internal systems, and donor reporting requirements.
Develop and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) across program areas, including VHA performance, health facility engagement, and community mobilization.
Establish and manage project data systems including databases, data collection tools, reporting templates, and dashboards.
Conduct baseline, midline, and endline assessments to evaluate program outcomes, with specific attention to malnutrition rates, immunization coverage, and access to child health services.
Train Village Health Assistants (VHAs), health facility staff, and implementing partners on M&E tools, protocols, and standards.
Coordinate and supervise routine data collection, data entry, and quality assurance across 28 wards, 6 health facilities, and 5 aid posts.
Lead regular data quality assessments, site visits, and supervision to ensure data integrity and compliance.
Analyze program data and generate monthly, quarterly, and annual reports for CHAI, Provincial Health Authority, and donor stakeholders.
Prepare presentations, data visualizations, and briefs for internal and external use, highlighting key program trends and insights.
Support implementation of community-based monitoring tools such as the Community Scorecard and biannual household surveys.
Facilitate learning sessions and performance review meetings to discuss program progress, challenges, and evidence-based improvements.
Document best practices, lessons learned, and success stories for internal learning and external communication.
Monitor safeguarding indicators and community feedback mechanisms, including grievance reporting and PSEA compliance.
Support capacity building of PHA staff, VHAs, and local partners in M&E systems and practices.
Ensure alignment and integration with national health information systems, such as eNHIS.
Collaborate with government and development partners on harmonized monitoring strategies and shared learning platforms.
Any other responsibilities assigned by the Senior Program Officer and Special Advisor, Programs from time to time.

jobs.title: Trainee Officer, Safety & Health
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
In this opportunity, we are looking for a young local Lihirian, who is keen, determined and is passionate to build career in Health & Safety. You will be introduced to the foundations of a safe and healthy workplace by learning directly from experienced Health & Safety Advisors and supporting frontline teams to identify, manage, and eliminate safety risks helping protect people from fatalities, injuries, illness and work-related harm.
As part of our team, you will
Participate in field inspections and safety audits to identify hazards and support compliance with safety standards and regulations.
Support the delivery of hands‑on safety coaching and training for site personnel, including pre‑task hazard assessments, general risk assessments, event reporting, and 5‑Why investigations.
Observe and reinforce site‑specific safety procedures, ensuring teams understand and follow established protocols.
Contribute to key safety programs such as fatal risk management, incident management, injury reduction, and health and wellbeing initiatives by applying field observations and feedback.
Assist in the execution of site‑based Health & Safety plans.
Support the Health & Safety Representative (HSR) program and promote a culture of speaking up and stopping unsafe work.
Actively contribute as a team member by asking questions, seeking feedback, sharing improvement ideas, and continuously learning.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring:
Experience in a School to Mine or similar early‑career development program.
The ability to follow procedures, apply practical judgement, and seek guidance when required.
A developing problem‑solving mindset, with the ability to learn through observation, experience, and trial and error.
Basic computer skills to support reporting and documentation.
Strong self‑awareness, adaptability, and a willingness to learn from feedback.
The ability to collaborate effectively with a diverse range of stakeholders and work productively within a team environment.
Drive, determination, and commitment to delivering high‑quality work aligned with Newmont’s values and safety culture.
Your work environment
This is a two year fixed term, full time position, operating Monday to Friday, with camp accommodation provided. Our employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will work closely with operational supervisors, superintendents, Health & Safety peers, site representatives, and reporting teams across the business. This is a practical, site‑based role that offers exposure to real‑world safety challenges, supported by experienced professionals who are committed to your development and success.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, safety is our first value. We offer meaningful early‑career opportunities where you can learn, grow, and make a genuine impact from day one. You’ll be supported by experienced leaders, exposed to industry‑leading safety practices, and empowered to contribute to a culture where everyone is accountable for keeping themselves and others safe.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

This position is responsible for the service and maintenance of fixed plant equipment in a safe and appropriate manner. You will ensure a preventative maintenance schedule is adhered to as well as perform reactive maintenance when equipment breaks down to ensure downtime of machinery is minimized.

Maintain and repair fixed plant equipment onsite in a safe, responsible and timely and effective manner ensuring all Fixed Plant and K92 mining standards are met.

Maintain all plant equipment and ensure all planning and scheduling maintenance activities are performed safely and more effectively.

Willingness to assist other trades as and when required.

Good working knowledge of the principles and practices of OH&S and Fixed Plant.
Be flexible and adaptable to the needs of the business and ability to work harmoniously as part of the team.

Current PNG Drivers Licence.

Looking for a Change?
Join CARE International in PNG and be part of an organisation that serves the needs of Papua New Guineans living in remote PNG.
EXTERNAL RECRUITMENT
Consultant
To lead - The Peacebuilding and Agriculture Project Endline Evaluation
CARE International in PNG is looking to recruit a suitable Consultant or Firm. CARE began working in partnership with remote and rural communities, government, non-government, and private sector partners in 1989. With over three and a half decades of experience, CARE has developed in-depth institutional knowledge of the complex operating environment, and expertise in building gender equality, empowering communities, brokering relationships, and supporting local organizations. The operations team is skilled in overcoming barriers such as limited in-country infrastructure, unpredictable weather, and local security concerns. CARE aims to create a more equal world for women and girls by building agency, changing relations, and transforming structures through its programming and partnerships, focusing on increasing women’s leadership and decision-making, challenging discriminatory social norms, improving access to health services, and supporting women's economic empowerment.
The purpose of the end-of-project evaluation is to assess outcome-level progress made against baseline values, measurement of outcome indicators, focusing on sustainability of key practices, behaviors, and systemic changes. It will also serve as a means to verify overall impact, extracting best practices for replication or scale-up, and ensuring that sustainability strategies are robust and meaningful in the long term as well as future program recommendations
Project Overview
PNG Enga Peacebuilding and Agriculture Support is an 18-month project funded by Minderoo Foundation Trust and implemented by CARE International in PNG from 1 December 2024 through 31 May 2026. The project aims to support communities affected by inter-communal conflict in Enga Province to improve peace, social cohesion, and livelihood resilience.
The overall goal of the project is to contribute to improved peace and social cohesion among the various ethnic groups in Enga Province. The project seeks to achieve the following outcomes, namely:
Outcome 1: Communities and key stakeholders establish stronger collaboration and dialogue, contributing to positive social contact between communities, effective conflict resolution, and lasting peace.
Outcome 2: Targeted communities and key stakeholders have enhanced capability to detect early warning signs of conflict and take collective actions, reducing the likelihood of violence.
Outcome 3: Women and marginalized groups in the communities achieve increased food security and sustainable livelihoods, fostering resilience, promoting gender equity, and strengthening conflict resolution capacities
The project operates in seven communities across Enga Province, including locations in Wabag and Lagaip districts, which were selected based on their high levels of conflict, accessibility for implementation, and the absence of other international peacebuilding initiatives.
Throughout the targeted seven wards across Wabag and Lagaip districts in Enga Province, the project works directly with community members, local leaders, women and youth groups, civil society organisations, and government stakeholders. These groups represent the primary impact and target populations who will benefit from strengthened peacebuilding mechanisms, improved conflict prevention capacities, and increased livelihood opportunities.

Familiarity with DFAT design monitoring evaluation and learning standards; and

Job Title:
Construction Site Engineer
Reports To:
Projects Manager

Campus and Facilities Management
Location:
IBSUniversity, Mt. Eriama, 11 Mile Campus
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS) began its journey in 1987 as a modest initiative under Nades & Associates, primarily offering revision classes to support the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants, now known as CPA PNG. Over the past 36 years, IBS has grown steadily into a private university-level institution. Today, IBS is recognised as one of the largest business schools in Papua New Guinea, offering degree programmes in Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology. In addition, the institution continues to provide academic pathways for Grade 10 and 12 school leavers, as well as industry-recognised certification opportunities for experienced professionals seeking formal qualifications in their respective fields. This success has been made possible through the dedication and commitment of our team, whose collective efforts continue to make a meaningful contribution to Papua New Guinea by helping to educate and empower both current and future citizens.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but also enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
ABOUT THIS ROLE:
Construction Site Engineer will be responsible for overseeing all the activities on the construction site. The Construction Site Engineer ensures that projects are completed on time, with a budget, and our client’s specifications. This includes planning, coordinating, and supervising onsite functions, staffing, scheduling, and material control.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
Execution of site work—Directing, executing, consulting, monitoring, quality controlling, and punch listing (rectifications) of relevant Civil Engineering construction works including earthwork, drainage work, road construction, and building construction (concrete and steel) along with incidental construction (curb laying, paving Interlocking concrete blocks, etc.).
Workplace Communications- Methods applicable to target groups, providing specific information to workers about their safety and developing team performances, commitment, and corporation.
Technical supervision during construction - Assess performances according to approved plans and drawings and consult the manager/professionals for any predicted problems and changes in the ongoing construction.
Supervise construction projects to ensure they are completed in line with the scope, time, budget, and set quality standards.
Ensure all work complies with building codes and safety regulations.
Inspect project sites regularly to identify and eliminate potential safety hazards.
Supervising and instructing the construction team as well as subcontractors
Communicating with clients’ suppliers, and laborers effectively
Prepare and submit progress reports.
Ensuring the quality of materials and workmanship meet specified standards and codes.
Manage the procurement of materials, machinery, tools and equipment necessary for the project.
Resolving conflicts or miscommunication that may happen onsite quickly and amicably.
Education and Qualification
Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or a related field preferred.
Minimum of 5 years’ proven experience in a similar role.
In-depth knowledge of construction procedures, equipment, OSHA guidelines, and project management principles
Excellent organizational, leadership and management skills
Ability to communicate and report effectively.
Aptitude in Math and strong problem-solving skills
Good physical condition and stamina
Current state licensure for contacting or similar, if required
Exceptional attention to detail with an ability to spot potential risks or issues before they arise.

The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners.

:

Ensure timely follow-up on action points from meetings.
Maintain confidentiality of sensitive information.
Support the Vice Chancellor and Council members with administrative tasks.

Good knowledge of legal procedures and documentation.
Strong organizational and communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
Responsible, reliable, and detail-oriented.

Full-time, Monday to Friday, with occasional extra hours for meetings or urgent tasks.

About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
This role will manage supplier performance and provide the timely purchasing and procurement of goods delivered on time according to specified quantity, quality and cost requirements and within the supply policy guidelines.
This role will also be responsible to minimize the impact of the Section on the environment and ensure the workplace health & safety of employees, Contractors and other stakeholders are maintained
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Recommend sources for supply of goods and services, and obtain quotations from suppliers
Analyse quotes provided for quality against specification, price, timely delivery and innovation and select the best value supplier
Ensure purchasing at the optimal price in relation to quality, quantity and delivery method.
Issue Purchase Orders that follow K92 Mining policies and standards
Ensure appropriate documentation is completed and filed for all transactions.
Develop an understanding of the supply market and ensure well documented cost management.
Review performance of key suppliers across KPIs including price competitiveness, lead time compliance, delivery completeness & number of discrepancies.
Investigate invoice discrepancies to ensure suppliers are paid in a timely manner.
Investigate PO and goods receipt discrepancies to ensure that goods are available on site to meet requirements
Recommend procure to pay process improvements in conjunction with systems enhancements
Encourage site users to follow Supply processes and reinforce the correct process where required
Regular communication with internal customers to understand expectations and required timeframes when issuing purchase orders.
Follow up with suppliers to understand delays in quoting and seek alternative quotes as required
Ensure purchase requests are converted to purchase orders and issued to suppliers in a timely manner.
Manage out of hours purchase needs.
Communicate with suppliers to ensure that specified delivery timeframes are met.
Seek alternative suppliers, logistics solutions or substitute products where emergency requirements or supplier failure may lead to goods not being available on site on the date required
Participate in the planning of shutdown maintenance and project work to ensure the availability of goods during periods of unusual demand.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential and/or preferred that you:
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining values
Understanding of ERP systems (Pronto) to support purchasing processes.
Understanding of purchasing strategies, supplier evaluation and selection tools and their interaction with other supply processes.
Possess the ability to draft and compile quote request.
Possess Negotiation skills and understanding of negotiation techniques.
Understand Commercial analysis and evaluation.
Understanding total cost and life cycle costing.
Possess problem solving and decision-making capability.
Possess excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Have experience communicating with vendors in PNG and internationally
Possess the ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders.
Possess minimum 3 years’ experience in industry with relevant experience in transactional purchasing
Mining Industry experience preferred. Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

Lead growth, innovation, and transformation across all banking operations.

Executive Opportunity – Chief Executive Officer
We are partnering with Teachers Savings and Loan Society Limited (TISA Bank) to identify an accomplished Chief Executive Officer to lead the Bank through its next phase of growth and transformation.
About TISA Bank:
TISA Bank is Papua New Guinea’s first homegrown commercial bank, built on a 50+ year legacy of the Teachers Savings and Loan Society. The Bank was granted their commercial banking licence in August 2024 and provides innovative and secure banking solutions across Personal, SME, Corporate, Agency and Digital Banking, supporting individuals, families, start-ups, small businesses, and large corporates. As a locally-owned institution, TISA Bank is committed to delivering better banking options for Papua New Guineans and shaping the development of the local financial sector.
The Role:
Reporting to the TISA Bank Board of Directors and the Group CEO, the incumbent will lead TISA Bank through its next phase of growth, setting and executing the Bank’s strategic direction while ensuring financial strength, regulatory compliance, and sustainable long-term performance. This high-profile role carries full accountability for the Bank’s overall performance, risk management, governance, and stakeholder engagement. You will lead a high-performing executive team, foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, and innovation, and act as the Bank’s principal representative with regulators, government, shareholders, and other key stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities:
Steer the Bank’s Strategic Direction
– Develop long-term strategies with the Group CEO and Board, and oversee operational, financial, and risk management functions.
Drive Operational Excellence
– Implement the Bank’s annual operational plan and budget, optimise cost-to-income ratios, and improve financial performance metrics
Cultivate a High-Performing Culture
– Foster an innovative, customer-focused environment that empowers employees and drives exceptional service
About You:
The successful candidate will be a proven executive leader with:
CEO or senior executive experience within a regulated financial institution
Deep experience across Retail, SME, and Corporate banking, including digital and agency channels
Strong track record of delivering financial and operational performance, including profitability, efficiency, and balance sheet growth
Demonstrated capability in risk management, regulatory compliance, and governance
Experience in emerging or frontier markets; Papua New Guinea or similar environments highly regarded
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, including with regulators and government
Ability to lead organisational transformation and inspire high-performing teams
Degree or postgraduate qualifications in Banking, Finance, Economics, or a related discipline
Strong communication, negotiation, people management, interpersonal and influencing skills to build strong business relationships and drive a culture of collaboration and innovation
Ability to satisfy the Fit and Proper requirements as set out under the Bank and Financial Institutions Act
This is a unique leadership opportunity to shape the future of a growing, locally-owned bank, expand access to banking solutions across PNG, and make a lasting impact on the wider financial sector.

POSITION: Dean, Institute of Higher Education.
LOCATION: Popondetta, (Oro) Northern Province
DURATION: Three-year renewable contract with a 6-month probationary period
REMUNERATION: Competitive remuneration offered
ABOUT THE MODAWA INSTITUTE
The Modawa Institute is a newly established higher education provider in the Northern Province of PNG.  The Institute formally came into being as of 1 January 2024 but builds on more than 70 years of involvement in higher education within Papua New Guinea.  The Instutute is Registered with DHERST. There are three schools, each with a Head of School:
St Margaret’s School of Nursing and community health.
The Bishop Newton School of Theology.
The David Hand School of Teaching.
The institute seeks to develop a learning community where the various disciplines enrich each other, seeking to raise up leaders committed to excellence and innovation in their respective fields.
THE ROLE OF DEAN
The Dean will operate within the functions, roles and responsibilities outlined for the Principal in the Institute’s Canon (constitution) and under the guidance of the Chair of the Governing Council.
The Dean will have oversight of the institution, leading a team of academic, administrative and support employees. He or she will be the Executive Officer of the Council, the team leader within the Institute and its public face in the wider community. The Dean will nurture the academic life of the Institute and teach within one of its schools. He or she will maintain academic currency, model scholarship within the institute and contribute more widely to academic discussion in his or her field. The Dean may initially also be a head of school for one of the schools of the Institute.
He or she will have responsibility to oversight the administrative life of the institute, ensuring its financial and administrative integrity and ongoing viability. The Dean will be expected to encourage partners and build the financial base of the institute.
The Dean will be responsible for:
Maintaining and developing the ethos and vision of the college in line with Council strategies and directions.
Developing and leading a leadership team that will cultivate a positive environment for learning and work.
Collaborate closely with the other heads of schools.
Build the profile of the institute within the broader community and  strengthen relationships with business and industry representatives, donors, other Higher Education Institutions and national and overseas partners.
Contributing to the scholarly life of the institute.
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
The Dean will hold, appropriate post-graduate academic qualifications in the relevant field.  He or she will have had significant experience in the higher education sector. The person will have experience in organisational administration, be fluent in written and spoken English, and have excellent presentation and public speaking skills. A commitment to uphold the ethos and values of the Modawa Institute is essential.
The Modawa Institute looks for staff who will are:
Deeply motivated by a care for young people.
Have a passion for learning.
Are self-starters and disciplined in their use of time.
Hold spiritual values in line with those of the Church.
Have a relationship style that evokes contributes to team building.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS
Under the Canon (constitution) of the Institute the Principal of the Institute (Dean) must be a communicant member of the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea, or of a Church in Communion with the Anglican Church of Papua New Guinea.  If the Dean is also a Priest, he or she must hold a licence or permission to officiate from either the Archbishop or the Bishop of Popondetta.
CONDITIONS OF EMPLOYMENT
Remuneration:  By negotiation and in accord with qualifications and experience. A house on campus will be provided.  Relocation expenses by negotiation.
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG.
HOW TO APPLY:
Email your application to Modawa Institute with the following:
A cover letter addressing the following:
Your interest in becoming the Dean of the Institute.
Your educational leadership background and subject specialisations.
A description of your leadership style
Outline your teaching philosophy;
Your current resume;
A copy of your Academic Qualifications.
Two written references.

jobs.description:
Senior Project Associate (Emergency Preparedness & Response)
Job Description
Introduction
Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is committed to ensuring a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally, while working towards harnessing the full potential of migration. Read more about IOM's workplace culture at
IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration
Applications are welcome from internal and external candidates. For all IOM vacancies, applications from qualified and eligible first-tier candidates are considered before those of qualified and eligible second-tier candidates in the selection process. For the purpose of this vacancy,
internal and internal-equivalent candidates
are considered as first-tier candidates.
Organizational Context and Scope
IOM has been operational in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2001, supporting the Government and communities in addressing a wide range of migration and mobility-related challenges. Guided by IOM’s Strategic Vision and aligned with national priorities, IOM’s programming spans all four pillars of its global Strategic Results Framework: saving lives and protecting people on the move; driving solutions to displacement; facilitating safe pathways for regular migration; and strengthening migration governance.
Operating from its head office in Port Moresby and through decentralized field offices across the country, IOM in PNG implements integrated programming in disaster risk reduction and emergency response; climate change and human mobility; counter-trafficking and protection of vulnerable migrants; migration health; community stabilization and durable solutions; border and migration management; and assisted voluntary return and reintegration. IOM also plays a key role in supporting government-led efforts to improve migration data, enhance institutional capacity, and ensure whole-of-government and whole-of-society approaches to safe, regular, and inclusive migration governance.
Under the overall supervision of the Emergency Management and Peacebuilding Coordinator and the direct supervision of the National Project Officer-Resilience Building in Port Moresby, the incumbent will support the implementation of disaster risk reduction (DRR), disaster risk management (DRM), emergency preparedness and response, and community stabilisation initiatives across target locations. The role will provide day-to-day technical and operational support for the effective, timely, and high-quality delivery of programme activities, working closely with communities, local authorities, and partner organisations.
The incumbent will contribute to risk-informed programming and community-based resilience approaches, with a strong focus on quality assurance, accountability, and adaptive implementation. Through this work, the position supports IOM’s broader efforts to enhance community resilience and address underlying drivers of conflict, vulnerability, and displacement in Papua New Guinea.
Under this vacancy, IOM Papua New Guinea will recruit
5 Senior Project Associates (Emergency Preparedness & Response), one each to be based in Kokopo, Kimbe, Wewak, Mendi, and Kiunga.
Responsibilities
Support the coordination and implementation of disaster risk reduction (DRR), emergency response, and community stabilisation programming, contributing to project delivery, adaptive implementation across target locations.
Monitor field-level project activities, noting operational challenges, potential risks, and emerging issues, and provide practical inputs to support DRR, emergency preparedness and response, and stabilization activities.
Support the preparation and delivery of DRR, emergency preparedness and response, and community stabilization workshops, training sessions, and awareness campaigns, in in with local needs and programme objectives.
Support the preparation of high-quality internal and external reports that capture results, lessons learned, and recommendations for programme improvement.
Coordinate with the government authorities, Non-Governmental Organizations, United Nations agencies, civil society, partners as well as IOM field offices to facilitate implementation of programme activities.
Monitor internal displacement trends and emerging humanitarian situations within target locations, conducting field-based data collection missions in coordination with the Data and
Analytics Officer, the National Project Officer–Resilience in Port Moresby, and the Emergency Management and Peacebuilding Coordinator, and provide inputs for analytical briefs and situation updates to support programme implementation and operational follow-up.
Provide inputs for project development initiatives supporting the disaster resilient and recovery efforts in communities impacted by disasters and conflict.
Coordinate with local authorities to support at-risk, and disaster-affected communities in the implementation of local development and community stabilization activities.
In coordination with the Migration, Environment and Climate Change (MECC) Officer in Port Moresby, assist in integrating climate change adaptation consideration into DRR community resilience activities.
Support activities related to the development and implementation of early warning systems in collaboration with local authorities and stakeholders, contributing to strengthened community preparedness and resilience.
Provide weekly updates on field progress of DRR and community stabilization programming and escalate issues and concerns to the focal point and the Emergency and Disaster Management (EDM) Unit in Port Moresby for awareness and follow-up action.
Identify and report on emerging conflicts or risks in target areas, providing inputs for appropriate interventions and supporting programme adaptation to the evolving needs of the community. Assist in conducting regular conflict sensitivity and political economy analyses to support programme implementation and promote context-appropriate interventions that do not exacerbate existing tensions.
Coordinate the timely submission of the monthly financial expenditure report, asset inventory checklist, staff timesheets, and vehicle logbooks to the relevant focal points at the field level and in Port Moresby.
Perform such other duties as may be assigned.
Qualifications
Required Qualifications and Experience
Education
Bachelor’s degree in Disaster Management, Environmental Science, Social Science, Development Studies, or similar relevant field from an accredited academic institution with four years of relevant professional experience; or
High school diploma with six years of relevant professional experience.
Accredited Universities are those listed in the
UNESCO World Higher Education Database.
Experience
Experience in
DRR, emergency response,
transition and recovery, community development and activities supporting
Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs).
Knowledge of DRR, emergency response, community stabilization and (re) integration activities,
as well as peacebuilding
and development issues
.
Experience supporting the organization and facilitation of capacity building activities and training sessions for a variety of audiences.
Experience in liaising with governmental authorities as well as with national institutions or service providers.
Experience in peace reconciliation processes is an advantage.
Experience in facilitating consultative meetings and collecting qualitative and quantitative data is an advantage.
Experience coordinating operational activities with government counterparts, INGOs, UN agencies, or Private Sector in field locations in Papua New Guinea.
Skills
Ability to monitor field activities and compile operational updates and reports.
Good organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse stakeholders.
Proficiency in standard computer applications and data management tools relevant to programme implementation.
Languages
All IOM staff members in all categories are required to be fluent in one of the IOM's official languages (English, French, Spanish).
For this position, fluency Tok Pisin and English is required.
Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

link
