About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government, through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program focuses on supporting the Government of PNG to strengthen the national TVET system to promote quality TVET; supporting technical colleges to deliver high-quality TVET training; enhancing the diversity and employability of TVET graduates; and elevating Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG in the TVET sector.
SWLT is the primary mechanism to support PNG and Australia to deliver on commitments made under the revised Joint Statement of Intent on TVET signed at the 2024 Australia-Papua New Guinea Ministerial Forum. It also aligns with PNG’s
Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
, as well as broader goals articulated in the
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, including locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth.
This Opportunity
The
Deputy Director Operations
is responsible for managing the efficiency and effectiveness of the SWLT operations and administrative functions, including management of systems and processes that comply with DFAT and Palladium policies and local PNG laws.
By aligning internal practices with external policy priorities, the Deputy Director Operations helps to lead a responsive, adaptive, and values-driven workplace and models a positive and effective approach to mentoring, learning, probity and compliance.
Primary Responsibilities
The
Deputy Director Operations
will be responsible for setting and managing a robust operational baseline from which SWLT delivers technical inputs. This includes the following key functions:
Implement, review and update operational policies and procedures related to HR, finance, risk and fraud management, procurement, logistics, travel and safety and security. Ensuring all policies and procedures are in line with Palladium guidelines, and in compliance with Papua New Guinean and Australian Government policies
Drive continuous improvement through feedback, reflection and innovation to adapt operational systems in line with SWLT requirements, and introduce new ways of working including through technology, data, and AI to improve operational efficiency
Lead and manage relationships with key stakeholders including DFAT, Government of PNG counterparts, service providers, implementing partners and internal colleagues, ensuring clear communication, alignment with program objectives, and effective resolution of operational issues
Provide senior‑level operational support to financial oversight, including contributing to budgeting, forecasting, expenditure tracking and financial risk management, and ensuring operational decisions support sound financial management and Head Contract requirements
Supervise, support and mentor operations staff, providing clear direction, coaching and performance feedback, and fostering an inclusive, respectful and high‑performing office culture that values learning, accountability and continuous improvement
Lead operational planning and coordination for field activities, including cohesion between travel, security, logistics and resource allocation, ensuring activities are well‑planned, appropriately resourced and responsive to program priorities and contextual risks
Ensure risk management frameworks are in place and actively monitored, identifying emerging operational, financial, safety and reputational risks and working with senior leadership to implement timely mitigation measures
Ensure strict adherence to security protocols and duty of care policies for all staff and consultants, including oversight of security planning, incident management, compliance with DFAT and Palladium requirements, and promotion of a strong safety culture across the program
Understand and contribute to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required
Adhere to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and commit to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.
Model, contribute to and support an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts
Support and uphold the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as reducing resource use and promoting climate-friendly practices.
Contribute to the development and implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles are embedded within program delivery.
About You
You will have proven experience in the following areas:
Managing large-scale donor-funded development programs, including financial oversight and accurate budget management, experience overseeing large and complex procurements and contracts, and quality assurance of operational processes.
The ability to mentor, coach, and lead diverse teams, fostering a positive culture of learning, open communication and collaboration, including conducting performance management of staff, working with team members in setting key performance indicators, monitoring results and applying remedies as required.
Sound problem-solving and decision-making skills, applied in dynamic and complex settings, and a demonstrated ability to be adaptive in managing competing and changing priorities and delivering results.
Closely monitoring risks and issues, including identifying, managing and implementing appropriate mitigation strategies, including fraud prevention and compliance monitoring adhering to Australian and Papua New Guinean policies and legislations.
Strong interpersonal skills with the ability to operate diplomatically and cross-culturally with government, private sector, and community stakeholders.
Demonstrated ability to work autonomously while contributing effectively within a team.
Participation and positive engagement in diverse teams, supporting a results-driven culture of learning and inclusion.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
To Apply
Please submit your application online at
https://palladium.csod.com/ux/ats/careersite/2/home/requisition/24985?c=palladium
, including your CV and detailed cover letter, outlining your suitability and experience in line with the requirements of the position.
Closing date: End of day Sunday 5 April 2026.
Candidates may be interviewed on a rolling basis.
Equity, Diversity & Inclusion -
Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We welcome applications from all sections of society and actively encourage diversity to drive innovation, creativity, success and good practice. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.
Should you require any adjustments or accommodations to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at
[email protected]
and we will be in touch to discuss.
Safeguarding -
We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. We are committed to ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with Palladium are treated with respect and are free from abuse. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced selection process including safeguarding-focused interviews and a rigorous due diligence process.

Operations Coordinator -
YUS Coffee Cooperative
Reports to: TKCP Livelihoods Program Coordinator & YUS Conservation Coffee Cooperative Boards
Term: Annual contract, renewable based on performance
Location: YUS Conservation Area, Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea
About the YUS Conservation Coffee Cooperatives
The Yopno, Uruwa, and Som (YUS) Conservation Coffee Cooperatives represent over 500 coffee-farming families across more than 30 villages in the YUS Conservation Area. Farmers grow coffee sustainably under native forest canopy at elevations of 1,000-2,200+ meters. Coffee is selectively harvested, manually washed, and dried on raised beds. Through a long-standing partnership with the Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program (TKCP), the Cooperative has supplied specialty markets for nearly 15 years. With cupping scores averaging in the low- to mid-80s and microlots reaching the high 80s, YUS coffee has strong potential for growth. However, logistics, communication, and coordination challenges continue to limit production and delivery.
Position Overview
The YUS Coffee Cooperative Operations Coordinator is responsible for implementing the Cooperative's annual business and operating plans. Contracted through TKCP and seconded to the Cooperative, the Coordinator ensures smooth, transparent, and effective operations throughout each coffee season. This role is ideal for PNG-based agribusiness professionals with strong experience in supply chains, cooperative management, and rural community engagement.
Key Responsibilities
Develop annual operating plans and budgets with Cooperative Directors, Coffee Inspectors, and Cluster Leads.
Coordinate sourcing of coffee from clusters according to agreed volumes, quality, and timelines.
Organize cost-effective logistics for coffee movement from villages to the mill.
Negotiate sales contracts with buyers, including pricing, delivery terms, and quality expectations.
Maintain communication with airstrip inspectors, freight providers, mills, buyers, and TKCP.
Oversee Airstrip Inspectors and ensure quality control at the zone level.
Work with CICL, Morobe Provincial Government, and Kabwum District Development Authority to secure air freight financing.
YUS Coffee Cooperative Operations Coordinator
Coordinate with partners on quality evaluation, lot management, and buyer expectations.
Manage Cooperative finances with transparency and accountability.
Coordinate farmer payments through Cluster Leaders.
Train Coffee Inspectors and Cluster Leaders on quality control, record-keeping, and production management.
Standardize record-keeping systems across clusters and inspectors.
Support Cooperatives in maintaining records on membership, compliance, production, payments, and traceability.
Prepare and present annual business and financial performance reports.
Ideal Candidate
PNG national with experience in agribusiness, coffee value chains, or cooperative management.
Strong communication and negotiation skills.
Experience working in rural or remote settings.
Ability to coordinate logistics and manage multiple stakeholders.
Commitment to transparency, accountability, and community development.
Willingness to travel frequently within the YUS landscape.
Has relevant qualifications, trainings, and experience.
Preferably based in Lae or Morobe province.

jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Madang, Milne Bay, New Ireland, West New Britain, Western Highlands
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an
Advisor, Maintenance Dispatch
, you'll be at the centre of real‑time maintenance coordination for our heavy mobile fleet. Your decisions will directly influence fleet availability, maintenance efficiency, and safe production outcomes. You'll use live equipment health data and mine dispatch systems to guide operators, prioritise work, minimise downtime, and ensure maintenance events run smoothly and accurately.
As part of our team, you will
Manage all equipment maintenance down and up events, ensuring safe and timely coordination.
Collaborate with maintenance supervisor and dispatch heavy mobile equipment in line with the approved maintenance schedule.
Work closely with Mining and Maintenance Supervisors to action priorities and optimise workflow.
Monitor real‑time equipment health data (Mine Star, telemetry) to identify issues early and support defect elimination.
Liaise with fuel bay and maintenance personnel to action corrective tasks at optimal times.
Ensure high‑quality data capture throughout your shift, including accurate down‑event coding.
Actively contribute to team discussions, raise issues, seek feedback, and stop unsafe work.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Mechanical Trade Qualification or extensive mechanical experience.
Strong communication skills with the ability to explain technical issues in simple language.
Confident in machine analytics, problem‑solving, and making fast decisions with limited information.
Solid understanding of heavy mobile equipment telemetry and sensor data.
Proficient in SAP and computer‑literate in MS Office.
Experience with (or willingness to learn): Modular Mining, Cat SIS, Mine Star, Power BI, Cat ET.
Excellent attention to detail, time‑management, and the ability to work autonomously under pressure.
Strong interpersonal skills for collaboration, feedback, and conflict resolution.
Familiarity with PNG Mine Safety Act, safety systems, and operational procedures.
Current PNG Driver’s Licence.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 28:14 Day / Night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an ensuite and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

41931

jobs.title: National Consultant – Needs Assessment and Ward Development Planning
jobs.description:
National Consultant – Needs Assessment and Ward Development Planning
Job Description
Introduction
Established in 1951, IOM is a Related Organization of the United Nations, and as the leading UN agency in the field of migration, works closely with governmental, intergovernmental and non-governmental partners. IOM is dedicated to promoting humane and orderly migration for the benefit of all. It does so by providing services and advice to governments and migrants.
IOM is committed to ensuring a workplace where all employees can thrive professionally, while working towards harnessing the full potential of migration. Read more about IOM's workplace culture at
IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration
Nature of the consultancy:
The consultancy is a short-term, specialized technical assignment aimed at supporting the implementation of the Pilot Ward Development Plans initiative in two selected pilot wards — one in Enga Province and one in Western Highlands Province.
The consultant will provide expert technical support to conduct a comprehensive, gender-, youth-, and disability-sensitive needs assessment in these two wards and contribute to strengthening inclusive, accountable, and displacement-sensitive local governance systems.
The consultancy is analytical, facilitative, and advisory in nature. It requires demonstrated expertise in inclusive governance, gender equality and social inclusion (GESI), disability inclusion, migration and displacement dynamics, participatory planning methodologies, and community engagement in fragile, conflict-affected, and disaster-prone contexts.
Project Context and Scope:
Papua New Guinea’s Highlands Region continues to experience recurrent conflict, displacement, weak local governance structures, and limited service delivery capacity. These conditions have contributed to growing numbers of internally displaced persons and heightened community fragility. Ward officials who serve as the first level of local governance often lack the tools, skills, and inclusive processes needed to effectively identify community priorities, coordinate stakeholders, and manage development planning. The absence of structured, inclusive, and evidence‑based Ward Development Plans makes it difficult for displaced and vulnerable communities to articulate needs or access district and provincial funding channels.
To address these gaps, Project seeks to strengthen local governance and community resilience through the development of pilot Ward Development Plans in two selected wards, with a focus on the needs of internally displaced populations and marginalized community groups. As reflected in project documents and activation correspondence, the initiative aims to operationalize inclusive community consultations, improve participatory decision-making processes, and support local authorities and communities to jointly plan and prioritize development interventions. The project complements broader efforts in the Highlands to stabilize conflict‑affected areas, promote social cohesion, and align community-led planning with district and provincial development systems
Responsibilities
Under the overall supervision of the Emergencies and Disaster Management (EDM) Coordinator and the direct supervision of the Highlands Region Focal Point, the consultant will provide technical support to inclusive needs assessments, ward-level consultations, and the drafting, validation, and launch of Ward Development Plans, in line with the National Framework for Ward Development and relevant provincial plans. The consultant will work closely with Ward Development Committees, local authorities, and communities to ensure quality, inclusivity, and accountability across all project outputs, contributing to community resilience, peacebuilding, and the prevention of conflict and displacement in the Highlands Region of Papua New Guinea., the consultant will be responsible for the following:
Lead the design and implementation of a comprehensive, gender-, youth-, and disability-sensitive needs assessment in prioritized wards in the Highlands Region, applying Leave No One Behind (LNOB) and conflict-sensitive approaches, including the development and application of appropriate assessment tools and methodologies.
Facilitate ward- and community-level consultations with ward officials, community leaders, women’s groups, youth representatives, and persons with disabilities to ensure inclusive participation, context-specific analysis, and locally grounded findings.
Analyse assessment findings to identify priority needs, service gaps, protection risks, and resilience priorities, and prepare a gender-, youth-, and disability-sensitive needs assessment report for review and validation.
Support the organization and facilitation of feedback and validation consultations with communities, Ward Development Committees (WDCs), and relevant stakeholders to review, refine, and validate draft Ward Development Plans.
Provide technical support and capacity strengthening to Ward Development Committees (WDCs) on inclusive ward development planning, ensuring alignment with the National Framework for Ward Development (NFWD) and relevant provincial integrated development plans.
Provide technical guidance to IOM and WDCs during participatory planning processes leading to the drafting and development of tailored, gender-responsive Ward Development Plans, responsive to local context, displacement dynamics, and disaster and conflict risks.
Support the integration of resource mobilization strategies into Ward Development Plans to enhance feasibility, sustainability, and implementation potential.
Organize and facilitate community-based workshops, dialogues, training sessions, and awareness activities related to disaster risk reduction/management (DRR/M), stabilization, peacebuilding, conflict resolution, and social cohesion, ensuring inclusivity and relevance to local needs.
Develop two gender‑responsive Ward Development Plans through community‑based participatory approaches, and conducting  ward-level consultations and feedback sessions to finalize the Ward Development Plans and contribute to the formal validation and launch of the plans, in coordination with local authorities and stakeholders.
Support reporting and documentation, ensuring the preparation of high-quality, comprehensive reports capturing project outputs, outcomes, lessons learned, and recommendations for future programming.

jobs.description:
PAPUA NEW GUINEA UNIVERSITY OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND ENVIRONMENT
Preamble
On 19 March 2026, the Interim Council of the Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNG UNRE) approved the recruitment of a Dean for Position No.:
UNRE – GB
001
, Designation:
Dean for the School of Sustainable Resources Management and Business Studies
.
The incumbent for the position is required by the Council to lead the establishment of the
Momis Ocean and Climate Research Institute
and a Momis Fellowship for the Institute as approved by the Council on 28 November 2025.
About the University
PNG UNRE is a specialised national university mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNG UNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development outcomes across Papua New Guinea and the Pacific region.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from distinguished and highly motivated academics for appointment as
Dean / Fellow – Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute (MOCRI)
.
This is a flagship, internationally significant leadership role responsible for establishing and advancing the Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute as a centre of excellence in climate science, ocean research, disaster risk reduction, and environmental sustainability in the Pacific.
Based at the Vudal Campus with operational engagement in Rabaul and key field sites, the Institute will focus on cutting-edge research in ocean systems, climate change, environmental monitoring, and early warning systems. The successful appointee will lead multidisciplinary research programs, develop postgraduate training, and build global partnerships aligned with Papua New Guinea’s national priorities and international climate commitments.
The role reports directly to the Vice Chancellor and is central to PNG UNRE’s strategic ambition to strengthen its global research profile and leadership in climate resilience and sustainability.
Key Responsibilities
Provide strategic leadership in the establishment and growth of the Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute.
Lead high-impact, multidisciplinary research programs in climate science, oceanography, environmental systems, and disaster risk reduction.
Develop and oversee environmental monitoring systems and early warning mechanisms for climate-related hazards.
Establish and grow postgraduate (Masters and PhD) research programs in climate and ocean sciences.
Secure competitive research funding and build international research collaborations.
Publish in high-impact academic journals and contribute to global scientific discourse.
Build strong partnerships with government agencies, international institutions, and development partners.
Lead community-based research and outreach initiatives supporting climate resilience and sustainable livelihoods.
Integrate traditional knowledge systems with modern scientific approaches in addressing environmental challenges.
Provide high-level advisory input to the University and national stakeholders on climate and environmental policy.
Oversee Institute governance, staffing, budgeting, and operational frameworks.
Qualifications, Knowledge, Skills & Experience
PhD in Climate Science, Oceanography, Environmental Science, Engineering, Geophysics, or a closely related discipline.
Minimum of 15–20 years’ experience in academic, research, or scientific leadership roles.
Demonstrated success in leading large-scale research programs or institutes.
Strong publications record with a high citation level and proven ability to secure research funding.
Expertise in areas such as climate systems, ocean science, environmental monitoring, or disaster risk management.
Experience working in developing country contexts or the Pacific region is highly desirable.
Proven ability to build and sustain international collaborations and partnerships.
Strong leadership, strategic planning, and organisational capabilities.
Excellent communication, stakeholder engagement, and policy advisory skills.
Commitment to sustainability, climate resilience, and community impact.
Salary Range
Professor Base Salary: PGK81,707.00 – PGK99,864.00
International Market Allowance: PGK76, 146.00 – PGK113, 092
(plus applicable allowances, housing, research support, and benefits)
Why Join PNGUNRE?
This is a rare opportunity to lead a transformative research institute positioned at the forefront of global climate science in one of the world’s most environmentally significant regions.
Papua New Guinea is home to some of the planet’s largest remaining rainforests and ocean ecosystems, making it a critical frontier for climate research, biodiversity conservation, and sustainability innovation.
The Momis Ocean & Climate Research Institute offers:
A unique platform to shape global climate research agendas
Opportunities to influence national and international policy
Access to rich, under-researched environmental systems
Strong institutional support for research, innovation, and collaboration
The chance to integrate indigenous knowledge systems with modern science

A detailed Curriculum Vitae, including publications and research funding record
Certified copies of academic qualifications

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
About this Role
Our Lihir operation in the Power & Utilities department has an opportunity for a
Superintendent – Power & Utilities Electrical Maintenance
. Reporting to the Manager – Power & Utilities, the successful candidate will lead the electrical maintenance, engineering, planning, reliability & high voltage operations. Monitoring, diagnosing & improving electrical maintenance work & systems across the various power generation & distribution assets on Lihir Island.
Key Responsibilities
Lead Power & Utilities electrical maintenance, engineering, planning, reliability & high voltage operations across Power & Utilities assets, ensure safety is top priority & assets are maintained & available to support the site power demands.
Develop maintenance strategies, procedures and guidelines for effective maintenance of P&U assets, in line with site maintenance business practices & systems.
Adhere to compliance with safety, environmental & mining regulations.
Monitor, Diagnose & Improve teams’ performance & implement improvement strategies.
Run budget and resources for Power & Utilities electrical maintenance & reliability teams.
Accountable for Electrical reliability across Power & Utilities electrical assets.
Conduct regular inspections and safety audits all assets, work & systems.
Solve maintenance issues and streamline power and utilities processes.
Coach and guide the team on safe work practices & procedures.
Responsible for identifying relevant risks, implementing mitigation measures, and continuous risk monitoring.
Appointed Mine Electrician for the department.
Training & Experience
A bachelor’s degree in engineering, Electrical Engineering, diploma, Electrical Tradesman or a related field.
Several years of experience in power generation & high voltage management and systems, demonstrating progression through roles of increasing responsibility.
Advanced understanding of power generation & utilities such as reciprocating engine generation, control systems, high-pressure steam boilers, potable water plants, demineralization plants, incinerators, safety compliance, and stakeholder collaboration.
Advanced knowledge and practical application in maintenance scheduling, performance monitoring, budgeting, risk mitigation and compliance with safety and environmental policies.
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices.
Competent understanding of cost management and financial principles.
Advanced understanding and application of maintenance systems, SAP, scheduling software programs and tools Competent knowledge of key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics for performance.
Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices.
Competent ability to interact, influence and resolve conflict with various stakeholders.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21  Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you! jobs.description:
Project Lead - GBV Training Program
FHI 360 is a global development organization with over 50 years of experience partnering with governments, civil society, and communities to deliver evidence-based solutions that improve health, promote gender equality, and strengthen social systems. In Papua New Guinea, FHI 360 works with national and subnational stakeholders to address complex development challenges, including gender inequality and violence against women and girls, while upholding strong safeguarding, ethical, and accountability standards in line with DFAT and international best practice.
Gender-Based Violence (GBV) remains a critical human rights and public health issue in PNG, driven by unequal power relations, harmful social norms, and structural barriers to accessing services. FHI 360 adopts a survivor-centred, trauma-informed, and rights-based approach to GBV prevention and response, focusing on strengthening the capacity of frontline service providers, improving referral and coordination mechanisms, and ensuring safe, confidential, and ethical engagement with survivors. This position will support the delivery of high-quality GBV training across selected provinces, contributing to improved service quality and strengthened GBV response systems.
Job Summary:
The Project Lead will provide overall technical, operational, and strategic leadership for the delivery of Gender-Based Violence (GBV) training across five selected provinces under the ABT–PATH subcontract. The role ensures high-quality implementation, strong stakeholder coordination, compliance with DFAT and FHI360 safeguarding standards, and timely delivery of outputs and reports.
Accountabilities
Program Leadership & Management
Lead planning, coordination, and implementation of GBV training activities across all five provinces.
Oversee development and adaptation of training schedules, workplans, and budgets.
Ensure alignment with ABT/PATH objectives, DFAT requirements, and national GBV policies.
Provide day-to-day supervision and mentoring of GBV Training Officers and M&E Officer.
Stakeholder Engagement
Act as the primary focal point with ABT, Provincial Health Authorities (PHAs), and key GBV stakeholders.
Strengthen coordination with health, police, welfare, and referral pathway actors.
Represent FHI360 in technical meetings and provincial engagements related to GBV.
Quality Assurance & Safeguarding
Ensure all training activities adhere to FHI360 and DFAT safeguarding, PSEAH, and child protection policies.
Maintain high technical and ethical standards in GBV training delivery.
Address implementation risks and escalate issues promptly.
Reporting & Compliance
Review and approve programmatic and narrative reports for submission to ABT.
Ensure accurate documentation of activities, lessons learned, and outcomes.
Support audits, performance assessments, and compliance reviews as required.
Required Qualifications & Experience
Postgraduate qualification in public health, social sciences, gender studies, development, or related field.
Minimum 7–10 years’ experience in GBV programming, training, or gender-focused development work.
Proven experience managing donor-funded programs (DFAT experience highly desirable).
Strong leadership, coordination, and stakeholder management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Physical Demands and Working Conditions
Typical office environment; ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (10-25%).
Occasional work outside regular office hours may be required for urgent project needs.
Technology to be Used
Microsoft Office Suite, project management software, and other standard office equipment.
LOCATION OF EMPLOYMENT:
Country Office - Port Moresby
This job posting summarizes the main duties of the job. It neither prescribes nor restricts the exact tasks that may be assigned to carry out these duties. This document should not be construed in any way to represent a contract of employment. Management reserves the right to review and revise this document at any time.
FHI 360 is an
equal opportunity and affirmative action employer
whereby we do not engage in practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, physical or mental disability, protected Veteran status, or any other characteristic protected under applicable law.
Our values and commitments to safeguarding: FHI 360 is committed to preventing any type of abuse, exploitation and harassment in our work environments and programs, including sexual abuse, exploitation and harassment. FHI 360 takes steps to safeguard the welfare of everyone who engages with our organization and programs and requires that all personnel, including staff members and volunteers, share this commitment and sign our code of conduct. All offers of employment will be subject to appropriate screening checks, including reference, criminal record and terrorism finance checks. FHI 360 also participates in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme (MDS), facilitated by the Steering Committee for Humanitarian Response. In line with the MDS, we will request information from job applicants’ previous employers about any substantiated findings of sexual abuse, exploitation and/or harassment during the applicant’s tenure with previous employers. By applying, job applicants confirm their understanding of these recruitment procedures and consent to these screening checks.
FHI 360 will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with criminal histories, in a manner consistent with the requirements of applicable state and local laws.
FHI 360 will never ask you for your career site username or password, and we will never request money, goods or services during the application, recruitment or employment  process. If you have questions or concerns about correspondence from us, please email

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. Joining our Fixed Plant Maintenance team, the Maintenance Planner ensures that all routine maintenance activities for our process plant are appropriately planned (with input from operations and maintenance) so that the work can progress in a safe, environmentally responsible, efficient, cost effective and repeatable manner.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Continually monitor compliance to, and optimize preventative maintenance programs and schedules, to deliver performance targets for equipment availability and reliability.
Work with mechanical/electrical Supervisors to develop, implement and optimize preventive maintenance (PM) programs for fixed plant assets based on RCM principles.
Develop and update maintenance Safe Operating Procedures (SOPs), inspection sheets and checklists for PMs and other routine maintenance tasks.

ATS, load banks, and paralleling systems

Proficiency with
multimeters, meggers, and diagnostic tools

control panels, wiring diagrams, and synchronization

jobs.title: Engineer, Process Safety
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Workplace Type: Onsite
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
We are seeking a proactive and technically skilled Process Safety Engineer to join our Health & Safety team. This role is responsible for implementing process safety strategies and providing subject matter expertise to enhance safety performance across our operations.
Essential Duties
Implement strategies to manage process safety risks across operations.
Develop and support Process Safety Management Plans and systems (e.g., Management of Change, operational readiness).
Facilitate HAZOP studies and operational risk assessments.
Support integration of Bowtie risk analysis into broader risk frameworks.
Provide expert advice to Operations Managers, Superintendents, and Supervisors on process safety matters.
Conduct assurance activities for Process Safety Standards and related systems.
Monitor and maintain process safety metrics to evaluate performance.
Investigate and report process safety incidents.
Qualifications & Skills
Degree in Engineering or Science is essential. Postgraduate qualifications in Process Safety, Risk Management, or Occupational Health & Safety are highly regarded.
Minimum years of relevant working experience in process safety or related roles within high-risk industries (e.g., mining, oil & gas, chemicals).
Certifications in NEBOSH, IChemE, or equivalent safety certifications are advantageous.
Deep understanding of Process Plant operations and safety systems.]Proficiency in risk assessment methodologies (e.g., HAZOP, Bowtie, LOPA).
Familiarity with process safety software tools and data analysis.
Experience with incident investigation and root cause analysis.
Knowledge of regulatory compliance and industry standards (e.g., ISO, OSHA, COMAH).
Strong problem-solving and decision-making abilities.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work collaboratively across multidisciplinary teams.
High attention to detail and a proactive approach to safety.
Demonstrated commitment to continuous improvement and safety culture.
Ability to influence and engage stakeholders at all levels.
Working Conditions
Must be open to FIFO in PNG
Roster 22:20
Ability to complete a pre-employment medical assessment
Must have proof of a completed Police Clearance within the last six months
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to send in your updated resume and your cover letter before the advertised closing date of 20 August 2025 by qouting the role's reference number: 39133 – we’d love to hear from

The Branch Manager is responsible for overseeing the overall operations, commercial performance, and administrative functions of the branch office. Master’s Level Health qualification.

Social Science
Community Development & Technology
Research Methods
Mathematics

Delivery of the curriculum;

Professional Development

Discuss professional pathways with line management during PD sessions;
Engage with Student Feedback Unit reflections with your line management and facilitate the completion of these with the students;

Support the Principal to implement the Balimo College Professional Learning and Development Policy where it aligns to your specialism.

Knowledge of a range of educational theories, techniques, and methodologies of personnel and management and a strong interest in current educational and technological trends;
High level of communication, mentoring and interpersonal skills, and the ability to work independently or as a member of a team;
A good understanding and competence of technology for email communications, data management, and administration;
Strong problem-solving skills with an ability to analyse and assess classroom contexts and decisively take a course of action;
Ability to research, select and use a wide range ot teaching and assessment strategies to suit the needs of a diverse range of students, including those with disabilities and from other disadvantaged groups;
Open to learning new and innovative approaches to learning through the use of technology.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Mine Technician, you’ll play a key role in safely operating haul trucks and mobile plant to meet daily, weekly, and long‑term production targets. Your work ensures consistent, high‑quality ore supply to the crushers—directly contributing to Lihir’s monthly and annual gold output. You’ll be part of a team that values discipline, teamwork, and a strong commitment to safety, working in accordance with Newmont’s Health, Safety and Environmental policies and the PNG Mine Safety Act.
As part of our team, you will:
Operate haul trucks and mobile mining equipment in the open‑cut mine to achieve production targets.
Deliver consistent ore feed to support crusher performance and gold production goals.
Maintain strict compliance with all safety, environmental, and operational procedures.
Conduct pre‑start inspections and ensure equipment is operated safely and efficiently.
Work collaboratively with supervisors and team members to maintain a productive, safe work environment.
Identify and report hazards, minimise waste, and support continuous improvement initiatives.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Prior experience in heavy industry, ideally within mining.
Ability to operate heavy earthmoving equipment is desirable
Certification on CAT 777/785 haul trucks and ancillary fleet.
Experience with modular mining systems.
Effectively manages own time to complete tasks in line with job expectations and requirements adjusting plans to cater for unforeseen events / disruptions. •
Recognises problems and proactively works towards resolution under the guidance of immediate Supervisor.
Recognises opportunities to minimise waste and addresses it according to the OHSE and operational standards and practices
Work in accordance with PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Safety System, Safety Policies and Procedures and Newmont Environment policies and all departmental operating procedures
Ability to communicate effectively both written and verbally
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 28:14 day/ night Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Reporting to the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation, this role will be required to ensure the installation of underground paste reticulation and infrastructure is carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures. Paste Crew – Leading Hand personnel are also tasked with assisting paste filling operations in the function of conducting routine checks and responding to potential issues that may arise while backfilling. The Paste Crew – Leading Hand is expected to provide instruction, guidance and training to their crew.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate and maintain underground mobile plant including light vehicles, Volvo L120 IT and Normet scissor lift.
Perform prestart and troubleshooting of fleet and tooling to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Install Paste Reticulation and associated infrastructure, including Quattro diverter valves.
Operate airleg rock drills while working at heights.
Pre-start inspections of paste filling reticulation lines and exclusion zones.
Respond in a timely manner to any paste blockage events according to response plans.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair, service and/or support as required to ensure downtime on plant and equipment is minimised.
Other duties as directed by the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation or Senior Specialist – Paste Operations.
Lead a team of two Paste Crew providing instruction, guidance and training.
Support and assist the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation to ensure the rectification of identified clashes in planned paste reticulation areas.
Planning and assigning duties to Paste Crew to achieve planned production in a safe and efficient manner.
Work closely with the Senior Specialist – Paste Operations to ensure that all installation QA/QC processes and routine condition monitoring are implemented to maximise results and reduce risk of unplanned downtime.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure equipment maintenance is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possess the following.
Experience underground or in a similar role
Tickets in LV, IT, scissor lift & handheld rock drill tools
Ability to work in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment
Commitment to safety
Ability to work autonomously with limited supervision
Demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment to achieve a common objective
Knowledge of paste backfilling systems
General knowledge of underground equipment –
Ability to understand and read Engineering drawings and plans
Experience in the installation of Quattro diverter valves
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Strong computer skills, attention to detail, and the ability to remain calm under pressure are essential.

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are in one of the largest business schools in the country and offer degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruit of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts to help educate current and future citizens of Papua New Guinea.
A CAREER WITH US:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learned skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but also enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us, and we believe that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression—this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.

The Assistant Lecturer in Business Management plays a pivotal role in delivering quality education and fostering the academic development of students in business-related disciplines. This position involves assisting with teaching, curriculum development, research, and mentoring, contributing to the overall success of the Business Management Course run at IBS College of TVET.

Engage with local businesses and organizations to create partnerships and learning opportunities.

Knowledge of core business functions such as marketing, finance, management, HR management, and entrepreneurship.

Collaborative and dynamic work environment.
Access to modern teaching resources and tools.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
We are seeking an experienced
Superintendent - Mine Control
to lead our Dispatch team and oversee the performance, integrity, and continuous improvement of our Fleet Management System (FMS). This role is critical in ensuring safe, efficient, and cost‑effective mining operations by combining technical system expertise with strong people leadership.
As the
Superintendent - Mine Control
, you will be accountable for the strategic and operational performance of the Dispatch function, ensuring high-quality data, system availability, and effective decision-making across the mine fleet. You will lead a team of Dispatchers, collaborate with multiple operational stakeholders, manage risks, and ensure alignment with Newmont’s Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) expectations.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Lead and develop a team of Dispatchers, setting clear expectations and creating an inclusive environment where people feel safe to contribute ideas and raise critical issues.
Formulate the biennial Fleet Management Dispatch outlook, contributing to long-term operational planning.
Act as the custodian of the Fleet Management System, ensuring system health, reliability, and optimal fleet utilisation to improve safety, efficiency, and cost performance.
Plan, coordinate, and oversee technical system upgrades to maintain functionality, data quality, and operational integrity.
Collaborate with Operations and Maintenance to verify accuracy of Time Usage Model events and ensure alignment with FMS data.
Execute work in full compliance with Newmont’s Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) standards, policies, and procedures.
Support dispatch operations by guiding daily tasks, providing system oversight, and stepping in as required to ensure continuity.
Identify operational and system-related risks, implement mitigation measures, and continuously monitor risk exposure.
Ensure all work within Mine Control aligns with Newmont’s HSE requirements, supporting a strong and proactive safety culture.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Significant experience in mine control, fleet management, or dispatch operations within a mining environment.
Proficiency with Dispatch 6 Modular
Strong technical knowledge of fleet management systems, system maintenance, and operational data accuracy.
Demonstrated leadership experience, including team development, coaching, performance management, and building inclusive team environments.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills with an ability to build strong relationships across departments.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret data trends and make informed decisions.
Solid understanding of risk management, compliance requirements, and safe operational practices.
Qualifications in Mining, Operations Management, or a related field (preferred).
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a
22:20 roster
to Lihir Island, PNG. We are we are flexible in considering residential housing options or FIFO roster arrangements for the right candidate.
Our accommodation offers a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 24th March 2026 – we’d love to hear from you!

The Institute of Business Studies (IBS) began its journey in 1987 as a modest initiative under Nades & Associates, primarily offering revision classes to support the needs of the Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants, now known as CPA PNG. Over the past 36 years, IBS has grown steadily into a private university-level institution. Today, IBS is recognised as one of the largest business schools in Papua New Guinea, offering degree programmes in Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology. In addition, the institution continues to provide academic pathways for Grade 10 and 12 school leavers, as well as industry-recognised certification opportunities for experienced professionals seeking formal qualifications in their respective fields. jobs.description:
Relief Travel Supervisor
Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our Simberi Operations consists of an open cut mine on the northernmost island in the Tabar group of islands in the province of New Ireland in Papua New Guinea. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Relief Travel Supervisor
to join our team on a Fixed Term position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Buka, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Wewak, Vanimo, or Tabar group of Islands.
(
Locals are encouraged to apply)
.
Reporting to the Travel Superintendent, the Travel Supervisor is primarily responsible for supervising the management of Travel and Hotel Accommodation Bookings which is the control source for making travel arrangements, enforcing the company travel policy, and helping with the administration of domestic and international travel bookings and company charter.
Everyone at St Barbara Limited is required to understand and act in accordance with St Barbara’s Values, Code of Conduct and all Company Policies and meet all relevant internal and external compliance obligations. The role incumbent and manager will identify and review the specific compliance requirements of the role.
The opportunity
Technical accountabilities
Undertake arrangements and booking of all SGCL employees, contractor and visitor flights including local and international charters, local and international airlines as well as any other mode of transport as directed.
Undertake arrangement and booking of all necessary and applicable accommodation locally and internationally as required.
Issuing purchase orders to airflight companies and hotels.
Prepare and distribute, in a timely fashion, all necessary itineraries for flights and accommodation in relation to the above.
Identifies and enforces corporate travel policies and procedures to improve workflow efficiency and reduce cost savings in overall operation.
Determines best booking procedure based on cost savings and communicates itinerary and instructions to senior staff and employees.
Prepare and filing of all flight related manifests, consignment notes and flight documentation.
Preparation and distribution of all flight and charter schedules.
Responsible for transporting staff to and from Mine and Airport.
Loading/unloading, pick up and transport of all personnel, baggage, and freight to and from the Simberi accommodation camp and Simberi airstrip.
All other travel and accommodation related work as directed.
Scheduling accountabilities
Demonstrated supervisory/leadership capacity and continuous improvement mindset.
Management reporting
The ability to meet safety targets and requirements.
Actively participate and promote a safe working environment.
Actively participate in departmental safety meetings and display a safe attitude.
Competent, accurate and time-based record keeping.
Punctual attendance for all rostered shifts.
People accountabilities
Using established training methods and in conjunction with the Training Department train subordinates to achieve competency in the area identified and within the scope of their position.
Participate in training provided by the business.
Are you ready to come and build your future with us?
We need the best people. People who have the drive, energy and are genuinely passionate about the work they do and provide a positive impact. Additionally, we need people who see a challenge as an opportunity for growth and value working with others towards a common goal.​
We would love to hear from you if you have​:
Essential
Behaviour consistent with St Barbara’s Values
Previous experience working in the mining industry.
Previous experience in the travel industry.
Must have current Driver’s Licence.
Working knowledge of travel policies and procedures.
Aircraft handling/loading/refuelling procedures.
Excellent PC skills including word processing, spreadsheet applications and internet functions.
Excellent organization, planning and supervisory skills.
Excellent interpersonal skills including oral and written communication.
Desirable
Physically fit and healthy.
Prepared to work outside normal hours as required.
Ability to work under minimal supervision.
For further information on the
Simberi Operations
and to apply for this role, please visit:
https://www.livehire.com/job/stbarbara-png/F7DFA
