jobs.description:
Build a Legacy: Lead transformative projects shaping the future of Port Moresby.
Grow Your Career in a dynamic urban environment.
Join a passionate team dedicated to a stronger, more vibrant capital.
NC Salary Grade:
NC.10
Location:
NCDC City Hall, Waigani, National Capital District
Reporting to:
Manager – Urban Planning
About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Customary Lands Officer
supports traditional landowning groups within the National Capital District to document, protect, and manage their customary land interests in line with legislation and urban development priorities. The role acts as NCDC’s key liaison on customary land matters, working with landowners, government agencies, and statutory bodies to support tenure recognition, boundary verification, and dispute resolution.
Role Purpose
The purpose of the Customary Lands Officer is to ensure customary land interests are accurately identified and appropriately considered in planning and development processes. Through community engagement, documentation, and advisory support, the role promotes culturally respectful land governance, legal compliance, and inclusive urban development across Port Moresby.
Key Responsibilities
Verify and document customary land boundaries, ownership claims, and land use through field engagement and consultation.
Liaise with traditional landowners, DLPP, statutory bodies, and internal NCDC branches to support tenure recognition, planning decisions, and dispute resolution.
Provide advisory input, reports, and mapping information to inform development proposals, infrastructure planning, and land governance.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum: Diploma in Land Administration, Customary Land Studies, Urban and Regional Planning, or a related field, supported by relevant training in land management, dispute resolution, or community engagement.
Preferred: Bachelor in Land Management, Geography, Urban Planning, or Customary Land Tenure from a recognised institution.
Required: Valid PNG driver’s licence
Preferred: Eligible for membership with a recognised professional body (e.g., PNG Institute of Planners, Institute of Surveyors PNG, or equivalent).
Skills & Knowledge
Knowledge of customary land systems, traditional land ownership structures, and urbanisation impacts on customary land within the National Capital District
.
Familiarity with the
Land Act (1996)
,
Physical Planning Act (1989 & 2001)
,
Survey Act (1969)
,
NCDC Act (2001)
, and willingness to gain deeper understanding of customary land rights and dispute processes.
Understanding of formal lease conversion pathways and issues surrounding informal settlements on customary land.
Awareness of inter-agency roles and procedures involving DLPP, the Surveyor General’s Office, and community dispute mechanisms.
Knowledge of ethical and culturally sensitive practices when working with traditional landowners and clan-based landholding systems.
Customary Land Practice: Ability to document traditional land claims, support verification of landowner identities, and assist in resolving encroachment or land use disputes.
Community Engagement: Skilled in communicating respectfully with landowners, clan leaders, and community groups, and representing NCDC in culturally appropriate ways.
Documentation and Records: Competent in preparing tenure documentation, land history records, and correspondence relating to customary land.
Stakeholder Coordination:Strong liaison skills with DLPP, legal services, civil society partners, and internal NCDC teams.
Technical Proficiency: Proficient in Microsoft Office and capable of using basic GIS tools or mapping software.
Ethical Standards and Reliability: Demonstrated integrity, discretion, and commitment to responsible public sector land management.
Work Experience
Minimum of 3 years’ experience in customary land matters, community-based land management, or land dispute mediation
Experience working with or alongside DLPP, surveyors, or planning authorities in documenting or verifying land tenure.
Prior involvement in community awareness or advisory activities related to land rights, leasing options, or informal settlement impacts.
Experience supporting urban planning or development programs through customary land documentation or stakeholder engagement.
Why Join NCDC?
This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.
Ready to Make an Impact?
If you are passionate about data-driven decision-making and city transformation, we encourage you to apply.
How to Apply
Interested candidates are encouraged to:
Review the available roles and position requirements
Prepare to upload relevant supporting documentation
Cover Letter
Up-to-date CV, include in the one file along with your CV: copies of educational qualifications and a copy of a valid driver's licence (if applicable)

Open to Port Moresby residents only.
Due to volume of candidates, only short-listed candidates will be contacted regarding applicant progress.
Applications are assessed on merit, capability, and alignment with NCDC’s values and service mandate.
Be part of the team shaping the future of Port Moresby — apply today.

jobs.description:
Terms of Reference (ToR)
Consultancy to Develop a Child Safeguarding Policy and Child-Friendly Version for the National Office of Child and Family Services (NOCFS), Papua New Guinea
Project:
Together for Safe Families
Organization:
Save the Children in Papua New Guinea
Location:
Port Moresby
Duration:
40 days over a period of five months
Background
Save the Children is implementing the
Together for Safe Families
project in Papua New Guinea, which aims to reduce violence against children by strengthening families, challenging harmful gender and social norms, empowering children, and improving child protection systems.
The project supports the Government of Papua New Guinea in strengthening the child protection system at provincial and national levels, including improvements to policy and legal frameworks and institutional capacity.
As part of this commitment, Save the Children will provide technical support to the
National Office of Child and Family Services (NOCFS)
to develop a comprehensive
Child Safeguarding Policy
. This policy will ensure that children are protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation, and harm when engaging with NOCFS staff and services. The policy will operationalize safeguarding standards within NOCFS to ensure that all staff, contractors, volunteers, and partners working with children uphold child-safe practices consistent with PNG’s legal framework. The policy will contribute to improving child protection services and strengthening institutional accountability.
In addition, a
child-friendly version
of the policy will be developed to ensure children understand their rights, available reporting mechanisms, and the responsibilities of adults working with them.
Purpose of the Consultancy
The purpose of this consultancy is to:
Develop a comprehensive Child Safeguarding Policy for NOCFS aligned with Lukautim Pikinini Act and other relevant national laws, international standards, and best practices.
Ensure meaningful consultation with key stakeholders, including children, to help guide the development of this policy
Develop a child-friendly version of the (same) safeguarding policy.
Facilitate validation of the final policy and work with the NOCFS to develop a dissemination plan for the final policy (and child-friendly version).
Scope of Work
The consultant will undertake the following tasks:
3.1 Review and Analysis
Review existing national laws, policies, and regulations related to child protection and safeguarding in Papua New Guinea.
Review relevant international frameworks and standards.
Map safeguarding requirements under the Lukautim Pikinini Act to NOCFS operational mandates.
Identify gaps between current NOCFS practices and statutory child protection obligations.
Ensure the safeguarding policy complements statutory child protection responsibilities under the Act.
Clarify reporting obligations consistent with national referral pathways and legal requirements.
Align procedures with PNG’s existing case management and child welfare systems.
3.2 Stakeholder Engagement
Identify and engage key stakeholders including:
Relevant government agencies
NGOs and civil society organizations
Child protection experts, academic institutions
Development partners
Facilitate structured consultations to gather inputs and ensure the policy reflects local realities and institutional capacity.
Facilitate safe and ethical consultations with children to gather age-appropriate inputs into policy development.
3.3 Policy Development
Develop a comprehensive Child Safeguarding Policy including, but not limited to:
Policy statement and guiding principles
Definitions and scope
Code of conduct
Prevention measures (safe recruitment, background checks, staff training, supervision)
Reporting mechanisms and complaint procedures
Response protocols and case management guidance
Confidentiality and data protection
Risk assessment and mitigation measures
Roles and responsibilities
Monitoring and accountability mechanisms
Alignment with Papua New Guinea’s legal and regulatory frameworks
3.4 Validation and Finalization
Facilitate validation workshop(s) with stakeholders.
Incorporate feedback and finalize the policy.
Ensure the policy is practical, implementable, and context appropriate.
3.5 Child-Friendly Version
Develop an accessible, age-appropriate child-friendly version of the safeguarding policy.
Use simple language and culturally appropriate examples.
Ensure clarity on:
Children’s rights
Expected behaviour of adults
How and where children can report concerns
Deliverables
The consultant will deliver:
Inception report (methodology, timeline, stakeholder mapping)
Summary of stakeholder consultation findings
Draft Child Safeguarding Policy
Validation workshop report
Final Child Safeguarding Policy
Child-Friendly Version of the Policy
Required Qualifications and Experience
The consultant should have:
Advanced degree in Child Protection, Social Work, Law, Public Policy, International Development, or related field.
Minimum 7–10 years of experience in child protection or safeguarding or code of conduct policy development.
Demonstrated experience developing safeguarding and/or protection policies for government or large institutions is preferred.
Strong knowledge of Papua New Guinea’s child protection legal and policy environment.
Experience conducting participatory consultations, including with children.
Strong facilitation and drafting skills.
Experience developing child-friendly materials.
Excellent written and spoken English.
Ethical Considerations
The consultant must:
Adhere to Save the Children’s Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
Ensure safe and ethical engagement of children.
Maintain confidentiality of all sensitive information.
Ensure informed consent and child-appropriate safeguarding protocols during consultations.
Reporting and Supervision
The consultant will report to the Protection Manager, Save the Children in Papua New Guinea. Technical oversight will be provided jointly by Save the Children and NOCFS.
Application Process
Interested consultants should submit:
Technical proposal (methodology and workplan)
Financial proposal
CV(s)
Samples of previous policy work
Contact details of three professional referees

K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Technician – Geothermal Operations, you will play a vital role in supporting Lihir’s geothermal monitoring and safety systems. Your work ensures accurate data collection, reliable operation of geothermal systems or similar geotechnical operational systems, and strong hazard awareness across the open pit. By applying your technical skills, attention to detail, and commitment to safety, you’ll help maintain safe mining conditions, support geothermal project delivery, and contribute to the ongoing development of geothermal monitoring across operational teams.
As part of our team, you will
Ensure full compliance with all HSE requirements, policies, and Fitness for Work standards.
Complete HSE tasks only when hazards, risks, and controls are clearly understood and agreed with your Supervisor.
Work constructively within a diverse team and take accountability for your own development and performance.
Lead the installation and data collection of geothermal monitoring systems in the open pit.
Contribute to the execution of mine geothermal projects and support geothermal hazard training for operational and technical teams.
Conduct preventative maintenance inspections on geothermal equipment, including steam relief wells.
Identify cost‑saving opportunities and report any cost wastage within your area of responsibility.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Essential
Grade 12 education.
PNG Class 6 Driver’s Licence.
More than 1 year of experience in a mining or technical role.
Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and problem‑solving skills.
Ability to work safely and effectively in a multicultural team.
Competency in Microsoft Word and Excel.
Strong communication, interpersonal, and active listening skills.
High attention to detail, good time management, and the ability to work independently when required.
Desirable
Diploma in IT Networking, Electronics, Instrumentation, or a similar technical field.
Experience with data and software networking, system communications, and technical reporting.
Familiarity with geothermal or geotechnical monitoring systems.
Your work environment
This position is based at the Lihir Gold Operation on a
22:20 FIFO roster – days only
. You’ll be part of a small, supportive team within Mine Technical Services, working closely with the Supervisor – Geothermal Systems.
The role offers hands‑on fieldwork, exposure to geothermal monitoring technologies, and clear development pathways, including opportunities to progress into supervisory or geotechnical operations roles. You’ll thrive in an environment that values safety, teamwork, continuous learning, and technical excellence.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an ensuited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, natural resource management, environmental stewardship, and applied development disciplines.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching and research programs
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training and community development initiatives
The University emphasises practice-oriented teaching, field-based learning, and strong industry collaboration, producing graduates who are work-ready and capable of contributing meaningfully to sustainable development and climate-resilient outcomes across Papua New Guinea.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified and motivated candidates for appointment as
Tutor (Technical Instructor – Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering)
within the Department of Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering, School of Environment and Climate Change (SECC).
This position supports the delivery of tutorials, laboratory sessions, and applied practical learning in Renewable Energy and Environmental Engineering programs. The role contributes to undergraduate teaching, laboratory-based instruction, applied research support, and industry- and community-linked activities aligned with PNGUNRE’s mandate in renewable energy development, environmental sustainability, and climate change response.
The successful appointee will work under the direction of a Lecturer and report to the Head of Department, Renewable Energy & Environmental Engineering.
Key Responsibilities

Assist with reviewing, drafting, and interpreting contracts and variations.

A bachelor’s degree in law.

The Blast Engineer / Magazine Keeper is responsible for the safe planning and governance of underground blasting and explosives storage activities at Kainantu Gold Mine.
The role ensures that the mine’s Explosives and Electronic Blasting System assets are maintained, audited and reconciled; and that all work complies with company procedures and statutory requirements.
The position works cross functionally with Underground Operations, Electrical and IT to ensure reliable blast initiation and continuous operational readiness.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Maintain and audit explosives stock levels in the magazine, ensuring safe storage, access control, and compliance with explosives handling regulations.
Working with the mine’s shotfirers and blast crews on a shift-by-shift basis to ensure blast plans for the shift and the explosive used are aligned and reconciled to comply to site policies regarding explosive orders.
Record and reconcile explosive stocks and inventory using Magman Explosives Management System.
Conduct weekly and monthly magazine stocktakes and reconciliations, maintaining accurate records for regulatory compliance.
Conduct required weekly and monthly Magazine 274 inspections to ensure structural integrity, dryness, ventilation, and safety standards are met (including housekeeping).
Place orders when critical explosives stock levels are reached to ensure uninterrupted blasting operations.
Liaise with Orica, the mine’s main explosive supplier as required to facilitate replenishment.
Maintain and audit blasting system components including detonators, blast boxes, cables, and network hardware.
Perform weekly and monthly CEBS stocktakes and reconciliations, ensuring accuracy and readiness. Update CEBS registry to reflect accordingly.
Place orders for CEBS components when critical stock thresholds are attained.
Troubleshoot CEBS network faults and system failures to minimise misfires and improve system reliability.
Coordinate with IT and Electrical teams on CEBS installation, connectivity, power supply integration, and commissioning requirements.

Valid PNG driver licence Class 6
2+ years’ underground drill & blast and/or 5+ years blast crew / explosives magazine experience.
Strong inventory control, reconciliation, and record keeping discipline for explosives and initiation systems

Effective collaboration with Operations, Electrical and IT; clear written and verbal communication.
High attention to detail, risk awareness, and commitment to safety and housekeeping standards.
Behaviour consistent with K92 Mining’s Values.

Authorisation/permit for explosives handling and magazine keeping

Prosecution Quality: Boost legal integrity and development.

The opportunity
A high-impact policing partnership is looking for a Police Prosecutions Capability Advisor based in Port Moresby to serve as a key pillar of the RPNGC Prosecutions Directorate. You will ensure that prosecution structures, workflows, and legal practices are managed with the highest level of professional excellence. The role provides the essential technical support and mentoring required to reduce case attrition and protect the interests of the justice sector while ensuring efficient organizational flow.
This is an ideal opportunity for a self-motivated, highly ethical professional in criminal law or justice sector advisory. You will interact with key actors in this key arm of Government, supporting police prosecutors, brief managers, and supervisors, ensuring seamless compliance with national laws and providing sound legal advice to the directorate. The role requires excellent analytical skills and deep technical knowledge to navigate a complex legal environment within an organization undergoing significant capacity development.
The role
The Police Prosecutions Capability Advisor plays a central role in safeguarding the Directorate’s legal and regulatory standing through meticulous capacity building. Responsibilities include assessing existing prosecution structures, supporting provincial functions, and providing expert advice on criminal procedure and rules of evidence. The role serves as a key point of contact for the Office of the Public Prosecutor and the judiciary, providing the mentorship needed to ensure successful case outcomes. The overarching goal is to maintain a legally sound prosecutorial environment through proactive coaching and standardized practices.
Main duties include:
Assess and strengthen police prosecution structures, staffing, and workflows within the Directorate.
Provide expert legal advice on criminal law, procedure, and evidentiary standards to support charge selection and trial preparation.
Provide ongoing mentoring and case-based coaching to prosecutors and brief managers to improve file quality.
Assist in developing and updating prosecution policies, SOPs, manuals, and standardized templates.
Strengthen working relationships between police prosecutors, the Office of the Public Prosecutor, and the judiciary.
Facilitate Prosecution Review Committees to identify and solve systemic issues contributing to case backlogs and failed prosecutions
Qualification and Experience:
Formal Education: Bachelor of Laws (LLB) or an equivalent recognized law degree.
Professional Admission: Admission as a legal practitioner in PNG or another common law jurisdiction.
Core Experience: Significant post-admission experience as a criminal prosecutor, defense lawyer, or legal practitioner with substantial criminal law practice.
Technical Expertise: Demonstrated experience in criminal procedure, evidence, written submissions, and courtroom advocacy.
Mentorship Background: Extensive experience advising or mentoring prosecutors or police legal officers is highly desirable.
Regional Context: Proven ability to build capability of local counterparts within developing countries or Pacific justice sector contexts is preferred.

Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Reporting to the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation, this role will be required to ensure the installation of underground paste reticulation and infrastructure is carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures. Paste Crew personnel are also tasked with assisting paste filling operations in the function of conducting routine checks and responding to potential issues that may arise while backfilling.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate and maintain underground mobile plant including light vehicles, Volvo L120 IT and Normet scissor lift.
Perform prestart and troubleshooting of fleet and tooling to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Install Paste Reticulation and associated infrastructure, including Quattro diverter valves.
Operate airleg rock drills while working at heights.
Pre-start inspections of paste filling reticulation lines and exclusion zones.
Respond in a timely manner to any paste blockage events according to response plans.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair, service and/or support as required to ensure downtime on plant and equipment is minimised.
Support and assist the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation to ensure the rectification of identified clashes in planned paste reticulation areas.
Work closely with the Senior Specialist – Paste Operations to ensure that all installation QA/QC processes and routine condition monitoring are implemented to maximise results and reduce risk of unplanned downtime.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure equipment maintenance is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possess the following.
Experience underground or in a similar role
Tickets in LV, IT, scissor lift & handheld rock drill tools
Ability to work in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment
Ability to work autonomously with limited supervision
Demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment to achieve a common objective
Knowledge of paste backfilling systems
General knowledge of underground equipment
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Location: Port Moresby
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s most recognised automotive groups, representing Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Our vehicles are everywhere — now we need someone who can help tell those stories properly, in a way that feels real, local, and worth watching.

You’ll help manage and create the content that keeps PNG Motors active online. That means creating posts, reels, videos, captions, and stories that people actually stop for — not content that gets scrolled past. You’ll be out in dealerships, at launches, on the road, and sometimes in the sun getting the shot because that’s where the good content happens.

You’ll work closely with the marketing and sales teams to support promotions and launches, and sometimes you’ll need to move quickly when something is happening now, not next week.

International Food Corporation ltd, the leading manufacture of Besta Mackerel and Tuna products in PNG and South Pacific seeking to recruit highly motivated and qualified experience individual to fill the position of
Generator Specialist.
OVERALL RESPONSIBILITY:
The responsibilities of Generator specailist are to ensure the safe installation and operation of electricity generators on location to manage, balance load, distribution of power to equipment as required, ensuring that electrical circuits do not become overloaded and continue power supplies to all area without interruptions.
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES:
Conduct pre-start up checks ensuring all parameters and requirements are met for safe and efficient operation of the generator,
Start or stop generators, auxiliary equipment, and other power plant equipment and connect or disconnect equipment from circuits,
Adjust generator output controls to match the phase, frequency and voltage of electricity supplied to specified plants and control panels,
Monitor, inspect and report for generator and associated auxiliary components and indicators to detect evidence of operating problems,
Take readings from meters, gauges and charts to establish intervals and take necessary steps as necessary,
Collect oil, water or electrolyte samples for analysis as required,
Examine and perform the report for test power distribution,
Inspect records and log book entries and communicate with superiors to assess operating status,
Attend to calls, call in necessary personnel during outage and emergencies,
Record and compile operational data, logs and reports,
Perform routine health check, maintenance on equipment and determine types of major maintenances needed,
Inform/Report immediately any abnormality to the superior,
Perform the genset activity plan schedule to superior,
Conduct the preventive/predictive for the parts/lubricant replacement, services and overhauling,
Inspect and perform the parts, equipment and tools inventory.
Evaluate, identify and do the parts ordering to replenish the inventory.
Inspect safety devices on daily basis by running tests and reporting any unusual situations/abnormality,
Conduct regular improvement plan,
Maintain the regular communication with the superior,
Execute daily and weekly cleaning/5S procedures, e.g. clean, dry, organize, bright/shine paint, sort, shining clean floor walls ceiling, functioning electrical appliances, shut close align panel, zero dust and tidy surroundings.
SKILLS
3-5 years of related experience.
Certified Internal Combustion Engines.
Inspect generator engine and mechanical/electrical components to diagnose issues accurately.
Knowledge of 12-24 VDC electrical systems and procedures, methods and techniques to design, install, repair and maintain generators, by-pass pumps, starters, pumps, valves, motors and gauges.
Knowledge of diesel, gasoline, propane driven internal combustion engines.
Knowledge of laws and regulations governing the operation of equipment and materials.
Knowledge of occupational hazards, safety precautions, and safety regulations related to equipment operation, hazardous materials and other work-related precautions.
Provide accurate estimates (cost, time, effort) for a repair or maintenance job
Keep logs on work and issues.
Ability to work independently and make routine decisions on the operation of the plant processes and equipment.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and resolve issues quickly and effectively.
Knowledge of AC/DC power systems.
REQUIREMENTS
Minimum grade 12 level / High school diploma.
Electrical qualification.
Have a working knowledge of basic machinery preventive maintenance and repair.
Electrical exposure/understanding.
Ability to work independently and make routine decisions on the operation of the plant processes and equipment.
Strong problem-solving skills, with the ability to identify and resolve issues quickly and effectively.
Comfortable working in a fast-paced environment with changing priorities.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Reporting to the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation, this role will be required to ensure the installation of underground paste reticulation and infrastructure is carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures. Paste Crew personnel are also tasked with assisting paste filling operations in the function of conducting routine checks and responding to potential issues that may arise while backfilling.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate and maintain underground mobile plant including light vehicles, Volvo L120 IT and Normet scissor lift.
Perform prestart and troubleshooting of fleet and tooling to identify and remedy issues that may arise.
Install Paste Reticulation and associated infrastructure, including Quattro diverter valves.
Operate airleg rock drills while working at heights.
Pre-start inspections of paste filling reticulation lines and exclusion zones.
Respond in a timely manner to any paste blockage events according to response plans.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair, service and/or support as required to ensure downtime on plant and equipment is minimised.
Support and assist the Coordinator – Paste Reticulation to ensure the rectification of identified clashes in planned paste reticulation areas.
Work closely with the Senior Specialist – Paste Operations to ensure that all installation QA/QC processes and routine condition monitoring are implemented to maximise results and reduce risk of unplanned downtime.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
Ensure equipment maintenance is conducted by competent technicians in a safe manner and in accordance with established procedures.
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possess the following.
Experience underground or in a similar role
Tickets in LV, IT, scissor lift & handheld rock drill tools
Ability to work in a fast-paced, physically demanding environment
Ability to work autonomously with limited supervision
Demonstrate abilities to work within a team environment to achieve a common objective
Knowledge of paste backfilling systems
General knowledge of underground equipment
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Program Overview:
The
Australia–Papua New Guinea Economic Partnership (APEP)
is a flagship partnership supporting Papua New Guinea’s economic development priorities. Delivered by the Government of Australia in close collaboration with the Government of Papua New Guinea, APEP focuses on strengthening economic systems, institutions, and opportunities that support sustainable and inclusive growth through to 2028.
Working alongside government, research institutions, and development partners, APEP delivers coordinated and high‑impact outcomes across four key engagement areas:
Safeguarding Macroeconomic Stability
Supporting More Efficient and Inclusive Markets
Fostering Inclusive Growth and Expanded Livelihoods
Catalysing Economic Research and Dialogue
Gender equality, disability social inclusion (GEDSI), women’s economic empowerment, and climate are central to APEP and integrated across all engagement areas and activities.
Position Overview:
The position is responsible for developing a range of communications products and supporting the delivery of public diplomacy (PD) events.  The role will require a high level of expertise and skills in writing for external audiences and stakeholders, as well as photography skills.  The role will report to the Communications Adviser and work closely with all members of the communications team to deliver effective communications support across all the APEP workstreams.
Specific Responsibilities:
Prepare high-quality content for a variety of communication formats, including media releases, reports, talking points, and social media content including short videos.
Ensure that all written content is consistent with DFAT’s style guide and branding protocols.
Plan and develop communications products which promote the impact of APEP’s support.
Attend events and forums as required to capture content for communications products.
Engage closely with all APEP workstreams to proactively monitor upcoming events and PD opportunities.
Develop creative communication materials for a range of projects, such as events, campaigns and launches.
Work closely with the communications team to create innovative and impactful communications products.
Engage with the DFAT Communications and PD team as required – this may include attending contractor meetings and forums.
Manage the partnership brand in line with DFAT guidelines.
Develop and deliver communications training to APEP team members as required.
Contribute to reporting, administration, data collection and other tasks as directed by the Communications Adviser
Implement relevant components of the APEP GEDSI strategy into all communications products.
Any other reasonable duties as required.

a response to the Selection Criteria below should be provided
.
A degree in Communications, Public Relations, Marketing, or a related area is preferred.
A minimum of 3-5 years of professional experience in communications and marketing, ideally within a development context.
Demonstrated strong verbal and written communication skills through extensive experience in writing and editing for a variety of media platforms and diverse audiences.
Demonstrated capability to offer technical communications guidance and assistance to APEP teams.
Proficient in Microsoft Office, Adobe Creative Suite, and Mailchimp.
Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively and effectively as a member of a team
Consistently demonstrated dedication to GEDSI, climate considerations, and safeguarding as integral cross-cutting priorities for APEP.

CASUAL WORKER
DRIVER -
(Lae Based Only)
CONTEXT
Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Taric, Bougainville, Gulf Province and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in Lae, Jiwaka and Highlands.
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE POSITION:
Performing the tasks of transporting authorized goods and passengers in an
MSF
vehicle, ensuring its technical and safety conditions and respecting the country's traffic rules and
MSF
security rules, in order to provide a safe, smooth and efficient service
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Checking daily, the technical conditions of the assigned vehicle (state of the tires, oil, fuel, brakes, radio equipment, spare parts, vehicle body etc.), performing weekly check according to the MSF Logbook, refilling it when necessary, and keeping it clean to ensure it can be driven in perfect conditions.
Carrying out a proper handover of the vehicle from one driver to another during shift/ driver change.
Ensuring the security of passengers in the vehicle, driving carefully, observing speed limits and traffic rules in the country as well as MSF security rules, in order to avoid car accidents.
Ensuring all passengers have all necessary paperwork in order before travelling and ensuring non-MSF staff sign discharge of liability before using the vehicle.
Ensuring that all vehicle documents and the driver's driving license are valid, up to date and stored the vehicle.
Informing the line manager of any incident involving the transportation of passengers and/or goods.
Knowing how to use all types of radios, codes, call numbers and radio alphabets by heart and communicating with base according to MSF communications policy to inform the driver's position and any potential implications.
Knowing and respecting the security rules related to vehicle movements, specifically those related to customs, checkpoints and roadblocks. Ensuring all passengers know and respect the security rules.
Good knowledge of roads in Morobe and its environs.
Ensure comprehensive handover is conducted between drivers during shift/ driver change.
Renewal of your driver’s licence before its expiration.
Monitoring the fuel gauge levels to ensure refuelling is done in a timely manner; and monitoring vehicle maintenance to know when it is close to the service km/period and inform the Logisitcs Supervisor/ Manager.
Proper recording of fuel dispensed into vehicle in the vehicle’s fuel log book.
Respect of defined MSF speed limits.

jobs.description:
Senior Marine Finance Officer
The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government, and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being. WCS PNG is recruiting a
Senior Marine Finance Officer
based in Kavieng, New Ireland Province and may be expected to travel within PNG, especially to WCS marine field sites. The position will report to the Kavieng Program Manager with a dotted line to the Finance Manager.
Role Dimension
The Senior Marine Finance Officer is responsible for managing the financial systems and administrative functions of the Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) Kavieng office. The role ensures full compliance with WCS policies, donor requirements, and applicable local regulations, while supporting efficient, transparent, and accountable financial operations. The position also provides financial oversight and administrative support to the Kimbe and Manus offices, working closely with program and finance teams to ensure strong financial management and consistency across all locations.
KEY SELECTION CRITERIA
Financial Management & Oversight
Lead financial management and administrative functions for the Kavieng office and field operations.
Provide financial oversight and technical support to Kimbe and Manus offices.
Ensure compliance with WCS policies, donor requirements, legal agreements, and local laws.
Maintain high standards of financial accountability, transparency, and operational efficiency.
Banking and Cash Management
Monitor and control WCS-PNG Marine office cash positions, including daily bank monitoring and reconciliations.
Ensure adequate cash balances are maintained to support operational needs; notify the Finance Director of funding requirements.
Manage cash flow across WCS-PNG Marine bank accounts and facilitate inter-account transfers as needed.
Liaise with program teams to forecast cash needs and support timely monthly cash requests.
Process and reconcile banking transactions, petty cash, staff advances, and acquittals.
Verify supporting documentation for all bank and cash transactions.
Review weekly accounting records prior to submission to the Finance Director.
Perform monthly balance sheet reconciliations (payables, receivables, advances, bank, petty cash, and prepayments).
Monitor bank balances to ensure uninterrupted Marine field operations.
Petty Cash Management
Process petty cash advances and expenses daily in compliance with WCS and donor requirements.
Prepare journal vouchers and post petty cash transactions in SAP with correct coding.
Conduct daily petty cash reconciliations and month-end cash counts.
Maintain an imprest petty cash system with monthly reviews and approvals by the Program Manager.
Employee Advances and Expense Management
Process employee advances and expense claims in line with WCS and donor policies.
Review and reconcile employee acquittals, including necessary bank lodgments.
Prepare journal entries for advances and acquittals for month-end reporting.
Maintain monthly employee advance balance reports.
Ensure complete and organized documentation filing.
Provide guidance and training to program staff on financial procedures and timelines when required.
Processing of Local Expenses
Review and process non-employee program expenses in compliance with donor and procurement requirements, ensuring:
Proper procurement procedures are followed
Appropriate approvals and signatures are obtained
Accuracy of amounts and purchase requisitions
Correct financial coding
Process payments through online banking or petty cash as appropriate.
Prepare journal entries for expense postings in SAP.
Track expenditures against approved budgets and Allocate expenses accurately to donor-funded projects.
Reporting & Coordination
Prepare and submit financial reports to the Senior Finance Coordinator in Goroka.
Respond promptly to finance-related queries.
Support program managers with financial planning and budget monitoring.
Coordinate financial processes for major and complementary projects.
Administrative & Asset Management
Process office bills and authorized expenditures in a timely manner.
Maintain and update asset registers and support proper care and tracking of equipment.
Reconcile travel advances and reimbursements promptly.
Maintain organized filing systems for financial and personnel records.
Update staff leave databases and manage induction and exit documentation.
Perform other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Minimum Requirements:
Education/Credentials
A degree in accounting / Business Administration or qualification from a recognized professional accounting body (CA/ACCA/CPA)
Experience
Requires a minimum of 3 years accounting and administrative management experience
Exposure to non-profit sector (NGO, International organisations) is an added advantage
Critical Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
Good analytical and problem solving skills
Preferably familiar with requirements of different donors.
Good knowledge of accounting system.
Competent in the use of Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint etc.
Require knowledge of financial systems, internal controls and procedures
Able to work and interact with diverse group of people
Experience in the most current technologies and products used in the industry.
Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
Being a self-starter with drives and initiative and able to work as a team/individual with a positive attitude and open minded
Ability to work with less supervision and under pressure
Excellent multi-tasking, organized and follow-up skills,
Demonstrated work experience providing customer service.
Application process
Please send a CV and letter of interest to
[email protected]
with the subject line: Application for Kavieng Senior Marine Finance Officer. Applications accepted until
Friday 13 March 2026
. Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for interviews.

Qualifications in law, finance or contract management

Simberi Operations

Job Purpose
To operate the side-lift equipment mounted on a 20-foot truck to safely load, unload, lift, and position containers. The role ensures precise handling, equipment care, and strict adherence to safety standards.
Key Responsibilities
Equipment Operation
Operate the hydraulic side-lift system to lift, lower, and transfer 20-foot containers.
Ensure stabilizers, chains, and lifting arms are correctly positioned before lifting.
Conduct site checks to confirm safe lifting conditions (ground stability, clearance, angles).
Perform container placement according to customer or site requirements.
Qualified to serve as a backup driver when needed.
Guide prime mover drivers when reversing, parking, or positioning trailers and containers.
Safety, Maintenance & Compliance
Maintain full compliance with lifting procedures and safety protocols.
Monitor safe working loads, lifting angles, and equipment limits.
Ensure all exclusion zones are set and respected during lifting operations.
Report unsafe conditions, near misses, or equipment malfunctions immediately.
Conduct daily pre-operation inspections (hydraulics, hoses, chains, controls, remotes).
Report faults or wear promptly to prevent breakdowns.
Keep lifting equipment clean and properly secured during travel.
Container & Job Documentation
Record container numbers, lift locations, and any issues encountered.
Ensure accurate completion of lift logs or operator sheets.
Coordination
Work closely with the truck driver during positioning and stabilizer setup.
Communicate clearly with site personnel to coordinate safe lifting.
Provide guidance on vehicle positioning for optimal lifting angles as well as when prime mover is manoeuvring with in container yards, terminals and client’s premisses.
Qualifications & Experience
Certification or company training for side-lift or hydraulic lifting equipment (as required).
Experience handling containers or similar lifting operations.
Strong knowledge of lifting safety standards and equipment operation.
With valid driver’s license.
Skills & Competencies
Precision and situational awareness.
Strong focus on safety and risk management.

Credit Corporation Properties Limited seeks an experienced person to fill in the role of Maintenance On-Call Officer.

The role ensures tenant safety, protects company assets, and maintenance continuity of essential services in apartments and staff. This role is based in Port Moresby.
Primary Responsibilities:
A. Emergency Response (Residential Focused)
Respond immediately to tenant emergency calls (e.g., power outages, broken locks, water leaks, flooding, faulty air‑conditioning).
Prioritize tenant safety during incidents involving fire alarms, gas leaks, smoke, or security-related issues.
Secure units during emergencies (e.g., damaged doors or windows).
B. General Residential Maintenance
Perform minor and temporary repairs such as:
-Fixing leaks or burst pipes
-Restoring tripped breakers or power faults
-Replacing blown light bulbs or damaged fittings
-Temporary AC fault stabilization
-Clearing blocked drains or toilets
Provide temporary solutions until daytime technical teams conduct full repairs.
C. Residential Property Inspections:
Conduct checks on:
-Common areas (corridors, lighting, stairwells, parking areas)
-Water pumps, pressure systems, and tanks
-Perimeter lighting and security gates
-Smoke detectors and fire safety equipment
Identify hazards that could impact residents

Communicate effectively and professionally with residents, ensuring issues are understood and prioritized.
Explain temporary fixes or the next steps if a specialist is required.
Escalate issues to the Facilities Manager or contractors when urgent intervention is needed.
E. Coordination
Work together with:
-Security teams (access, safety, lockouts)
-Contractors (plumbing/electrical emergencies)
-Property officers/managers
Assist in escorting contractors for after-hours work, ensuring safety protocols.
F. Documentation & Reporting
Maintain an after-hours incident log including:
-Time of call
-Nature of issue
-Action taken
-Pending tasks
Provide daily reports for supervisor follow-up.
G. Safety & Compliance
Follow residential safety and access protocols, including secure handling of master keys.
Uphold tenant privacy and confidentiality.
Comply with building codes and HSE standards for residential spaces.
Qualifications & Experience:
Required
Trade qualification in maintenance, plumbing, electrical, or building services.
Minimum 2 years’ experience in residential or facilities maintenance.
Ability to diagnose and resolve common residential issues.
Strong communication skills and good attitude.
Driver's license (Class 3 or 6)
Preferred,
Experience in apartments, townhouses, or staff accommodation facilities.
Knowledge of residential electrical systems, water services, and HVAC basics.
Familiarity with PNG residential maintenance challenges (e.g., water pressure issues, tropical climate impacts).

Strong customer service mindset (tenant-centred)
Fast and effective problem-solving
Reliability and responsiveness
Ability to work independently at night
Awareness of safety and security risks in residential settings
Good record‑keeping and accountability

Part of an on‑call roster (after-hours, weekends, and holidays).
May be required to quickly travel to different residential sites.
Work may include climbing, lifting, confined spaces, and outdoor tasks.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You will drive local procurement initiatives that make a real impact on operational excellence and sustainable outcomes. You will lead key procurement projects, craft market documentation, evaluate bids, and build strong relationships with suppliers to deliver efficient, compliant, and high-value results. Your work will shape supplier development, strengthen community engagement, and enhance operational performance across the site.
As part of our team, you will
Lead and support PNG and Lihirian procurement activities, including running RFPs, negotiating with suppliers, and managing commercial disputes.
Support site stakeholders and the Category Management teams to identify and develop local procurement opportunities.
Ensure compliance with legal, regulatory, and company policies, including health, safety, environmental, ESG, and community engagement standards.
Build supplier capability through coaching, advisory documents, and ongoing support.
Contribute to the Local Procurement Plan and reporting, providing insights to improve processes and outcomes.
Present procurement outcomes to managers and other stakeholders, fostering collaboration and transparency.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business Administration, Procurement, or related field is desirable.
Proven experience in procurement and supplier capacity building, ideally in a mining environment.
Skilled in supplier negotiations, both to achieve great contract value and resolving contract related disputes
Competence in SAP, Fieldglass and Ariba is desirable.
Excellent communication, negotiation, public speaking, and stakeholder management skills.
Strong cultural awareness, particularly in engaging with Lihirian communities and local businesses.
Strong stakeholder engagement skills, with a focus on building long-term relationships and delivering value.
Ability to work independently as a motivated self-starter while collaborating effectively with cross-functional teams.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will engage with internal stakeholders including team leads, superintendents, and category management teams, as well as external stakeholders such as local suppliers and government officials. You will operate in a dynamic, collaborative environment, leading procurement activities that are critical to site performance and community impact.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will have the opportunity to make a tangible impact on site operations while developing your career in a global mining environment. You will work with a team that values collaboration, innovation, and cultural awareness, and you will contribute to sustainable, ethical procurement practices that support local communities and operational excellence.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

(SALP)
at the field level. Lead Field Delivery of SALP:
Coordinate and deliver agriculture and livelihoods activities across coffee, cocoa, fresh produce, apiculture, and agroforestry programs, aligned to SALP phases and annual work plans.
Supervise & Support Extension Teams:
Supervise Agricultural Extension Officers, manage daily schedules, provide coaching, and ensure inclusive participation of women and youth in program activities.
Farmer Training & Demonstration Programs:
Plan and deliver farmer training, demonstration plots, and community workshops, supporting adoption of climate-smart and improved agricultural practices.
Monitoring, Evaluation & Reporting:
Track yields, household income, participation, and environmental outcomes; maintain accurate SPMS records; and provide regular field reports to the Superintendent SALP.
Technical Agriculture Support:
Coordinate input distribution, monitor utilization and productivity, support certification pathways, and assist with processing infrastructure such as coffee wet mills, cocoa fermentry and driers,  nurseries,  bee keeping and honey processing, fresh produce post- harvest consolidation, and livestock breeding and distribution center.
Collaboration & Market Integration:
Work with Social Development, Business Development, government agencies, NGOs, and private sector partners to strengthen cooperatives, market access, and SME participation.
Commitments & Expectations Management:
Deliver agriculture-related MOA and CSDP commitments, manage community expectations, maintain grievance mechanisms, and escalate emerging risks or issues as required.
Health, Safety & Environment:
Ensure agricultural activities are implemented in accordance with company HSE requirements and promote safe, environmentally responsible field practices.
About You
To be considered for this role, candidates must have strong practical experience delivering agricultural extension programs in rural or community-based environments. In addition, you should be able to demonstrate:
Diploma or degree in Agriculture, Agronomy, Agribusiness, or a related discipline, with at least 5 years of experience in agricultural extension or rural development, ideally within Papua New Guinea.
Strong technical knowledge of coffee, cocoa, fresh produce, agroforestry, apiculture, and small livestock systems suited to PNG conditions, including climate-smart agriculture and pest and disease management.
Practical experience working with farming households and community cooperatives, with exposure to cooperative development, market integration, and value-chain initiatives.
Experience supporting organic or quality certification systems for coffee or cocoa is highly desirable.
Ability to collect, analyse, and report program data for monitoring, evaluation, and SPMS reporting, including quarterly indicator tracking.
Strong communication skills in English and Tok Pisin; local dialects are advantageous.
Must have PNG driving License - Class 6
Culturally sensitive, community-focused, and able to manage expectations in complex social environments.
Committed to ethical, transparent, and accountable program delivery aligned with K92’s values.

Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a strong commitment to equal opportunity, ensuring individuals can reach their full potential in a respectful and inclusive workplace.
We offer a supportive work environment, competitive remuneration, access to wellbeing and employee assistance programs, and the opportunity to contribute meaningfully to sustainable community development in Papua New Guinea.

jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Port Moresby, the JV Accountant – Oil will prepare Joint Venture billings for operated license areas, including Development Operations and Exploration, manage and coordinate the monthly cash calling process, and perform related analyses to ensure all information complies with Joint Venture Operating Agreements.
Key Responsibilities:
Prepare Joint Venture Billing (JVB) statements for all operated assets
Facilitate and manage the cash call process, including analysis and reconciliation of cash statements
Perform month-end support tasks, including manual cost allocations (Gobe Common WC, KPS Capex, Gobe Main LNG Sharing), PCO calculations, and other ad hoc cost adjustment journals
Track JVB queries and coordinate responses with the Finance Team
Perform General Ledger account reconciliations
Ensure compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and Corporate Governance and Safety requirements
What you’ll bring:
Essential
Bring proven experience in joint venture accounting
Leverage broad experience in accounting within a large organisation
Demonstrated proficiency in MS Excel and MS Word
Manage emails effectively using Microsoft Outlook
Build and maintain strong relationships with Joint Venture partners
Prioritise tasks and manage time efficiently to meet deadlines
Possess a bachelor’s degree in business (Accountancy, Finance, Management, or related discipline
Possess CPA PNG qualification or be actively working towards completion
Experience in SAP Financial Accounting Systems would be ideal
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB 11 March 2026.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply

There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. The Opportunity
The Reservations Manager is responsible for leading the reservations function across Holiday Inn Express Port Moresby and Holiday Inn & Suites Port Moresby. This role is a key position within the Commercial Team and plays a critical part in driving rooms revenue through effective reservations management, conversion and reconversion, rate integrity, distribution performance, and strong collaboration with Sales and Revenue. The role supports both Transient and Group business, ensuring enquiry handling, quoting, follow-up, and booking conversion is completed to a high standard, in line with IHG brand standards and property commercial priorities.

Lead, coach and develop the reservations team to deliver high performance and strong guest service.
Set daily priorities, manage workload, and ensure coverage across both hotels.
Maintain clear standards for response times, quoting quality, follow-up, and booking conversion.
Support recruitment, onboarding, training, and ongoing performance management.
Maximize conversion of all reservation enquiries across direct, indirect and group channels.
Drive reconversion activity (lost business recovery) for both transient and group enquiries.
Monitor booking pace and support the Revenue team with demand trends and pickup insights.
Ensure accurate reservation input, correct segmentation, and strong data quality.
Support the Sales team with group quoting, rate loading, room blocks, cut-off dates, and group pick-up tracking.

Maintain professional and consistent communication across all channels (email, phone, portals).

We’re Hiring: Assistant Reservations Manager – Port Moresby
Holiday Inn & Suites Port Moresby
Holiday Inn Express Port Moresby
At Holiday Inn, we’re all about making travel easier and more enjoyable for our guests — and that starts with the people who bring our brand to life. If you’re a relationship-builder, a natural connector, and someone who loves driving commercial results while keeping things genuine and human, we’d love to meet you.
The Opportunity
The Assistant Reservations Manager supports the day-to-day operation of the reservations function across Holiday Inn Express Port Moresby and Holiday Inn & Suites Port Moresby. This role works closely with the Cluster Reservations Manager and is a key support role within the Commercial Team, helping to drive rooms revenue through strong enquiry handling, conversion, reconversion follow-up, rate integrity, and accurate booking administration. The role supports both Transient and Group business, ensuring all reservations processes are delivered consistently, professionally, and in line with IHG brand standards and property commercial priorities.
What You’ll Do
Support the Reservations Manager in managing daily reservations workflow and priorities across both hotels.
Ensure reservations enquiries are handled promptly, accurately and professionally across all channels.
Assist with team coverage planning and ensure consistent service levels are maintained.
Provide guidance and support to Reservations Agents to ensure standards and procedures are followed.
Support conversion of transient and group enquiries through accurate quoting and strong follow-up.
Assist with reconversion activity (lost business recovery) by contacting clients and following up on declined enquiries.
Ensure response times meet agreed standards and all enquiries are actioned within required timeframes.
Support the tracking of conversion and reconversion performance.
Support group room block setup, updates, and maintenance, including cut-off dates and rooming list requirements.
Assist Sales with group quoting and administration, ensuring accuracy and compliance with agreed rates and terms.
Monitor group pick-up and report any wash risks or block issues to the Cluster Reservations Manager.
Support rate loading accuracy and ensure correct rate application in all reservations.
Assist with identifying rate issues, mapping errors, or channel problems and escalate for correction.
Support distribution performance by ensuring bookings are correctly segmented and coded.
Assist with weekly/monthly reporting including conversion, enquiry response times, group pick-up and booking accuracy.
Maintain strong booking data quality, ensuring correct market segmentation and profile information.
Support the upkeep of reservations procedures, templates and documentation.
Work closely with Front Office to support arrivals, VIP requirements, special requests and rooming list accuracy.
Coordinate with Finance for billing requirements, deposits, and payment terms where required.
Support collaboration with Sales, Revenue and Conference & Events teams to ensure smooth communication and outcomes.
Ensure reservations handling meets IHG standards and supports a positive guest experience.
Maintain professional and consistent communication across all channels (email, phone, portals).
Support guest issue resolution related to reservations and booking discrepancies.
What we need from you
3–5 years’ experience in hotel reservations (international brand preferred).
Proven experience leading a reservations team and driving conversion performance.
Strong understanding of transient, group and long-stay booking processes.
Experience supporting Revenue Management strategies (MPI, ARI, RevPAR and rate integrity).
Strong knowledge of distribution channels (IHG.com, OTAs, GDS, travel agents and corporate negotiated rates).
High attention to detail with strong reporting, forecasting and administration skills.
Good understanding of Port Moresby market dynamics, including mining and FIFO travel patterns.
Join us today!
In return for your hard work, you can look forward to a highly competitive salary and benefits package. What’s more, because your career will be as unique as you are, we’ll give you all the tailored support you need to make a great start, be involved and grow.
And because the Holiday Inn & Suites Port Moresby brand belongs to the IHG® family of brands, you’ll also benefit from all of the opportunities that come from being part of a successful, global hospitality company with over 6000 hotels in over 100 countries around the world.
So, whoever you are, whatever you love doing, bring your passion to Holiday Inn and IHG and we’ll make sure you’ll have room to be yourself.
