jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a School to Mine (STM) Teacher, you will play a pivotal role in shaping the future of young Lihirians. Through the delivery of high-quality education aligned to the Australian and PNG Curriculum, you will empower students with the skills, confidence and aspirations needed to succeed, whether in further education, employment or within the business.
Focusing on High School English, Humanities and Social Sciences, you will bring learning to life, preparing students and young adults to transition successfully from school to meaningful careers. Your work will directly contribute to nurturing local talent and strengthening education outcomes across Lihir.
As part of our team, you will
Create Safe and Supportive Learning Environments
– Provide social and pastoral care by actively listening to student concerns and responding in accordance with school policies. Maintain a strong focus on student wellbeing and safety, including completing first aid training, monitoring student behaviour and use of school equipment, and contributing to OHS risk management by identifying hazards, assessing risks, implementing mitigation strategies, and investigating/reporting incidents.
Learning Curriculum Delivery
– Prepare and deliver engaging subject material aligned to approved curriculum frameworks. Conduct research to support lesson preparation, design well-structured lesson plans, and create flexible, intellectually challenging learning experiences that cater to diverse learners.
Extra-Curricular Learning
– Enhance the broader student experience by contributing to learning beyond the formal curriculum. Design and support programs and initiatives that broaden engagement, build capability and encourage participation.
Assessment and Recording of Progress – Evaluate student performance, identify individual learning needs, and maintain accurate assessment records. Communicate outcomes effectively with students and the school administration team in accordance with assessment and reporting policies.
Co-Curricular Participation
– Actively participate in school co-curricular activities as directed by the Principal and Deputy Principal (STM), supporting a holistic educational environment.
Professional Representation and Compliance
– Operate in accordance with the standards and expectations of Newmont Corporation, demonstrating due diligence when representing Lihir International School and the School to Mine Campus. Uphold the values of both Newmont and the school community at all times.
Contribution to Professional Teams
– Establish and implement effective personal work practices to meet goals and priorities. Collaborate closely with STM and LIS teachers, Newmont personnel and other stakeholders to ensure strong team performance. Participate in school and STM meetings and represent the school at relevant internal and external functions.
Other Duties
– Perform additional responsibilities as assigned by the Principal and Deputy Principal, School to Mine.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Tertiary qualification in Education (Bachelor level or higher).
Accredited High School Teacher with Teacher Registration.
Specialisation in English, Humanities or Social Sciences (preferred).
Relevant teaching work experience (essential), particularly within secondary education.
Excellent understanding of current learning theory principles, practices and methodologies.
Excellent understanding of individual and group learning principles, approaches and delivery methods.
Experience working with secondary students; experience with young adults highly desirable.
Adult Education experience, including distance/flexible learning programs (advantageous).
Strong understanding of Australian and PNG Curriculum frameworks.
Ability to plan, deliver and continuously improve structured education programs.
Excellent communication, public speaking and interpersonal skills.
Confident use of Microsoft Office Suite, particularly PowerPoint.
Technically capable and data-literate, with the ability to analyse educational outcomes.
Self-motivated, adaptable and able to take initiative.
Strong teamwork capability and ability to foster inclusive, collaborative environments
Willingness to actively contribute to extra-curricular activities and broader school initiatives.
Current First Aid Certificate (desirable).
We recognise that no candidate will meet every requirement. If you are a passionate, capable educator with the ability to grow into the role, we encourage you to apply.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will be based on Lihir, collaborating closely with colleagues at Lihir International School and the School to Mine Campus. You’ll work within a supportive, professional team that values continuous learning, safety and collaboration.
This is a dynamic, evolving program. You will have the opportunity not only to deliver established modules, but also to enhance and refine them — conducting research, introducing improvements and helping shape the future direction of STM programs.
You will operate in a culturally rich and community-focused environment where your contribution has visible and lasting impact.
Why Join Newmont
Through the School to Mine initiative, Newmont invests in education and local capability building ensuring that future generations are equipped to thrive.
When you join us, you will:
Contribute to a program with genuine community impact.
Be part of a global organisation with strong safety and professional standards.
Work in a collaborative and values-driven culture.
Develop professionally within a respected international company.
Help shape the future of education and employment pathways on Lihir.
If you are a passionate High School educator who thrives on adapting, improving programs and inspiring young people to succeed, we would love to hear from you.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 41546 before the advertised closing date: 10 March 2026.

jobs.title: Site Business Director, Lihir
jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Madang, Milne Bay, New Ireland, West New Britain, Western Highlands, Papua New Guinea
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Director Finance – Site Business, you will play a pivotal leadership role in overseeing site financial performance to strengthen decision-making and deliver sustainable business outcomes. You will drive operating cost discipline and capital efficiency while ensuring the site meets its financial commitments. Your leadership will directly influence profitability, operational performance, inventory optimisation, and long-term value creation.
About the Role
Reporting to Head, Finance - Africa Asia Pacific you will oversee site financial performance to strengthen decision-making, and in this role you will:
Drive
annual business planning, cost management, variance analysis, and long-term budgeting to support profitable operations.
Lead
the development of Life of Mine (LOM) budgets and deliver accurate monthly and quarterly forecasts in line with corporate requirements.
Analyse
financial performance, identify key cost drivers, and provide actionable recommendations for cost reduction and capital optimisation.
Oversee
site reporting of operating costs and capital expenditure to regional leadership, including detailed variance analysis.
Establish and optimise
financial systems and processes to strengthen economic modelling and business decision-making.
Ensure
strong SOX compliance, internal controls, and adherence to accounting standards.
Embed
an Always Safe culture aligned with Newmont’s safety strategy.
Lead and mentor
a high-performing finance team, building capability, succession strength, and an inclusive, collaborative culture.
About You
You are a commercially astute leader with a strong background in mining operations and a proven ability to influence performance outcomes at site level. You bring strategic thinking, strong governance knowledge, and the leadership capability to drive financial discipline while partnering effectively with operational stakeholders.
To be successful in this role, you will have:
Proven mining industry experience, preferably within a site-based environment.
Tertiary qualification in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related discipline.
Financial management experience within mining operations, including advanced proficiency in cost and capital management.
Experience leading diverse teams and driving performance across cross-functional environments.
A strong understanding of the financial metrics that underpin site performance and profitability.
Membership in a professional accounting or finance body is desirable.
Demonstrated experience leading diverse teams and influencing senior stakeholders.
Knowledge of US GAAP, SOX compliance, and internal control frameworks.
Advanced financial modelling, budgeting, and forecasting expertise.
Strong ERP proficiency (e.g., SAP) and familiarity with business planning systems.
Ability to analyse complex datasets and communicate insights clearly to non-financial stakeholders.
Strong commercial acumen and negotiation capability.
Proven ability to identify and implement process improvements and drive change.
Advanced verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to present complex financial information clearly to non-financial stakeholders.
Collaborative leadership style that fosters accountability, development, and inclusivity.
Your work environment
You will be a key member of the Site Leadership Team, partnering closely with operational leaders, regional finance teams, corporate supply chain, and external stakeholders including contractors and suppliers. This role operates at the intersection of strategy and execution, providing visibility across financial operations, and long-term planning. Safety, transparency, and continuous improvement underpin everything we do.
This is a full-time, two-year fixed-term residential role on a 5:2 roster, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life. You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependants. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will join a global leader in gold mining with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, and operational excellence. You will be empowered to influence strategic decisions, lead meaningful change, and contribute to long-term value creation for our people, communities, and shareholders. We foster a culture where accountability, collaboration, and innovation drive success.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 41604 before the advertised closing date: 9 March 2026.

About Us

More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, with more than 90% of our employees and contractors drawn from PNG. Our local education and skills development initiatives, including scholarships, agricultural support and health outreach programs, help to improve quality of life and build long-term capacity in the communities in which we operate.
About the Role
The Supervisor – Community Projects is responsible for the day-to-day supervision and delivery of community infrastructure projects, including schools, health centres, water systems and other facilities agreed through the Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) and community development plans.
The role ensures projects are delivered safely, on time and to agreed quality standards, while maximising local participation and ensuring compliance with company requirements, government regulations and IFC standards. This position supports the Community Infrastructure & Asset Delivery Standard under the Social Performance Management System (SPMS) and contributes to the material issue of Community Infrastructure & Access.
Key Accountabilities
This role supports the delivery of community infrastructure projects across the mine life cycle, ensuring outcomes are sustainable and beneficial beyond mine operations.
Project Supervision & Delivery:
Supervise day-to-day site activities, contractors and community labour to ensure construction projects meet technical specifications, schedules and budgets.
Leadership & Workforce Coordination:
Supervise project assistants, site supervisors and community labourers; prepare weekly work plans and schedules aligned with overall project timelines; provide on-the-job technical guidance and capacity building to local workers.
Safety, Quality & Compliance:
Monitor contractor performance, safety and workmanship to ensure compliance with site safety requirements, engineering standards and approved designs.
Technical Implementation & Reporting:
Implement SOPs and workflows under the Community Infrastructure & Asset Delivery Standard; monitor material usage and site-level budget performance; maintain accurate daily logs, attendance records and progress reports.
Collaboration & Integration:
Coordinate with Social Development, Agriculture Projects and Business Development teams to align infrastructure delivery with broader community programs and local contractor participation.
Stakeholder & Government Engagement:
Interface with local government engineers, inspectors and relevant authorities to ensure regulatory compliance and technical approvals.
Commitments & Expectations Management:
Deliver infrastructure commitments under the MOA and local development agreements; manage community expectations through clear communication on project scope, timelines and standards; provide transparent updates during construction and communicate changes as required.
About You
To be successful in this role, you will bring practical construction supervision experience and the ability to work effectively with contractors and local communities.
You will also demonstrate:
• Diploma or degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, Project Management or a related discipline
• At least 5 years of experience supervising infrastructure or construction projects, preferably in PNG or rural development contexts (experience with Community Projects is highly regarded)
• Experience implementing or monitoring compliance with site safety policies in construction or mining environments
• Experience using AutoCAD, Civil Cad and MS Project
• Sound understanding of Occupational Health & Safety principles, risk assessments and safe work procedures
• Proven ability to manage contractors, community labour and site-level reporting
• Strong record-keeping and project monitoring skills
• Proficiency in Tok Pisin and English (local dialects advantageous)
• PNG Driver’s Licence (mandatory)
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced produce, as well as internet access, cable television and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive remuneration, we offer savings programs, medical assistance, access to wellbeing and employee assistance programs, and a supportive roster environment.
If you share our values and are looking to contribute to meaningful community development outcomes, we encourage you to apply via our website.
This position is open only to candidates who have the right to live and work in Papua New Guinea without sponsorship.

.

More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Database & GIS Superintendent and will oversee management of all data and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) files emanating from the exploration teams activities.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Maintain safety incident records and manage geological databases.
Validate and QA/QC all field and drill data; compile weekly, monthly, and drill grade reports.
Create maps, tables, and 3D geological models for reporting and interpretation.
Prepare internal and statutory reports, forecasts, and SOPs.
Ensure accurate core logging, sampling, and adherence to QA/QC protocols.
Conduct regular database checks and monitor drilling productivity.
Train and mentor geologists and technicians on data entry, validation, and SOPs.
Promote high-performance culture and provide feedback on team performance.
Support talent development and succession planning.
Review historical data and update geological interpretations.
Participate in target reviews, ranking, and planning exploration programs.
Conduct technical reviews with senior geologists and assist in report compilation.
Promote and enforce a safe work culture and legal compliance.
Ensure drilling and sampling are conducted safely and competently.
Maintain housekeeping and uphold HSE standards.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Bachelor’s Degree in Geology (Preferable), Geophysics or Geoscience or Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
10+ years relevant exploration, mining or GIS work experience essential.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite, including Access and SQL Database systems software. Proficiency in GIS software. The ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble-shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

We are seeking a skilled and safety-conscious Heavy Duty Dump Truck Driver to join our dynamic construction and materials transport team. The ideal candidate is a reliable professional with a strong work ethic, exceptional driving skills, and a steadfast commitment to safety protocols and equipment care.
Position Overview
As a Heavy-Duty Dump Truck Driver, your primary mission is to operate and maintain heavy-duty dump trucks to transport bulk materials such as gravel, sand, topsoil, asphalt, and construction debris to and from various job sites. You will work in a fast-paced environment, often navigating challenging terrain and tight spaces, while coordinating closely with site supervisors and dispatchers to optimize delivery schedules and maintain project efficiency.
Reporting to:
Fleets Coordinator
Key Responsibilities & Duties
Daily Operations & Driving
Safely operate a heavy-duty dump truck to transport loose materials to designated locations.
Manoeuvre and position the vehicle for efficient loading and unloading at pits, quarries, and construction sites.
Navigate public roads and private job sites, adhering to all traffic laws and on-site safety rules.
Perform controlled dumping of materials in specified areas as directed by site personnel.
Coordinate with loaders, excavators, and ground crew to ensure safe and accurate loading/unloading cycles.
Vehicle Maintenance & Safety
Conduct thorough pre-trip and post-trip inspections of the vehicle, including brakes, tires, lights, hydraulics, and fluid levels.
Complete mandatory Driver Vehicle Inspection Reports (DVIR) and report any mechanical defects or safety issues immediately.
Perform basic maintenance tasks such as cleaning the truck, checking and adding fluids, and greasing fittings.
Secure all loads properly to prevent spillage during transit.
Maintain a clean and organized cab and logbook.
Site Coordination & Compliance
Communicate effectively with dispatchers and site supervisors via radio or mobile device.
Follow detailed delivery instructions and site-specific safety plans.
Ensure all documentation, including delivery tickets and hours-of-service logs, is accurately completed and submitted.
Represent the company professionally in all interactions with clients and the public.

Valid required licence with a clean driving record.

Current Medical Examiner's Certificate.
Strong knowledge of RTA regulations and road safety rules.
Ability to pass a pre-employment drug screen and background check.
Preferred Skills & Experience
Experience hauling construction materials in a live-bottom, end-dump, or transfer dump configuration.
Familiarity with operating in active construction zones and uneven terrain.
Basic mechanical aptitude for performing minor roadside repairs and troubleshooting.
Proven record of safety and reliability.
Physical Demands & Work Environment
This role is physically demanding and requires working in all weather conditions. Candidates must be able to:
Sit for extended periods and climb in and out of a tall truck cab repeatedly.
Perform physical tasks such as tarping loads, connecting/disconnecting trailer lines, and minor clean-up.
Work variable hours, including early mornings, overtime, and occasional weekends as project demands require.
Wear all required personal protective equipment (PPE), including hard hat, safety vest, steel-toe boots, and glasses.

Competitive remuneration package

Parts Interpreter
(The detail-focused kind — the ones who get the right part, the first time)
Location:
Kokopo
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s most recognised automotive groups, representing Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. Behind every vehicle on the road is a parts operation that has to be accurate, efficient, and responsive. When the right part is supplied quickly, workshops run smoothly and customers stay loyal.
We’re looking for a capable Parts Interpreter to join our Kokopo team.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be the link between the workshop, the customer, and the warehouse.
Your role is to correctly identify, source, and supply parts for service jobs, retail customers, and trade clients. That means interpreting parts using catalogues and systems, checking availability, preparing quotes, processing orders, and ensuring accurate documentation.
You’ll work closely with technicians to confirm specifications and avoid errors. You’ll liaise with suppliers when required, follow up backorders, and keep customers informed. Accuracy is critical — one incorrect part can delay a job, increase costs, and damage trust.
You’ll also support stock control processes, assist with inventory management, and help maintain an organised and professional parts counter environment.
Speed matters. Accuracy matters more.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone organised, technically minded, and confident communicating with both workshop staff and customers.
You’re comfortable using parts catalogues and computer systems. You pay attention to detail. You double-check part numbers. You don’t guess.
Experience in automotive parts interpretation is strongly preferred, particularly within dealership or branded environments. However, strong automotive knowledge, discipline, and willingness to learn will also be considered.
If a technician asks for a part — you confirm it properly.
If stock is low — you flag it early.
If a customer needs clarity — you explain it clearly.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is a national business with established brands, structured systems, and long-term investment in the PNG market.
Safety, accuracy, and professionalism are taken seriously. Performance is recognised, and capable operators have room to grow.
If you want a role where technical knowledge, accuracy, and professionalism are valued — this is it.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will assist with underground drilling, maintaining good housing practices, and adhering to workplace health and safety policies. Safety is the top priority.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Provide assisting role in all underground drilling activities.
Assist drillers and always under the guidance and direction of the driller.
Ensure that all aspects of duties and tasks outlined are undertaken in accordance with K92 mining procedures and practices.
Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
Ensure a high standard of personal presentation, behaviour, and conduct.
Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply within varying site operation
Work closely with the Underground Driller to assess Operational requirements
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture within the teams.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
About You
It is requirement of the position that the incumbent possess the following.
Grade 6, but preferably of Grade 10 or Technical Courses.
Must have current Class 6 PNG Driver’s License.
Has one (1) or more years work experience.
Ability to perform duties with minimum supervision.
Maintain work relationship with colleague workers
Must be a Local from the Mine impact areas.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.

This position is responsible to execute electrical installation & corrective, preventive electrical maintenance on all electrical and electronic equipment and components.

Monitor and troubleshoot equipment and create reports on efficiency.
Working along with maintenance supervisor, lead and senior engineer to create a long-term plan.
Ensuring compliance with company regulations
Assemble, install, test, and maintain electrical or electronic wiring, equipment, appliances, apparatus on all sites.
Diagnose malfunctioning systems, apparatus, and components, using test equipment and hand tools, to identify root cause of a breakdown and correct the problem.
Inspect electrical systems, equipment, and components to identify hazards, defects, and the need for adjustment or repair, and to ensure compliance.
Perform other duties instructed by the Maintenance Manager.

Quality assurance: Maintains a high level of work quality and complies to Electrical standards.
Safety: Maintains a high level of safety awareness. PPE/JSA/Permits
Productivity: Works efficiently & completes task on time without compromising quality.
Candidates Requirements
The person we seek must have the following:
Trade Certificate / Diploma in Electrical Engineering
Certified Electrician with High Voltage Certification
PPL License
3-5 years’ experience as an Electrical Technician or similar role in an oil & gas or mining industry
Electronics Trouble shooting Experience.
Electrical Knowledge – understands electricals system, wiring, circuits and components.
Drawing (SLD) – Able to read and interpret single line drawings (electrical & instrumentation)

Troubleshooting

Well-organized and adaptable

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
We are looking for a dynamic Lead – Agreements Implementation to join our Social Performance Team on Lihir Island, PNG. This exciting opportunity is a residential role on an attractive 5:2 roster.
Reporting directly to the Director of Social Performance Lihir, the Lead - Agreements Implementation will manage community agreement obligations and facilitating agreements between Newmont and the host communities of Lihir Island. This role is essential for maintaining Newmont’s social license to operate, fostering sustainable community and mine development, and ensuring mutual benefits for all parties involved.
As part of our team, you will
Lead community engagement initiatives to reinforce Newmont’s social license, gain community and government support, and strengthen relations.
Oversee and coordinate the implementation and tracking of community agreement obligations, addressing challenges to achieve sustainable and long-term benefits for both the community and Newmont’s operations.
Manage the execution and ongoing support of the Mine Management Plans (MMP) across accountable areas of Lihir Island, ensuring all obligations are fulfilled.
Serve as the secretariat for the Lihir Interim Agreement Committee (IIA), ensuring effective and transparent committee functions.
Oversee the resolution of outstanding issues from past agreements by monitoring commitments, engaging stakeholders, developing action plans, and ensuring transparent communication and compliance.
Build trust-based relationships with community leaders and stakeholders, foster collaborative partnerships, and integrate community perspectives into decision-making.
Ensure transparency and accountability through open communication and systematic reporting in line with Newmont’s ethical and sustainable practices.
Promote a collaborative culture within the Social Performance team to advance strategic initiatives and achieve positive outcomes for the Lihir host communities.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will be a strategic and business-savvy professional with proven experience in bridging business objectives and community interests. You will have a track record of managing complex stakeholder relationships, leading cross-functional teams, and influencing outcomes to achieve sustainable results.
You will also bring:
Tertiary qualifications in stakeholder engagement, planning, management, or commercial (essential).
Experience in cost management, account reconciliation, and budgeting.
PNG National Driver’s License (essential).
Actively promote and demonstrate a strong safety culture, leading by example to prioritize the well-being of all stakeholders.
Establish trust-based relationships with host communities and stakeholders to support mutual benefits and sustainable engagement.
Experience facilitating complex multi-party negotiations with landowners.
Ability to find middle ground between business interests and community needs.
Knowledge of traditional negotiation protocols in PNG communities.
Ability to facilitate resolution of historical grievances.
Proven ability to lead cross-functional teams and collaborate effectively to achieve results.
Proficiency in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Demonstrated success in developing team capacity and fostering growth.
Proficiency in the MS Office suite, with strong planning, analytical, and problem-solving capabilities.
Excellent organisational and time management skills to meet deadlines and maintain high-quality standards.
Active listening, rapport-building, and conflict resolution abilities to effectively handle diverse stakeholder interactions.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a residential 5:2 roster, based in Newmont’s Lihir townsite community, a gated precinct based on the coastline cliff with magnificent ocean views.
The townsite has Company provided housing (inc. utilities), international school (up to and including Year 10) and a range of recreational facilities including gym, sports club with restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts and playground areas for the kids. There is also a 9-hole golf course on the island! Healthcare services are provided at the Lihir Medical Clinic.
An onsite deli and café provide access to fresh local and imported produce including grocery items, as well as barista-made coffees and freshly baked cakes. The company offers regular shipment of groceries and care packages for townsite residents to access goods not available on the island.
The Lihir fishing and boating clubs offer the opportunity to get out and enjoy the pristine waters and beaches around the island on the weekends.
A generous relocation package is provided to ensure smooth integration for you (and your family) to settle into island life. You will also be eligible for medical insurance cover, annual flights home and schooling for eligible dependants. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and bonus scheme.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you will make a tangible difference in the lives of communities while contributing to one of the world’s leading gold mining operations. You will join a supportive, high-performing team, with opportunities for professional growth, leadership development, and the chance to deliver sustainable outcomes that matter.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

The
Head of Business Lending (HoBL)

The HoBL acts as a trusted financial advisor to clients, partnering closely with internal teams—including credit, risk, operations, and product specialists—to deliver tailored financial solutions.

Identify, pursue, and convert new business lending opportunities within target industries and segments.
Develop strategic networks with industry partners, brokers, accountants, and community organisations.
Achieve growth targets for lending and deposits.
Conduct regular market research to identify trends and emerging opportunities.

Observe and follow to Standard protocols of credit files before handling over to support / back-office team. Aim to improve customer experience, quality and TAT.
Quality Control & Compliance - ensure quality submission to achieve high accuracy and correctness

Add value to the client and stay ahead of the competition by structuring and implementing innovative deals based on program guidelines.
Increase wallet share by cross selling products to the customer.
Create excellent customer experience to generate business referrals

Liaise with various divisions like Risk / Back Office for onboarding the client and then servicing them

Ensure effective training is given to direct reports so that staff are fully versed with the product knowledge to effectively sell existing and potential clients.
Manage Relationship Managers performance assessments to the performance targets for Commercial Lending.

About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The
Quality Control Officer
is responsible for monitoring, maintaining, and continually improving the laboratory’s Quality Management System (QMS) to ensure the laboratory demonstrates competence and operates consistently in accordance with ISO/IEC 17025 requirements.
Essential Duties
QMS Maintenance & Document Control
Maintain the laboratory’s Quality Manual, ensuring all policies reflect current operations and ISO 17025 requirements.
Manage the Document Control System: Ensure all Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), forms, and work instructions are current, and accessible to staff.
Archive obsolete documents and ensure strict version control to prevent the use of invalid procedures.
Prepare and provide weekly summaries on Labs compliance to the management system to lab management.
Internal Audits & Compliance
Develop and execute the Annual Internal Audit Schedule covering all elements of the management and technical requirements.
Conduct vertical and horizontal audits to verify compliance with methods and standards.
Non-Conformance & Corrective Action (CAPA)
Lead Root Cause Analysis (RCA) investigations for all non-conformances and customer complaints.
Monitor Corrective and Preventive Actions to ensure they are implemented effectively and verify their long-term effectiveness.
Equipment & Metrology
Oversee the equipment master list, ensuring all critical equipment is calibrated by ISO 17025 accredited providers (metrological traceability).
Review calibration certificates for compliance with required specifications before equipment is returned to service.
Ensure intermediate checks (e.g., balance verifications, pipette checks) are performed and recorded as scheduled.
Training & Experience
A commitment to Safety
Minimum 2–3 years of experience working within an ISO 17025 accredited laboratory environment.
Technical Knowledge: Strong understanding of ISO/IEC 17025:2017 standards, particularly regarding risk-based thinking and impartiality.
Formal Internal Auditor Training certificate (based on ISO 19011).
Experience with Laboratory Information Management Systems (LIMS).
Statistical analysis skills

About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
The Papua New Guinea (PNG)–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a new Australian Government investment that will be working in partnership with PNG to strengthen its technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program will work closely with TVET stakeholders and select technical colleges to grow the number of skilled individuals with industry relevant skills.
This Opportunity
As
Procurement Manager
you will be responsible for leading on all procurement activities for the program, ensuring it is conducted in accordance with company and client compliance requirements and is delivered with considerations towards value-for-money, localisation and other program and government objectives.
This will include:
Planning, directing and coordinating all procurement activities in compliance with the
Australian Commonwealth Procurement Rules (CPR’s)
, DFAT
Value for Money
principles, and Palladium procurement and due diligence standards.
Advising management on procurement strategies and sourcing options. Managing the full procurement cycle, including planning, market engagement, solicitation, evaluation, contracting and mobilisation. Procurement may range from simple three quote evaluations to complex competitive tender processes, requiring in-depth preparation and evaluation.
Integrating social procurement principles into all sourcing activities by prioritising suppliers that deliver measurable social, economic and environmental benefits to local businesses, women, youth owned enterprises, people with disability and marginalised groups
Developing and maintaining procurement plans, schedules and templates, and ensuring all procurement documentation—including due diligence records, vendor/contractor files, contract registers and tracking tools—is complete, accurate, auditable, up to date, and fully compliant with DFAT and Palladium requirements.
Reviewing procurement requests to ensure clarity, accuracy, and alignment with SWLT objectives, and support specification and scope development.
Preparing bidding documents (RFQs, RFPs) and leading tender evaluations to ensure transparent bid analysis. Negotiating contracts, pricing and terms with suppliers.

Providing regular reports on procurement progress, risks, timelines and delivery status, including up-to-date strategic advice to senior management.
Developing and maintaining an approved supplier database. Conducting supplier performance evaluations.
Identifying and mitigating procurement risks, escalating critical issues—including conflicts of interest, integrity concerns or suspected fraud—as required, and promote ethical, transparent procurement practices across all SWLT teams and partners.
Understanding and contributing to SWLT gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives as relevant to this role and participate in GEDSI learning and engagement as required.

Championing ethical procurement practices across all SWLT teams and partners.
Modelling, contributing to and supporting an office culture of learning and performance with colleagues, junior staff and counterparts, building procurement capability across the SWLT team through coaching, guidance and practical support.
Supporting and upholding the organisation’s commitment to environmental sustainability, such as integrating environmental sustainability considerations into procurement decisions, including climate‑friendly options and reduced resource use.
Contributing to the implementation of solutions that deliver value and ensure SWLT principles

are embedded within program delivery.

A strong understanding of the Commonwealth Procurement Rules, DFAT procurement requirements and PNG Government procurement processes.

Using strong analytical thinking and proactive problem solving.

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Officer Emergency Response will coordinate the preparation, execution, and improvement of emergency response plans and procedures including emergency drills and compliance.
Essential Duties
Support in the preparation and execution of emergency response plans and procedures, ensuring alignment with site-specific needs and regulatory requirements.
Provides coordination and technical guidance to Voluntary ERT members.
Perform regular inspections and maintenance checks of emergency response equipment.
Engage in emergency drills and simulations, helping to prepare and conduct these exercises and deliver feedback for continuous improvement
Provides coordination and guidance for ERT training activities.
Training & Experience
A personal commitment to Safety
Certification in fire and rescue, medical response or other emergency response discipline
Industry recognized emergency response systems, standards and processes
Relevant regulations and compliance requirements
Communication and Influencing skills
Risk Management processes
Emergency incident management
Competent proficiency in implementing occupational emergency response systems
Foundational proficiency in managing and applying operational risk management processes
Foundational proficiency in implementing emergency response standards, best-fit practices, monitoring processes, regulatory compliance
Advanced proficiency in executing emergency response activities
Foundational commercial skills: budgets, forecasting, planning, analysis, reporting and communicating result
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 28/14 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. The Papua New Guinea (PNG)–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) program is a new Australian Government investment that will be working in partnership with PNG to strengthen its technical and vocational education and training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. Activities will cover a diverse portfolio of technical assistance including grants, infrastructure, organisational capacity assessments, labour market analysis, gender and inclusion work, safeguards and sector coordination activities.

Hargy Oil Palms Limited (HOPL) is an Oil Palm plantation company based in Bialla, West New Britain Province. A remote location situated approximately 2 and half hours’ drive east of Kimbe town.
HOPL currently has a vacancy for a suitably qualified and experienced Lands Officer who will join its General Administration Department and deliver support services to HOPL, its Oil Palm Growers and stakeholders.
Primary Objectives:
Reporting to the Lands Manager, the Lands Officer will be required to provide support to the Small Holder Oil Palm growers and facilitate the dissemination of land instruments related to the acquisition and granting of state leases and where possible assist in the processing of land applications for Oil palm land settlement schemes and Village Oil Palm blocks. The role will also be required to assist in the maintenance and registration of any Oil Palm extension projects for the HOPL and ensure that all statutory requirements are fully ascertained for the company under the RSPO, free, prior informed consent process.
Competencies
To perform the job successfully, it is expected that the applicant can demonstrate the following competencies:
Arrange community engagement message tracks for Free, Prior and Informed consent for land acquisition expansion projects.
Assist in the facilitation and formation of ILGs to ensure that all have proper constitutions and work closely with the district commerce officers to establishing solid business practices for the registered groups.
To facilitate the process of registration of all Lease-Leaseback land dealings involving ILGs desirable in new Oil Palm development projects and guide them on the rights and obligations conversant with the laws of PNG.
Able to assist in the delivery of alternate dispute resolution mechanism approaches where there is dispute over ownership of land with the support from the relevant government agencies.
Work with Smallholder Extension services officers and the OPIC to ensure that Clan Land Use Agreements (CLUA for all Village Oil Palm blocks are appropriately registered using the FPIC process.
Assist in the preparation and delivery of awareness on important land matters to the Bialla Smallholder Oil Palm growers.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our supply team, you will assist the Supply & Logistics Manager and Senior Offshore Superintendent with the overall Offsite Materials chain to continually maximise efficiencies whilst minimizing cost to the company & overall material supply chain. In this integral role you will assist with establishing and maintaining close relationships with all external parties being dealt with to ensure timely and seamless process of import and export of materials. You will also ensure the workplace health & safety of employees, contractors and other stakeholders and to minimize the impact of the Supply chain on the environment.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Develop for approval, Implement, and supervise systems and procedures consistent with the Supply Departments governance and policies for proficient management across all functions of the offsite material chain.
Work together with Supply Superintendent, Infield Logistics section, & Managers to plan and execute development of a co-operative operational process and procedures to provide seamless transfers of materials
Manages employees responsible for preparing, staging, and distributing materials as needed to mine site.
Assist with ensuring that KPI goals are met
Adhering to approved budgets and cost transfers within K92 Mining.
Provides input to strategic decisions that affect the functional area of materials responsibility.
Confident in resolving escalated issues arising from operations and requiring coordination with other departments.
Cultivate positive relationships through effective communication and provides constructive feedback to the Supply & Logistics Manager.
Demonstrate commitment to and hold others accountable to complying with the K92 safety management systems and strategies.
Develop succession plans through leading, training and mentoring direct reports to deliver the plan with aim of building a high performing team.
Positively influence and shape the material department culture to ensure a safe, sustainable and disciplined approach to work.
Set weekly and daily priorities for the team, monitor progress and report on activity and outcomes.
Ensure the timely completion of all tasks for both staff and contractors
Liaise with representatives from K92 Mining logistics to ensure that co- operative working relationships are maintained.
Liaise with external parties of Government departments, Contractors, to ensure a positive and seamless process for material imports and exports
Maintain and perform approvals in the Pronto system
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have all or the following
Experience communicating with providers in PNG and internationally
Ability to lead and coach a team with diverse skills
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders
7 years’ experience in a supervisory role within logistics or materials in mining or similar environment
5 years’ experience of Pronto
Demonstrated problem solving and decision-making capability.
Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly to and influence internal and external stakeholders.
Negotiation skills and understanding of negotiation techniques.
Strong Ability to understand, promote, forward improvements within Material process and Procedures
Excellent Microsoft packages, written and verbal communication skills.
Proficient in the operation of Pronto
Experience in Microsoft suite office tools – Excel Word
Ability to manage a diverse range of staff
Strong communication skills. Both written and spoken.
Qualifications in leadership management and business strongly encouraged
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Advisor Power & Utilities Operations will support operations team in P&U to ensure efficiency and compliance with safety standards.
Essential Duties
Adhere to daily P&U operations
Execute strategies to enhance operational efficiency
Support, collaborate with, and provide assistance to Supervisors P&U Operations
Assess data and report on improvement outcomes
Administer safety protocols and execute regular safety audits
Responsible for assessing relevant risks, executing mitigation measures, and continuously monitoring for risks
Provide technical expertise and support for operational troubleshooting
Produce weekly High-Level Plan (HLP) for execution.
Engauge in weekly planning meetings.
Training & Experience
A commitment to Safety
Relevant academic qualification or trade qualification in Power Generation, Practical knowledge gained from working in relevant Power Station roles - applied knowledge of technical aspects of the role including Power systems, equipment and systems
Practical and applied knowledge of working safely and sustainably in this area of Power generation.
Proven ability to identify risk and taking active steps to mitigate risk
Acquired knowledge of business and process improvement identifying improvement opportunity and taking appropriate action
Competent in safety, health, and sustainability
Knowledge in operation of boiler and steam systems is an advantage.
Knowledge in Heavy Fuel Oil separators operations is an advantage.
Knowledge in Demineralising operation for producing Boiler water is an advantage

•             Crushing and ore handling system
•             Comminution circuit comprising the SAG and Ball mills and gravity concentrator
•             Flotation circuit
•             Thickening and filtration circuits
•             Concentrate loading
The Processing plant operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Perform the day-to-day operation of the process plant including, Crushing and ore handling system, Comminution circuit comprising the SAG and Ball mills and gravity concentrator, Flotation circuit, Thickening and filtration circuits, Concentrate loading, Preparation of reagents

Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.

Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.

Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure that adequate duty of care is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
Ensure utmost compliance of Occupational Health and Safety Regulations and any site-specific rules which may apply.

ROLE DESCRIPTION
ROLE TITLE : Head of Research
ROLE ID : HOR-001
DEPARTMENT : RESEARCH
DIVISION : IBSUniversity
ROLE TERM : 24 MONTHS
ROLE TYPE : FULLTIME
EFFECTIVE DATE: : TBA
REPORTING TO : PRO VICE-CHANCELLOR (Academic)
ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a
difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999
and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The
affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer
internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea.
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments
to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching,
learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and
partners. The role of the Head of Research needs to be modern, innovative, and strategically
positioned.
POSITION OVERVIEW
The Head of Research will provide strategic leadership and operational oversight to promote a
research culture of excellence, innovation, and integrity at IBSUniversity. This role is central to
strengthening the University’s research systems, advancing staff capacity, fostering student
research engagement, and ensuring alignment with national higher education priorities.
The role includes academic engagement through teaching two units - one each from
IBSUniversity and Southern Cross University - to strengthen the connection between teaching
and research, and to better understand student expectations and academic progression.
The Director of Research will also support the broader institutional strategy by ensuring that all
research activities are in harmony with the expectations of the Department of Higher Education,
Research, Science and Technology (DHERST), contribute to the University’s strategic goals, and
uphold the Vision, Mission, Values, and non-negotiable IBS Culture.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
1.1. Strategic Research Leadership
Implement the University’s research strategy, policies, and annual research plan.
Promote a culture of research excellence, innovation, and interdisciplinary collaboration across schools and faculties aligning research priorities with Papua New Guinea’s national development goals.
2.2. Academic Contribution through Teaching
Undertake two units per semester (one IBSU, one SCU) to maintain academic connection and student engagement.
Use teaching to identify talent and cultivate a research mindset among students and faculty.
2.3. Research Management and Capacity Building
Oversee the planning, execution, and dissemination of research projects.
Organize and conduct of National and International Conference.
Continue to publish “IBSU Journal of Business and Research” biannual journal.
Support faculty and postgraduate students (Commencement of master’s Programme from 2026) in developing research proposals, securing grants, and publishing in reputable journals.

Job Description
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Processing -Department as a
Autoclaves Supervisor - Processing.
About the role
Reporting to the Process Foreman, the Autoclave Supervisor is responsible for the safe and efficient operation of the autoclave circuit, leading a team of operators to deliver reliable production performance while upholding the highest standards of process safety and environmental compliance. This role requires hands-on autoclave operational experience, a strong understanding of high-pressure process safety, and the ability to drive positive change in work practices, team culture, and plant performance. A key accountability of this role is the development and training of both national and local staff, ensuring the transfer of technical knowledge and building long-term operational capability within the workforce.
In this role, you will:
Lead day-to-day operation of the autoclave and associated circuits to ensure production targets are met safely and efficiently.
Supervise, coach, and develop autoclave operators, ensuring adherence to safe operating procedures and compliance with permits and regulatory standards.
Monitor process conditions, troubleshoot deviations, and coordinate corrective actions to maintain plant stability and product quality.
Champion process safety by enforcing critical controls, conducting safety interactions, and fostering a strong safety culture.
Drive the structured development and training of national and local staff, ensuring competency growth, knowledge transfer, and career progression opportunities.
Collaborate with maintenance, engineering, and technical teams to plan and execute shutdowns, inspections, and repairs.
Ensure accurate reporting of shift activities, production data, and incidents into plant systems.
Contribute to operator training programs, competency assessments, and continuous skills development.
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To
succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Proven operational experience in POX autoclave circuits.
Demonstrated leadership ability in supervising teams in a processing environment.
Strong understanding of process safety principles (e.g., high pressure, high temperature, hazardous materials).
Excellent problem-solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to communicate effectively across teams and disciplines, with a focus on mentoring and capability development.
Commitment to fostering a culture of accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
High level of initiative with an eagerness to drive positive change and challenge the status quo.
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
