About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The
Reliability Engineer
will improve the safety, availability, and life-cycle performance of process plant assets by preventing mechanical failures through proactive reliability engineering, data-driven analysis, and continuous improvement.
Essential Duties
Identify issues/defects and improvement opportunities by analyzing equipment performance, process delays, costs, asset management KPI’s and maintenance history in SAP
Develop project plans for reliability improvement initiatives in line with Newmont’s Defect Elimination Process
Develop and manage equipment maintenance strategies using Reliability Centered Maintenance methodology and PM optimization for existing strategies on equipment not meeting availability or reliability requirements
Compile and distribute key asset performance indicators including availability and utilization
Facilitate Root Cause Analysis (RCA) sessions using RCA guidelines to identify failure causes, containment and counter measures as necessary
Develop lifecycle cost models for critical assets and monitor and quantify equipment lifecycle costs
Investigate and adopt alternative strategies to support capital replacement plan
Actively participate and contribute to safety improvements and environmental awareness.
Training & Experience
A committment to Safety
Bachelor’s Degree qualification in Mechanical Engineering
Registered with IEPNG
Demonstrated fixed plant reliability engineering experience in large-scale mine operations
Understanding of mining industry asset maintenance and reliability methods i.e. defect elimination, criticality analysis, asset strategy development, operate for reliability, condition monitoring, etc
Understanding of safety compliance and regulations
Knowledge of root cause analysis, problem solving, and other analytical techniques
Knowledge of mine operations Fixed Plant and mine processing equipment
Knowledge of maintenance strategies, Master data management and Reliability Centred Maintenance principles
Experience in Failure Modes Effects Analysis facilitation and workshop delivery
Skills in mining industry specific failure metrics and data analytics – i.e. MTBF, MTTR
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21:21 roster.

jobs.description:
Provincial Trainer – Education and Social Emotional Learning Project
ChildFund PNG is seeking a committed and skilled Provincial trainer to deliver School Leadership and Social Emotional Learning (SEL) training to secondary school leaders, teachers, and students in project target areas. The role plays a key part in strengthening school leadership, promoting safe and inclusive school environments, and building the leadership capacity of young people.
This position require regular travel to remote and rural communities and close collaboration with provincial education offices, school leaders, students, and ChildFund project staff.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
Provincial Trainer is responsible for delivering training and monitoring progress against project targets for Head Teachers, Principals, School Boards of Management (BoM), using the School Leadership Management Training Package. This role is responsible for working closely with secondary school students and building leadership, GEDSI skills to ensure proper peer to peer support mechanism in targeted schools using Rights, Responsibility and Resilience  for Respectful Relationship training. The role requires regular travel to remote locations to conduct trainings within schools. Provincial Trainers will also follow up with schools to support the development and implementation of School Learning Improvement Plans (SLIPs) and Behaviour Management Plans. In addition, the Provincial Trainer will work closely with provincial partners to coordinate training logistics, including school and teacher selection, preparation of training venues, and scheduling of district-level trainings. The position requires maintaining regular, open communication with Lead Trainers and the Provincial Liaison Officer (PLO) to ensure smooth coordination of training activities, logistics, and provincial office requirements.
Key Duties
Deliver School Leadership and 5R Learning Resource Manual (LRM) trainings to achieve project targets and outcomes, ensuring GEDSI, Child Protection, and Safe Schools principles are mainstreamed across all sessions.
Facilitate Safe Schools and respectful relationships sessions with secondary school students, strengthening student leadership, peer-to-peer support mechanisms, and positive behaviour.
Provide follow-up support to trained school leaders on the development and implementation of School Learning Improvement Plans (SLIPs), Behaviour Management Plans, and delivery of 5R sessions, in collaboration with provincial and district-level staff.
Review and provide technical advice on draft plans to strengthen quality, effectiveness, and stakeholder engagement.
Participate in regular coordination meetings with project staff to review progress, identify challenges and risks, and develop corrective or mitigation actions in consultation with Lead Trainers, PDOE, and District Officers.
Work with school leaders and teachers to strengthen parental and community engagement in children’s learning, school planning, and the implementation of school development and behaviour management plans.
Prepare timely training and activity reports for each project target area, highlighting effective practices, lessons learned, and challenges encountered.
Contribute to training planning in target areas, anticipate operational risks, and support contingency planning; assist with administrative and financial requirements as required.
Work closely with sub-national NDOE counterparts (provincial and district levels) to plan, deliver, and monitor project activities.
Ensure full compliance with ChildFund’s policies, safeguarding standards, and procedures.
Qualification & Experience:
Degree or Diploma in Education, Social Work, Adult Education, or a related discipline recognized in PNG.
Experience working with secondary school students and young people, including facilitating Safe Schools or respectful relationships activities.
Experience working in INGO in implementing, managing, coordination educational programs
Sound understanding of the PNG education system, school leadership, and school management processes.
Demonstrated experience in training, mentoring, and coaching teachers, school leaders, or young people to achieve positive outcomes.
Experience delivering training in diverse and remote settings in PNG.
Sound knowledge of quantitative and qualitative monitoring and reporting
Desirable:
Experience trainer, school Inspector in PNG.
Knowledge of participatory adult learning methodologies.
Experience in child rights, Safe Schools, SLIP training.
Skills:
Strong training skills – confidence, clarity and responsiveness
Ability to engage trainees from a diverse setting.
Strong organizational and planning skills and ability to meet deadlines.
Sound evaluative skills, able to assess trainees progress and make adjustments where necessary.
Flexible and willing to travel to project target areas.
Safeguarding
Remain alert and responsive to any child safeguarding or sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment (SEAH) risks, acquire relevant knowledge and skills to promote strong safeguarding practices, understand the child safeguarding and PSEAH policy and procedures, and conduct yourself consistent with those policies
Appointment to this position is subject to
criminal background checks and reference checks.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department. This rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.
Key Accountabilities
Give direction, delegate tasks and provide technical assistance to subordinates.
Liaise with senior maintenance leadership on planned maintenance.
Maintain stock levels and place orders as required.
Ensure cost control measures are considered by utilizing resources available to full capacity.
Report and rectify any hazardous sightings to the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent in the 800L workshop.
Ensure training requirements are met.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings workshop safety representatives.
Regularly monitors and evaluates staff performance in consultation with Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Provide coaching for performance improvement.
In conjunction with mobile maintenance superintendent, takes disciplinary action to address performance deficiencies, in accordance with the Company’s rules, policies and procedures.
Personally, responds to inquiries and complaints from the employees.
Responds to emergency situations as necessary.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Mobile Maintenance Superintendent.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
Qualifications & Experience
Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation. Minimum Certificate III required.
7+ years relevant work experience essential.
Underground mobile fleet such as Sandvik and Caterpillar and provide guidance of Methods, practices, techniques.
Ability to plan, assign, direct and coordinate a variety of functional specialties (areas) with overlapping work areas.
Must have at least 3 years in mobile fleet maintenance in a supervisory capacity. Should also have experience in training of both operating and maintenance personnel.
Experience in the use of Pronto will be advantageous.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Job Description
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mineral Resources Department as
Geologist- Underground.
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Underground Geologist, the Underground Geologist is responsible for supporting and developing
the orebody definition through underground mapping, sampling, data interpretation, and reconciliation. This role plays a key part in ensuring efficient resource extraction by providing timely and accurate geological information to mine planning and operations teams.
In this role, you will:
Conduct underground geological mapping and face sampling
Ensure accurate and timely geological data capture using mine software and databases.
Log and sample underground diamond drill core (if applicable).
Update 3D geological models in coordination with resource geologists.
Communicate geological information to mine operations to support production and development activities.
Monitor ore and waste boundaries and ensure compliance with mine design.
Assist in ore mark-ups and dilution control.
Liaise with survey and engineering teams to ensure alignment of plans and geological reality.
Contribute to daily, weekly, and monthly geological reports and reconciliation of mined material vs. resource models.
Monitor ore production to ensure grade and tonnage targets are met.
Contribute to the improvement of geological systems, processes, and standards.
Provide feedback and suggestions for improved ore control and data collection practices.
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To
succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, or a related field
Minimum 2–3 years’ experience in an underground mining environment.
Strong skills in underground mapping and sampling.
Proficiency in geological software such as Datamine, Leapfrog, Deswik or similar.
Familiarity with mining operations and ore control practices.
Experience with underground diamond drilling programs.
Knowledge of resource modeling and reconciliation practices.
Previous experience with mine site databases (e.g., acQuire, Datashed).
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Geologist – Underground
Embark on a rewarding career with New Porgera Limited as a Geologist - Underground. This role offers a unique opportunity to work with a dynamic team to contribute to NPL’s success. Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

World Vision International Papua New Guinea (WVIPNG) has an exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for a suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the role of
Education Technical Specialist
to be based in

PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
This role provides technical leadership across the full education grant lifecycle, including framework development, readiness assessments, baseline studies, implementation, and integration of education policies to ensure strong processes, aligned plans, and quality reporting. It oversees education implementation through field support, evaluations, data quality assurance, and consultancy management to ensure results, learning, and credible evidence inform decision-making and grant performance. The role also leads reporting, knowledge management, tools development, learning, and capacity strengthening by supporting staff and partners, disseminating lessons learned, implementing evaluation recommendations, and strengthening education capacity and collaboration at national and sector levels.
Education Grant Framework & Planning
Develop the overall framework for grant EDUCATION in accordance to the design document and donor requirements, ensuring an effective EDUCATION framework is in place.
Identify the core information needs of grant management, partners, and funding agencies; participate in development of the annual work plan and budget, ensuring alignment with technical strategy so that EDUCATION is aligned to grant objectives and the EDUCATION Plan is in place and budget available on time.
Contribute substantial information and analyses to interdepartmental working groups on the education sector, ensuring stakeholders are included in the EDUCATION process as appropriate.
Education Grant Readiness, Design & Baseline Assessment
Conduct readiness assessment: the incentives at the system level, the beneficiaries and existing capacity, ensuring strong EDUCATION processes are applied.
Give technical lead on the development, processing and administration of the grant projects in the education sector, ensuring the education design and project plan is in place.
Provide technical leadership and integrate Grant Education policies and guidelines in the design and implementation of education projects, ensuring EDUCATION reports are available.
Identify the requirement for collecting baseline data, prepare terms-of-reference for and arrange the conduct of a baseline survey, as required, ensuring the baseline research report is available.
Education Implementation, Evaluation & Data Quality Assurance
Oversee and execute EDUCATION activities with particular focus on results and impacts as well as in lesson learnt, ensuring strong EDUCATION processes are applied.
Undertake regular visits to the field to support the implementation of EDUCATION and to identify where adaptations might be needed, ensuring EDUCATION reports are available and include lessons learnt.
Clarify and/or facilitate the process for the technical evaluation of the Grant project’s implementation process and progress, ensuring strong EDUCATION processes are applied.
Identify the need and draw up the ToRs for specific studies; recruit, guide and supervise consultants or organisations that are contracted to implement special surveys and studies required for evaluating grant effects and impacts, ensuring well-documented and targeted consultancy outcomes, if consultants are hired to support EDUCATION.
Perform regular field visits to ensure the quality of data collected by Programs and to verify the accuracy of reported data, ensuring field staff is included in the EDUCATION process as appropriate, and sub-grantees demonstrate the required M&C capacity and produce quality EDUCATION reports
Education Reporting, Knowledge Management & Tools Development
Work closely with Project managers/ Coordinators, M & E Coordinator, and the education project team in preparing the progress reports in accordance with approved reporting formats and ensure their timely submission, including quarterly progress reports, annual project reports, inception reports, and ad-hoc technical reports, ensuring reporting is submitted on time.
Prepare consolidation progress reports for grant management, including identification of problems, causes of potential bottlenecks in the project implementation, and providing specific recommendations, ensuring high-quality reporting is in place with actionable next steps and learning and major challenges are anticipated and mitigation actions planned.
Identify strengths and weaknesses in existing data collection and management systems and propose solutions to improve knowledge management activities, ensuring high-quality reporting is in place with actionable next steps and learning.
Draft tools/manuals (eg. Teacher Training, Coaching, etc.) and their revisions as well as data collection procedures (eg. logical framework, project performance tracking, indicators, data flow chart, EDUCATION manuals), ensuring teacher training manuals, coaching guide/tools reviewed and updated.
Learning, Evaluation & Capacity Strengthening
Design and implement a system to identify, analyze, document and disseminate lessons learned, ensuring lessons learnt and refresher training are well documented and include NO stakeholders and proper communication of EDUCATION findings at all levels.
Monitor the follow up on evaluation recommendations, ensuring evaluation recommendations are implemented.
Support project/program staff on ways to properly document, organize and capture program progress, ensuring proper communication of EDUCATION findings at all levels.
Facilitate, act as resource person, and join, if required any technical supervision and evaluation initiatives, ensuring EDUCATION expertise is available to the grants team and stakeholders.
Organize (and provide) refresher training in EDUCATION for grants staff, implementing partners, local organizations and primary stakeholders with view of strengthening local EDUCATION capacity, ensuring EDUCATION Capacity is provided to grants team and stakeholders and local expertise is built.
Network with external and WV internal partners to promote learning and achieve EDUCATION excellence, ensuring external networking is in place and WV represented in relevant TWGs and cluster (eg. Education Cluster).

Advanced degree (Master’s) in Education, Economics, Public Policy or closely-related Social Science field from an internationally recognized university, or bachelors degree with equivalent experience

Minimum of 5 years of experience living or working in a developing country is desirable; experience living or working in a Pacific island nation is preferred

Experience with programming to address gender and protection concerns and programming for very young children and adolescents/youth required

Strong knowledge in literacy and learning; specific experience in one or more of the areas of materials development, conduct of teacher training, teacher education and/or language and literacy policy reform is desired
Strong analytical skills required
Proven skills in report writing
Fluency in English is required.
Strong interpersonal, writing and oral presentation skills in English are also required.
Professional working proficiency in Tok Pisin is viewed as an asset
Teaching experience.
Development of Manuals/tools for teacher capacity building/development especially in the areas of literacy and numeracy as well as coaching.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Compliance Officer is responsible for designing, implementing, and monitoring internal AML/CTF procedures and policies relating to record keeping, reporting, risk assessment, customer due diligence measures, and management control systems. The Officer will also be responsible for organizing and conducting training for staff on anti-money laundering procedures and for receiving internal disclosures of suspected money laundering or terrorist financing activities. They will also be responsible for recommending whether there is sufficient evidence to warrant a disclosure to FASU.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Develop and implement internal policies and procedures relating to Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) regulations.
Advise management of any implications of changes to internal policies and procedures.
Implement the annual compliance plan and perform relevant quality assurance checks to ensure adherence
Assist in the preparation and management of inspections by financial authorities such as the FASU/BPNG.
Conduct due diligence reviews on customers and transactions.
Report results of reviews of AML/KYC risk assessments and monitor remedial proceedings.

ORGANATIONAL CONTEXT
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999 and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching, learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and partners. The role of the Head of Research needs to be modern, innovative, and strategically positioned.
Job Summary:
The Secretary will assist the Council and the Vice Chancellor by managing official communications, preparing documents, and organizing meetings. The ideal candidate must be a qualified lawyer with at least one year of legal practice experience. The role requires strong organizational skills, professional handling of legal and administrative tasks, and the ability to support high-level university governance.
Key Responsibilities:
Prepare agendas and organize meetings for the Council and the Vice Chancellor.
Take minutes and keep records of meetings.
Handle official correspondence and document filing.
Provide legal advice when needed, based on your legal background.
Assist in drafting and reviewing legal and administrative documents.
Ensure timely follow-up on action points from meetings.
Maintain confidentiality of sensitive information.
Support the Vice Chancellor and Council members with administrative tasks.
Requirements:
Qualification: Bachelor's degree in Law or related field (LL.B.) with at least one year of legal practice.
Good knowledge of legal procedures and documentation.
Strong organizational and communication skills.
Ability to handle confidential information professionally.
Responsible, reliable, and detail-oriented.
Working Hours:
Full-time, Monday to Friday, with occasional extra hours for meetings or urgent tasks.
Who Can Apply:
Qualified lawyers with at least one year of legal practice and administrative experience, preferably with experience supporting executive or academic bodies in a university setting.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Metallurgist at Newmont, you will be instrumental in optimising metallurgical performance, supporting safe and efficient processing operations, and ensuring we maximise value from every tonne processed. Your work will directly influence gold recovery, plant stability, and continual improvement across our processing systems.
As part of our team, you will
Provide technical support and troubleshooting for metallurgical and processing site operations.
Collaborate with geology, mining, maintenance, plant operations and other key operational teams to resolve operational challenges.
Contribute to process improvement initiatives and the deployment of new technologies.
Deliver accurate metallurgical analysis, reporting, plant surveys, testwork programs and plant equipment inspections.
Coach, mentor, and support colleagues and graduate metallurgists to build team capability.
Uphold Newmont’s safety values through visible leadership, Critical Control Verifications, and proactive risk management.
Identify cost‑reduction opportunities and minimise waste within the processing value chain.
Ensure compliance with the PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Safety Systems, Environmental policies, and departmental procedures.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Bachelor’s degree in Metallurgy, Mineral Processing, Chemical Engineering, or similar.
Postgraduate qualification is desirable.
A PNG Class 6 driver’s licence is required.
Site‑based metallurgical experience in a large-scale mining environment.
Strong understanding of metallurgical testwork, sample preparation, comminution, hydrometallurgy, mineral processing, and metallurgical accounting.
Experience across key processing areas including ore blending, crushing, milling, flotation, thickening,
pressure oxidation, CCD washing, CIL, AARL elution, electrowinning, lime slaking, process control and metallurgical accounting.
Demonstrated ability to design, execute, and interpret plant trials, metallurgical surveys, and laboratory testwork.
Proficiency in PI Process Book (or similar) and MS Office Suite.
Ability to analyse, interpret, and present metallurgical data effectively to stakeholders at all levels.
Proven capability in reviewing and updating technical documents, including SOPs and MSDS.
Strong verbal, written, and interpersonal communication skills.
Strong attention to detail, planning capability, and problem‑solving skills.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 22:20 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, Papua New Guinea.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will be part of a high-performing Processing team working closely with operations, geology, mining, and commercial groups. This role requires strong collaboration, continuous communication, and an ability to work alongside diverse technical specialists across the site and broader Newmont organisation. The environment is fast-paced, safety‑focused, and designed to support continuous learning and professional growth.
Why Join Newmont
Be part of a global leader in gold mining with a strong commitment to safety, sustainability, and operational excellence.
Opportunity to contribute directly to maximizing gold recovery and optimizing plant performance.
Enjoy a workplace culture that prioritises safety, inclusion, and respect for people and communities.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number
41375
before the advertised closing date: 23 February 2026.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Supervisor, Back-End Shutdowns will manage back-end shutdown activities to ensure efficient planning and execution.
Essential Duties
Coordinate and execute equipment shutdown processes
Follow compliance with safety protocols during shutdown activities
Prepare and schedule execution schedules and tasks, including identification of guide resources and onboarding planning tasks
Assist execution teams as guide for delivery of shuts during execution phases
Assess progress of shutdown tasks and supervise contractors involved in shutdown activities
Assess shutdown performance vs. plan and provide improvements
Plan and deliver front-end shutdown tasks
Prepare new employees on shutdown procedures
Execute regular inspections of front-end equipment
Responsible for assessing relevant risks, applying mitigation measures, and continuously monitoring for risks
Training & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or relevant trade qualification. Several years of experience in engineering process safety management, mechanical systems monitoring, and preventive maintenance, and safety audits in a large scale Fixed Plant Environment.
Competent ability to interact, influence and resolve conflict with various stakeholders.
Competent experience in leading and developing teams.
Competent experience in complex work Management execution
Advanced understanding of engineering process safety management, mechanical systems monitoring, and preventive maintenance, and stakeholder collaboration.
Advanced knowledge and practical proficiency in engineering standards, engineering process safety management systems, risk mitigation, data recording and reporting.
Competent knowledge of key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics for performance. Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices.
Competent understand of project cost management and financial principles.
Working Conditions
This is a FIFO role on a 21:21 roster.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Supervisor, Front-End Shutdowns will manage front-end shutdown activities to ensure efficient planning and execution.
Essential Duties
Coordinate and execute equipment shutdown processes
Follow compliance with safety protocols during shutdown activities
Prepare and schedule execution schedules and tasks, including identification of guide resources and onboarding planning tasks
Assist execution teams as guide for delivery of shuts during execution phases
Assess progress of shutdown tasks and supervise contractors involved in shutdown activities
Assess shutdown performance vs. plan and provide improvements
Plan and deliver front-end shutdown tasks
Prepare new employees on shutdown procedures
Execute regular inspections of front-end equipment
Responsible for assessing relevant risks, applying mitigation measures, and continuously monitoring for risks
Responsible for managing cost control of all shutdown related Purchase Orders and budgets for your relevant area of responsibility
Identify and enter Cancelled/Late/Emergent Work forms to ensure only critical tasks are included/excluded when required
Training & Experience
Bachelor’s degree in engineering, or relevant trade qualification. Several years of experience in engineering process safety management, mechanical systems monitoring, and preventive maintenance, and safety audits in a large scale fixed plant environment.
Competent ability to interact, influence and resolve conflict with various stakeholders.
Competent experience in leading and developing teams. Competent experience in complex work Management execution.
Advanced understanding of engineering process safety management, mechanical systems monitoring, and preventive maintenance, and stakeholder collaboration.
Advanced knowledge and practical proficiency in engineering standards, engineering process safety management systems, risk mitigation, data recording and reporting.
Competent knowledge of key performance indicators (KPIs) and metrics for performance. Competent knowledge of health, safety, environment and sustainability regulations and practices.
Competent understand of project cost management and financial principles.

This is a FIFO role on a 21:21 roster.

jobs.description:
Build a Legacy: Lead transformative projects shaping the future of Port Moresby.
Grow Your Career in a dynamic urban environment.
Join a passionate team dedicated to a stronger, more vibrant capital.
NC Salary Grade:
NC.06
Location:
NCDC City Hall, Waigani, National Capital District
Reporting to:
Senior Accounts Officer
About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
Accounts Officer
executes bank reconciliation functions between bank statements and cash book registries to ensure accurate and reliable financial records for NCDC. The role involves verifying transactions, reconciling accounts, maintaining documentation, and collaborating with internal teams to ensure compliance with financial procedures. Working within the Management Accounting Branch under the guidance of the Senior Accounts Officer, the position supports timely, accurate, and auditable financial operations.
Role Purpose
The purpose of the Accounts Officer is to ensure the integrity, accuracy, and compliance of NCDC’s financial records through effective reconciliation of bank and cash book accounts. This is achieved by identifying and resolving discrepancies, maintaining proper documentation, coordinating with internal and external auditors, and supporting financial reporting. The role contributes to transparent financial management, regulatory compliance, and sound accounting practices across the organisation.
Key Responsibilities
Perform regular bank reconciliations between bank statements and cash book registries, ensuring all transactions are accurately recorded and discrepancies promptly investigated and resolved.
Maintain complete and accurate financial records, prepare reconciliation reports, and liaise with internal teams and auditors to support compliance and audit requirements.
Identify opportunities for process improvements, adhere to financial procedures, ensure confidentiality, and perform additional duties as directed to support the Management Accounting Branch’s operations and objectives.
Education & Qualifications
Minimum Grade 12 and a Diploma in Accounting, however a Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, will be more highly considered.
Membership with a professional accounting body desirable, but not essential.
Skills & Knowledge
If not already held, to acquire a knowledge of Laws including (but not limited to): Public Finance Management Act (1995), Public Money Management Regularization Act (2017), National Procurement Act (2018), Public Service (Management) Act (2014), National Capital District Commission Act (2001) and their amendments.
Proven knowledge of financial and accounting practises, particularly financial reconciliations to bank statements, auditing standards, laws and regulations.
Knowledge and use of accounting software, with a preference for AddPac
Knowledge and experience of filing and financial records management

About the National Capital District Commission (NCDC)
The National Capital District Commission (NCDC) is the statutory authority responsible for governing and managing Papua New Guinea’s capital city, Port Moresby.
Unlike other parts of PNG that fall under provincial administrations, Port Moresby sits within a unique administrative area – the National Capital District (NCD) established under its own Act of Parliament. The NCDC is mandated to plan, manage, regulate and shape the capital city on behalf of its residents, communities, and the nation as a whole.
As the gateway to Papua New Guinea, Port Moresby plays a critical national role. The NCDC’s responsibilities extend beyond routine municipal services to include city-wide planning, regulation, infrastructure coordination, social development, and institutional reform in a rapidly growing and complex urban environment.
About the Role
The
MSME Training Officer – Innovation Development
is a specialised position within the National Capital District Commission (NCDC), responsible for a wide range of operational and strategic activities, including identifying emerging market opportunities in non-traditional sectors and designing tailored training programs for small businesses. The role involves significant fieldwork and stakeholder engagement, requiring the officer to build partnerships with technology providers, NGOs, and government agencies to facilitate the adoption of digital tools like e-commerce and mobile payment systems. Additionally, the position demands a high level of accountability in monitoring program outcomes and maintaining a results-oriented branch culture focused on NCDC’s core values of professionalism and productivity.
Role Purpose
The primary purpose of this role is to
foster innovation
within the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprise (MSME) sector by introducing new business models and supporting the integration of technologies that enhance performance. It specifically focuses on helping businesses—particularly those within the
informal economy
—to diversify their operations and access regional and international e-markets through digital literacy and innovative strategies. By driving the transition toward sustainable and adaptive business practices, the role aims to build resilient enterprises that serve as key drivers for
local economic growth
in Port Moresby. Ultimately, the position exists to bridge the gap between traditional business methods and modern, global best practices, ensuring MSMEs can thrive in a digital economy despite resource constraints.
Key Responsibilities
Driving Innovation and Technology Adoption: Identify market opportunities, introduce innovative business models, and facilitate the adoption of digital tools and technologies to enhance MSME operations and market access.
Capacity Building and Stakeholder Collaboration: Design and deliver tailored training programs, establish mentorship networks, and build partnerships with key stakeholders to support MSME innovation and sustainable growth.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting: Track and assess the outcomes of innovation initiatives, gather feedback to improve programs, and prepare detailed reports showcasing the impact on MSMEs and local economic development.
Education & Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in Business Innovation, Entrepreneurship, Marketing, Business Administration, or a related field.
Additional certifications or training in innovation management, market research, or technology adoption are highly desirable.
Strong understanding of MSME development, market trends, and innovative business practices.
Skills & Knowledge
MSME Development and Operations: In-depth understanding of the challenges, opportunities, and dynamics faced by MSMEs, particularly in informal economies and developing country settings.
Innovation and Business Model Design: Knowledge of innovative business models and strategies, including those successfully implemented in other developing countries, to support MSME diversification and growth.
Digital Tools and E-Market Access: Familiarity with digital tools such as e-commerce platforms, mobile payment systems, and digital marketing technologies that enhance business operations and enable market access.
Training Program Design and Deliver: Expertise in designing and delivering effective training programs tailored to the needs of MSMEs, incorporating principles of adult learning and practical application.
Economic Development and Local Context: Strong understanding of local economic conditions, the role of MSMEs in driving economic growth, and the unique challenges of working in resource-limited environments.
Market Linkages and Value Chain: Knowledge of strategies to connect MSMEs with local, regional, and global value chains, enabling them to access larger markets and achieve sustainable growth.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting: Proficiency in tools and methods for tracking the outcomes of innovation initiatives, assessing program effectiveness, and reporting results to stakeholders.
Training and Facilitation Skills: Ability to design, deliver, and facilitate engaging training programs tailored to diverse MSME audiences, including those with limited literacy or technical knowledge.
Innovation and Problem-Solving Skill: Capacity to identify market opportunities, develop innovative business strategies, and implement creative solutions to challenges faced by MSMEs.
Digital Literacy and Technology Skills: Proficiency in using and teaching digital tools such as e-commerce platforms, mobile payment systems, and digital marketing technologies to MSMEs.
Communication and Stakeholder Engagement Skills: Strong verbal and written communication skills to collaborate with diverse stakeholders, build partnerships, and convey complex concepts in simple, accessible terms.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting Skills: Competence in tracking program outcomes, analysing feedback, and preparing detailed reports to demonstrate the impact of innovation initiatives.
Project and Time Management Skills: Ability to manage multiple projects, coordinate logistics, and meet deadlines while maintaining a high standard of work in a dynamic environment.
Networking and Relationship-Building Skills: Capacity to establish and maintain productive relationships with government agencies, NGOs, funding partners, technology providers, and industry leaders to support MSME innovation.
Dedication: Strong dedication to the advancement of NCDC, its goals, vision, and the development of Port Moresby.
Work Experience
2–4 years of experience in business development, innovation management, or market research, preferably within the MSME sector.
Proven experience in identifying market gaps and implementing innovative solutions to support business growth.
Experience in facilitating the adoption of new technologies and digital tools to improve business efficiency and competitiveness.

This role offers a unique opportunity to influence how data shapes the future of Papua New Guinea’s capital city. You will work at the centre of urban development, infrastructure planning, and service delivery—contributing to projects that leave a lasting legacy for Port Moresby.

provides strategic and operational leadership of the Commission’s geospatial and spatial data functions. The role ensures accurate, integrated, and accessible spatial data supports urban planning, infrastructure development, service delivery, and informed decision-making across all NCDC directorates.
Leading a specialised GIS team, this position acts as the key link between City Data services and internal branches, translating operational and policy needs into practical, high-quality spatial data solutions aligned with NCDC’s strategic objectives.
Role Purpose
The Manager – City Data leads the Commission’s geospatial operations to ensure reliable spatial data underpins planning, infrastructure, asset management, and service delivery across the NCDC.
The role oversees the development, maintenance, and governance of key spatial datasets and systems, supports internal branches with tailored GIS solutions, and promotes a culture of data excellence, collaboration, and continuous improvement across the organisation.
Key Responsibilities
Provide strategic oversight of NCDC’s GIS and spatial data systems
Manage daily operations of the City Data Branch and lead a multidisciplinary GIS team
Develop and maintain enterprise geodatabases and spatial data standards
Deliver mapping, spatial analysis, and data solutions to support planning and service delivery
Coordinate GIS activities across branches and manage vendor and software relationships
Lead GIS-related planning, budgeting, and project delivery
Work closely with IT to integrate GIS with other city systems
Support staff and internal users through training and technical guidance
Contribute to GIS governance, policies, and standards
Education & Qualifications
Minimum:
Bachelor’s Degree in Geographic Information Systems (GIS), Cartography, Physical Science, Geography, Surveying, or a related discipline from a recognised institution
Preferred:
Bachelor’s Degree plus postgraduate qualifications, certifications, or a Master’s in GIS, Urban Planning, Spatial Sciences, or Geospatial Engineering
Valid Driver’s Licence (Class 3) – advantageous
Skills & Knowledge
Strong knowledge of GIS principles, spatial data management, and urban planning applications
Proficiency in GIS platforms such as ArcGIS, QGIS, or equivalent
Experience developing and managing enterprise geodatabases and spatial datasets
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
Ability to lead, mentor, and manage technical teams
Excellent written and verbal communication skills
Proven stakeholder engagement and cross-branch collaboration skills
Understanding of relevant legislation including the Physical Planning Act, Land Act, and NCDC Act
Commitment to NCDC’s vision and the development of Port Moresby
Work Experience

in GIS or spatial data management

Demonstrated experience managing enterprise GIS systems and spatial data infrastructure

Here you’ll make a difference
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organization, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods. Although not limited to one project, Save the Children anticipates that the ARoB Protection Coordinator will largely focus on the “Together for Safe Families” project, a four-year, DFAT-funded project implemented from August 2025 to July 2029 in the province of East Sepik and in the Autonomous Region of Bougainville (ARoB).
Here your skills will be valued
Role Purpose
Reporting to the Field Manager in the respective province, with a technical reporting line to the project lead, the ARoB Protection Coordinator will lead the implementation of all activities in his/her assigned province or region. This role will focus on coordinating and overseeing all project activities at the provincial/regional level, ensuring effective implementation, stakeholder engagement, and alignment with Save the Children, ARoB, and Government of PNG national objectives.
Key Areas of Accountability
Program Management and Delivery
Oversee the implementation of all project activities in the assigned province/region, ensuring project delivery that is implemented on time, within budget, and with quality.
Monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) for project and activity delivery; address any bottlenecks at the provincial/regional level; and keep the national project lead informed.
Ensure that delivery of all activities is in line with the project design and implementation approaches and strategies as guided by the technical teams.
Ensure timely and accurate reporting on project activities, including financial and narrative reports, and input of data and information into donor reports. Help maintain organized and accessible electronic files with the rest of the project locations.
Develop/refine provincial/regional implementation and procurement plans, ensuring alignment with national roll-out strategies and implementation plans.
Support the MEAL team in data collection and collation as needed, and any post-distribution monitoring (PDM) activities in the province
Contribute to the analysis of project data and the development of recommendations for improving project performance at the provincial level.
Support the project lead and Field Manager to identify, communicate, and plan mitigations against any risks arising in the province which may impact project implementation.
Team Management
Manage the performance and development of the Child Protection Officers in coordination with the Field Manager, Project Lead, and People & Culture.
Identify capacity-building needs for team members in line with the project lead and technical teams. Coordinate training opportunities and provide mentoring and coaching support.
Facilitate regular knowledge sharing and peer-to-peer learning within the province and with the other province implementing the project.
Ensure the compliance of all team members with Save the Children's policies, procedures, and donor requirements, including the completion of all mandatory trainings.
Budget and Financial
Oversee all approved activities, procurements, and payments that are specifically related to the project in that province.
Ensure activities are planned and implemented within the approved donor budget lines and rapidly communicate any pending challenges or risks to program expenditures.
May serve as bank signatory as requested.
External Stakeholder Engagement and Coordination
Support the Field Manager in engaging with key stakeholders at the provincial level, in particular those that are specifically linked with project implementation. Ensure that the team is maintaining positive relationships with stakeholders at the district and ward levels.
Represent Save the Children in relevant coordination meetings and forums at the provincial/regional level as requested by the Field Manager.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.
Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.
Work according to any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.

Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s
Child Safeguarding Policy
,
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.
Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behavior towards children in private and professional life.
Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.
Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.
Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.
Health, safety, security and risk management
Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training. Act safely at all times.
Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.
All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.
At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.

The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades &  Associates, primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private university-level Institution over the last thirty-four years. It was elevated as a University in January 2017 and offers its own degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies, and Information Technology.
Today, we are one of the largest business schools in the country and continue to grow into the future. These successes are the fruits of our dedicated team members’ commitment to making a
difference in Papua New Guinea through their efforts in helping educate fellow citizens.
The University has been affiliated with the Southern Cross University (SCU) of Australia since 1999
and offers its degree programmes in Accounting, Business, and Information Technology. The
affiliation with Southern Cross University has made IBS the first and only Institution to offer
internationally recognised Bachelor programmes face-to-face in Papua New Guinea.
We strive to be the pioneer institution for business education in PNG. Some of our accomplishments to date are listed below:
Only educational Institution to operate a Career Centre.
Only the organisation has a “Centre of Excellence” for Leadership & Management Development.
Only private University established as per the decision of NEC and Gazettal.
Only private Institution to hold the status of “Study Centre – for the University of Papua New Guinea.” Till 2016, for 22 years.
Examination Centre for the majority of Australian & NZ Universities.
Test Centre for ICDL, CISCO, Pearson VUE & Prometric.
Established partnerships with Oracle Academy, Red Hat Academy, and the All-India Management Association (AIMA), among others.
To bridge the gap between academia and industry, facilitated Memoranda of Understanding with organisations such as BSP, Telikom, CPL, Vodafone, Women’s Micro Bank, Theodist, Barlow Industries, and CEFI.
First, publish bi-annual Journal of Business & Research in Papua New Guinea.
Accredited professional bodies in PNG & Australia and ISO 9001:2015 certified University.
As a private tertiary institution, our survival and growth depend heavily on high-quality teaching,
learning, and impactful research that strengthens our reputation and attracts students and
partners. The role of the Head of Research needs to be modern, innovative, and strategically
positioned.
Position Overview:
The sole purpose of this role is to ensure that student data is correctly navigated and entered into the student management system. Guarantee that all student records are updated.
Key Responsibilities:
Screening of applications
Quality check and ensuring that all applications with necessary document have met the SCU requirement
Ensuring student data is appropriate and applicable for correct input into the student management system (ERP Academia) and create invoices accordingly.
Assisting in the institution’s organized activities
Engaged in orientation of students as well as product knowledge reviews
Ensuring student Data for Southern Cross University is accurate and updated
Qualifications
(1) Education:
Preferably a diploma or degree in any business field, Certificate II, III or IV in any business or ICT field
(2) Skills and Abilities:
Must have a minimum of 1 to 2 or more years of work experience in student administration at a Higher Educational Institution or related field.
Must have good communication skills
Must be computer literate and have a good knowledge on Microsoft Applications
Have good customer service skills
Must have adequate knowledge and Skills on CRM and SMS Software and ERP Academia
Working Conditions
You are required to work from 8:00a.m to 5:00p.m Mondays to Fridays and when require by the Team Leader or SCU Coordinator on weekends at IBSUniversity 11mile Campus. You are allowed to have an hour of lunch either 12:00noon to 1:00p.m or 1:00p.m to 2:00 p.m. Transportation to and from work is provided at your nearest Bus Station. In addition you are eligible for your annual leave whilst reaching one year of service at IBSUniversity and 10 days of sick leave.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position will provide support to the Senior Geologist – Database & GIS in managing all data and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) files emanating from the exploration teams activities.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Manage geological databases, validate weekly field and drill data, and perform QA/QC checks.
Compile reports and create maps, tables, and 3D geological models for presentations and interpretation.
Prepare internal and statutory reports, forecasts, and SOPs within strict deadlines.
Monitor drilling productivity, oversee sample submissions, and ensure accurate core logging and data processing.
Review historical data, update geological interpretations, and assist in target ranking.
Participate in planning exploration programs and conduct technical reviews with senior geologists.
Promote and enforce a safe work environment and adherence to HSE standards.
Ensure drilling and sampling are conducted safely and competently.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Bachelor’s Degree in Geology (Preferable), Geophysics or Geoscience or Geographic Information Systems (GIS).
5+ years relevant exploration, mining or GIS work experience essential.
Computer proficiency in MS Office suite, including Access and SQL Database systems software. Proficiency in GIS software. The ability to analyse numerical and graphical data, including experience with 3D modelling software.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble-shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Summary
We are seeking a skilled and detail-oriented Architectural Draftsman to join our team. The Architectural Draftsman will be crucial in assisting architects and engineers in creating detailed drawings and plans for various architectural projects. The ideal candidate should have strong technical skills, excellent knowledge of architectural design principles, proficiency in CAD software, and 3D modeling skills. The Architectural Draftsman will collaborate closely with the design team to produce accurate and precise drawings that adhere to project specifications and standards.
Duties and Responsibilities
Create detailed architectural drawings, plans, and layouts using CAD software (e.g., AutoCAD, Revit, SketchUp).
Interpret and translate architectural concepts and sketches into accurate technical drawings.
Collaborate with architects and engineers to develop design solutions and resolve technical issues.
Ensure compliance with building codes, regulations, and industry standards in all drawings.
Incorporate revisions and modifications to drawings as directed by the design team.
Generate 3D models of architectural designs using software (e.g., SketchUp, Revit, 3ds Max).
Create realistic renderings and visualizations of architectural concepts and designs.
Collaborate with the design team to present 3D models and visualizations to clients and stakeholders.
Assist in the development of virtual reality (VR) or augmented reality (AR) experiences for architectural projects.
Prepare comprehensive documentation, including construction drawings, details, and schedules.
Generate material lists and specifications for construction projects.
Maintain accurate records of drawings, revisions, and project-related documentation.
Organize and manage digital and physical drawing files for easy retrieval.
Coordinate with internal teams, consultants, and contractors to gather necessary information for drawings.
Collaborate with project stakeholders to ensure drawings align with design intent and project requirements.
Communicate effectively with team members to clarify design specifications and resolve design conflicts.
Participate in project meetings to provide input and present drawings and 3D models as required.
Review drawings and 3D models for accuracy, completeness, and adherence to design standards.
Conduct quality checks to ensure drawings and 3D models are error-free and meet project requirements.
Stay updated with industry trends, emerging technologies, and best practices in architectural drafting and 3D modeling.
Job Requirements
Diploma or degree in Architecture, Architectural Drafting, or a related field.
Proven experience as an Architectural Draftsman or similar role.
Proficiency in CAD software, such as AutoCAD, Revit, SketchUp, or similar tools.

Knowledge of architectural design principles, building codes, and regulations.
Experience with 3D modeling software (e.g., SketchUp, Revit, 3ds Max).
Familiarity with construction materials, methods, and specifications.
Attention to detail and a high level of accuracy in drawing production.
Excellent communication and collaboration skills.

Creativity, problem-solving abilities, and a keen eye for aesthetics.

We are seeking a skilled and proactive IT Systems Administrator to manage and maintain our organization's IT infrastructure. Administer and maintain servers, networks, and system software (Windows, Linux, etc.)

Collaborate with IT team members and other departments to support business needs

Reporting to the Commercial Manager, the Finance and Accounting Manager is responsible for managing the day-to-day finance and accounting operations, including entering journals, managing accounts receivable and payable, using financial technology systems, and other finance-related administration. The Manager ensures timely reconciliation and reporting of all financial statements and prepares financial analyses for the Commercial Manager and other key stakeholders as requested; and maintains fiscal records.
