jobs.title: Program Director
jobs.description:
Program Director – Strongim Wok Long TVET
Fixed term contract up to November 2029
Based in Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
About Palladium
Palladium is a global leader in the design, development, and delivery of Positive Impact – the intentional creation of enduring social, climate and economic value.  We work with governments, businesses, and investors to help solve the world's most pressing challenges. With a team of more than 2,000 employees operating in 75-plus countries and a global network of over 35,000 experts, we help improve economies, societies, the environment, and, most importantly, people's lives.
About PNG-Australia Strongim Wok Long TVET (SWLT)
PNG–Australia Strongim Wok Long Technical and Vocational Education and Training (SWLT) is a four-year, AUD 80 million investment by the Australian Government, through the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT), to support Papua New Guinea’s (PNG) efforts to strengthen its Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) sector. Aligned with PNG’s national priority to build an educated and skilled workforce for resilient economic growth, SWLT aims to enhance the quality, relevance, and inclusiveness of skills development. The program focuses on supporting the Government of PNG to strengthen the national TVET system to promote quality TVET; supporting technical colleges to deliver high-quality TVET training; enhancing the diversity and employability of TVET graduates; and elevating Australia’s visible and trusted development partnership with PNG in the TVET sector.
SWLT is the primary mechanism to support PNG and Australia to deliver on commitments made under the revised Joint Statement of Intent on TVET signed at the 2024 Australia-Papua New Guinea Ministerial Forum. It also aligns with PNG’s
Higher and Technical Education Reform Act 2020
, as well as broader goals articulated in the
Australia–PNG Development Partnership Plan 2024–2029
, including locally led development, education investment, and inclusive growth.
This Opportunity
The
SWLT Program Director
leads the delivery of all aspects of the program, including strategic oversight of program objectives and team activities and delivery.
This role involves ensuring SWLT is agile and responsive to the PNG Government’s higher education reform priorities, fosters locally driven innovation, and delivers high-quality, cost-effective development outcomes in accordance with the DFAT Head Contract.
The Program Director will also support DFAT in its engagement in the TVET sector, including with key PNG Government partners and stakeholders.
The primary responsibilities of the
Program Director
can be broadly described as follows:
Program Leadership
Provide strategic leadership and advice to ensure SWLT delivers on the shared policy objectives of the Government of Australia and the Government of PNG, including as outlined in the Joint Statement of Intent on TVET, Comprehensive Strategic and Economic Partnership, PNG’s Medium Term Development Plan IV and PNG’s National Higher and Technical Education Plan 2021-2030.
Lead and be accountable for the delivery of all aspects of the program, including the achievement of end of program outcomes and intermediate outcomes, operational oversight and engagement with program partners.
Lead on deliverable outputs, including ensuring high-quality strategies, plans, reports and analyses are developed and delivered on-time and in accordance with DFAT standards and expectations.
Maintain strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including DFAT, Government of PNG, industry and other development partners / TVET investments.
Develop and maintain a good understanding of the political economy and dynamics of the TVET sector and provide timely and relevant advice to inform DFAT’s engagement in the sector.
Support coordination across Australian Government funded TVET investments, including with the Improved TVET for Employment Project and Pacific Australia Skills.
Lead by the six SWLT principles that build and support locally owned improvements in the TVET sector in all aspects of program implementation and operating culture, including: i) promoting locally driven approaches; ii) fostering flexible, iterative, adaptive and evidence based approaches; iii) ensuring the program is responsive and outcomes focussed; iv) promoting social inclusion; v) ensuring decisions are politically informed; and vi) promoting partnerships and visibility.
Oversee robust operational compliance mechanisms, ensuring adherence to all relevant policies, processes, and legislations to maintain the program’s integrity and operational excellence. This includes financial management, procurement, and fraud control.
Work with DFAT to strengthen coordination in the TVET sector, enhance program delivery, shape ways of working, propose amendments, evaluate contract performance and address any other matters that arise in line with achieving the end of program outcomes.
Oversee risk management strategies, ensuring the identification, assessment and mitigation of risks and issues to safeguard the program’s activities, performance, personnel and reputation.
Travel within PNG and internationally, as required.
Managing and Leading People
Lead and guide SWLT staff in a culture of learning and performance that promotes teamwork, collaboration, growth and a style of working that is congruent with problem-solving and adaptability.
Provide leadership to direct and indirect reports; creating an environment that will drive continuous learning and growth to achieve employee satisfaction and retention.
Motivate and foster a positive culture among staff, both formally and informally, investing time in their success and ensuring messages from DFAT and Palladium leadership are supported and clearly cascaded.
Demonstrate accessible language and communication and adapt leadership styles for different audiences to ensure messages are communicated effectively.
Support the engagement of personnel and subcontractors in line with an inclusive and diverse approach, focusing on drawing on capabilities within PNG and/or the region.
Development Priorities and Integrity
Support and uphold a commitment to environmental sustainability, such as reducing resource use and promoting climate-friendly practices.
Role model, advocate for and comply with SWLT’s gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) objectives and DFAT’s policies in all aspects of implementation.
Operate with high levels of integrity, consistent with the intent of DFAT’s Ethics, Integrity and Professional Standards Policy Manual.
Adhere to DFAT and Palladium safeguarding standards and policies and commit to prevent harm, and to promoting safe, inclusive environments, including reporting concerns appropriately.
About you
You will have:
Significant relevant work experience, preferably managing large, complex development programs, including planning, monitoring and evaluation.
Significant experience successfully managing large government-funded budgets; and highly developed financial and commercial acumen.
Demonstrated experience in building and maintaining strong collaborative relationships with senior leaders and stakeholders both internally and externally, including donors, government agencies and senior officials, and local communities.
Strong written and verbal communication skills to effectively develop and write reports and undertake presentations for diverse audiences, including DFAT, partner organisations and the broader development community.
Ability to rapidly analyse program risks and challenges, assess performance and identify areas for improvement.
Understand compliance requirements and risk management practices to ensure programs meet DFAT’s standards and mitigate potential risks.
Strong leadership, coaching and mentoring skills, and prior experience leading effective teams.
Demonstrated commitment to the principles of locally-led, socially inclusive, politically informed and adaptive programming.
To Apply
Please submit your application online at
https://thepalladiumgroup.com/careers
, including your CV and detailed cover letter, outlining your suitability and experience in line with the requirements of the position.
Closing date:
Close of business Friday 20 February 2026. Candidates may be interviewed on a rolling basis.
Equity, Diversity & Inclusion -
Palladium is committed to embedding equity, diversity, and inclusion into everything we do. We welcome applications from all sections of society and actively encourage diversity to drive innovation, creativity, success and good practice. We positively welcome and seek to ensure we achieve diversity in our workforce; and that all job applicants and employees receive equal and fair treatment regardless of their background or personal characteristics. These include: (but are not limited to) socio-economic background, age, race, gender identity and expression, religion, ethnicity, sexual orientation, disability, nationality, veteran, marital or Indigenous status.
Should you require any adjustments or accommodations to be made due to a disability or you are a neurodivergent individual or for any other circumstance, please email our team at
[email protected]
and we will be in touch to discuss.
Safeguarding -
We define Safeguarding as “the preventative action taken by Palladium to protect our people, clients and the communities we work with from harm”. We are committed to ensuring that all children and adults who come into contact with Palladium are treated with respect and are free from abuse. All successful candidates will be subject to an enhanced selection process including safeguarding-focused interviews and a rigorous due diligence process.

Coordinator – Clinical Support & Case Management
to join the 1-Tok Kaunselin Helpim Lain, or our national 24/7 counselling, information, and referral service.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Coordinator – Clinical Support and Case Management provides specialist clinical leadership and case management oversight for the 1-Tok Kaunselin Helpim Lain, a national 24/7 counselling, information, and referral service supporting adolescents and adult survivors of gender-based violence and children in need of care and protection.
The role is responsible for strengthening the quality, safety, and consistency of counselling and case management practice across the helpline. Working closely with the Helpline Service Manager and counsellors, the Coordinator ensures trauma-informed, survivor-centred, and child-centred approaches are consistently applied, particularly in complex and high-risk cases. The position plays a key role in mentoring staff, supporting reflective practice, and promoting clinical excellence and safeguarding compliance.
Clinical Leadership & Case Management
Provide clinical oversight and coordination of counselling and case management services delivered through the helpline.
Support the management of complex and high-risk cases, including GBV, child protection, and safeguarding concerns, ensuring appropriate risk assessment, safety planning, escalation, and referrals.
Review case files and counselling records to ensure quality, consistency, and compliance with minimum standards and professional practice.
Provide timely clinical advice and guidance to helpline counsellors to  improve of the counselling, case management and documentation
Ensure survivor-centred, child-centred, and trauma-informed practices are embedded across all case management processes.
Staff Support, Mentoring & Practice Development
Provide regular clinical supervision, coaching, and case consultations to helpline counsellors and case workers.
Promote reflective practice and support staff wellbeing, particularly in managing secondary trauma and high-stress situations.
Contribute to the design and delivery of internal learning and development activities related to counselling, GBV, child protection, and safeguarding.
Support onboarding and mentoring of new counsellors and interns, ensuring they understand clinical standards, protocols, and referral pathways.
Quality Assurance & Safeguarding
Support the implementation and consistent application of the 1-Tok Kaunselin Helpim Lain Minimum Standards, Operational Parameters, and Guidance.
Monitor clinical quality, identify practice gaps, and recommend improvements to strengthen service delivery.
Ensure safeguarding principles are integrated into all counselling and case management activities.
Escalate safeguarding concerns and critical incidents to the SMT in line with organisational procedures.
Referral Pathways & Coordination
Support effective coordination with internal teams and external service providers to ensure safe, timely, and appropriate referrals.
Maintain up-to-date knowledge of referral pathways and services available to survivors and children.
Contribute to strengthening partnerships through good communication and consistent application of referral protocols.
Data, Documentation & Reporting
Support accurate and timely case documentation in client management systems.
Contribute to analysis of case trends and service data to inform practice improvement and learning.
Provide clinical input into reports, reviews, and learning briefs as required by the Helpline Service Manager.
Monir quality of the documentation and provide ongoing mentoring support to improve the quality.

Demonstrated experience managing complex and high-risk cases.
Strong understanding of trauma-informed, survivor-centred, and child-centred practice.
Sound knowledge of GBV dynamics, child protection systems, and safeguarding principles.
Experience providing clinical supervision, mentoring, or practice support to staff is highly desirable.
Experience using client management systems and case documentation tools.

Strong clinical judgement and ethical decision-making skills.
Ability to support staff working in high-pressure and emotionally demanding environments.

High level of professionalism, confidentiality, and integrity.

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Technician,
Geothermal Drilling
, you will play a vital role in supporting safe, efficient, and high‑quality technical drilling activities within Lihir’s unique high‑temperature geothermal environment.
Your work will directly contribute to the integrity of drilling programs, the reliability of geotechnical and geothermal monitoring systems, and the ongoing safety of mine operations. By applying strong field capability, sound judgement, and a commitment to safety, you will help ensure that technical drilling activities are executed to the highest operational standards.
As part of our team, you will
Ensure full compliance with all HSE requirements, policies, and procedures, including Fitness for Work standards.
Carry out HSE‑related tasks only when hazards, risks, and controls are clearly understood and agreed with your supervisor.
Identify, manage, and escalate geothermal hazards such as high temperatures, steam, gas, and unstable ground conditions.
Work collaboratively with drilling contractors, technical teams, and operational personnel to support safe and productive outcomes.
Promote a positive safety culture through communication, coaching, and active field engagement.
Lead the installation, monitoring, and data collection of geotechnical and geothermal instrumentation across the open pit.
Contribute to the planning and execution of all mine technical drilling programs.
Support geohazard awareness and training initiatives for operational and technical teams.
Conduct preventative maintenance inspections on geothermal wells and monitoring equipment, including steam relief wells.
Provide technical field support to diamond drilling activities to ensure drilling integrity, data quality, and compliance with geothermal controls.
Identify opportunities to reduce costs and eliminate waste while maintaining safety and operational standards.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Minimum Grade 12 education.
Class 6 PNG Driver’s Licence.
Minimum 1 year experience in a mining or technical services role.
Ability to use software applications and data systems relevant to drilling and geothermal monitoring.
Competency in Microsoft Word and Excel for data entry, reporting, and basic analysis.
Strong communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in multicultural teams.
Demonstrated commitment to safety, attention to detail, and sound problem‑solving capability.
Ability to work independently while maintaining alignment with Supervisor direction.
Desirable
Diploma in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or similar technical qualification.
Familiarity with geothermal instrumentation, drilling equipment, and monitoring systems.
Experience working within the PNG Mine Safety Act and Newcrest/Newmont Safety Management Systems.
Your work environment
This position is based at the Lihir Gold Operation and operates on a 20:20 FIFO roster (days only).
You will enjoy the opportunity to work with a diverse range of people while benefiting from a roster that supports strong work–life balance. Employees are accommodated in a secure and comfortable camp, featuring air‑conditioned, en‑suited rooms equipped with a mini‑fridge, TV, and Wi‑Fi. Healthy and varied meal options are provided at the site mess, and the wet mess offers a relaxed social space to unwind with a game of pool or darts after shift. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and an annual incentive program, supporting both professional and personal wellbeing.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Supervisor, Processing Services and will be responsible for the day-to-day operation of the:
mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system.
concrete batching plant and agitator trucks
pastefill binder preparation plant
The Processing Services division operates on a continuous shift roster operating on both day and night shift.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Perform the day-to-day operation of the:
mobile crushing and screening plant, conveying and stacking system.
concrete batching plant and surface agitator trucks
pastefill binder preparation plant
Effectively operate and maintain mobile equipment including Light Vehicle, Front End Loader, Excavator, telehandler and forklift according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems
Operate fixed plant equipment including jaw and cone crushers, screening plant, concrete batching plant, binder preparation plant, and cement offloading facility according to all K92 Operation & Maintenance procedures and fault reporting systems.
Monitor equipment and systems to ensure correct and safe operation.
Ensure quality of material being crushed, batched and prepared meets the correct quality standards by taking regular samples
Perform minor maintenance activities on all equipment and provide input and assistance maintenance personnel as needed.
Perform clean-up and housekeeping to ensure a safe, clean and productive work area.
Conduct machinery inspections throughout to ensure all systems are functioning properly.
Perform daily safety prestart maintenance checks.
Ensure all K92 safety standards, policies & procedures are always adhered to
Ensure that adequate DUTY OF CARE is exercised in all aspects of work activities.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Grade 10 Qualification or Trade Technical qualifications.
Loader and excavator licences and relevant experience (essential)
Valid PNG Class 3 and Class 6 licence
Forklift, telehandler licences (desirable)
Five (5) or more years relevant work experience
Experience with operation and maintenance of mobile crushing equipment including but not limited to jaw crushers, cone crushers, screens, conveyors and stackers
Experience with concrete batching plant operations.
High risk work certificates including, Working at Heights, Confined Space Entry, Equipment Isolation
Ability to work shift work
Able to communicate effectively at all levels, with good written communication skills.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.description:
Storeman
(The ones who get it right the first time)
Location: Port Moresby
PNG Motors operates a national parts network that keeps our branches, dealers, and workshops running. Behind every vehicle sold and every service job completed is a warehouse operation that has to work — accurately, safely, and on time.
This role exists because parts accuracy and safety are non-negotiable. A Storeman at PNG Motors plays a critical role in making sure the right parts get to the right place, without putting people, vehicles, or stock at risk.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for receiving, storing, controlling, and dispatching automotive parts within the National Parts Distribution Centre. That starts with checking incoming deliveries against supplier documents, inspecting for damage, and confirming quantities and part numbers before stock is accepted.
You’ll accurately bin and label parts, maintain an orderly warehouse layout, and pick, pack, and dispatch parts for PNG Motors branches and sub-dealers according to picking slips and delivery schedules. Handling and packaging must be done properly to prevent damage and injuries.
You’ll keep stock records up to date in the computer system, assist with cycle counts and stocktakes, and help investigate variances when they occur. You’ll also support dealer and workshop teams by locating and issuing parts promptly and safely.
Warehouse safety is a core part of the role. You’ll keep aisles, racking, and emergency exits clear, follow all housekeeping standards, and operate material-handling equipment such as pallet jacks or forklifts (where licensed) in line with procedures and legal requirements. Any hazards, near misses, or incidents must be reported immediately.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone who is reliable, safety-conscious, and detail-oriented. You don’t rush, you don’t cut corners, and you understand that accuracy matters.
Warehouse, parts, or automotive experience is an advantage, but not essential. What matters most is your attitude — willingness to learn, follow instructions, work as part of a team, and take responsibility for safety and accuracy.
If you say stock is checked — it is.
If a load is heavy — you lift it properly or get help.
If something looks unsafe — you report it.
Safety Expectations
Safety is not optional at PNG Motors. You’ll be expected to comply with all company safety policies, standard operating procedures, and PPE requirements at all times. You’ll use correct manual-handling techniques, keep work areas tidy, and cooperate with safety inspections, audits, and training.
Skills and Qualifications
You’ll ideally have completed Grade 12. A certificate in warehousing, logistics, or occupational health and safety is an advantage. You’ll need basic computer skills, the ability to read part numbers and delivery documents accurately, and basic maths skills for counting and reconciliation. You must be physically fit to work safely in a busy warehouse environment.
Reporting and Working Conditions
You’ll report to the Warehouse OIC or National Parts Manager and work primarily in the National Parts Distribution Centre. The role involves regular lifting, use of material-handling equipment, and PPE. Overtime or weekend work may be required during peak periods.
Working Hours
Monday to Friday:
8:00am – 5:00pm
Saturday:
8:00am – 12:00pm
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is not a short-term operation. We’re a national business with strong brands, proper systems, and a long-term commitment to Papua New Guinea. Our parts operation supports dealerships across
Port Moresby, Lae, Kokopo, Mount Hagen, and Kimbe
, and good Storemen are a critical part of that system.
If you want a hands-on role where reliability, safety, and consistency matter — this is it.

About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Engineer, Maintenance will provide mechanical engineering support for safe and efficient plant operations by delivering fit for purpose designs, driving reliability and delivering cost effective maintenance and improvement projects.
Essential Duties
Provide Mechanical Engineering support to the site’s production and maintenance teams.
Drive continuous improvement initiatives to improve reliability, reduce downtime, and lower lifecycle costs.
Undertake Mechanical design tasks from concepts through to execution.
Delivering OPEX projects within budget and time constraints. This includes conducting engineering trials on assets to achieve extended life.
Participating in CAPEX projects as part of a stakeholder.
Monitor plant performance metrics and collate engineering reports.
Analysing losses and conducting investigations using Root Cause Failure Analysis (RCFA) standards.
Assessing criticality of assets and developing, recommending, and implementing strategies for improving equipment reliability.
Champion Change through Management of Change (MOC).
Mentor and provide technical guidance to tradesmen, planners and junior/ graduate engineers.
Working collaboratively with personnel across all business units.
Training & Experience
A bachelor’s degree in mechanical engineering, or related fields.
Registered IEPNG member would be an advantage
Project and Asset management Experience
At least 5 years of experience in mining or related industry
Knowledge of Fixed Plant systems including crushers, conveyors, grinding mills, flotation, tanks & tailings.
Ability to provide mechanical engineering support to Fixed Plant Assets. Must have CMMS experience - preferably SAP.
Have practical understanding of crushers, conveyors, grinding mills, flotation, tanks, and tailings systems.
Effective organisation and planning skills
High attention to detail and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work under less supervision
Mechanically minded, self-motivated, result driven individual with excellent written and verbal communication skills.

New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.

Reporting to the Superintendent – Metallurgy, you will be responsible for the development, implementation, and monitoring of metallurgical systems across the Porgera process plant. This includes leading technical projects, supporting plant performance, and mentoring the metallurgy team.
Support production, recovery, utilization, and cost targets in collaboration with Metallurgy and Operations Superintendents
Oversee and optimize plant operations including Crushing, Grinding, Flotation, Pressure Oxidation (4 autoclaves) refinery, and Oxygen Plants
Provide technical guidance and mentoring to metallurgists and operational staff
Drive continuous improvement through performance analysis, troubleshooting, and process optimization
Lead and execute capital and improvement projects using formal project management systems
Contribute to change management processes and ensure alignment with operational priorities

POSITION TITLE:
RADIO OPERATOR – JIWAKA
CONTEXT:
Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Taric, Bougainville, Gulf Province and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in Lae, Jiwaka and Highlands.
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE POSITION:
Operating means of communication in accordance with the MSF security protocols and rules, in order to ensure quality and confidential radio communications for the operational needs of the mission/projects.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Operating the means of communication, avoiding using any sensitive or security related information and following the MSF security rules. Ensures quality and transmission capacity of communication tools.
Ensuring that messages are well copied/passed to all people concerned and records the messages on the radio logbook.

jobs.title: Accountant
jobs.description:
Job Summary
The Group Accounting Supervisor is responsible for overseeing and coordinating accounting activities across multiple entities within the Group. This role ensures accurate financial records and reporting, compliance with statutory and internal and external requirements, timely month-end and year-end closings, and effective supervision of accounting staff. The position supports the Group Finance Manager by providing reliable financial information and maintaining strong internal controls across the Group. The position also requires hands-on involvement and the ability to step in and perform accounting officer duties when required to ensure business continuity.
Key Responsibilities
Group Accounting & Reporting

Oversee daily accounting operations for all companies within the Group.

Review and ensure accuracy of general ledger entries, journal postings, and account
reconciliations.

Prepare and review monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reports for group
consolidation.

Ensure timely month-end and year-end closing for all entities.

Assist in the preparation of consolidated financial statements and management
reports.
Compliance & Statutory Requirements

Ensure compliance with applicable accounting standards, tax regulations, and
statutory requirements.

Coordinate external audits and liaise with auditors, tax agents, and regulators.

Review tax computations, GST/VAT returns, and statutory filings before submission.

Ensure proper documentation and audit trails are maintained across all entities.
Budgeting & Analysis

Assist in annual budgeting and forecasting processes for the Group.

Monitor actual results against budgets and provide variance analysis.

Support the Finance Manager with financial analysis and cost control initiatives.
Internal Controls & Process Improvement

Implement and monitor internal control procedures across the Group.

Review accounting processes and recommend improvements for efficiency and
accuracy.

Ensure adequate coverage of duties within the accounting team and reallocate or
personally assume responsibilities during staff absences or peak periods.

Ensure consistent accounting policies and procedures are applied across all entities.
Team Supervision & Coordination

Supervise and guide accountants and finance officers within the Group.

Review work performed by subordinates and provide technical guidance and training.

Assist in performance evaluation and workload planning for the accounting team.
Other Responsibilities

Support Finance Manager on special projects and ad-hoc reporting.

Assist in system implementation, upgrades, or integration across group companies.

Perform other duties as assigned by management.
Qualifications & Requirements
Education

Bachelor’s Degree in Accounting, Finance, or related field.

Professional qualification (CPA, ACCA, CA or equivalent) is an advantage.
Experience

Minimum 5–7 years of accounting experience, preferably in general accounting

At least 2–3 years in a supervisory or senior accounting role.
Skills & Competencies

Strong knowledge of accounting standards and financial reporting.

Experience in group consolidation and multi-entity accounting is an advantage.

Proficient in accounting software (Quickbooks preferred) and Microsoft Excel.

Strong analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.

Good leadership and communication skills.

Ability to meet tight deadlines and work under pressure.

Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Moro, the Community Development Officer coordinates and supports the day-to-day delivery of Santos Foundation programs across Health, Education, Community Development, and Gender in the Southern Highlands and Gulf Provinces. This is a residential role (not FIFO) with a strong focus on Education programming and regular engagement with local communities and partners.
Key Responsibilities:
Planning, liaising, coordinating, and mobilising resources to support implementing partners delivering Health, Education, Community Development, and Gender program activities in the Southern Highlands and Gulf Provinces
Monitoring Santos Foundation’s support to Literacy Libraries
Ensuring Literacy Library activities align with Santos Foundation, Santos, and PNG Government policies, strategies, and plans
Engaging with Education sector stakeholders, particularly at the sub-national level, to align Santos Foundation programming
Ensuring timely collection, collation, and sharing of activity and partner reports with internal teams and relevant program managers
Leading the organisation and facilitation of assessments, including data collection and report preparation, to support the development of new activities in Hela Province
Maintaining accurate and up-to-date filing and records for all Santos Foundation program activities in Hela Province
Ensuring compliance with Santos health, safety, environmental, security, and HR policies while sourcing resources or delivering program activities
Actively participating in job start meetings, learning sessions, and ongoing self-learning and professional development opportunities
Complying with the Santos Management System, Delegation of Authority, and corporate governance and safety requirements
What you’ll bring:
Essential
3–5 years in the development sector, preferably in Health, Education, or Gender programs
Proven track record in project and program management, including planning, implementation, and reporting
Skilled in partner and stakeholder engagement, including networking, coordination, and relationship building
Background in early childhood teaching, assessment, and program management
Strong ability to collect, manage, and report program data accurately
Hands-on involvement in delivering Health, Education, and Gender programs, particularly in remote communities
Solid understanding of Early Childhood Education programs
Ideally a Diploma or Degree in Community Development Studies or Social Sciences from a recognised university in Papua New Guinea
Desired
Able to work independently with minimal supervision
Critical thinker, able to assess risks, identify opportunities, and solve problems
Collaborative team player, fostering productive teamwork and cooperation
Adaptable to new work environments and capable of working long hours under pressure
Diploma in Early Childhood Education from a recognised tertiary institution
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.

Reporting to the Emergency Response Supervisor, the Emergency Response Trainer is responsible for developing, delivering, and maintaining emergency response training programs tailored to mining operations. This includes preparing personnel for incidents such as fires, explosions, cave-ins, hazardous material spills, and medical emergencies. The role supports both proactive safety culture development and reactive incident readiness. The role will be responsible for transforming our ERT & volunteer ERT into a world-class, independent response unit capable of managing complex risks in a remote mining environment.

Design and update emergency response training programs based on site-specific risks, regulatory requirements, and industry best practices.

Evaluate team performance and provide feedback for improvement.

Maintain accurate records of training outcomes and certifications.

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
We are seeking a committed and safety‑focused
Barge
AB Seaman
to join our high‑performing Marine Operations team. This position plays a crucial role in supporting the safe movement, berthing, and operational readiness of our barges, ensuring that all marine activities are carried out efficiently and in full compliance with Newmont’s world‑class safety and environmental standards.
Working closely with the Marine Barge Supervisor and Barge Masters, you will contribute to the smooth running of daily operations while helping maintain the integrity of our marine assets and the wellbeing of everyone on board. This is an opportunity to be part of a team that values professionalism, teamwork, and a strong safety culture in a dynamic marine environment.

Assisting the Barge Master with safe berthing and un‑berthing operations.
Reading, understanding, and signing off on all Newmont Barge Operations SMS requirements.
Always maintaining personal and team safety, applying Zero 3 and hazard identification practices.
Conducting shift‑based inspections of all FFA and life‑saving equipment, including life buoys and buoy lights.
Performing general housekeeping on the barge, including deck washdowns and maintaining clean, hazard‑free work areas.
Reporting defects, damages, or near‑miss incidents immediately to the Barge Master.
Applying Newmont’s Safety and Environmental Protection Policies, including pollution prevention during bunkering.
Maintaining clear communication with the Barge Master and wharf rope personnel during operations.
Participating in all scheduled safety and emergency drills.
Ensuring mooring ropes are well maintained, stored correctly, and kept clear of operational areas.
Supporting weekly barge servicing, inspections, and PM maintenance activities.
Assisting with marine tasks such as wharf dredging, depth soundings, and debris removal using small workboats.
Filling in as Rope Man when required.
Managing fatigue by ensuring adequate rest before each shift.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Must have at least General Purpose Deck Rating Certificate of Competency with all valid SOLAS certificates and current seafarer medical fitness certificate.
Proven experience in a similar role within a mining or a like industry
Communicate clearly and work well within a marine operations team
Proactive, reliable, and committed to maintaining high operational standards
Can adapt to a dynamic work environment and support additional marine tasks as needed

Alignment with Newmont’s values, culture, and expectations for safe and reliable operations.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You will play a critical role in keeping Newmont’s mobile mining fleet operating safely, reliably, and efficiently. Your leadership will directly influence safety outcomes, fleet availability, cost control, and team capability, making a tangible impact on production performance and workplace culture.

Supervise daily maintenance activities to ensure optimal fleet availability and reliability and strict compliance to plan targets.
Ensure all employees, contractors, and visitors comply with site HSE standards, permit systems, and isolation requirements.
Plan and allocate work effectively, considering environmental conditions, operational risks, and resource requirements.
Lead, coach, and develop your Fleet Maintenance team, including training and upskilling leading hands.
Ensure mobile equipment is maintained to OEM specifications, statutory requirements and site equipment strategy.
Oversee maintenance administration processes, ensuring accuracy, timeliness, and compliance.
Manage maintenance budgets, monitor variances, and actively identify cost-reduction opportunities.
Support breakdown response in the field and drive component rebuild schedules to meet performance targets.
Foster a collaborative, inclusive team environment where feedback, learning, and accountability thrive.
Champion visible, proactive safety leadership and foster a culture where everyone goes home safe.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Trade Certificate in Diesel Fitting, Heavy Equipment Fitting, or Auto Electrical.
PNG Driver’s Licence (Class 6 essential).
Proven experience in a mobile maintenance environment, including supervisory responsibilities.
Extensive knowledge of Diesel Engines and Mining Fleet Equipment.
Proven experience with large-scale mining equipment, including CAT 785, 777F, 773 Trucks; Dozers (D11, D10T); Graders (16, 24); Loaders (992, 993, ); and Excavators (336)
Strong mechanical and/or auto-electrical technical capability on heavy mining equipment.
Previous CAT OEM experience highly regarded.
Solid working knowledge of SAP and CAT SIS systems (or willingness to learn).
Strong planning, execution, and problem-solving skills with a high attention to detail.
Confident communication skills with the ability to lead, influence, and resolve conflict.
Self-motivated, adaptable, and able to work autonomously in a demanding operational environment.

You’ll be part of a high-performing maintenance team operating in a dynamic, safety-focused mining environment. This role requires hands-on leadership, strong field presence, and collaboration with cross-functional stakeholders to deliver results.

jobs.description:
Position
:                                                      Sustainable Livelihoods Officer
Reports to (Supervisors)
:                           Senior Community Relations Manager
Location:
Goroka Eastern Highlands, Papua New Guinea
Country Program
:                                       WCS Papua New Guinea Program
Position Type
:                                             Full-Time
Expected travel
:                                          If/when needed to field offices or other location
Organization Background
:
The Wildlife Conservation Society (“WCS”) is a New York not-for-profit corporation founded by statute in 1895 as the New York Zoological Society. WCS saves wildlife and wild places worldwide through research, science, conservation action, education, and inspiring people to value nature. That mission is achieved through our global conservation programs (WCS currently oversees a portfolio of more than 500 conservation projects in 65 countries in Asia, Africa, Latin America, and North America, and the oceans between them) and through the management of the world’s largest system of urban wildlife parks–the Bronx Zoo; the New York Aquarium; and the Central Park, Queens, and Prospect Park Zoos (the City Zoos).
Program Overview:
WCS is the longest established international non-government conservation organisation within Papua New Guinea (PNG). At key and representative landscapes and seascapes, from the country’s coral islands to its forested highlands, WCS works with local communities and provincial, national and international partners, to sustainably manage and conserve the biodiversity and cultural values of Papua New Guinea’s wildlife and wild places. WCS PNG vision is “Gutpela sindaun, gutpela bus, gutpela solwara” (“Empowered people with healthy forests and seas”). The WCS PNG program is headquartered in Goroka. WCS PNG employs about 52 full time staff and implement and administer about 10 projects annually funded by governments and private donors.
Job Summary:
The Sustainable Livelihoods Officer will design, implement, and support community-based livelihood initiatives that strengthen household resilience while reducing pressure on biodiversity. The role focuses on developing environmentally sustainable, culturally appropriate income-generating activities in partnership with local communities, aligning livelihood outcomes with conservation goals. The position works closely with Community-Based Organizations (CBOs), customary landowners, women and youth groups, and local leaders to co-design, implement, and monitor sustainable livelihood activities. The officer will support participatory planning, community consultation, and capacity building while strengthening community ownership and long-term sustainability of interventions. The position requires travel within PNG, especially to WCS field sites in the Highlands and to the marine programme sites in New Ireland, West New Britain and Manus.
This Job Description is progressive in nature and shall be reviewed and amended from time to time to meet the current program needs.
While the position focuses on livelihoods, individuals who demonstrate an interest in leading project activities across other programmatic areas as and when required will be preferred. We are looking for a dynamic individual interested in and excited about taking on significant programmatic responsibilities beyond their existing skillsets.
Major Responsibilities:
Conduct assessments to understand livelihood needs and opportunities in partner communities
Lead implementation of nature-positive livelihood interventions through ongoing projects
Ensure livelihood interventions are inclusive and culturally appropriate.
Document impacts of livelihood interventions, including but not restricted to harvests, sales, profits, etc.
Support and conduct trainings on family business management, financial literacy, etc.
Work with partner CBOs to widen the impact of livelihood interventions
Translate scientific information into simple English and Tok Pisin to allow it to be easily understood by a variety of stakeholders, including those with low literacy skills.
Provide capacity building to local staff and partners.
Represent WCS during stakeholder/partner engagement and outreach
Other duties as directed by your supervisor.
Minimum Requirements:
Education/Credentials
A bachelor’s degree or higher qualifications in a relevant discipline. Applicants with a bachelor’s degree in other fields but with full-time professional experience in implementing livelihood projects will also be considered.
Experience
At least 2 years’ full-time, professional experience in implementing livelihood projects with an NGO or a government agency or equivalent
Strong understanding of and experience with conducting financial and business management trainings for communities
Good interpersonal skills and experience in liaising with a range of stakeholders, including traditional owners, local and state government, special interest groups and individuals regarding natural resource management issues.
Critical Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Experience in community engagement, facilitation, and participatory planning.
Experience working with Community-Based Organizations (CBOs) and customary institutions.
Strong facilitation and conflict-sensitive communication skills.
Understanding of social safeguards, inclusion, and gender-sensitive approaches.
Ability to work respectfully within diverse cultural contexts.
Excellent computer literacy & skill of MS office applications (Word/PowerPoint/internet etc.)
Good analytical and problem-solving skills
Good knowledge of written and spoken English and Tok pisin
Strong interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence
Being a self-starter with drives and initiative and able to work as a team/individual with a positive attitude and open minded
Excellent organizational and leadership skills
Excellent communication skills
Ability to work with less supervision and under pressure
Excellent multi-tasking, organized and follow-up skills
Willingness and enthusiasm for being in the field in remote locations with very basic facilities

th

Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
As Planner - Mechanical, you will provide instrumentation planning expertise to ensure maintenance work is sufficiently planned and ready for scheduling for the Fixed Plant, and Asset Management maintenance teams to execute work safely.
Essential Duties
Review and prioritise work requests/work orders, confirm scope, safety hazards, and planning requirements.
Plan work in SAP/CMMS with clear job instructions, safety analyses, OEM specs, and drawings.
Estimate resources, materials, and duration in collaboration with requesters/supervisors.Plan modular shutdowns and overhauls, including scope, risk assessment, and scheduling.
Update work orders with task lists, documentation, materials, and resource requirements.
Order materials via SAP and arrange vendor purchases or external services.
Expedite materials and adjust schedules to align with plant downtime.
Create and update ARs for BoMs, task lists, and improvements.
Hand over work orders to the scheduler and ensure readiness for execution.
Review completed work packs for improvements and submit ARs.
Ensure all approved work orders have complete information for scheduling.

Technical Diploma or Trades Certificate in Electrical Engineering, Maintenance or similar

Proficient in planning concepts and sound understanding of Work Management processes.
Proficient in English with excellent verbal and written communication skills.
Computer proficiency in the MS Office suite.
Sound planning, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.

Job Description
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
The New Porgera Limited now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mineral Resources Department as
Mine Geologist - Open Pit
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Mine Geologist (Open Pit), the Mine Geologist is responsible for collecting, interpreting, and reporting geological data to support efficient and safe mining operations. This includes grade control, ore body interpretation, and liaising with mine planning and production teams to optimize ore recovery and minimize dilution. The role plays a critical part in the short-term and long-term success of mining activities.
In this role, you will:
Conduct daily geological mapping, sampling and ore control in active open pit mining areas
Monitor ore and waste boundaries to ensure adherence to grade control plans
Assist in the design and execution of RC grade control drilling programs (e.g. Leapfrog, Vulcan).
Interpret geological data and produce models to support mine planning and forecasting
Collaborate closely with the mining, planning and processing teams to ensure proper material handling
Provide timely geological input for daily, weekly and monthly production reports
Ensure compliance with safety, environmental and regulatory standards
Participate in continuous improvement initiatives for geological processes and systems
Maintain strong stakeholder engagement with internal departments and external partners.
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Bachelor’s degree in Geology, Geoscience, or a related field
2-5 years’ experience in an open-pit and or underground mining environment
Proficiency in 3D geological modelling software (e.g., Vulcan, Leapfrog, Datamine or similar)
Familiar with RCGC drilling and QAQC sampling practices
Experience with grade control systems and reconciliation process
Exposure to resource modelling and estimation techniques
Ability to shift priorities to respond to changing requirements
Strong commitment to workplace safety and environmental standards
Previous experience in a gold mining environment
Mobilization Requirement
This is a PNG National position, a site-based role on a FIFO arrangement with a rotation of 21 days on and 14 days off. Candidates must successfully pass a pre-employment medical, including drug and alcohol screening (to be arranged only for successful candidates after the interview stage), and provide an up-to-date Police Clearance Certificate (acquired within the last 6 months). Candidates must be PNG Nationals and available to start immediately. Females are encouraged to apply.
Join Our Team as a Mine Geologist – Open Pit

Enjoy a balanced work schedule, competitive compensation, and a chance to develop your career and technical expertise in a supportive and professional environment.

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
This is an opportunity to lead where it matters most. You will be at the forefront of keeping Newmont’s Hydraulic Shovel, Excavator, drill and pump fleet operating at its best. Your leadership and technical expertise will shape high-quality rebuilds and maintenance programs that enhance equipment reliability, uphold the highest safety standards, and deliver maximum asset availability to support uninterrupted production.
As part of our team, you will
You will be at the forefront of planning, supervising, and executing rebuild and maintenance programs that make a real impact on operational reliability and safety.
Your key responsibilities will include:
Lead and coordinate the safe, efficient rebuild, repair, and preventive maintenance of Shovels, Excavators drill rigs, pumps, and associated systems.
Plan, schedule, and allocate PCR and Shutdown work work for mechanics and technicians engaged in major overhauls and rebuild programs.
Supervise rebuild activities to ensure compliance with engineering specifications, OEM standards, and quality benchmarks.
Conduct inspections in workshops and the field to verify equipment functionality, reliability, and safety compliance.
Champion safety by enforcing policies, leading risk assessments, promoting Lock-Out Tag-Out (LOTO) practices, and embedding a “stop unsafe work” culture.
Provide hands-on technical leadership in diagnosing complex mechanical, electrical, and hydraulic faults.
Manage critical spare parts inventory and coordinate with Supply Chain to ensure timely availability for rebuild activities.
Maintain accurate maintenance, labour, and parts records within the maintenance management system.
Monitor rebuild project costs and labour utilisation, identifying opportunities to improve productivity and reduce downtime.
Build a positive, high-performing team environment through coaching, recognition, and by developing and executing training plans to transfer technical skills to workforce.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
You will bring a combination of technical expertise, hands-on experience, and strong leadership skills that ensure safe, reliable, and high-quality maintenance outcomes.
Trade Certificate in Heavy Equipment, Diesel Fitting, or Maintenance Fitting.
Extensive experience in open-cut mining, including the mechanical and hydraulic rebuild of large Shovels, Excavators and drill rigs such as CAT6060, CAT6020, HIT2600, D65 & Pit Viper 231.
Hands-on experience in mobile equipment shutdowns and major overhaul programs.
Advanced knowledge of slurry and dewatering pump systems.
Proven ability to interpret OEM manuals and restore assets to zero-hour lifecycle standards.

Competence with maintenance management systems such as SAP, Ellipse, or AMT.

Strong communication skills in English; working knowledge of Tok Pisin is highly regarded.

The

is a critical support role responsible for ensuring strong financial management, compliance, and efficient operational systems for WaterAid’s East New Britain Program.
The position oversees financial and operational management for two key grants:
the
PacFresh H2O Program
in Rabaul and Pomio Districts; and
the
KIWA Initiative Grant
in Rabaul District.
Working across finance, administration, procurement, and operations, the role ensures accurate financial reporting, adherence to donor and WaterAid policies (including
GIZ and AFD procurement requirements
), and effective support to program implementation. The Finance and operations coordinator will manage internal control procedures to ensure WaterAid and donor policies and procedures are followed; support on project budget development, expenditure tracking and budget monitoring, and coordinating project audits. The position works closely with WaterAid’s East New Britain program team, local government partners, WaterAid PNG headquarters in Port Moresby, and the WaterAid regional support team in Australia.
About the Grants
The Finance and Operations Coordinator will provide support across two key grants:
Funded by GIZ, the
Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project
aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
Funded by AFD, the
Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project
aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key Performance Areas/Accountabilities
Financial Management and Compliance
Oversee day-to-day financial management of PacFresh H2O and KIWA grants, ensuring accuracy, transparency, and donor compliance.
Lead project budget development, budget conversions, reforecasting, and ongoing budget monitoring using WaterAid financial systems (including WAPS and SunSystems)
Prepare and submit timely and accurate financial reports for internal management and donors.
Manage internal control procedures to ensure compliance with WaterAid and donor financial policies.
Lead the Finance Compliance Checklist to ensure all documentation is complete before and after payment authorisation
Coordinate and support internal and external audits, including preparation of documentation and follow-up actions.
Lead quarterly project expenditure transactions review to ensure that all project expenditure is correctly coded. If there are any errors or any missing transactions must advise the Operations Manager for adjustments.
Lead the accurate monthly and quarterly cost recovery process for the projects and ensure sufficient supporting documents are attached such as payslips, payroll transactions and timesheets.
Payments, Accounting, and Systems
Support preparation and processing of payments, ensuring approvals are obtained prior to payment.
Maintain general ledgers and ensure correct coding, GST treatment, and documentation.
Upload payment journals to SunSystems weekly and payroll journals fortnightly.
Create payments via corporate online banking when required.
Ensure all payments complete required Anti-Terrorism checks.
Payroll, Statutory and Tax Obligations
Support or process payroll using Able Payroll software and ensure timely distribution of payslips.
Upload staff NCSL and Nasfund contributions in line with statutory requirements.
Remit Salary and Wages Tax (SWT) and file GST with the IRC, ensuring records are accurate and safely stored
Ensure all project staff's timesheets are signed off and maintained in safe place
Procurement and Administration
Ensure procurement processes comply with GIZ, AFD and WaterAid procurement policies.

TITLE
Grants Accountant and Compliance Coordinator

Senior Programs Manager
LOCATION
Kokopo or Rabaul, East New Britain Province
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
START DATE
END DATE
Full time

st
