Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG, guided by the National WASH Policy (2015-2030).
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Purpose of the Role
The Grants Accountant and Compliance Coordinator supports the Operations and Programs teams by coordinating the financial and compliance aspects of donor-funded grant agreements.
The role focuses on grant-level financial tracking, compliance oversight, donor requirements (including GIZ and AFD), procurement compliance, and budget monitoring, while working under the technical leadership of the Senior Grants Accountant. The position plays a key capacity-building role by leading training and induction for staff and partners on grant compliance, donor rules, and financial procedures.
Position Summary
This role is responsible for ensuring that donor-funded grants are implemented in line with approved budgets, contractual obligations, and WaterAid policies. The Grants Accountant and Compliance Coordinator acts as a focal point for grant compliance, providing hands-on support to program teams on budgeting, procurement processes, and financial reporting requirements.
The role works closely with the Senior Grants Accountant to support accurate accounting, reporting, audits, and risk management, and contributes to strengthening organisational grant management systems.
The role works closely with program teams, finance colleagues, and senior management to ensure grants are implemented efficiently, transparently, and in accordance with contractual obligations.
About the Grants
The Grant Accountant and Compliance Coordinator will provide support across two key grants:
Funded by GIZ, the
Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project
aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
Funded by AFD, the
Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project
aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.

About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Supervisor, Diamond Driller Underground and will be responsible for constructing, repairing and maintaining boilers and related tasks.
Key Accountabilities

Ensure that the sections daily work plans are executed as directed.
Competent in lifting and safe operation of workshop equipment.
Reading and understanding technical drawings and manuals.
Diagnose problems in all equipment with regular reference to equipment manuals.
Assisting supervisors with the preparation and planning of shutdowns.
Carry out equipment alignments with Dial Indicators.
Conduct accurate dimensional checks of crusher bushes, shafts or bearing clearances and recording data.
Attend to isolations required for simple tasks to major shutdowns.
Conduct general housekeeping at work area.
Identify and report safety hazards.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.

Recognized trade certificate in the Fabrication and welding or fitting and machining discipline.
5 years’ experience in relative technical area.
2 years in the Mining industry.
Sound communication & technical skills
Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, drawings, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
Sound planning and organization skills.
Able to work with minimum supervision.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination. Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE)
About the University
The Papua New Guinea University of Natural Resources and Environment (PNGUNRE) is a specialised national institution mandated to advance education, research, innovation, and community engagement in sustainable agriculture, land use, marine and environmental management, and natural resource development.
PNGUNRE operates across three campuses:
Vudal Main Campus (East New Britain Province) – home to core teaching, research, and administrative divisions
Takubar Campus (Kokopo) – host of Postgraduate Programs and the Department of Business & Economics
Popondetta Campus (Oro Province) – focused on agricultural training, community engagement, and regional development initiatives
Together, these campuses create a unique learning and working environment that integrates applied research, modern development practices, and sustainability initiatives in support of Papua New Guinea’s national development priorities.
About the Role
PNGUNRE invites applications from suitably qualified, highly organised, and professional candidates for appointment as Personal Assistant to the Vice Chancellor, based at the Vudal Campus.
This position provides high-level executive and administrative support to the Vice Chancellor and serves as a key liaison point between the Office of the Vice Chancellor, senior management, government agencies, and external stakeholders. The role requires sound judgement, discretion, confidentiality, and the ability to manage competing priorities within a fast-paced executive environment.
The successful appointee will report directly to the Vice Chancellor.
Key Responsibilities
Provide proactive, high-level secretarial and administrative support to the Vice Chancellor.
Manage the Vice Chancellor’s diary, appointments, correspondence, and travel arrangements.
Act as a primary point of contact between the Vice Chancellor, senior management, government officials, and external stakeholders.
Prepare agendas, briefing papers, minutes, presentations, and official correspondence for executive meetings.
Coordinate executive meetings, events, and official University functions.
Monitor incoming and outgoing correspondence, ensuring timely follow-up and appropriate action.
Support internal communications, record-keeping, reporting, and executive workflows.
Uphold strict confidentiality, professionalism, and high standards of customer service at all times.
Qualifications, Experience & Competency Profile
Bachelor’s degree from a recognised institution in Management, Administration, or a related discipline.
Minimum of three (3) years’ experience in an executive or senior administrative support role, preferably within a government, university, or institutional environment.
Sound knowledge of office administration, records management, and public sector or statutory processes.
High level of proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and executive office systems.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with strong organisational and time-management abilities.
Demonstrated discretion, professionalism, and the ability to work independently under pressure.
Proven experience liaising with senior executives, government officials, and external stakeholders is highly desirable.

This role offers a unique opportunity to work closely with the University’s executive leadership and contribute directly to the governance, administration, and strategic direction of PNGUNRE. jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Advisor People Training (Safety) will develop training programs, deliver training, coach, mentor and assess Newmont personnel in all aspects including but not limited to regulatory compliance on-the-job delivery, and a safe work environment.
Essential Duties
Develops training materials, delivers training and aligns with Newmont standards, Industry standards and HSE standards
Creates opportunities for people to work together to enable them to contribute to the business and learn from each other.
Deliver theory and 'on the job' training for all operators in various sections.
Communicating training plans to Team Lead and Peers
Conduct’s field observations and engagement with Operational Supervisors and Superintendents to understand the skill gap of employees and the business needs. Using that understanding to then modify training curricula to bridge the gap to ensure employees are fully developed upon completion of the training to contribute to safe production.
Drives and influences proactive safety and productive behaviors.
Sets objectives and expectations for themselves.
Ensures the recording of data into the LMS (Learning Management System) as required.
Prepares resource requests (PPE, Tools, Materials, etc) of their work area and justification for the Team Lead for review.
Actively seeks cost reduction opportunities.
Training & Experience
Minimum of 5 year’s experience in an industrial workplace.
Certificate 3 Trainer/Assessor or equivalent training in Professional Education/Training.
Subject matter expertise in OHS Training, Equipment qualifications.
Developing training materials and curricula, proficiency in Facilitation/Presentation skills and understanding of Learning Databases.
Well-developed computer skills – proficient in MS Word, excel & power-point.
Driver License PNG Class 6 and 7
Good interpersonal, oral and written communications skills in English.
Working Conditions
You’ll be part of the People team on a 21:21 roster, helping maintain regulatory compliance and a safe work environment.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
The Geotechnical Engineer will support safe and efficient mining operations by providing operational geotechnical monitoring, analysis, inspections, and technical input to identify and manage geotechnical and geothermal hazards.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Assist with ground control management, slope monitoring, data analysis, and field inspections to minimize risk to safety and production in a dynamic geothermal environment.Conduct routine geotechnical inspections of pit walls, dumps, stockpiles, harbour waste platform, and marine dumps.
Monitor slope stability using radar, prism, GNSS, and other monitoring systems.
Review and analyse monitoring data and report abnormal movement or trends.
Assist with geotechnical drilling, logging, mapping, and instrumentation programs.
Support slope reconciliation through Design, Implementation, and Verification processes.
Assist with geotechnical and geothermal risk assessments and implementation of controls.
Prepare technical reports, monitoring summaries, and presentations for stakeholders.
Support investigations into ground movement, instability, and incidents.
Provide input into short- and medium-term mine planning and operational designs.
Assist in maintaining and improving geotechnical monitoring systems and databases.
Support technical mentoring programs under guidance of senior engineers.
Actively promotes and demonstrates safe work practices and compliance with site HSE requirements.
Works collaboratively with geotechnical, mining, planning, survey, and operations teams.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Minimum of 2–4 years’ experience in open pit geotechnical engineering or related mining roles.
Experience in slope monitoring, field inspections, and geotechnical data collection.
Exposure to operational mining environments is desirable.
Sound understanding of open pit geotechnical principles and ground control practices.
Awareness of operational safety and risk management systems.
Working knowledge of PNG Mine Safety Act and Regulations.
Competency in MS Office applications.
Knowledge of slope stability monitoring and analysis software.
Basic knowledge of geological and mining modelling software (e.g., Minesight).
Familiarity with cost control systems (e.g., SAP).
Good verbal and written communication skills.
Strong analytical and problem solving abilities.
Good organisational and time management skills.
Ability to work independently and within a team environment.
Working Conditions
You’ll be part of the Geotechnical team on a 22:20 roster, requiring hands-on engagement and collaboration across disciplines.

People and Culture Manager
Position Description
Role Purpose
A member of the Senior Management Team (SMT), the People and Culture Manager (PCM) will report to the Country Director and have a matrix (functional) reporting line to the IP People & Culture Business Partner in Melbourne. The role is responsible for leading development of organisational culture and staff engagement, providing effective human resources management, administration and technology support to the Country Program. The role is responsible for all People and Culture (P&C) service delivery in country, including but not limited to setting and ensuring compliance with P&C policy and processes, recruitment, performance management processes, industrial and employee relations and operational HR services.
Key Areas of Accountability
Business Partnering
Provide quality advice on all Human Resources (HR)-related issues to the SMT and individuals, to ensure program expectations and goals are achieved.
In partnership with the Country Director, inspire and lead the development of a strong organisational culture and drive staff engagement strategies.
Manage and lead staff development and performance process, including the annual staff appraisal process through communication with managers, support for the process, training for managers, training for staff etc.
Research resources for professional development that aligns with Save the Childrn in PNG (SCiPNG) Country Strategic Plan and maintain dialogue with managers relating to recommendations made on performance appraisals.
Develop and implement an annual PNG People Plan.
Facilitate key cyclical people processes including annual performance cycle, remuneration, and talent reviews.
Work with the PNG Country Director to develop a performance culture, including ensuring robust performance processes (goal setting, reviews, improvement plans) are in place and follows
Oversee in-country recruitment and general HR Plans with each project to aid in prioritising project recruitments to avoid unnecessary delays to implementation.
Employee Relations
Review all SCiPNG policies and practices to ensure compliance with PNG employment and industrial relations laws (including compliance with PNG Common Rule Awards).
Build leadership capability to manage performance and employment related issues in a professional manner.
Develop and maintain employment-related policies and procedures and ensure their consistent application across the organisation.
Develop and maintain relationships with the Department of Labour and Department of Immigration to inform all aspects of engagement of non-citizens and compliance with the Employment Act, including the provision of accurate advice on new hires to hiring managers.
Consult with employees and managers on employee grievances and lead and advise on disciplinary matters.
Implement disciplinary procedures in accordance with SCPNG HR policies and provide advice and training to managers on performance management (poor performance) issues.
Operational HR Management
Ensure an appropriate efficient and consistent level of customer services is delivered across to all staff.
Assist project, area, and function managers in matters relating to employee relations, occupational health and safety, and staff training.
Oversee facilitation of Immigration requirements for international staff.
Ensure SCiPNG is compliant with all statutory obligations.

Joining our commercial team, the Team Lead – Contracts provides leadership and guidance to the Contracts team, ensuring high standards of contract administration, negotiation, and compliance. This role combines mentoring of team members with a strong technical focus, taking a lead role in procurement planning and market engagements under the direction of the Principal and Superintendent – Contracts. jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a
Technician Mechanical Fitter – Oxygen Plant
, you will play a key role in maintaining three oxygen plants to ensure safe, reliable, and efficient operation. You’ll apply your mechanical fitting skills to fabricate components, interpret technical drawings, troubleshoot issues, and support continuous improvement across the oxygen plant area. Safety is central to this role—you’ll follow all HSE requirements, understand hazards before starting work, and stop any unsafe activity. Working within a diverse team, you’ll contribute to production performance, uphold maintenance standards, and actively identify opportunities to reduce costs and improve work quality.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Ensure full compliance with company HSE policies, including Fitness for Work.
Strong understanding of hazard identification tools
Have experience working in Oxygen plants
Have experience with following work orders and basic work management skills
Work constructively within a diverse team and contribute positively to team outcomes.
Safely operate and maintain hand and power tools.
Demonstrate strong team behaviours—asking questions, raising issues, contributing ideas, seeking clarity, requesting feedback, and stopping unsafe work.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
You’ll thrive in this role if you bring strong mechanical fitting capability, a commitment to safe work practices, and a collaborative, proactive approach to maintenance.
Mechanical trade qualification certified to NATTB
Ability to follow procedural steps and complete practical, hands‑on tasks.
Practical judgment to solve problems or seek assistance when needed.
Willingness to learn and improve work methods through experience and observation.
Competence in mechanical fitting, fabrication, and interpreting technical drawings.
Ability to build positive working relationships across different disciplines.
Determination, persistence, and commitment to delivering productive, high‑quality work.
Alignment with Newmont’s values, culture, and expectations for safe and reliable operations.
Your Work Environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
Newmont offers a dynamic and inclusive workplace where your expertise drives real impact. You’ll have opportunities for professional growth, contribute to innovative projects, and be part of a team that values safety, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Papua New Guinea at Ridge Camp, the Operations Training Team Lead works closely with the PNG Business Unit Field Operations and Maintenance teams to ensure competency-based training and assessment are delivered in line with business priorities.
The role is the primary interface between the Manager Operations Readiness and PNG Field Trainers, with direct oversight of all training execution, logistics, and coordination across PNG operations. You will be responsible for the intake, coordination, and ongoing support of first-year apprentices in PNG.
Key Responsibilities:
Liaise with the Operations Leadership Team, Manager Operations Readiness, and the Competency-Based Training and Assessment (CBTA) team to prioritise frontline training needs for field personnel.
Lead PNG-based trainers in the implementation of CBTA across the PNG business.
Coordinate the delivery of training through in country and external training providers.
Coordinate mobilisation and group travel for PNG BU personnel undertaking out-of-country training.
Execute the intake of first-year apprentices and maintain accountability for apprentices during their institutional training year.
Work collaboratively with the CBTA team and key stakeholders to evaluate training and assessment outcomes and drive continuous improvement.
Liaise with the PNG National Apprentice and Trades Training Board (NATTB) regarding the Santos PNG Apprentice Program.
Manage and deliver training-related projects as assigned.
Administer the Learning Management System (SuccessFactors) in support of competency-based training and assessment.
Contribute to the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of Santos’ competency-based training and assessment framework.
Ensure compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and corporate governance and safety requirements.
What you’ll bring:
To be successful in this role, you will bring extensive operational experience combined with a proven background in training and competency assurance.
Essential
Minimum 10 years’ experience in oil and gas process or production operations.
At least 5 year’s experience in a training or learning delivery role.
Demonstrated experience in training and competency assurance systems, including competency-based training and assessment.
Proven experience in administration and working with Learning Management Systems, such as SuccessFactors.
Cert IV TAE40116, Cert IV TAE40122 or higher
Australian PMA 02/08 Cert III/IV or trade qualifications
Desired
Relevant Tertiary qualifications or trade background
SuccessFactors LMS or equivalent.
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB Tuesday 3 Feburary 2026.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply

There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
About the Role
As a
Technician Electrical
, you will carry out day‑to‑day electrical maintenance activities that support safe, reliable, and high‑performing operations within the Processing Department’s Oxygen Plants.
Your work ensures optimum equipment availability by taking ownership of electrical and instrumentation tasks and completing them to a high standard as directed by your Supervisor.
Key responsibilities include:
Ensuring personal and team compliance with all HSE requirements, policies, and Fitness for Work standards.
Utilize all hazard identification (PHA, JSEA, Permit to Work) tools for safe task execution
Completing electrical work in accordance with AS/NZS 3000, relevant standards, and internal procedures.
Familiar with work management and detailing work orders and updating supervisors
Executing electrical maintenance tasks to a high standard as allocated by Supervisors and leaders.
Contributing to continuous improvement by identifying electrical reliability issues and supporting strategic maintenance initiatives.
Communicating effectively with Supervisors, peers, and other teams on maintenance issues, priorities, delays, and roadblocks.
Conducting preventative maintenance inspections on plant equipment.
Upholding team behaviours such as asking questions, seeking clarity, contributing ideas, speaking up on issues, stopping unsafe work, and seeking feedback.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Recognized electrical trade certificate by NATTB
Proven experience working in a similar role preferably within the mining or a like industry
Proficient in English with excellent verbal, written communications and public speaking skills.
Proven capability in electrical maintenance and understanding of relevant standards.
Ability to apply technical knowledge using the correct tools, procedures, and safe work practices.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe work practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Work in accordance with PNG Mine Safety Act, Newmont Safety System, Safety Policies and Procedures and Environment policies and all departmental operating procedures
Alignment with Newmont’s values, culture, safety standards, and operational goals.
Working Conditions
This role is offered on a 21:21 Fly in, Fly out (FIFO) roster to Lihir Island, PNG.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of a global leader in mining that values safety, integrity, sustainability, and people. We invest in our workforce, encourage innovation, and foster a culture where everyone is empowered to contribute, learn, and grow. By joining Newmont, you’re not just taking on a role you’re building a career where your skills, ideas, and commitment help shape the future of responsible mining.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
This position reports to the Supervisor, Asset Protection and will be responsible for ensuring the safety of our growing gold site at Eastern Highlands.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Ensure asset protection and compliance with company policies, security standards, and safety regulations, including voluntary principles on security and human rights.
Monitor, inspect, and maintain security systems and conduct searches to prevent unauthorized items, theft and tampering.
Safeguard valuables and personnel through vehicle escort duties, perimeter patrols, and rapid response to emergencies or law-and-order issues.
Manage crisis situations and emergency preparedness, including fire and rescue training, arresting illegal miners, and making swift decisions during incidents.
Perform administrative and liaison duties, such as clearance of terminated employees, reporting suspicious activities, and collaborating with Community Relations on security matter
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have
Have at least 3 years or more in a mining environment but must have worked previously as police, correctional services, or military personnel or similar with no criminal record.
Possess training equivalent to Police/Correctional or Military.
PNG Drivers Licence
Strong leadership and decision-making skills.
Excellent interpersonal and negotiating skills.
Can be able to manage the safety and/or security and asset protection department.
Physically fit and healthy.
Prepare clear, concise, and accurate investigative and narrative reports
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

The Senior Mechanic specializing in Heavy Equipment is responsible for maintaining, repairing, and optimizing a wide range of heavy machinery used in construction, mining, and other industrial sectors. This role requires extensive knowledge of heavy equipment mechanics, hydraulics, and electronics, along with a commitment to safety and efficiency.

jobs.title: Civil Works/Infrastructure Engineer
jobs.description:
Summary
The Civil Works/Infrastructure Engineer is responsible for overseeing both the design and implementation of civil infrastructure projects, as well as managing surveying activities in the field. This role requires extensive fieldwork and collaboration with project teams to ensure projects are delivered with precision, quality, and integrity. The role involves the use of advanced surveying tools and technology, as well as ensuring adherence to engineering standards and regulations.
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Project Planning and Design
Develop detailed project plans, including scope, timelines, and resource allocation.
Collaborate with engineers and project managers to design civil works (roads, bridges, drainage systems, utilities).
Conduct feasibility studies and site assessments to determine project viability.
Prepare accurate engineering drawings and specifications in accordance with regulatory standards.
2. Surveying and Fieldwork
Conduct site surveys and inspections using equipment such as total stations, GPS receivers, and 3D laser scanners.
Analyze and interpret survey data to generate contour plans using Civil CAD software.
Incorporate survey data into civil infrastructure designs.
Ensure the accuracy of topography, boundaries, and measurements on-site.
3. Site Management
Oversee construction activities, ensuring compliance with project specifications and quality standards.
Coordinate with subcontractors and suppliers to facilitate smooth execution of project phases.
Conduct regular site inspections to monitor progress, address issues, and ensure project integrity.
Ensure proper implementation of survey data during construction phases.
4. Quality Assurance and Control
Ensure compliance with engineering standards, safety regulations, and quality control procedures.
Conduct material testing and maintain accurate project documentation.
Prepare progress reports and recommend corrective actions when necessary.
Document changes in project scope and manage approvals.
5. Team Collaboration and Leadership
Work closely with multidisciplinary teams to achieve project goals.
Provide guidance and mentorship to junior engineers and technical staff.
Ensure clear and effective communication among all team members and stakeholders.
Review and approve construction methods and materials for compliance.
6. Budgeting and Resource Management
Prepare and manage project budgets, ensuring efficient resource allocation.
Monitor expenditures and implement cost control measures where appropriate.
Oversee procurement processes and ensure ethical purchasing practices.
Recommend cost-saving measures while maintaining quality standards.
7. Regulatory Compliance
Ensure all projects comply with local, state, and federal regulations.
Obtain required permits and approvals from authorities.
Conduct environmental assessments as needed.
8. Problem-Solving and Decision-Making
Identify and resolve project challenges while maintaining compliance with safety and regulatory standards.
Make informed decisions regarding project modifications or design changes.
Implement risk management strategies and address safety concerns on-site.
9. Documentation and Reporting
Maintain comprehensive project documentation, including contracts, change orders, and reports.
Prepare and present progress reports to stakeholders.
Document best practices and lessons learned for continuous improvement.
10. Equipment Maintenance and Calibration
Ensure surveying equipment is maintained and calibrated for accurate data collection.
Coordinate equipment repairs and replacements as necessary.
Stay informed of technological advancements to enhance equipment performance.
Job Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or a related field.
Professional Engineer (PE) license preferred.
Minimum of 5 years of experience in civil engineering and/or surveying.
Proficiency in AutoCAD, Civil 3D, Civil CAD, and other engineering software.
Strong project management and organizational skills.
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills.
Familiarity with construction materials, methods, and surveying equipment.
Others
Working Conditions
This position involves extensive fieldwork and site visits, including travel to various project locations.
Some physical activities, such as walking long distances, climbing, or carrying equipment, may be required.
Split between office and fieldwork. Fieldwork involves outdoor site visits with varying weather and terrain.
Frequent travel to project sites, sometimes requiring overnight stays. Flexibility in travel is expected.The role is physically demanding, requiring good fitness for site work. Strong problem-solving skills and clear communication are essential.

jobs.description:
National Fleet Manager
(Not the spreadsheet-only kind — the one who knows fleets live on the road)
Location: Head Office, Port Moresby
PNG Motors is one of Papua New Guinea’s most recognised automotive groups, representing Ford, Mazda, Hyundai, Suzuki, JMC and Joylong. We supply fleet vehicles to government, corporates, NGOs, resource companies, and SMEs across the country — vehicles that must work reliably in real PNG conditions, long after the paperwork is signed.
This is a senior role for someone who understands that fleet is about trust, follow-through, and long-term relationships — not just pricing tables.
What You
’
ll Be Doing
You’ll be responsible for leading and growing PNG Motors’ national fleet business. That means managing key fleet accounts, developing new opportunities, and ensuring consistent fleet standards across the network.
You’ll work closely with branch teams, sales managers, service and parts departments, and senior leadership to deliver fleet solutions that actually perform in the field. From tender responses and pricing structures to delivery schedules and aftersales coordination, you’ll oversee the full fleet lifecycle.
This role requires balance. You’ll spend time with major clients, understand their operational realities, and make sure commitments made are commitments kept. At the same time, you’ll set national fleet processes, improve reporting, support branches, and ensure margins, compliance, and service levels are properly managed.
Fleet in PNG isn’t theoretical. Vehicles go remote. Conditions are tough. Timelines change. You’ll need to stay calm, adaptable, and decisive when things don’t go perfectly — because that’s when relationships are tested.
Who This Suits
This role suits an experienced fleet or automotive sales professional who has worked with large accounts, tenders, or multi-vehicle customers. You’re organised, commercially sharp, and comfortable dealing with senior decision-makers.
You understand pricing, contracts, and delivery logistics, but you also know that strong fleet partnerships are built on reliability and honesty. If you say something can be done, you make sure it happens — or you communicate early when it can’t.
If you enjoy complexity, accountability, and long-term client relationships, you’ll fit well here.
Why PNG Motors
PNG Motors is not a short-term operation. We’re a national business with real scale, strong global brands, proper aftersales support, and a long-term commitment to the market.
Our footprint spans Port Moresby, Lae, Kokopo, Mount Hagen, and Kimbe, allowing fleet customers to be supported well beyond the capital. What we sell is backed by parts, service, and people across the country — and that’s why fleets trust us.
Senior leaders here are trusted to lead properly, make decisions, and build businesses that last. If you want a role where you can shape national fleet strategy and see it delivered on the ground, this is it.

jobs.description:
Job Title: Field Service Engineer
Department:
Technical Services / Operations
Reports To:
Service Manager / Operation Manager
Location:
Port Moresby
Employment Type:
Full-Time
Company Overview
We are a leading distributor of pharmaceutical products and hospital equipment, dedicated to supporting healthcare providers with reliable medical technology and supply chain solutions. Our technical services team ensures that critical medical equipment is installed, maintained, and operational to the highest standards of safety and performance.
Position Summary
We are seeking a skilled and customer-focused Field Service Engineer to join our technical team. In this role, you will be responsible for the on-site installation, preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of a wide range of hospital and medical equipment. The ideal candidate combines technical expertise with excellent interpersonal skills, ensuring our healthcare clients receive prompt, professional, and compliant service that minimizes downtime and supports exceptional patient care.
Key Responsibilities
Installation & Commissioning:
Perform on-site installation, setup, calibration, and commissioning of new medical/hospital equipment (e.g., patient monitors, infusion pumps, ventilators, diagnostic devices, and hospital furniture systems).
Verify equipment functionality against specifications and conduct performance tests.
Provide initial operational training to clinical staff upon installation.
Maintenance & Repair:
Execute scheduled preventive maintenance (PM) services to ensure equipment reliability and longevity.
Diagnose, troubleshoot, and repair malfunctioning equipment efficiently to minimize client downtime.
Manage and replenish a car stock of essential spare parts and tools.
Compliance & Documentation:
Adhere strictly to all regulatory standards, including Good Distribution Practices, manufacturer guidelines, and hospital safety protocols.
Complete detailed service reports, installation certificates, and compliance documentation for each job.
Maintain accurate records of service activities, parts usage, and client interactions in the company CRM/ERP system.
Customer Support & Communication:
Serve as the primary technical point of contact for assigned clients, building strong professional relationships.
Communicate clearly with clinical staff, biomedical departments, and internal sales teams regarding service status and recommendations.
Proactively identify client needs and opportunities for service contracts or additional support.
Continuous Improvement:
Stay current with product training, technical manuals, and industry best practices.
Provide feedback to the management and procurement teams on equipment performance and recurring issues.
Qualifications & Experience
Essential:
Bachelor’s degree in Biomedical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Medical Technology, or a related technical field.
Proven experience (2+ years) as a Field Service Engineer, Biomedical Equipment Technician (BMET), or in a similar role servicing medical/hospital equipment.
Strong technical aptitude with the ability to read schematics, diagnose electrical/electronic systems, and use diagnostic software/tools.
Excellent problem-solving skills and a methodical approach to troubleshooting.
Outstanding communication and customer service skills.
Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel daily within the assigned region (occasional overnight travel may be required).
Physical ability to lift/move equipment (up to [e.g., 30 kg) and work in various hospital environments.
Preferred:
Certification as a Biomedical Equipment Technician (CBET) or similar credential.
Experience with specific equipment types (e.g., patient monitoring systems, infusion technology, laboratory analyzers, or imaging devices).
Familiarity with regulatory standards such as ISO 13485, FDA CFR 21, or local medical device directives.
Experience working directly with healthcare providers (hospitals, clinics, labs).
Key Competencies
Technical Proficiency:
In-depth understanding of electromechanical systems and medical device operation.
Reliability & Professionalism:
Punctual, trustworthy, and represents the company with the highest integrity.
Safety-Focused:
Uncompromising commitment to safety protocols for oneself, clients, and patients.
Adaptability:
Ability to work independently, manage a dynamic schedule, and handle pressure in critical clinical environments.
Proactive Learner:
Self-motivated to stay updated on new technologies and procedures.

" in the email's subject to ensure your application is processed.

jobs.description:
VACANCY ANNOUNCEMENT
Finance and Administration Officer
The Wildlife Conservation Society (WCS) is an international non-governmental organisation committed to working with communities, government and other partners to manage wildlife and wild places for biodiversity and human well-being.
WCS is recruiting for a
Full-Time Finance and Administration Officer
to manage the WCS Field office financial management systems, procedures, standard and maintain financial accountability and reporting on a timely manner. This position is also responsible for the overall administrative functions of the Wewak field office and offers support to Goroka Team. This position is based in Goroka, Eastern Highlands Province.
Job Summary:
The main objective of this position is to manage the WCS Field office financial management systems, procedures, standard and maintain financial accountability and reporting on a timely manner. This position is also responsible for the overall administrative functions of the Wewak field office and offers support to Goroka Team.
Major Responsibilities:
Advance Employee expenses
Process employees related advances and expenses in compliance with the WCS policies and procedures and relevant donor requirements for the Sepik region and support all other offices as required.
Process the Employee related advance acquittal forms and complete reconciliation as required – including banking lodgments.
Prepare the JV journals for the Employee Advance Forms and Acquittal for month end processing
Prepare the Employee Advance Balance Account on a monthly basis for month end reports.
Ensure all documentation is appropriately filed
Work with the program team to ensure that all internal policies and procedures are adhered to (where necessary provide training to the program staff on paperwork requirement and timelines)
Processing of local expenses
Process non-employee program expenses including reviewing and checking all required documentation in relation to donor requirements.
Ensure correct procurement process has been followed
Ensure appropriate signatures have been obtained
Check amount and purchase requisition
Ensure correct coding
Process the Expense payment via online banking or petty cash appropriate
Prepare the JV journals to process expenses in SAP
Petty Cash
Daily processing of petty cash – advances and expenses and ensure all documentations are in compliance with the WCS policies and procedures and relevant donor requirements.
Prepare the JV journals to process petty in SAP and ensure correct coding,
Reconcile petty cash on daily basis
Process cash counts for end of month check.
Payroll Process
Update Payroll System for all new employees, leavers and any additional changes in time for the bi-weekly payroll. Work with finance and payroll support officer and HR manager to ensure all HR confidential information is up to date
Work with Finance and payroll Support officers to ensure any changes to bank accounts are cross checked.
Process the bi -weekly payroll ensuring all deductions are correctly processed – Salary Save, Appropriate PNG taxes, pensions and superannuation.
Obtain appropriate approvals for the bi- weekly payroll.
Ensure all employee salary payments are appropriately financed – including any Salary Save payments.
Process monthly GST lodgment to the tax office and follow up of GST rebates and tax returns.
Provide necessary information and pay slips to the employees after each pay period ending.
Prepare JV journal for the payroll run payment.
Payroll accounting in SAP
Collect time sheets and prepare JV to allocate payroll costs to appropriate Grants and Funds based on the timesheet-% splits
Post JVs in SAP and review journals to ensure that payroll journals are reconciled
Ensure Net Pay Balance sheet account is reconciled and cleared
Ensure that all local PNG Accounting and tax reporting requirements are met and timely submission is
done to the IRC (Tax department) for the Salary and Wages Tax.
Prepare all Payroll related Balance Sheets
Follow up with IRC in relations to refunds.
Banking
Control and monitor WCS cash position, daily bank reconciliation and monitor bank activities daily to ensure adequate cash in bank account. Update Finance Manager when cash required
Manage cash across all PNG bank accounts so that each individual bank account has adequate cash for the current month’s cash requirements. Transfer cash across banks is required
Work with program teams to obtain upcoming cash requirements and update Finance Manager to ensure that monthly cash requests are up to date
Ensure Bank reconciliations and petty cash are processed on a daily basis.
Minimum Requirements:
Education/Credentials
A degree in accounting / Business Administration or qualification from a recognized professional accounting body (CA/ACCA)
Proficiency with use of Able Payroll System or other related systems
Experience
Requires a minimum of 3 years accounting and administrative management experience
Exposure to non-profit sector (NGO, International organisations) is an added advantage
Critical Knowledge, Skills and Abilities
Good analytical and problem-solving skills
Preferably familiar with requirements of different donors.
Good knowledge of accounting system(s).
Competent in the use of Microsoft Office such as Word, Excel and PowerPoint etc.
Require knowledge of financial systems, internal controls and procedures
Being a self-starter with drives and initiative and able to work as a team/individual with a positive attitude and open minded
Excellent multi-tasking, organized and follow-up skills,
Application process
Please send an up-to-date CV and letter of interest to
[email protected]
with the subject line: Application for
Goroka
Finance and Administration Officer
. Applications close:
Friday 30 January 2026 at 5pm
.
Due to large feedback, if you should not hear back within a week after application close, please consider your application unsuccessful. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for interviews.
WCS
is an equal opportunity and affirmative action employer whereby we do not engage in practices that discriminate.

jobs.employer_address: Level 3, Fincorp Haus, 30 Independence Drive, Waigani NCD, PNG
jobs.description:
POSITION
TERMS OF REFERENCE
POSITION TITLE: Stakeholder & Engagement Manager
LOCATION: KTF Port Moresby Office, Papua New Guinea
TYPE: Full-time
REMUNERATION: Competitive remuneration offered, commensurate with experience
ABOUT KTF:
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG).
We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and  primary
education
;
improving access to quality and accessible
healthcare
;
improving
equality
and access to sustainable income-generation opportunities, especially for women; and by fostering the next generation of
leaders
.
KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.
ABOUT THE ROLE:
The Stakeholder Engagement Manager (SEM) is a strategic and hands-on role responsible for strengthening, coordinating, and systematising KTF’s engagement with critical stakeholders.
Working closely with the General Manager, PNG, the SEM supports the development, maintenance and growth of relationships with key stakeholders including donors, partners, government representatives and officials, community leaders, sector peers and supporters.
The role is responsible for developing and implementing a stakeholder engagement framework and strategy, ensuring that priority stakeholders are informed, engaged and aligned with KTF’s mission, programs and impact.
This role requires excellent communication and relationship management skills, strong strategic thinking, initiative, and the ability to operate across organisational priorities in a fast-paced, mission-driven environment.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Stakeholder Strategy and Planning
Develop and maintain a comprehensive stakeholder engagement map identifying priority stakeholders across government, donors, partners, communities, sector networks and supporters.
Design and implement a stakeholder engagement strategy aligned with KTF’s organisational strategy, program priorities and growth objectives.
Segment stakeholders by influence, interest and engagement needs, and tailor engagement approaches accordingly.
Regularly review and adapt the stakeholder strategy to reflect organisational changes, new initiatives and emerging opportunities or risks.
Relationship Management and Engagement
Support the General Manager, PNG and Leadership Team in building, nurturing and strengthening relationships with key external stakeholders.
Act as a central coordination point for stakeholder engagement to ensure consistent messaging, follow-up and relationship continuity.
Prepare briefings, talking points and background materials for senior leadership ahead of stakeholder meetings and engagements.
Where appropriate, represent KTF in meetings, forums, events and sector engagements.
Government, Donor and Partner Engagement
Support engagement with government representatives and officials in Australia and PNG, ensuring alignment with national priorities and reforms.
Contribute to relationship management with donors, philanthropic partners and institutional funders, in close collaboration with the Head of Partnerships & Engagement and fundraising team.
Assist in identifying opportunities for new partnerships, collaborations and strategic alliances that support KTF’s mission and programs.
Support the coordination of donor and partner communications to ensure consistency, accuracy and professionalism.
Communications and Stakeholder Information
Develop and coordinate high-quality written communications for stakeholders, including briefings, updates, reports, presentations and correspondence.
Ensure stakeholders are well-informed about KTF’s programs, impact, innovations and strategic direction.
Work closely with internal teams to translate program information into clear, compelling external messaging.
Support the development of stakeholder-facing materials that strengthen KTF’s profile, credibility and influence.
Internal Coordination and Systems
Work across teams to ensure stakeholder engagement activities are planned, coordinated and tracked.
Establish simple systems to record engagement activities, contacts, outcomes and follow-up actions.
Provide advice and guidance to staff on stakeholder engagement approaches and protocols.
Support internal learning by sharing insights from stakeholder interactions that may inform strategy, programs or operations.
Strategic Support and Special Projects
Provide strategic advice to the General Manager, PNG on stakeholder dynamics, risks and opportunities.
Support priority organisational initiatives that require coordinated external engagement (e.g. new funds, flagship programs, major events).
Take initiative to identify creative and non-traditional engagement opportunities that enhance KTF’s reach and influence.
Safeguarding, Ethics and Compliance
Ensure all stakeholder engagement activities uphold KTF’s commitments to:
Child Protection and Safeguarding
PSEAH (Preventing Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment)
Code of Conduct
Gender Equality, Disability Inclusion and Do No Harm principles
Model ethical, respectful and culturally appropriate engagement at all times.
Ensure external communications and engagements align with organisational policies and reputational standards.
SELECTION CRITERIA:
Essential
Minimum 5+ years’ experience in a stakeholder engagement, partnerships, external relations, business development or similar role.
Demonstrated ability to build and manage relationships with diverse stakeholders, including senior decision-makers.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to translate complex information into clear messaging.
Strong problem-solving skills and the ability to think strategically and creatively.
Proven ability to take initiative, work independently and manage multiple priorities.
Experience working in or with NGOs, international development, government or mission-driven organisations.
Desirable
Experience working in or with international development or the PNG context.
Experience supporting senior leaders or executive teams.
Familiarity with donor, government or philanthropic engagement.
Strong organisational and coordination skills.
Tertiary qualifications in communications, international development, public policy, business, or a related field.
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG. This position will require frequent domestic travel in PNG (including remote and rural areas).
Closing date for applications: 30
th
January 2026, or earlier if the position has been filled.
Applications will be reviewed as they are received, so apply asap.
To apply click this
link
: Fill in the required fields and upload the relevant documentation, including your CV, cover letter, copy of your qualifications and one written reference.  In your cover letter, clearly address the selection criteria and your motivation to apply for this position.
KTF is a child safe organisation committed to the protection of people we serve. Our recruitment and selection procedures are designed to ensure we only recruit people who are suitable and aligned with our policies that ensure the safety of children and protection of all from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. All appointments are subject to appropriate background checks and screening, and the successful candidate will be required to get Working With Children check and a Police Certificate. We promote diversity and equality in all our practices and strongly encourage those with diverse backgrounds and/or disabilities and or those who identify as LGBTQI+ to apply for positions with KTF.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will assist the Mining Manager and Superintendents to provide medium, long term and /or strategic mine planning including underground mining optimization, design, production scheduling, cost estimations, underground expansion studies, administration of the computerized dispatch system, short term production and capital projects and to supervise, mentor and develop graduate mining engineers.

jobs.description:
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Purpose
The Technician, Core Shed is accountable for the efficient execution of all geological services activities, including end-to-end core sample processing and dispatch and all field logistics and other logistical or project assistance in support of the Exploration team.  The Technician, Core Shed, will provide support to the Technician, Exploration Drilling as required.
Essential Duties
Implement core handling, photography, mark-up, cutting, sampling and geotechnical logging procedures
Gather geological data in line with SOPs, including XRF, hyperspectral, density and other rock properties data from core and chips
Administer, store, and retrieve core samples according to SOP's
Adhere to procedures for core disposal, reuse and core shed operations to prevent environmental degradation
Maintain a high standard of housekeeping around Exploration work areas at all times
Support Exploration drilling operations by arranging for pad preparation and running water lines
Training & Experience
Literacy and numeracy skills are critical to underpin all other requirements.
The ability to work effectively in a team is critical.
A demonstrated ability to work independently on tasks assigned is critical.
Proficiency in core handling, mark-up, geotechnical logging, sampling and other data collection in line with SOPs is critical.
A Class 6 PNG Driver’s license is highly desirable
A certified forklift ticket is highly desirable.
Experience with surveying (e.g., GPS) or geotechnical tools would be highly desirable.
Experience with MS Office applications like Excel for data management and Word for documentation is highly desirable.
First Aid Training is desirable.
A basic understanding of drill rigs and drilling operations is desirable.
Experience conducting remote field programs in local communities is desirable.
Working Conditions
The position will typically be occupied by Lihirian team members who live on the island but drive-in, drive-out (DIDO) and reside in camp when on roster. A fly-in fly-out (FIFO) arrangement from approved ports of hire may may also be offered to other PNG-nationals at the discretion of the Manager Exploration Near-Mine and Brownfield, Lihir.
All Technician, Core Shed team members will work a 21/21 even-time roster. Working days are nominally 12 hours, though this excludes travelling time between camp and the Lihir operation.
Our FIFO and DIDO employees stay in secure and comfortable camp in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered at our mess. The wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package and annual incentive program.
If you feel that you could make a meaningful contribution in this role, we encourage you to discuss this opportunity with your current people leader and how it aligns with your longer term career goals.
To support you in your application, we have created a range of resources available to all Newmont People including information on eligibility criteria and FAQs. Find out more by visiting our page in Discovery: Internal Employee Resources
As a current employee or contractor, please submit your application is MS Word or Adobe format online via the Internal Job Postings link on Discovery.
If you have issues applying through Discovery or would like to learn more about the role before applying, please contact the relevant member of our Talent Acquisition Team.
