jobs.description:
POSITION TITLE:
PHARMACY SUPERVISOR – LAE
CONTEXT:
Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) is a private, non-profit international humanitarian organization, founded in 1971 and working in 70 countries around the world. MSF provides medical assistance to populations in crisis, regardless of race, religion, belief or political affiliation. In PNG, MSF has been working since 2007 in Lae, Taric, Bougainville, Gulf Province and NCD Province. MSF is now working to support the Department of Health to improve access to care for patients in Lae, Jiwaka and Highlands.
MAIN PURPOSE OF THE POSITION:
Ensuring general functioning of the pharmacy and supervising pharmacy supply chain processes in accordance with MSF standards, protocols and procedures, in order to ensure its efficiency and operating availability.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Ensuring storage, stock management and supply processes, as well as hygiene and security procedures, tools, and protocols (controlling pests and rodents), implementing appropriate quality controls and records, in order to ensure good storage conditions (temperatures, humidity and light exposure) and availability of drugs and medical material, according to
MSF
protocols, national regulations and in cooperation with the logistics department.
Coordinating the delivery, reception and recording of international and local orders, in close coordination with the logistics department, updating stock files and informing line managers on their status (shortfalls, over-stocking, expiry dates), in order to permanently ensure security of stock levels and ensure efficient management of stock.
Supervising orders of medical and drug material in order to ensure an efficient and appropriate consumption pattern under budget constraints.
Supervising the supply of drugs to patients, according to medical prescriptions, informing them on consumption patterns and keeping conditions in order to ensure their therapeutic progression
Ensuring efficient supply to other pharmacies managed/supported by
MSF
according to orders and stocks and using cold chain when needed. Monitoring and analyzing orders of depending on pharmacies in order to avoid ruptures of stock or having expired drugs.
Supervising, with the HR department, the associated processes (sizing, staff shifts, recruitment, training, performance evaluation, development and internal/external communication) of the pharmaceutical team and the nursing staff, in order to ensure both the sizing and the amount of knowledge required and to improve their dispensing capabilities.
Recording all items received and issued in computer (Isystock) and reporting on drug consumption and medical equipment dispensed according to protocols, informing on unusual patterns as well as forecasting future needs, in order to rationalize the budget and to ensure availability.
Assisting in training of nursing staff regarding dispensing of drugs and their side effects
SPECIFIC ACCOUNTABILITIES:
Monitor and maintain the pharmacy and ensure the security of related medical supplies under the Morobe Palliative Cancer Care Project as per MSF standard.
Assist the Project Medical referent with stock management through data entry into Isystock and stock cards which will be used to follow consumption.
Observe and report cold chain status daily and implement procedures to detect immediately any cold chain breaks or any defects.
Work in collaboration with Angau Memorial Hospital pharmacy staff to organize and implement a smooth supply system to end-users with quality and safety of supply maintained.
Identify any needs for support to Angau Memorial Hospital pharmacy staff in stock management, safe dispensing and identifying ways to mitigate any potential drug shortages.
Responsible for follow up and replenishment of all project First Aid Kits and EPREP.
Dispatch transit stock to MSF Jiwaka project and MSF Coordination office in Port Moresby as the main point of reception.
Ensure proper storage and disposal of all expired and damaged drugs according to MSF safety standards and waste management protocols both national and international legislation.
Participate in patient and staff education for Cancer prevention, screening and care.
Compile monthly reports and sitreps.
Manage batch recalls
Maintain an updated register for regulated drugs.
Participate in developing project documents, IMO and log frames
Assist the medical team in pharmacovigilance and reporting of SAE’s.
SKILLS AND REQUIREMENTS:
Education
Essential, degree of pharmacy management or nursing related studies., or medical profile.
Experience
At least 1-year certified work experience as a pharmacy manager.
Languages
English and Tok Pisin is essential
Knowledge
Computer literacy (word, excel, internet, power point) is mandatory.
Competencies
Results and Quality Orientation, Teamwork and Cooperation, Behavioral Flexibility, Commitment to MSF Principles, Stress Management
WORKING CONDITIONS
Fixed-term Contract
Based in Morobe
Candidates must be flexible with working hours and location
APPLICATION PROCESS
The applicants have to send their cover letter with an updated CV and a copy of any other relevant documents (diploma/degree/secondary school and training certificates, previous work certificates/recommendations) to:
By hand delivery:
Cassowary Road, Lae_Morobe province
Crane Street, Lot 93
By email:
[email protected]
Please clearly indicate on your application the position title and your phone number.  No document will be returned.
Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted
. Please note that
MSFF does not provide transportation or accommodation
for the written tests and interviews. Written tests and interviews will be held in Morobe since recruitment for this position is for Morobe.

About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Advisor, Maintenance Autoclaves, you’ll coordinate maintenance activities for 4 autoclaves and associated equipment, driving KPI compliance and continuous improvement. Your leadership will help ensure safe, efficient, and reliable operations, contributing directly to shutdown readiness, statutory compliance, and process plant improvements.
As Part Of The Team, You Will
Administer and optimize maintenance activities and weekly schedules
Ensure strict compliance with safety protocols
Lead and guide supervisors, trades, and new employees
Conduct inspections, safety audits, and troubleshoot issues
Compile performance reports and maintain accurate records
Assess risks and implement mitigation measures
Collaborate with internal teams and external contractors/suppliers
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Fitter and turner trade certificate is preferred
5 years experience in maintenance coordination and safety compliance
Experience with autoclaves is essential
Experience with positive displacement pumps (GEHO’s)
Advanced skills in maintenance scheduling, safety audits, and troubleshooting
Strong knowledge of maintenance management systems (SAP) and risk management
Effective communication, self-awareness, and teamwork abilities
Commitment to Newmont’s values and productive work culture
Your Work Environment
You’ll be based at the Lihir site, working within the Autoclave Maintenance department on a 21:21 roster. The role involves collaborating with a diverse team of technicians, engineers, contractors, and suppliers, and being part of a supportive leadership group focused on operational excellence.

Join a global leader in mining where safety, innovation, and teamwork are valued. You’ll have opportunities for professional growth, contribute to impactful projects, and be part of a supportive, high-performing team.

Job Description
About Us
New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a leading mining company dedicated to sustainable practices and community engagement in Papua New Guinea. As the operator of the Porgera Gold Mine, we focus on extracting high-quality mineral resources while prioritizing the well-being of our employees, the environment, and the local communities. Our commitment to safety, innovation, and responsible mining ensures that we not only contribute to the economy but also support the development and prosperity of the regions we operate in. At NPL, we strive to create a positive impact, fostering strong relationships with stakeholders and promoting sustainable growth for future generations.
NPL now has a vacancy for a qualified and experienced individual to join our Mine Technical Services Department as an
Engineer - Planning - MES Underground
.
About the role
Reporting to the Senior Planning Engineer, the Underground Engineer, Planning is responsible for development, optimization and maintenance of short to medium term underground mine plans. The role supports safe, efficient and cost -effective mining operations through high-quality technical planning, scheduling and engineering analysis, while ensuring compliance with statutory, safety and company standards.
In this role, you will:
Mine Planning & Design
Develop and maintain short-term, medium-term underground plans
Design underground development layouts, infrastructure plans in accordance with geotechnical, ventilation and operational requirements
Ensure integration of geology, geotechnical, ventilation and survey inputs into mine plans
Scheduling
Develop Short and Mid-Term schedule using Excel, Deswik scheduler.
Evaluation alternative mining methods and sequencing options to optimize productivity and cost.
Track plan versus actual performance and provide variance analysis
Conduct trade-off studies and risk assessments
Technical Services Support
Maintain a high level of health and safety awareness and comply with the NPL’s Occupational Health & Safety Policy and all health and safety rules and procedures
Provide engineering support to underground operations, including production trouble shooting and design modifications
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Tertiary Qualifications in Mine Engineering, or related
Minimum 3 years of experience working in Underground Mining environment
Experience with underground mining methods (Longhole open stoping)
Working knowledge of relevant mining legislation and safety standards
Membership of AusIMM and Engineers PNG (IEPNG)
Proficiency in mining technology and heavy equipment, advanced skills in mine planning software (preferably Deswik), strong computer skills, excellent Knowledge           of open pit mining technology and heavy production equipment
High level understanding of all relevant legislation affecting the employment and safety of persons in the mining industry in PNG.
Working Conditions
•    Combination of office-based planning work and Underground site exposure
•    May require rostered shift or site-based rosters depending on operation
•    Use of PPE and adherence to all safety protocols required
Mobilization Requirement
In return, you will be joining a world-class mining operation with the opportunity to impact the development and upskilling of our predominantly local workforce, combined with a team keen to learn and absorb knowledge.  This offers a unique opportunity to further shape the department and improve NPL’s social performance and people knowledge.
You will be joining an operation that values safety and lead a team towards best-in-class safety practices whilst contributing to the development of a highly capable national workforce, making a lasting impact on the industry.
This role is offered on a FIFO basis with a 21/14 roster and a highly competitive remuneration package.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
In this role you will direct, manage and ensure that mobile equipment repair is carried out in a productive and cost-effective manner to optimize mobile machinery availability and facilitate the delivery of Mining Services underground so productions targets can be met. You will provide management and leadership within our mobile maintenance department and this rewarding role will see you provide daily mentoring, guidance, instruction, and training to the national workforce to increase safety performance, machinery uptime and efficient outcomes within a motivated and talented department.
Key Accountabilities
Supervise all maintenance Personnel in the workshop, including recruitment and termination of personnel.
Liaise closely with the Production Superintendent in respect of equipment servicing and preventive maintenance scheduling and required equipment availability.
Supervise and control any sub-contractor activity at the workshop.
Supervise all workshop apprentices under the guidance of the Apprenticeship Co-ordinator.
Prepare estimates and quotes on repairs for work to be carried out in the workshop where applicable
Regularly assess and determine if upgrades are required and check designs of buckets booms and GET meet site and manufacturer’s specification in conjunction with HOD Mining.
Provide support to the Mine Superintendent to optimise efficiencies in the underground mine to achieve the Weekly Plan.
Work closely with the Mine Superintendent and Shift Supervisors to improve mining standards, assess operator performance and identify improvement projects to maximise results, reduce risk and implement cost management initiatives.
Establish a high-performance culture by motivating team members to strive for a high level of performance by rewarding and recognising high performance.
Ensure effective processes for communicating relevant information, including company, site, department, and team performance, to all team members are in place.
Continuously mentor and coach operators on acceptable mining standards and effective techniques on machinery to achieve these standards.
Identify skills gaps and training requirements and assist in developing training packages as required to close the skills gap.
Coordinate and assist with the delivery of training to employees.
Actively review the work performance of technicians and provide feedback to the area supervisors including the talent and succession planning for designated key roles.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Ensure general housekeeping within the mine is of a high standard.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values.
About You
Qualifications & Experience
Relevant trade qualification in Heavy Equipment Fitting, Auto Electrical and Automation
5+ years plus of underground mining experience (Essential)
2+ years Shift Supervisor experience (Essential)
Organisational skills – Good time management skills.
Good communication and interpersonal skills – Be an effective communicator and listener.
Extensive knowledge of SHE Management System relevant to K92 i.e. Policy and Procedures.
Supervisory skills – Be a good leader, motivator and teacher.
Good command of the English Language (oral & written).
Knowledge of various heavy earthmoving machinery components.
Knowledge and understanding of the Duty of Care standards, occupational Health & Safety Act & Regulations, Mining Inspection Act & Regulations.
Sound planning, analytical and problem-solving skills.
Excellent trouble shooting skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work under pressure and autonomously.
Excellent attention to detail and time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening & interpersonal skills for rapport building, conflict resolution & training.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.location: National Capital District, Morobe, Autonomous Region of Bougainville, Central, East Sepik, East New Britain, Eastern Highlands, Madang, Milne Bay, New Ireland, West New Britain, Western Highlands
jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer
– we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and caf
é serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As an Advisor, you will play a key role in driving the long-term reliability and performance of the Oxygen Plant’s electrical and instrumentation systems. You will lead and support maintenance teams to achieve KPI compliance, foster continuous improvement, and ensure safe and efficient operations. With a strong focus on statutory compliance, legislative requirements, and plant upgrades, you will contribute to the ongoing optimisation and resilience of critical plant infrastructure.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Champion proactive safety behaviors and ensure HSE compliance
Ensure Compliance to EIGA, AS and Mining Legislative Requirements
Have experience with Mines Inspector and Insurance audits
Develop and coach team members through feedback and training
Provide technical support for maintenance on three oxygen plants
Monitor and supervise maintenance activities to maximize productivity
Select, install, and commission electrical equipment and instrumentation
Recommend upgrades and improvements for plant control systems
Manage documentation and contribute to preventative maintenance strategies
Deliver work within budget and seek cost reduction opportunities
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Dual Electrical & Instrumentation trades qualification is desirable
Accreditation from the Institute of Engineers PNG Inc. will be completed as part of work permit process
Australian, New Zealand, or PNG Power Electrical License is essential
Certification in Workplace Assessment and Training or similar is desirable
PNG National Driver’s License

jobs.employer_address: POM, NCD, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Papua New Guinea Project Director, STRIDES
Job Summary:
The Papua New Guinea Project Director leads and directs implementation of the Strengthening Infectious Disease Detection (STRIDES) Activity in Papua New Guinea to enhance global health priorities in-country with the general objectives to strengthen capacity across laboratory and surveillance systems to prevent, detect, and rapidly and effectively respond to emerging infectious diseases and other public health threats. They will fulfill the diverse managerial requirements of the Activity and have technical and management responsibility for all activities, personnel, and budget/spending. The Papua New Guinea Project Director, STRIDES, serves as the Activity’s primary liaison with posts in country, local government, and other global health security implementing partners working in-country, in addition to overseeing STRIDES subcontractors operating in-country. The Papua New Guinea Project Director, STRIDES, will lead the development and implementation of annual work plans, monitoring and evaluation activities, technical and financial reporting, and other administrative elements of the Activity.
Accountabilities:
Plans, directs, and coordinates implementation of Activity to ensure that goals and objectives are accomplished within prescribed timeframes and funding parameters.
Establishes work plans, teams, and SOPs to meet Activity goals and ensure compliance with policies.
Directly manages technical, financial, and operational staff responsible for all aspects of the STRIDES Activity in Papua New Guinea.
Responsible for creating, promoting, and maintaining safe and equitable work environments for all personnel, including a harassment- and violence-free work culture, and systems for safeguarding Activity participants.
Manages in-country relationships with national, regional, and local government counterparts and multisectoral partners to fulfill national global health security objectives and targets and operationalize implementing activities.
Serve as the primary point of contact and collaboration for the team and in-country partners, including Department of State, implementation partners, government partners, and other key partners.
Leads in-country team and liaises with Activity leadership at the global level to define, develop, implement, monitor and adjust technical work plans, budgets, presentations, and reports.
Ensures on-time delivery of high-quality deliverables and reports.
Provides guidance and training to managers and staff to achieve Activity goals.
Responsible for onboarding of Activity staff, ensuring their familiarity with organizational and Activity values, quality standards, policies and procedures and their individual responsibilities in upholding them.
Supports performance management and professional development of direct reports, including ongoing feedback, coaching, and career support.
Applied Knowledge & Skills:
Comprehensive knowledge of theories, concepts, and practices with project management, process development, and execution. Familiarity with international Global Health Security frameworks and initiatives, particularly in relation to Department of State’s Programs and priorities, is highly preferred.
Excellent and demonstrated project management skills, including leadership to develop annual work plans and deliverables to State while overseeing the Activity’s monitoring and evaluation plan to ensure achievement of Activity goals and objectives.
Articulate, professional, and diplomatic with the ability to communicate using a clear and positive manner with clients and staff.
Strong influencing, negotiation, and collaboration skills; Prior experience developing partnerships and managing relationships with State, host country government, key partners, and other implementing partners in country is highly preferred.
Demonstrated leadership skills in managing staff within a matrixed organization. Prior experience working in an international non-governmental organization (INGO) is a plus.
Strong critical thinking and problem-solving skills to plan, organize, and manage resources for the successful completion of the Activity.
Problem Solving & Impact:
Deploys sound decision-making skills and proactive problem-solving when encountering highly complex, varied problems to mitigate risks and promote effective and continuous Activity implementation.
Exercises judgment to meet business strategies and develops objectives that align with donor and Activity goals.
Quickly identifies and notifies management of potential issues during implementation.
Strong analytical and problem-solving capabilities.
Supervision Given/Received:
Sets goals and budgets and leads the in-country team to achieve strategic goals.
Leads coordination of resources for Activity implementation, addresses/resolves Activity issues.
Reports to the Health Programs Program Manager
Education:
Bachelor’s degree or its international equivalent in public health or other health- related fields related to the functions of the position;
Master’s degree or its international equivalent preferred.
Project management certification preferred.
Experience:
Typically requires 10+ years of relevant experience with project management principles and practices, including 5+ years of managing staff.
Proficient with applicable Department of State or other USG donor rules, regulations, and policies
Demonstrated knowledge and experience working on the management and implementation of human or animal health projects and interventions for infectious diseases
Knowledge and experience working on Global Health Security projects or activities preferred; experience working across multiple sectors (One Health) desirable
Demonstrated experience in developing and mentoring staff and building the capacity of local teams and partners.
Demonstrated experience in managing complex, multidisciplinary projects and/or activities.
Proficiency in the English language is required
Fluency in Tok Pisin language is required
Experience operating in insecure environments.
Experience working in an NGO is preferred
Experience working in a Government Human, Animal, or Environmental Health Ministry/Agency is desirable.
Typical Physical Demands
:
Typical office environment.
Ability to spend long hours looking at computer screen and doing repetitive work on a keyboard.
Ability to sit and stand for extended periods of time.
Ability to lift/move up to 5 lbs.
Technology to be Used
:
Personal Computer/Laptop, Microsoft applications (i.e., Office 365, SharePoint, Skype/Zoom/Teams), cell phone/mobile technology, and standard office equipment.
Travel Requirements:
10% - 25%

jobs.description:
Service Clerk
(The organised, detail-driven kind)
Location: Papua New Guinea
PNG Motors is a market leader in automotive and mobility services across Papua New Guinea. Our service departments are busy, practical environments where accuracy, follow-through, and communication matter just as much as technical skill.
We’re looking for a Service Clerk to support our service operations and keep the front end of the workshop running smoothly.
This is not a “sit quietly and file things” role. If you don’t like phones ringing, customers asking questions, or juggling multiple tasks at once, this probably isn’t for you.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be the link between customers, service advisors, technicians, and administration. That means booking vehicles in and out, preparing and updating job cards, managing service paperwork, assisting with invoicing, and making sure information is accurate and up to date.
You’ll deal with customers face-to-face and over the phone, answer service enquiries, and help keep daily workflow organised. Things won’t always run perfectly to schedule, so staying calm, clear, and organised is part of the job.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone who is naturally organised, reliable, and comfortable in a fast-moving environment. Experience in an automotive service department or a similar administrative role is highly regarded, but attitude, attention to detail, and willingness to learn are just as important.
You’re confident using computers, comfortable dealing with people, and understand that small details matter when vehicles, invoices, and customer trust are involved.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors operates nationwide and supports real customers who rely on their vehicles every day. Our service teams are professional, practical, and focused on doing the job properly. You’ll be part of a structured organisation with clear processes, experienced colleagues, and room to grow if you prove yourself dependable and capable.

If you’re organised, people-focused, and take pride in keeping things running smoothly, we’d like to hear from you.

jobs.employer_address: Cameron Road, Waigani, NCD, 121
jobs.description:
MARINE AUTO ELECTRICIAN / MARINE MECHANIC
(The actual marine kind)
Location: Papua New Guinea
PNG Motors is growing its marine operations and we’re looking for experienced Marine Auto Electricians and Marine Mechanics to support Suzuki Marine and associated marine brands across Papua New Guinea.
This is not a “close enough” role. If your marine experience starts and ends with standing near a boat, this probably isn’t for you.
What You’ll Be Doing
You’ll be working on marine engines and marine electrical systems, diagnosing faults, servicing and repairing equipment, and keeping vessels operating in conditions where saltwater, heat, vibration, and weather are part of the job. Work is split between workshop and field, and not everything arrives neatly scheduled. When something fails at sea, it needs to be fixed properly, not creatively explained.
You’ll be expected to work independently, follow manufacturer standards, and maintain strong safety discipline, even when conditions are uncomfortable and time is tight.
Who This Suits
This role suits someone with genuine marine experience. Not automotive experience with an interest in boats, but real hands-on work with marine engines and marine electrical systems. You understand outboard servicing, marine electrical fault finding, wiring and control systems, charging systems, and engine management. You’ve worked on equipment that lives in saltwater and you know why that matters.
Experience supporting offshore, commercial, or professional marine operations is highly regarded and will feel familiar rather than intimidating.
Qualifications & Training
Formal marine trade qualifications are highly regarded, as is manufacturer training such as Suzuki Marine or equivalent. Relevant electrical or mechanical certifications will be viewed favourably.
Why You’ll Like Working Here
PNG Motors is a well-established organisation supporting marine and mobility operations across Papua New Guinea. We work with recognised global marine brands and operate in real conditions, with real customers who depend on their equipment. When things go wrong on the water, they go wrong quickly, and we understand the responsibility that comes with that.
You’ll be trusted to do the job properly, supported by a professional technical team, and given work that values skill, judgement, and reliability.
How to Apply
If you know marine work, respect the ocean, and take pride in fixing things properly the first time, we’d like to hear from you.

jobs.description:
Finance & HR Coordinator
Overview
The Clinton Health Access Initiative, Inc. (CHAI) is a global health organization committed to our mission of saving lives and reducing the burden of disease in low-and middle-income countries. We work at the invitation of governments to support them and the private sector to create and sustain high-quality health systems.
CHAI was founded in 2002 in response to the HIV/AIDS epidemic, with the goal of dramatically reducing the price of life-saving drugs and increasing access to these medicines in the countries with the highest burden of the disease. Over the following two decades, CHAI has expanded its focus. Today, along with HIV, we work in conjunction with our partners to prevent and treat infectious diseases such as COVID-19, malaria, tuberculosis, and hepatitis. Our work has also expanded into cancer, diabetes, hypertension, and other non-communicable diseases, and we work to accelerate the rollout of lifesaving vaccines, reduce maternal and child mortality, combat chronic malnutrition, and increase access to assistive technology. We are investing in horizontal approaches to strengthen health systems through programs in human resources for health, digital health, and health financing. With each new and innovative program, our strategy is grounded in maximizing sustainable impact at scale, ensuring that governments lead the solutions, that programs are designed to scale nationally, and learnings are shared globally.
At CHAI, our people are our greatest asset, and none of this work would be possible without their talent, time, dedication and passion for our mission and values. We are a highly diverse team of enthusiastic individuals across 40 countries with a broad range of skill sets and life experiences. CHAI is deeply grounded in the countries we work in, with the majority of our staff based in program countries. Learn more about our exciting work:
http://www.clintonhealthaccess.org
.
CHAI is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and is committed to providing an environment of fairness, and mutual respect where all applicants have access to equal employment opportunities. CHAI values diversity and inclusion and recognizes that our mission is best advanced by the leadership and contributions of people with diverse experience, backgrounds, and culture.
Position Overview
Reporting directly to the Country Manager, the Finance & HR Coordinator will provide professional accounting, budgeting, compliance, payroll, treasury, and HR support within the CHAI Papua New Guinea office while working closely with different
stakeholders across all levels of the organization including CHAI’s Boston based finance team.
The Finance & HR Coordinator will supervise and finance and procurement officer building their capacity and ensuring smooth running of the finance and accounting function within the country office. Because of the fluid nature of our work, specific responsibilities may change over time and these responsibilities listed here should not be construed as being comprehensive but rather indicative of what is expected.
Responsibilities
Budgeting and Reporting
Lead the development of the annual office budget and all donor-specific program budgets, recommending budget adjustments and other cost improvement measures.
Review and monitor country financial performance against budget, identify variances, and provide timely analysis and recommendations for corrective actions.
Support program teams to develop proposal budgets.
Prepare and maintain relevant financial reports for internal and external stakeholders and ensure all fund activities are following organization and grant requirements.
Financial Accounting, Reporting, and Controls
Implement all necessary internal accounting and control procedures.
Review all monthly balance sheets reconciliation conducted by the Finance and Procurement Officer for accuracy.
Supervise the Finance and Procurement Officer in making sure entries in Quickbooks have followed the application of GAAP and any prevalent CHAI standards in reporting financial data.
Supervise the Finance and Procurement Officer in making sure that a proper filling system for both hard and soft copy financial documents is implemented and maintained.
Perform quarterly reconciliation between the GL and the asset register to ensure information recorded on the GL matches what is reported in the register.
Review remittances of all applicable taxes in accordance with legal requirements in the country.
Ensure accurate and timely submission of financial reports to HQ, donors and government regulatory agencies.
Grants Management and Risk Monitoring
Lead grant close-out process as per grant agreements.
Lead the process of risk management by logging identified risks and mitigation across different grants and the office.
Maintain a risk log and submit quarterly reports to facilitate management discussions regarding current and emerging risks.
Treasury
Manage the country’s treasury function (cash, bank, receivables, and payables) and ensure adequate resources are available for both administrative and programmatic spending.
Manage local payments and process wire requests to Boston.
Manage monthly cash forecasting and cash requests from Boston treasury team.
Payroll Management
Conduct monthly payroll reconciliation to ascertain that payroll register reconciles with the financial entries as per General Ledger (GL) distributed.
Filling returns and making sure remittances to all relevant tax and social security agencies are made by the due dates without any errors.
Lead the consolidation and review process of salary allocation files to be submitted to HQ and flagging any deviation from the original budget.
Compliance and Audit
Conduct quarterly spot checks to ensure internal control are being adhered to.
Prepare and coordinate annual statutory audit, donor specific audits/assessments and CHAI internal audits.
Ensure follow-up with audit observations and maintain an up-to-date remediation log (corrective action plan log).

Maintain and track all records on employee leave, benefits, and changes in personal details.
Coordinate HR administrative processes that include new hire, job changes, contracts management and termination process in-country and with the Global HR team ensuring coordination with payroll.
Coordinate the pre-hiring process including candidate sourcing, job posting and interview coordination.
Coordinate the post-hiring process, including delivering onboarding and orientation activities.
Support the Country Manager in ensuring that compensation practices are following current legislation and CHAI global compensation framework.
Others

ACCA/CPA -PNG- Papua New Guinea qualification

Strong analytical and financial modelling skills; advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and accounting software (e.g., QuickBooks).
Proven ability to implement internal controls and manage compliance in a complex donor-funded environment.
Excellent communication, leadership, and team collaboration skills.
Attributes
Demonstrated integrity, accountability, and attention to detail.
Strong problem-solving and organizational skills.
Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment with multiple priorities.
Commitment to CHAI’s mission of saving lives and strengthening health systems.

The Principal – Business Development is responsible for driving sustainable local business participation across K92’s supply chain. This role links operational procurement needs with community enterprise capabilities, fostering opportunities across the mine life cycle, from exploration support services to closure-related remediation contracts.
The role supervises the Superintendent – Business Development, who implements supplier readiness programs, delivers business training, and coordinates enterprise development activities.
Key Accountabilities
This position provides strategic direction and operational oversight for landowner and local enterprise development. Part of the responsibilities include:
Lead and Manage Business Development:
Direct and mentor the Superintendent – Business Development, set clear annual objectives and budgets, and collaborate with Supply Chain to identify procurement opportunities for local SMEs.
Strategic Partnerships & Capacity Building:
Develop partnerships with training institutions, NGOs, and financial service providers to strengthen supplier capacity and promote long-term business sustainability.
Governance & Compliance:
Embed SPMS Technical Standards into all business development initiatives, ensuring compliance, audit-readiness, and alignment with corporate governance frameworks.
Local Business Participation:
Increase the number and value of contracts awarded to local suppliers, contributing to economic growth and ensuring compliance with MOA local content commitments.
Annual Planning & Reporting:
Prepare annual business development plans and budgets; report quarterly on procurement outcomes, supplier performance, and training impacts.
Delegation & Financial Authority:

jobs.description:
Protected Area Network Development Project Manager
Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program-PNG
JOB DESCRIPTION
Position Title:
Protected Area Network Development Project Manager (PNG National)
Position type:
Full Time
Reports to:
Executive  Director, TKCP-PNG
Supervises:
Stakeholder Engagement Facilitator
Location:
Based in Lae with travel (20%) around the Huon Peninsula (Morobe)
Remuneration:
A competitive salary package including family medical coverage, Nasfund contributions, worker’s compensation, and professional development opportunities.
Background:
The Tree Kangaroo Conservation Program has worked with communities and landowners on the Huon Peninsula for nearly 30 years, to facilitate the designation and management of the 162,800-hectare YUS Conservation Area for the benefit of the area’s wildlife, environment, and people. The YUS Conservation Area serves as a national model for community-based conservation in Papua New Guinea, and its accomplishments have generated significant interest among landowners, communities, and government representatives throughout the Huon Peninsula in pursuit of locally-led protection and sustainable development.
Purpose:
The Protected Area Network Development Manager will lead an exciting new initiative for TKCP, collaborating with Provincial, District, and Local Government partners to promote and facilitate community-based conservation throughout high-biodiversity areas across the Huon Peninsula. He/she will build and maintain close partnerships with PNG’s Conservation and Environment Protection Authority (CEPA) as well as the Morobe Provincial Government Administration to enable and formalize provincial-level support for protected area creation and management. During the next 18 months, in close consultation with Provincial and District partners, this role will determine the appropriate legal, financial, governance, and operational models in order to design and establish the Saruwaget Range Protected Area Network which, subject to further funding, will facilitate creation of  Community Conservation Area throughout the project’s target Districts.
Summary of key responsibilities
Facilitate and complete the design and road map for establishment and activation of the Saruwaget Range Protected Area Network, leading to the designation of new protected areas throughout target Districts across the Huon Peninsula.
Establish and maintain productive partnerships and effective coordination with key project stakeholders including CEPA, Morobe Provincial Administration, and District Administrations.
Organize and facilitate project governance structure through the Saruwaget Range Protected Area Working Committee to ensure shared responsibility and active stakeholder engagement.
Develop contracts and manage contractors’ timely delivery of key project outputs, to inform the Working Committee’s decisions and actions.
Facilitate Working Committee consultation and decision-making throughout key project stages, including National and Provincial endorsement for the Network’s formal legal establishment and resourcing.
Produce and distribute communications and informational materials to raise awareness and generate local interest throughout the target areas across the Huon Peninsula.
Lead and coordinate community outreach and engagement with Local Level Government partners throughout the target area to undertake steps toward protected area creation, designation, and management.
Develop and maintain networks within Papua New Guinea’s conservation community, and represent TKCP in conferences and workshops as appropriate.
Maintain close control and adaptive management of project plans and budgets throughout implementation, and produce regular reports for TKCP management and project funders.
With input from TKCP’s technical staff, refine and document the processes and tools for protected area establishment including FPIC, Land Use Planning, Conservation Deeds, etc.
Provide leadership and supervisory oversight to the Stakeholder Engagement Facilitator and collaboratively implement designated responsibilities.
Participate and contribute to the development of funding proposals to support the future phase(s) of the Saruwaget Range Protected Area Network initiative.
Selection criteria
Demonstrated experience and established networks with Provincial and Sub-Provincial Government.
Bachelor’s degree in natural resource management, conservation, environmental studies, or related fields (Master’s degree preferred)
Significant experience (5+ years) with program/project management in community-based conservation or a related field
Experience working with an NGO or government agency in increasing positions of reporting and responsibility.
Confidence and demonstrated ability to liaise with government officials at all levels, and with community leaders/landowners
Demonstrated leadership and problem-solving skills
Experience working with local communities and traveling to remote areas in PNG.
Well- developed interpersonal and communication skills.
Detail-oriented, organized, and able to meet deadlines. Ability to achieve deliverables and work independently.
Proficient spoken and written English and Tok Pisin language skills required.
A demonstrated high work ethic and ability to assume a high level of responsibility
Commitment to the goals and philosophy of TKCP
Work Environment:
The role will require frequent travels into harsh rugged mountainous terrains and geographical settings and requires a person who has prior experience into very remote community settings as well as someone who is of good physical health.
TKCP is an Equal Opportunity Employer, and considers all applicants based on merit without regard to race, sex, colour, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, or disability

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our supply team, you will manage supplier performance and provide the timely expediting of purchasing and procurement of goods ensuring delivered on time according to specified quantity, quality and cost requirements and within the supply policy guidelines
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Expediting on the purchases and ensure that the quality of goods and materials purchased is to K92 Mining standards and specifications.
Ensure purchasing at the optimal price in relation to quality, quantity and delivery method.
Issue recommendation for Purchase Requisition that follow K92 Mining policies and standards have been met.
Ensure appropriate documentation is completed and filed for all transactions.
Manage the supplier base ensuring high level supplier performance and cost management through regular contact with suppliers.
Review performance of key suppliers across KPIs including lead time compliance, delivery completeness & number of discrepancies
Investigate discrepancies and identify opportunities in the procure to pay process.
Investigate invoice discrepancies to ensure suppliers are paid in a timely manner.
Investigate PO and goods receipt discrepancies to ensure that goods are available on site to meet requirements
Recommend P2P process improvements in conjunction with systems enhancements
Ensure the timely completion of all expediting purchase requests.
Regular communication with internal customers to understand expectations and required timeframes when issuing purchase orders.
Follow up with suppliers to understand delays in quoting and seek alternative quotes as required
Ensure purchase requests are converted to purchase orders and issued to suppliers in a timely manner.
Manage out of hours purchase needs.
Monitor the delivery of goods and materials ensuring conformation that deliveries are completed to the K92 Mining schedules and plans.
Communicate with suppliers to ensure that specified delivery timeframes are met.
Seek alternative suppliers, or substitute products where emergency requirements or supplier failure may lead to goods not being available on site on the date required
Ensure Safety, Health and Environmental legislation is recognised in all purchasing activities.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have all or the following
Minimum 3 years’ experience in industry with relevant experience in transactional expediting purchasing
Understanding of ERP systems (Pronto) to support purchasing and expediting processes.
Negotiation skills and understanding of negotiation techniques.
Commercial analysis and evaluation.
Problem solving and decision-making capability.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
Experience communicating with vendors in PNG and Internationally to expediting according to T&C’s for supply to K92
Ability to communicate clearly with people at all levels of the organisation and engage all relevant stakeholders.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

PORT MORESBY, Papua New Guinea.
jobs.description:
Woodlark Mining Limited (WML) is engaged in Mineral Exploration and Development of Woodlark Gold Project, MBP, PNG. WML has entered an exciting phase and is now well positioned to invest and unlock the potential of the Project over the next 18 months. The Company is undertaking a comprehensive exploration program of soil sampling, trenching and drilling to continue to advance and grow the Project. With this comes new opportunities to joint WML Exploration Team on Woodlark Island, as we ramp up activities. The following FIFO National role is now available in our Exploration Team.
Senion Exploration Geologist
The Role
Reporting to the Exploration Manager, the incumbent will play a key role and lead all field teams, tasked with progressing our exploration and resource development targets from generative to resource stage. Woodlark deposit styles range from low to intermediate sulphidation with limited to data rich targets, hosted in volcanogenic terrain with complex lithologies and structural settings. This role will lead the field teams in exploration and is well suited to a field orientated senior Geologist with diverse experience in the exploration sector who wants to join a well-funded project. Possessing a real passion for exploration and a drive to find the next discovery your skills will lead and support the team to advance several exciting projects on Woodlark Island.
Safety is one of our core values at Woodlark Gold, and we expect employees to always act in a manner that seeks to enhance the safety culture and performance of our operation. Environmental stewardship and ethical conduct in exploration activities is expected.
This is a FIFO position working a roster of 4 weeks on, followed by 2 weeks off. Preferred Points of hire are subject to incumbents’ skills and experience.
About the Role:

Secondary School Teacher
EDU - RBBA - Newtown
ABOUT KTF:
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG). We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary
education
;
improving access to quality and accessible
healthcare
;
improving
equality
and access to sustainable income-generation opportunities, especially for women; and by fostering the next generation of
leaders
.   KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.
ABOUT BALIMO COLLEGE EDUCATIONAL CAMPUS
The Balimo College was established by SDP in 2019 as a pathway to brighter futures in Western Province through education. The campus is an integrated, multi-disciplinary hub that improves access to studies in education and health at all levels, through:
Balimo College - offering tertiary qualifications at the School of Teaching (Diploma & Degree studies in primary teaching) and the School of Nursing (Bachelor of General Nursing)
Balimo FODE - secondary school certification and GPA upgrades through Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE)
Western Province E-learning & teacher in-service Project - professional development and resourcing programs in schools around the area.
The Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy (RBBA) - offering a high standard of education from K1 to Grade 12, with quality resourcing across all grades and disciplines, including a library, ICT and science labs and boarding facilities for students from remote villages across Western.
HON. ROY BIYAMA BALIMO ACADEMY (RBBA):
The school commenced in 2024 and is growing rapidly, aiming to cater for 1000 students in Grades K–12 by 2028. The Academy operates in an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning that is inclusive and responsive to additional needs and removing educational barriers for local students to learn and grow in a safe and supportive environment.
ABOUT THE ROLES:
We are recruiting passionate experienced educators to join our growing team in 2026. We are seeking educators who will foster a positive school culture and the ability to drive academic excellence among their students.  Successful candidates will be part of a team of approximately 15 secondary teachers (Grades 9–12) and deliver across a combination of core and elective subjects.
Subject specialisms we are particularly seeking include:
English & Language & Literature
Social Science (History, Geography, Social Science)
Business & Economics (Business Studies, Economics)
ICT (Grades 9–12, stand-alone subject)
Agriculture (Grades 9–12, with capacity for Science support)
Teachers should be able to deliver at least one major subject and one minor (related) subject in line with the RBBA’s staffing model. Other major/minor combinations of the above subjects may be considered. Well qualified applicants with diverse skill sets will be highly received.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching: Develop and deliver lesson plans aligned with the SBC curriculum and PNG educational standards; conduct assessments and provide feedback; utilise varied teaching methods.
Student support and classroom management: Foster a positive and inclusive classroom environment; implement effective classroom management strategies; support students as they prepare for examinations.
Student Assessment: Conduct marking and assessment; provide constructive feedback; create individualised learning plans where needed.
Collaboration: Work collaboratively with colleagues within RBBA, SDP and KTF; participate in meetings and professional development activities.
Parent and Guardian Communication: Maintain open communication with parents and guardians regarding student progress; attend parent-teacher conferences and school events.
Operations: Maintain accurate student records, attendance, and assessment data; report to the Principal, Deputy Principal and Head of Teaching and Learning.
Professional Development: Stay abreast of current educational trends and participate in ongoing training.
Other: Any other duties as directed by RBBA management; adherence to all KTF policies and safeguarding standards.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor of Education – or equivalent - ESSENTIAL
Minimum 2 years teaching experience - ESSENTIAL
Full (secondary) teaching registration – ESSENTIAL
Please note that if these requirements are not met, your application will not be considered.
SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES:
Knowledge of PNG educational regulations and compliance standards.
High-level communication, mentoring and interpersonal skills.
Ability to research and apply a range of teaching strategies for diverse learners.
Competence with information and communication technologies for teaching and administration.
Openness to learning new and innovative approaches to teaching and learning.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS:
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG
Willingness to relocate to Balimo during the academic year
Compliance with KTF safeguarding standards (police check, child protection, etc.)
HOW TO APPLY:
Click the ‘Apply for This Job’ button on the right-hand side of this screen.
Fill in the required fields and upload the relevant documentation, including CV, cover letter, copy of your bachelor’s degree, your teaching registration certificate, and one written reference.
In your cover letter:
Clearly state your subject specialisms
Outline your teaching philosophy
Address your willingness and personal requirements for relocation to Balimo during the academic year
Applications will be reviewed as received.
Closing date: 4th January 2026
KTF is a child safe organisation committed to the protection of people we serve. Our recruitment and selection procedures are designed to ensure we only recruit people who are suitable and aligned with our policies that ensure the safety of children and protection of all from sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment. All appointments are subject to appropriate background checks and screening, and the successful candidate will be required to get a Police Clearance Certificate. We promote diversity and equality in all our practices and strongly encourage those with diverse backgrounds and/or disabilities and or those who identify as LGBTQI+ to apply for positions with KTF.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
At Newmont, your expertise will truly make an impact. In this role, you will enhance equipment availability and reliability, improve schedule compliance, and drive meaningful knowledge transfer across the workforce. Through hands-on coaching, you will build technical capability, strengthen problem-solving skills, and support efficient, high-performing operations.
You will play a critical role in supporting and optimising heavy mobile equipment in the mining industry, including drills, excavators, and shovels, working across major OEM platforms such as Sandvik, Epiroc, Caterpillar, and Hitachi.
As part of our team, you will
Be a trusted technical partner, working closely with maintenance and operations teams to uplift capability and improve outcomes.
Your role will include:
Coaching and mentoring the workforce in maintenance and troubleshooting activities.
Providing technical support to maintenance and operations teams to resolve complex issues.
Investigating, solving, and managing technical problems as they arise.
Collating and analysing data to identify improvement opportunities and trends.
Ensuring strict adherence to safety standards and compliance during all technical activities.
Liaising with maintenance teams to coordinate timely and effective equipment repairs.
Assisting in the development and delivery of technical training programs.
Conducting regular inspections and audits of technical processes.
Recommending and implementing improvements to technical and maintenance practices.
Managing inventories of critical spare parts and equipment.
Identifying risks, implementing mitigation strategies, and continuously monitoring risk exposure.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
To thrive in this position, you will bring a strong technical foundation and a practical, solutions-focused mindset, including:
Trade Certificate (including auto electrical and air conditioning).
Experience in technical support, maintenance, troubleshooting, data analysis, safety compliance, and process optimisation.
Proven experience with heavy mining equipment, particularly drills, excavators, and shovels.
Strong product knowledge across Sandvik, Epiroc, Caterpillar, and Hitachi equipment.
Open-cut mining experience preferred.
International assignment experience and the ability to work effectively in remote locations are advantageous.
Ability to obtain and maintain a PNG Licence.
Advanced technical capability in troubleshooting, process improvement, and safety systems.
Strong problem-solving skills with the ability to analyse complex information and turn insight into action.
Experience in risk management and supporting technical training programs.
Proactive, energetic, and able to work independently.
Adaptable to change, with the ability to think creatively and “outside the box”.
Self-aware, collaborative, and confident in giving and receiving feedback.
Your work environment
This role is offered on a 21:21 FIFO roster from Australia to tropical Lihir Island, PNG, with day shifts that may change to day and night shifts based on operational requirements.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
You will work in a collaborative, safety-first environment, partnering with supervisors, engineers, technicians, HSE teams, and external contractors and suppliers to drive continuous improvement.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll be part of a global leader in mining that values safety, integrity, sustainability, and people. We invest in our workforce, encourage innovation, and foster a culture where everyone is empowered to contribute, learn, and grow. By joining Newmont, you’re not just taking on a role you’re building a career where your skills, ideas, and commitment help shape the future of responsible mining.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply – we’d love to hear from you!
Submit your application through our website quoting reference number 41102 before the advertised closing date: 5 January 2026.

role to be based in

MAJOR ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Education Grant Framework & Planning
Develop the overall framework for grant EDUCATION in accordance to the design document and donor requirements, ensuring an effective EDUCATION framework is in place.
Identify the core information needs of grant management, partners, and funding agencies; participate in development of the annual work plan and budget, ensuring alignment with technical strategy so that EDUCATION is aligned to grant objectives and the EDUCATION Plan is in place and budget available on time.
Contribute substantial information and analyses to interdepartmental working groups on the education sector, ensuring stakeholders are included in EDUCATION process as appropriate.
Education Grant Readiness, Design & Baseline Assessment
Conduct readiness assessment: the incentives at the system level, the beneficiaries and existing capacity, ensuring strong EDUCATION processes are applied.
Give technical lead on the development, processing and administration of the grant projects in the education, ensuring education design and project plan is in place.
Provide technical leadership and integrate Grant Education policies and guidelines in the design and implementation of education projects, ensuring EDUCATION reports are available.
Identify the requirement for collecting baseline data, prepare terms-of-reference for and arrange the conduct of a baseline survey, as required, ensuring baseline research report is available.
Education Implementation, Evaluation & Data Quality Assurance
Oversee and execute EDUCATION activities with particular focus on results and impacts as well as in lesson learnt, ensuring strong EDUCATION processes are applied.
Undertake regular visits to the field to support implementation of EDUCATION and to identify where adaptations might be needed, ensuring EDUCATION reports are available and include lessons learnt.
Clarify and/or facilitate process for the technical evaluation of the Grant project’s implementation process and progress, ensuring strong EDUCATION processes are applied.
Identify the need and draw up the ToRs for specific studies; recruit, guide and supervise consultants or organizations that are contracted to implement special surveys and studies required for evaluating grant effects and impacts, ensuring well documented and targeted consultancy outcomes, if consultants are hired to support EDUCATION.
Perform regular field visits to ensure the quality of data collected by Programs and to verify the accuracy of reported data, ensuring field staff is included in EDUCATION process as appropriate and sub grantees demonstrate required M&C capacity and produce quality EDUCATION reports

Work closely with Project managers/ Coordinators, M & E Coordinator, and education project team in preparing the progress reports in accordance with approved reporting formats and ensure their timely submission, including quarterly progress reports, annual project reports, inception reports, and ad-hoc technical reports, ensuring reporting is submitted on time.

Identify strengths and weaknesses in existing data collection and management systems and propose solutions to improve knowledge management activities, ensuring high quality reporting is in place with actionable next steps and learning.
Draft tools/manuals (eg. Teacher Training, Coaching, etc.) and their revisions as well as data collection procedures (eg. logical framework, project performance tracking, indicators, data flow chart, EDUCATION manuals), ensuring teacher training manuals, coaching guide/tools reviewed and updated.
Learning, Evaluation & Capacity Strengthening
Design and implement a system to identify, analyze, document and disseminate lessons learned, ensuring lessons learnt and refresher training are well documented and include NO stakeholders and proper communication of EDUCATION findings at all levels.
Monitor the follow up on evaluation recommendations, ensuring evaluation recommendations are implemented.
Support project/program staff on ways to properly document, organize and capture program progress, ensuring proper communication of EDUCATION findings at all levels.
Facilitate, act as resource person, and join, if required any technical supervision and evaluation initiatives, ensuring EDUCATION expertise is available to the grants team and stakeholders.
Organize (and provide) refresher training in EDUCATION for grants staff, implementing partners, local organizations and primary stakeholders with view of strengthening local EDUCATION capacity, ensuring EDUCATION Capacity is provided to grants team and stakeholders and local expertise is built.
Network with external and WV internal partners to promote learning and achieve EDUCATION excellence, ensuring external networking is in place and WV represented in relevant TWGs and cluster (eg. Education Cluster).
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Advanced degree (Master’s) in Education, Economics, Public Policy or closely-related Social Science field from an internationally recognised university, or equivalent experience

Experience with programming to address gender and protection concerns and programming for very young children and adolescents/youth required

Experience leading capacity building initiatives and/or developing adult education materials for low-literacy audiences

Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What You’ll do:
Are you ready to lead impactful infrastructure projects that support community development across the Santos Foundation’s global footprint?
Based in Port Moresby we’re seeking a
Program Manager – Infrastructure
to oversee the planning, delivery, and quality assurance of our infrastructure portfolio. This is a pivotal leadership role that ensures our infrastructure initiatives—from health clinics to youth centres—are delivered to the highest standards, on time, and within budget.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of infrastructure projects across all Foundation programs.
Provide technical leadership in civil construction and infrastructure development.
Collaborate with Program Managers (Health, Youth Opportunities, FSV, Community Development) to integrate infrastructure into broader program strategies.
Manage contractors and vendors, ensuring compliance with safety, quality, and regulatory standards.
Monitor project performance, risks, and budgets, reporting to senior leadership and the Santos Foundation Board.
Build and mentor a high-performing infrastructure team.
Ensure alignment with Santos Foundation priorities, GoPNG policies, and the Santos Management System.
What You’ll bring:
You’re a seasoned infrastructure professional with:
10+ years’ experience in civil construction or engineering project management.
Proven success managing large-scale infrastructure projects in complex environments.
Strong leadership and team development capabilities.
Expertise in contractor management, budgeting, and risk mitigation.
Excellent communication skills and experience reporting to senior stakeholders.
Experience with donor-funded projects and community engagement.
Familiarity with climate-resilient and sustainable infrastructure practices.
Professional certifications (e.g., PMP, Chartered Engineer).
Degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Management, or related field.
