jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As Superintendent Geotechnical, you will play a pivotal role in safeguarding operational excellence and safety across our mining operations. Entrusted with the oversight of geotechnical activities, you will lead the formulation and execution of strategic plans to enhance slope stability, manage advanced instrumentation and monitoring programs, and ensure the integrity of mine design parameters. Your expertise will be instrumental in driving continuous improvement, risk mitigation, and the delivery of timely, accurate geotechnical insights to support our operational teams. This leadership position offers the opportunity to collaborate with multidisciplinary stakeholders, manage complex projects, and contribute meaningfully to Newmont’s commitment to responsible mining and sustainable growth.
As part of our team, you will
Lead the Mine Geotechnical team, fostering a collaborative and inclusive environment.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
In this role, you will be instrumental in supporting Newmont’s commitment to safe, efficient, and reliable operations. You will lead and develop a high-performing team of Cranes & Rigging Technicians, Supervisors, and a Coordinator. Your focus will be on delivering high-quality training, maintaining compliance, and ensuring operational excellence in equipment reliability and plant availability.
As part of our team, you will
Collaborate closely with the on-site Training team to assess and address training needs.
Conduct Cranes and Rigging training needs analysis.
Deliver training using a range of methods, including online training, developing new programs and training plans that build workforce capability.
Supervise team members in executing operational and maintenance activities within the Asset Management area.
Oversee inspections, identifying defects, system verifications, routine schedules and SOPs are completed within all safety, environmental and company compliance processes and guidelines.
Provide clear and detailed handovers each shift, outlining the status of the plant.
Prioritise and oversee contractor work, ensuring scope, parts, timing, and labour costs are agreed upon and documented in the Purchase Requisition before commencement.
Contribute to SOP creation, training record management, shift reports and SAP work request lodgements.
Coach, mentor, and support team development through regular feedback and structured training.
Ensure all operators perform isolations and issue safe work permits for maintenance activities in compliance with the site’s Permit to Work system.
Model and reinforce proactive safety behaviours.
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Proven experience working with Registered Training Organisations (RTOs) and training frameworks.
Knowledge and application of adult learning principles to enhance training delivery and team development.
Demonstrated supervisory experience coordinating and training staff in technically challenging and remote work environments.
Experience in mineral processing environments involving large-scale fixed assets.
Extensive experience in relevant rigging and crane operating roles.
Ability to conduct audits and verify competencies effectively.
Advanced Rigging Licence and Crane Open Class (High Risk Licence) is essential.
Certificate IV in Training and Assessment is essential.
Proficiency in SAP and Microsoft Office Suite.
Self-motivated, with the ability to work autonomously and perform well under pressure.
Excellent attention to detail and strong time management skills to meet deadlines.
Strong active listening and interpersonal skills for rapport building and effective training delivery.
Previous expatriate experience working in remote locations.
Your work environment
This is a 2-year, full-time fixed-term role offered on a 21:21 FIFO roster from Australia to Lihir Island. You will be working day shifts and shift work during the shutdown peak periods.
Our FIFO employees stay in a secure and comfortable camp, in an en-suited and airconditioned room equipped with mini fridge, TV and Wi-Fi. A variety of healthy meal options are catered for at our mess; and the wet mess provides a relaxed social setting where employees can unwind with a game of pool or darts.
We offer a range of recreational activities including our on-site gym and basketball court. Paid members can access the Lihir Club which has a swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, restaurant/bar area and deck with amazing Pacific Ocean views! Our café and deli are available for take away coffees and snacks, as well as local and imported grocery items (inc. fresh fruit).
Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary package, options for salary packaging and annual incentive program.
Why Join Newmont
Newmont offers more than just a job. We offer a career with purpose.
Join a global leader in responsible mining.
A global company culture built on safety, inclusion, integrity, responsibility and sustainability.
Opportunities for career growth, learning, and leadership development.

jobs.description:
With more than 40 years of experience working in PNG, World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) focuses on helping the most vulnerable children and adults experience fullness of life.  Inspired by our Christian faith, WVPNG has an exciting opportunity for someone who may be looking for a change and wants to become part of a dynamic team helping vulnerable people and communities.
World Vision Papua New Guinea (WVPNG) has an exciting opportunity for those of you who want a change and want to become part of a dynamic team. We are currently looking for a suitable, qualified, experienced, and highly motivated professional to fill the
MEAL Officer
role to be based in
Port Moresby, National Capital District.
PURPOSE OF THE POSITION
The Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) Officer for the Economic Empowerment & Resilience projects is responsible for implementing a functional MEAL system for these projects. He/she supports the project team in designing, monitoring, and evaluating Accountability and Learning in all the project’s interventions. Moreover, he/she works with the direct supervisor to coordinate and/or implement project baselines and evaluations, and to implement standardized MEAL processes and tools across all Economic Empowerment & Resilience sector projects at the field level.
1.
Program Design
Support EER MEAL Coordinator as requested in contributing to WVPNG, strategy, sectoral frameworks, overall, MEAL system set-up, and ad-hoc requests.
Support the MEAL Coordinator in leading the proposal development process regarding MEAL input (logframe, budgeting for MEAL activities and staffing, MEAL narrative plan, etc.)
Develop project-specific MEAL frameworks for EER projects in coordination with project staff.
2.
Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting
Develop methodologies, sampling plans, and tools for outcome and process monitoring studies, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, FGDs, KIIs, etc.
Plan, lead, and oversee the implementation of outcome monitoring studies for grants such as PIMs/PDMs, midline and endline studies, pre/post-tests, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (coordinate, follow up, and review the outcome monitoring methodology, tools, and reports for grants.
Lead assigned project-specific evaluations and baselines at the field level (development of ToR, selection and short-listing consultants, coordination with the consultant, review of design methodology and tools, review final reports, attend interpretation workshops, etc., if externally led; and conduct data analysis and report writing if internally led)
Implement field-level tasks for the outcome and process monitoring of the project, including pre-/post-tests, PIMs/PDMs, midline and end-line studies, FGDs, KIIs, etc. (training of casual workers, planning field data collection, coordination of data collection, supervising, facilitating, coding tools, developing datasets, data cleaning, analysis, reporting)
Provide support in training project staff and partners on reporting requirements, output level monitoring, and conduct regular training for project staff on data collection and data entry for pre-post-tests.
Conduct ITT verifications of projects in coordination with project staff each month and ensure project-level ITTs are updated with accurate data. Key findings are shared with the project team and management at the program review meetings.
Conduct regular project site visits and monitor partner & direct implementation against quality standards through scheduled visits, data quality audits, and spot checks.
Support the project teams in compiling regular quality project reports, including monthly (Monthly Management Report), Quarterly, mid-year, annual, and end-of-project reports.
Ensure that the project team and other stakeholders discuss and address critical MEAL findings and recommendations.
3
.
Accountability to Children & Communities
Assess community preferences and needs to inform the design of contextually appropriate accountability processes and share outcomes/results with communities, colleagues, and partners.
Implement the project accountability plan/design developed based on the community's preferences for providing information, consulting with communities, promoting participation, and collecting and acting on feedback and complaints.
Receive, process, and respond to feedback and complaints, and communicate progress to the children, communities, and stakeholders.
Implement the plan for sharing information based on community stakeholders' needs and preferences and adjust as needed. Collaborate with colleagues to gather relevant and accurate project information to be shared openly with communities, stakeholders, and partners.
Ensure that all feedback and complaints received from communities are promptly and accurately recorded/updated in the system, and that loops are closed within the timeline.
Sensitize community members about their right to information, consultation, participation, and providing feedback and complaints, while emphasizing their responsibility to support solutions.
Support investigation of allegations of irregularities, fraud, corruption, or other forms of misconduct by directly liaising with the affected communities, according to guidelines, and promptly, promoting trust and safety.
Engage community members in measuring the effectiveness of Accountability practices, providing recommendations for and addressing areas that need improvement in coordination with the accountability core team, and conducting other consultation activities that can support the design of new programmes.
Conduct exit interviews, observation, and reporting.
4. Research and Learning
Co-lead lessons learned events for the project with project managers and technical staff (preparation, facilitation, and report writing). Implement any potential research studies at the field level (data collection, cleaning) - (based on WVPNG strategic priorities for Evidence Building)
5. Miscellaneous
Support WVPNG-wide PQ assignments such as assessments and program design, as assigned by the supervisor.
Attend internal and external meetings relevant to assigned projects
Attend internal and external training, workshops, events, etc.
EDUCATIONAL QUALIFICATION
/SKILLS, KNOWLEDGE & EXPERIENCE
Minimum one to two years of experience in working in a relief or development NGO with a focus on MEAL processes
A BA Degree in international development, international relations, public health, nutrition, statistics, community development, project management or other relevant disciplines is required.
Experience in the design and implementation of MEAL systems, including qualitative and quantitative approaches to baselines, monitoring, and evaluations, is required
Good understanding of Accountability to communities
Good working knowledge of statistical packages (Excel, etc.) is required
Excellent knowledge of ODK database
Expert data handling skills (classification, categorization, tabulation, etc.) and demonstrates diligence in data management
Good knowledge of information presentation techniques (graphing, charting, tabling, etc.) and interpreting them
Information dissemination skills are required
Ability to work effectively under pressure
Organization, planning, and time management skills
Detail-oriented and able to verify data quality
Stays open to internal and external feedback
Good contextual knowledge of the local community and social/cultural constraints, realities, and organizational relationships
Ability to understand, explain, and contextualize MEAL tools
High-level communications skills
Ability to build positive relationships in a cross-cultural environment
Preferred working knowledge of advanced statistical packages (SPSS, etc.)
The position requires the ability to attend and participate in capacity-building opportunities, training, and meetings locally as required by the organization
A competitive salary, benefits, and career development opportunities will be offered commensurate with relevant experience, knowledge, and qualifications.

Balimo College is Western Province’s newest Higher Education Institute. In 2025, Balimo College opened the new School of Nursing and commenced a 4-year Bachelor of General Nursing program. The College’s vision is to advance Western Province by providing high-quality education, research and community engagement. The Balimo College School of Nursing Principal is responsible for upholding the College’s Vision, Mission, Core Values, Educational Philosophy and Goals. The Principal will operate within the Balimo College School of Nursing leadership structure as determined by the Chair, Governing Council, to disseminate strong, effective educational leadership, and manage all information technology within the parameters identified in this position description.
The Principal will have an in-depth knowledge of the ethos and purpose of the Balimo College School of Nursing and the principles by which it operates. jobs.description:
Summary
The Project Planner / Scheduler is responsible for developing, monitoring, and updating the project schedule across all phases of construction. This role ensures alignment between time, cost, and resource planning to support on-time and on-budget delivery. The position requires close collaboration with engineers, quantity surveyors, and project managers to monitor performance and mitigate delays.
Duties and Responsibilities
1. Pre-Construction Stage
Develop the Master Project Schedule using Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or similar tools.
Define the Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), activity sequences, durations, and dependencies.
Identify project milestones, deliverables, and critical paths for effective tracking.
Support the preparation of manpower, material, and equipment forecasts.
Coordinate with the commercial and cost teams to ensure schedule-cost alignment.
Review cost estimates with quantity surveyors and estimators for scheduling accuracy.
2. Construction Stage
Monitor actual work progress against the baseline schedule and identify variances.
Update schedules regularly based on site conditions, change orders, or revised scopes.
Highlight potential delays and assess their impact on overall project timelines.
Coordinate with project teams to propose recovery plans when needed.
Generate weekly and monthly project progress reports with visual timelines and critical path tracking.
3. Post-Construction Stage
Prepare detailed close-out schedules to support final inspections and commissioning activities.
Analyze and compare planned versus actual performance data to assess overall schedule efficiency.
Develop delay analysis and Extension of Time (EOT) reports with supporting documentation for claims.
4. Final Completion & Handover
Ensure all project planning and scheduling records are updated and properly archived.
Document lessons learned and provide input to improve future scheduling methodologies and project planning processes.
Job Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Civil Engineering, or a related field.
Minimum 3 years of hands-on experience in project planning and scheduling.
Proficient in Primavera P6, Microsoft Project, or other recognized scheduling software.
Solid understanding of construction processes, project phases, and planning principles.
Strong analytical, organizational, and time management skills.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills for preparing reports and coordinating with project stakeholders.
Ability to work independently and collaboratively under pressure in dynamic project environments.

May require occasional extended hours to meet reporting deadlines or resolve schedule issues.
Work may involve outdoor site inspections in varying weather and environmental conditions.

Simberi Gold Company Limited forms part of the St Barbara Group. Our vision is to grow sustainably and create enduring, positive impacts for the people and communities touched by our operations.
Now is an exciting time for our business and for our people. We’re going through a period of significant change and are gaining momentum in transforming our business. We’re looking for people who are ready to grow through opportunity and build a bright future with us.​​
We are currently seeking a
Senior Training Supervisor
to join our team on a permanent full-time position at our Simberi Operation. Your work location is Papua New Guinea, working a 21/14 Roster from Kavieng, Rabaul, Port Moresby, Lae, Mt Hagen, Buka, Madang, Goroka, Alotau, Wapenamanda, Popondetta, Hoskins, Vanimo, Wewak or Tabar group of Islands.

The opportunity

Ensuring safe work practices, own health and safety and all other workers by identifying hazards and ensuring issues and risks are reported and addressed.
Supporting Mining, Mill, Processing and Mobile Maintenance trainers to deliver training plans and outcomes as per the 12-month training plan
Assisting trainers to update skills matrix with current training and assessments conducted
Coordinating, overseeing, and supervising trainers to carry out their duties effectively and efficiently as per training guidelines
Providing training governance, guidance, and support for implementation of system/enablers of the training business processes
Liaising with line managers to identify training gaps and develop training need analysis
Contributing to the development of training policies and procedures

jobs.description:
Marketing Manager
Marketing - Port Moresby, NCD
Role Title: Marketing Manager
Role Type: Senior Level
Department: Marketing
Reports to: The Director – Institutional Development
Location: IBSUniversity & IBS College of TVET
Employment Type: Full-Time
Organizational Context:
The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are one of the largest business schools in the country and off degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.
Our success is the fruits of our dedicated team committed to making a difference in Papua New Guinea, through their efforts to help educate current and futures citizens on Papua New Guinea.
A Career with Us:
At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. We also have a lot of staff events that enable us to celebrate as a team and give recognition where it's due.
Job Purpose
The Marketing Manager is responsible for leading and managing all marketing, branding, promotions, recruitment support, call center operations, and stakeholder engagement across IBSUniversity, IBS College of TVET, IBS Centre of Excellence, the Research Division, and the Career Development Centre.
The role drives student enrolments, strengthens the IBS brand, builds strong school and industry partnerships, and ensures coordinated communication across all IBS business arms.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Marketing & Branding
Develop and execute annual marketing strategies aligned with IBS’s goals.
Lead brand positioning and ensure consistent branding across all IBS entities.
Oversee all advertising campaigns, promotional activities, and media engagements.
Conduct market research and track competitor trends to inform strategy.
Student Recruitment Support
Implement comprehensive recruitment campaigns for all programs.
Coordinate closely with the Call Centre, Enrolment Team, and Academic Schools to support lead conversion.
Lead Open Days, Roadshows, Career Fairs, and School Awareness events.
Call Centre Leadership & Customer Engagement
Manage and supervise the Call Centre team to ensure high-quality enquiry handling.
Set call handling standards (speed, tone, conversion approach, follow-ups).
Monitor call logs, response times, lead follow-ups, and enquiry conversion rates.
Develop call scripts, FAQs, and customer service guidelines.
Ensure daily, weekly, and monthly reporting from the Call Centre to track lead generation and conversion performance.
Coach call center staff on customer service excellence and enrolment messaging.
Partnership & MOA Development
Lead MOA signings with secondary schools in NCD, Central, and provincial areas.
Maintain strong relationships with principals, career advisers, and education leaders.
Conduct partner school outreach activities, including workshops and career sessions.
Digital Marketing & Social Media
Oversee social media strategy and content creation (Facebook, LinkedIn, Instagram, YouTube).
Manage online enquiry responses and ensure customer-friendly engagement.
Track digital analytics (leads, reach, engagement, conversion) and improve ROI.
Marketing Team Leadership
Provide direction, coaching, and performance management for all marketing staff and call center officers.
Set monthly KPIs and targets for marketing and call center teams.
Facilitate ongoing training for digital marketing, branding, and customer service skills.
Stakeholder Engagement & Community Relations
Represent IBS in community events, education expos, and corporate networking.
Strengthen IBS visibility through CSR programs and community outreach.
Build productive partnerships with churches, NGOs, businesses, and local leaders.
Support to IBS Business Arms
Deliver tailored marketing and branding support to:
IBSUniversity – academic programs and Schools
IBS College of TVET – certificate & diploma programs
IBS Centre of Excellence – corporate training, workshops & team building
Research Division – publications, conferences & awareness activities
Career Development Centre – student employability, employer partnerships
Reporting & Performance Management
Monthly marketing and call center performance reports.
Maintain updated databases for leads, conversions, partner schools, and industry stakeholders.
Ensure proper use of marketing and call center budgets.
Key Deliverables
Annual Marketing Plan & Budget
Monthly Enrolment Campaigns
Operational Call Centre Dashboard & Conversion Reports
Digital Marketing & Social Media Analytics
Signed MOAs with Secondary Schools
Updated Marketing Collateral
High community visibility and strong stakeholder networks
Qualifications & Experience
Minimum Requirements
Bachelor’s degree in marketing, Communication, Business, or related field.
Experience: 8 + years of marketing experience including minimum 3 years in a Managerial role and team leadership.
Strong experience in customer service, call center management, or sales.
Demonstrated experience in digital marketing and branding.
Desirable
Experience in education sector marketing.
Knowledge of the PNG education landscape.
Experience in public speaking or community outreach.
Skills & Competencies
Technical Skills
Marketing strategy & execution
Call center operations management
Digital marketing & social media
Event management
Market research & data interpretation
Stakeholder engagement
Soft Skills
Excellent communication and customer service
Leadership and people management
Creative problem-solving
Cultural awareness
Strong organizational ability
Personal Attributes
Confident, professional, and people-oriented
High integrity and work ethic
Passionate about youth development and education
Adaptable and able to travel as required
Committed ambassador of the IBS brand

jobs.employer_address:
PO Box 1290,
Lae, Morobe Province 411,

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
The Permit to Work (PTW) Supervisor is a part of the Processing Department who leads and guides the permit to work team to ensure the energy control & isolations and permits to work are completed to a standard that ensures that safety, environmental, and operational risks are maintained at an impeccable standard for those relying upon them to safely complete their work.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Provide leadership, coaching and mentoring to a team of Permit Issuers in their role to ensure the PTW system is being followed, eliminating exposure to risks while workers are carrying out work.
Identify and carry out safe and effective isolations in the field to ensure the safety of all personnel who are required to perform work on the equipment.  Confirm IRS documents are correct and relevant to the job to be performed.  Create new IRS documents as required.
Verify that all necessary safety procedures and controls are in place before issuing any permit. This includes confirming of risk assessments, JSEAs, and required personal protective equipment (PPE).
Take part in shutdown planning meetings, prepare IRS documents in line with shutdown plan and work lists, ensuring they are prepared for issue in line with the shutdown schedule.
Perform isolations as per the shutdown schedule, prepare permit control boards and issue permits to those performing the work. Deisolate and return the plant to operating condition as jobs are completed on equipment items.
Work closely with supervisors and safety personnel to ensure that all isolation safety precautions are understood and implemented. Provide clear guidance to workers regarding the requirements outlined in the permit, emphasising safety and emergency procedures. Notify relevant stakeholders of any changes to work conditions or permits and ensure that any new permits or revised permits are issued promptly.
Before issuing a permit, review permit receiver’s JSEA and other related documents and ensure the documents are in line with the task. Ensure compliance with established isolation and permit practices, ensuring that all personnel involved in the work are adhering to safety regulations.
Maintain filing system where all completed and returned permits are scanned into the correct folders on the K92 Processing storage. Keep accurate and up-to-date records of all issued permits, including work details, personnel involved, safety precautions, and any changes made during the work process. Report any violations of safety protocols or non-compliance with issued permits to relevant supervisors or management. Ensure that records are complete and readily available for internal and external audits, ensuring compliance with safety regulations and standards.
Organise and document weekly safety toolbox meetings.
Carry out other relative duties as directed by the Coordinator Processing
Utilising available resources, maintain equipment to a safe and efficient standard in accordance with government regulations and company policy.
Cost control.
About You
To be considered for this role, you will have some or all the following.
High school diploma or equivalent. Technical diploma or higher in engineering, such as Processing, Mechanical or Electrical, or a related field is preferred
Certification in Occupational Health and Safety, First Aid, or a relevant PTW certification is highly recommended.
Familiarity with HSE Systems: Experience with Health, Safety, and Environmental management systems and regulations (e.g., OSHA, ISO 45001, etc.).
At least 3 years of PTW experience working in minerals Processing, Oil & Gas, construction, or maintenance environments, with a specific focus on safety management.
Have worked in the mineral processing or oil and gas industry in a similar role for at least 5 years.
Proactive and able to maintain continuous improvement of the PTW system.
Proven ability to lead a team of permit issuers
Ability to maintain the high-level standards required by a PTW team and infrastructure, equipment and tooling.
Exceptional planning and execution skills
Clear understanding of P&ID and PFD drawings
Demonstrated ability to lead a team in Energy control and isolation systems
Demonstrated ability to lead a team to maintain PTW activities including for high-risk tasks.
Demonstrated knowledge and understanding of Safety, environmental systems, procedures and standards
Demonstrated ability to work with planning and scheduling teams, for preparing isolations and permits for plant shutdowns
Experience with gas testing equipment control, care, servicing and testing.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high-quality Flour, Stock Feed, Rice, Snacks, and Bakery products throughout the country. Well-known products and brands include Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Flame Oil & Sugar, Flame Rice, Bilas Bread, Skel Rice, Twisties snacks, Arthurs Pies, and the Meadow Lea range.
At GFI, we care about making food better for everyone.
Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.
We currently have an immediate vacancy for a Electrical Engineer who will be responsible for ensuring the safe, reliable, and efficient operation of all electrical systems, automation equipment, and production machinery within the Utilities Department at Goodman Fielder Lae. This role supports continuous improvement, reduces downtime, and ensures compliance with safety and quality standards across the manufacturing site. Also Responsible for following up on work in the utilities area and coordinating the daily operations of generators, air compressors, and water treatment systems. Proficient in computer operation and able to independently operate equipment such as air compressors and generators.
Your
responsibilities
will include
:
Electrical Maintenance & Troubleshooting
Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on electrical systems, motors, drives, PLCs, and control panels.
Diagnose electrical faults and implement timely solutions to minimise production downtime.
Ensure all electrical work complies with PNG electrical standards and internal safety policies.
Automation & Control Systems
Support PLC programming, SCADA systems, and automated production lines.
Monitor and optimise machine performance through control system adjustments.
Assist in upgrades, modifications, and commissioning of new equipment.
Project Engineering
Participate in engineering projects including installations, upgrades, and plant expansions.
Prepare technical specifications, drawings, and documentation for electrical works.
Liaise with contractors, suppliers, and internal stakeholders to ensure project success.
Compliance, Safety & Quality
Ensure all electrical systems meet safety, environmental, and food manufacturing compliance requirements.
Conduct risk assessments, JHAs, and contribute to continuous improvement initiatives.
Maintain accurate maintenance records and ensure audit readiness.
Continuous Improvement
Analyse equipment performance data to identify improvement opportunities.
Recommend and implement solutions to improve reliability, efficiency, and energy usage.
Support TPM, Lean, and other operational excellence programs.
To be considered for the role, you will need to have
:
Bachelor’s Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field.
Minimum 3–5 years’ experience in industrial or manufacturing environments.
Strong knowledge of PLCs (Siemens/Allen Bradley), VSDs, sensors, and automation systems.
Experience with high-voltage and low-voltage electrical systems.
Proven troubleshooting and problem-solving skills.

jobs.description:
Goodman Fielder Papua New Guinea is one of PNG’s largest food companies, manufacturing and distributing high-quality Flour, Stock Feed, Rice, Snacks, and Bakery products throughout the country. Well-known products and brands include Flame Flour, Flame Stockfeed, Flame Oil & Sugar, Flame Rice, Bilas Bread, Skel Rice, Twisties snacks, Arthurs Pies, and the Meadow Lea range.
At GFI, we care about making food better for everyone.
Our goal is to be the leading and most innovative food company with a mission to meet our customers’ needs for superior quality foods with brands that are trusted by families everywhere.  We are the go-to source of consumer, shopper, and customer insights to help our customer and business partners succeed.
We currently have an immediate vacancy for a Boiler Technician who is responsible for the safe, efficient, and compliant operation of the site’s boiler systems and associated utilities. This role ensures continuous steam supply to production lines, performs routine maintenance, and supports the overall reliability of utilities infrastructure at GFI Lae. This Purpose of this position is to Monitor all boiler operators and attend to any Boiler maintenance problem or break down including boiler water quality testings as well(Contains some statistical analysis) Able to operate the RO system proficiently and continuously monitor water quality.
Your
responsibilities
will include
:
Boiler Operation & Monitoring
Operate, monitor, and control boiler systems to ensure consistent steam supply for production.
Conduct routine checks on pressure, temperature, water levels, fuel supply, and safety devices.
Record operational data in logbooks and digital systems.
Maintenance & Repairs
Perform preventive and corrective maintenance on boilers, feed pumps, valves, burners, and water treatment systems.
Troubleshoot mechanical, electrical, and control issues affecting boiler performance.
Assist in major shutdowns, overhauls, and inspections.
Safety & Compliance
Ensure all boiler operations comply with PNG safety regulations and internal GFI policies.
Maintain and test safety valves, alarms, gauges, and emergency shutdown systems.
Support workplace safety initiatives, including hazard identification and risk assessments.
Water Treatment & Quality Control
Monitor and maintain boiler water quality, including chemical dosing and blowdown procedures.
Conduct water tests to prevent scaling, corrosion, and carryover.
Documentation & Reporting
Maintain accurate maintenance records, daily logs, and incident reports.
Report abnormalities, breakdowns, and potential risks to the Utilities Supervisor.
Cross‑Functional Support
Assist with other utilities systems such as air compressors, generators, and refrigeration units when required.
Support production teams during peak operations or emergencies.

:
Trade Certificate in Mechanical Engineering, Fitting & Machining, or related field.
PNG Boiler Operator Certification (Class 1 or Class 2).
Minimum 3 years’ experience operating industrial boilers (fire‑tube or water‑tube).
Strong understanding of boiler safety standards and water treatment processes.
Work Environment
Industrial manufacturing setting with exposure to heat, steam, noise, and rotating machinery.
Requires use of PPE and adherence to GFI safety protocols at all times

ABOUT KTF:
KTF is an Australian international aid and development organisation working in Papua New Guinea (PNG). We work with people and communities to improve the lives and futures of Papua New Guineans. We do this by: assisting remote and rural communities with access to elementary and primary
education
;
improving access to quality and accessible
healthcare
;
improving
equality
and access to sustainable income-generation opportunities, especially for women; and by fostering the next generation of
leaders
.   KTF is a member of the Australian Council for International Development and is accredited with the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade’s Australian Not-for-Profit Cooperation Program.
ABOUT BALIMO COLLEGE EDUCATIONAL CAMPUS
The Balimo College was established by SDP in 2019 as a pathway to brighter futures in Western Province through education. The campus is an integrated, multi-disciplinary hub that improves access to studies in education and health at all levels, through:
Balimo College - offering tertiary qualifications at the School of Teaching (Diploma & Degree studies in primary teaching) and the School of Nursing (Bachelor of General Nursing)
Balimo FODE - secondary school certification and GPA upgrades through Flexible Open Distance Education (FODE)
Western Province E-learning & teacher in-service Project - professional development and resourcing programs in schools around the area.
The Hon. Roy Biyama Balimo Academy (RBBA) - offering a high standard of education from K1 to Grade 12, with quality resourcing across all grades and disciplines, including a library, ICT and science labs and boarding facilities for students from remote villages across Western.
HON. ROY BIYAMA BALIMO ACADEMY (RBBA):
The school commenced in 2024 and is growing rapidly, aiming to cater for 1000 students in Grades K–12 by 2028. The Academy operates in an environment conducive to quality teaching and learning that is inclusive and responsive to additional needs and removing educational barriers for local students to learn and grow in a safe and supportive environment.
ABOUT THE ROLES:
We are recruiting passionate experienced educators to join our growing team in 2026. We are seeking educators who will foster a positive school culture and the ability to drive academic excellence among their students.  Successful candidates will be part of a team of approximately 15 secondary teachers (Grades 9–12) and deliver across a combination of core and elective subjects.
Subject specialisms we are particularly seeking include:
English & Language & Literature
Social Science (History, Geography, Social Science)
Business & Economics (Business Studies, Economics)
ICT (Grades 9–12, stand-alone subject)
Agriculture (Grades 9–12, with capacity for Science support)
Teachers should be able to deliver at least one major subject and one minor (related) subject in line with the RBBA’s staffing model. Other major/minor combinations of the above subjects may be considered. Well qualified applicants with diverse skill sets will be highly received.
RESPONSIBILITIES:
Teaching: Develop and deliver lesson plans aligned with the SBC curriculum and PNG educational standards; conduct assessments and provide feedback; utilise varied teaching methods.
Student support and classroom management: Foster a positive and inclusive classroom environment; implement effective classroom management strategies; support students as they prepare for examinations.
Student Assessment: Conduct marking and assessment; provide constructive feedback; create individualised learning plans where needed.
Collaboration: Work collaboratively with colleagues within RBBA, SDP and KTF; participate in meetings and professional development activities.
Parent and Guardian Communication: Maintain open communication with parents and guardians regarding student progress; attend parent-teacher conferences and school events.
Operations: Maintain accurate student records, attendance, and assessment data; report to the Principal, Deputy Principal and Head of Teaching and Learning.
Professional Development: Stay abreast of current educational trends and participate in ongoing training.
Other: Any other duties as directed by RBBA management; adherence to all KTF policies and safeguarding standards.
QUALIFICATIONS:
Bachelor of Education – or equivalent - ESSENTIAL
Minimum 2 years teaching experience - ESSENTIAL
Full (secondary) teaching registration – ESSENTIAL
Please note that if these requirements are not met, your application will not be considered.
SKILLS & ATTRIBUTES:
Knowledge of PNG educational regulations and compliance standards.
High-level communication, mentoring and interpersonal skills.
Ability to research and apply a range of teaching strategies for diverse learners.
Competence with information and communication technologies for teaching and administration.
Openness to learning new and innovative approaches to teaching and learning.
OTHER REQUIREMENTS:
Applicants must have the right to work in PNG
Willingness to relocate to Balimo during the academic year
Compliance with KTF safeguarding standards (police check, child protection, etc.)
HOW TO APPLY:
Click the ‘Apply for This Job’ button on the right-hand side of this screen.
Fill in the required fields and upload the relevant documentation, including CV, cover letter, copy of your bachelor’s degree, your teaching registration certificate, and one written reference.
In your cover letter:
Clearly state your subject specialisms
Outline your teaching philosophy
Address your willingness and personal requirements for relocation to Balimo during the academic year
Applications will be reviewed as received.
Closing date: 4th January 2026

jobs.description:
TITLE
Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Coordinator
REPORTING TO
Senior Program Manager, East New Britain
LOCATION
Kokopo or Rabaul, East New Britain Province
START DATE
END DATE
1 January 2026
31 December 2028
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is within the National Capital District, Central Province in the Southern Region, East Sepik Province in the Momase region and East New Britain Province in the New Guinea Islands. We work nationally through a system strengthening approach with the Government of PNG.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations, and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
Position Summary
WaterAid is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Coordinator to join our team in East New Britain Province. The role will work collaboratively with the project implementation team to coordinate collection, analysis, reporting and use of project monitoring from two key projects: The PacFresh H20 Program implemented in Rabaul and Pomio districts and the KIWA Initiative implemented in Rabaul district. The role will also involve close collaboration with WaterAid PNG Headquarters located in Port Moresby, and the Regional team based in Australia. They will also contribute to broader organisational learning initiatives, helping to share key lessons from East New Britain across the region.
About the Projects
The Protecting Freshwater Resources in the Pacific (PacFresh H2O) Project aims to strengthen the climate resilience of rural communities in Rabaul and Pomio districts by improving access to safe, reliable water and sanitation, protecting freshwater resources, and advancing gender equality and social inclusion. Through a system-strengthening approach, the project builds the skills of local decision-makers and community groups, improves coordination and planning, implements priority measures to address water insecurity, and supports the scale-up of climate-resilient WASH approaches through stronger policy integration, learning and financing. The project ensures that women, people with disabilities and other marginalised groups benefit from more resilient WASH services and improved livelihoods.
The Kiwa Initiative Preserve Project aims to strengthens climate resilience in vulnerable rural and coastal communities by protecting and restoring freshwater and watershed ecosystems through nature-based solutions. The project seeks to improve reliable access to safe water, reduce climate-related risks such as droughts, flooding and contamination, and promote community-led resource management that embeds gender equality, disability inclusion and local knowledge. By building the capacity of government partners, community groups and rights-holder organisations, the project embeds sustainable ecosystem management practices and supports more resilient and secure livelihoods in the face of increasing climate impacts.
Key performance areas / Accountabilities
Project Monitoring
Work with Programs Team members to develop, implement and review project-level monitoring, evaluation and learning frameworks and theories of change to ensure they are feasible, meaningful, and fit for purpose.
Lead development of data collection tools and coordinate regular collection of quantitative and qualitative project monitoring data aligned with project MEL Frameworks.
Lead and oversee the MEL framework in WaterAid Programme Systems (WAPS) updating the indicator and results for the projects and report to the SMT and WA Regional Team.
Ensure all the indicators and results are updated and reviewed on monthly and quarterly basis and reported aligning to the CCPM.
Build capacity of project staff and partners in MEL and support regular analysis of data to inform project activities and reporting.
Ensure that cross cutting issues, such as gender equality, disability equity, climate change and sector strengthening are adequately and appropriately reflected in project MEL Frameworks and reporting;
Identify opportunities to further engage the community in the planning, monitoring and review of WASH services and work with local authorities and community representatives to design and implement feedback mechanisms about community access to water, sanitation and hygiene services.
Leader the use of dashboard in WAPS to monitor the programming work and the support to provide fortnightly and monthly.
Support the filling of the WA Risk template offline and upload to WAPS register and regular monitor and update in WAPS.
Project reviews and evaluation
Support project reviews and evaluations, including contributing to developing Terms of Reference, coordinating in-country field work, collating and sharing existing project monitoring data with the evaluation team and contributing to sense-making activities.
Support the program team to carry-out the Project Health Checks using the template in WAPS and review the MEL information and complete the rating for projects on six monthly basis.
Learning & Documentation
Support to gather information on practices in the field and support staff and partners to document best practices from their work and disseminate internally and externally
Collect and disseminate results, best practices and lessons learned internally and externally
Support the Senior Program Manager to organise and facilitate regular project reflections, and contribute to broader organisational reflections such as quarterly reflection meetings and annual meetings.
Support WaterAid staff and partners to use WAPS M&E data and information to improve programme and organisational performance. Develop and coordinate learning processes between project teams within WaterAid PNG and implementing partners to encourage cross-project learning and information sharing.
Actively promote and engage in learning processes between WaterAid country programs and contribute to global publications and global learning events based on the PNG experience
Communications and Working Relationships
Internal
WaterAid PNG
WaterAid Australia (participation in learning events etc)
WaterAid global intranet (participation in webinars and other online learning platforms)
External
Multiple governmental, non-government and community stakeholders
Physical Environment and Demands
High travel requirements within East New Britain Province and potentially occasional travel to Port Moresby.
Level of contact with children
The role may involve engaging with communities to develop and collect monitoring information, and as such may come into contact with children. The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times.
Person Specification and Selection Criteria
The following criteria will be used to assess candidates for the post.
All applicants must address these criteria in their application:
Criteria
Experience
Substantial experience working on monitoring, evaluation and learning in the community/ international development sector (experience in the WASH sector is an advantage but not essential), including designing monitoring tools, collecting data and analysing and reporting.
Experience integrating cross-cutting issues such as gender equality and social inclusion, climate change and sector strengthening into MEL systems.
Knowledge and skills
A thorough understanding of, and experience using different monitoring and evaluation theories and practices, including both qualitative and quantitative approaches.
A high degree of knowledge of theory of change and how to use data and evidence to improve practice.
An understanding of gender equality and social inclusion issues in the PNG context, and good practice approaches to addressing these.
Knowledge of good practice capacity building approaches and skills to implement them.
Education
Minimum Bachelor degree in a relevant field such as Project Management, Social Sciences, Development Studies or a related field.
Personal qualities
Commitment to WaterAid’s values and safeguarding standards
Personable with a sensitivity to the communication styles of external stakeholders and internal staff.
Confidence working with both government and non-government stakeholders.
Commitment to the ‘Do No Harm’ approach to aid and development work.
Recruitment process
This position is open to Papua New Guinean candidates only
Applications for this role must comprise of:

A curriculum vitae (maximum 4 pages). The CV must include three professional referees (referees will not be contacted until after interviews, with permission from the candidate).
Applications which do not address the Selection Criteria specified and the page limits will NOT be considered.
Late and incomplete applications will not be accepted.

jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our growing mine site, the Senior IT Officer will ensure all IT systems, equipment, and services at the mine are set up, maintained, and secure. This role supports the team by solving IT issues onsite, guiding and coaching junior staff and technicians, and ensuring all work follows company IT and Communications policies.
The Senior IT Officer also helps with the installation and support of hardware and software, provides administration support, and keeps safety and health as top priorities. This role is key in making sure the mine can operate smoothly and safely with reliable technology.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include
Oversee the day-to-day running of IT systems and services across the site.
Provide technical support and guidance to users, addressing IT issues and requests.
Lead and support the setup, maintenance, and improvement of computers, servers, networks, and communication equipment.
Coordinate and deliver IT projects and upgrades as needed.
Ensure regular maintenance, monitoring, and backup of IT systems and data.
Work with business applications and provide administration support.
Ensure IT systems and practices remain secure, up to date, and aligned with company policies.
Train and support staff in using IT systems and following best practices.
Guide, mentor, and provide leadership to junior IT staff and technicians.
Collaborate with external IT vendors and partners as required.
Support safety standards and company values in all IT activities.
Maintain clear documentation and records.
Take part in IT planning and budgeting for the site.
Review and recommend improvements to current IT processes and systems.
Support audits and compliance activities related to IT.
Assist with asset management of IT equipment and resources.
Communicate updates and changes in IT systems or processes to all relevant staff.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must have a Diploma or Tertiary qualification in IT with a minimum of 2 years work experience in IT roles in extractive industry (mining preferred). In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Good understanding of IT and Communications Systems, both hardware and software.
Able to explain technical ideas simply, both in writing and speaking.
Good organisational and problem-solving skills.
Ability to coach, mentor, and support junior IT staff and technicians.
Additional training or certificates in IT, business analysis, project management, or IT security.
Knowledge of best practices for IT security and data protection.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.

jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your impact
As a Supervisor, Planning and Scheduling you’ll support the execution of maintenance planning activities, helping ensure efficient scheduling, resource coordination, and compliance with operational and safety standards. Your work will directly contribute to operational reliability and team development at the Lihir site.
As part of our team, you will
Assist in developing and executing maintenance plans aligned with operational goals
Coordinate personnel, equipment, and materials for effective maintenance
Monitor asset performance and track KPIs to support improvement initiatives
Ensure compliance with health, safety, environmental, and regulatory standards
Conduct reliability checks and support root cause analysis
Implement preventive maintenance programs
Use predictive maintenance tools under guidance
Compile and submit reports on maintenance activities
Support budget monitoring and report variances
Contribute to team development through feedback, coaching, and training
Prerequisites for your success in this role
Trade qualification or relevant technical background is highly regarded
Solid understanding of maintenance planning and reliability principles
Proven track record in effectively managing maintenance planning and scheduling processes
Familiarity with safety and regulatory requirements
Experience in building team capabilities and providing leadership in change management
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, Outlook)
Proficient in relevant planning and scheduling systems and tools (SAP and FRM systems)
Strong attention to detail and administrative skills
Effective communication and collaboration skills
Commitment to Newmont’s values and operational goals
Your work environment
You’ll be part of the Fixed Plant Maintenance team at the Lihir site, leading 8–10 direct reports. You’ll collaborate with internal teams like Asset Management, Maintenance Execution, Supply Chain, Health & Safety, Reliability Engineering, and Finance, as well as external partners such as OEMs, contractors, government agencies, and community representatives. The environment is inclusive and safety-focused, with a strong emphasis on team development and open communication. You’ll also enjoy a family-friendly 21:21 roster, designed to support your work-life balance.
Why Join Newmont
Newmont offers a supportive, inclusive, and safety-driven culture where your contributions are valued. You’ll have opportunities for professional growth, team development, and the chance to make a meaningful impact on operational reliability and safety at one of the world’s leading mining companies.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 18 December 2025– we’d love to hear from you!

The Institute of Business Studies (IBS), from its’ humble beginning in 1987 as an arm of Nades & Associates primarily providing revision classes for the needs of Papua New Guinea Institute of Accountants (now CPA PNG), has evolved into a private University level Institution over the last 38 years. Today we are one of the largest business schools in the country and off degree programmes in the fields of Accounting & Finance, Business & Management, Economics & Development Studies and Information Technology. We also continue to provide study pathways for grade 10 & 12 school leavers including industry accreditations for those seasoned professionals who want to get certified in their field.

At IBS we believe that everyone has been gifted with natural talents and learnt skills. Our recruitment process is designed to help candidates understand this and enable us to better match you with a role that you will not only be able to do but enjoy doing. Career progression is also important to us and believes that each employee should be at the driving seat of their career progression - this means your manager will discuss with you where you want to be in the future and be more of a coach for you in terms of giving you feedback on areas you need to work on to be your best and achieve your goals. Managing a team of QA Officers and Analysts, coordinating testing activities across projects, liaising with other departments, providing technical guidance, and ensuring quality standards are met.

Manage the day-to-day work of Level 3 and Level 4 staff (Officers and Analysts).

Ensure the team follows the established QA framework and standards.
Contribute to the compilation of Quality Assurance reports.

A degree or equivalent in the relevant discipline.
Professional Qualification (Or reaching the final level) in Accounting, Auditing, Risk Management, Compliance, or any other relevant field.
Two to Three Years' Experience in Risk Management, Auditing, Compliance, Education Administration, or any similar relevant field.

Upward movement to Quality Assurance Manager (Level 1) shall take place after 4-6 years of experience, with a proven track record of leadership and successful project delivery.

jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
Based in Moro, Southern Highlands Province, you will serve as the Team Leader – Aviation, supporting the Manager Aviation, EA, and PNG, while working closely with the management of Santos’ Aviation Operations in PNG.
In this role, you will be responsible for:
Fixed-wing and rotary-wing operations, including charter, company-owned aircraft, and regular public transport.
Aerodrome and helicopter landing site operations
Emergency response (ER) and Search and Rescue (SAR) capabilities
Security flights coordination
Reporting and compliance in alignment with company values and the Santos Management System.
This is a FIFO position offered on a 28/28 roster. We are open to expatriate applications with a point of hire Brisbane airport.
Key Accountabilities:
Assist in identifying, assessing, and monitoring aviation-related risks across Papua New Guinea operations.
Manage and support implementation of risk control measures and continuous improvement initiatives.
Provide coaching and mentoring to Papua New Guinean teams to support safe and efficient operations.
Assist with oversight of regional aviation activities, including helicopter operations, aerodrome and heli-base management, fixed-wing charter, and Regular Public Transport (RPT) services.
Support the establishment and coordination of Level 1 and Level 2 assurance activities and compliance programs.
Monitor contractor performance against service level agreements and contract scopes.
Support the Aviation Manager EA/PNG with designing and optimising aviation solutions and developing aviation contracting and commercial strategies
Provide aviation subject matter input during major incident and emergency response scenarios.
What you’ll bring:
Your proven experience in aviation operations including onshore/offshore aviation support, Emergency response and SAR, CASA key personnel responsibilities under AOC/MRO frameworks are essential.
You will have knowledge of Civil Aviation Safety Regulations, IOGP standards, IATA/ICAO frameworks, SMS, risk assessment, incident investigation, and operational auditing.
Your ability to travel domestically and internationally, including remote locations is required and you must meet CASA “fit and proper person” criteria.
Ideally you will also have:
Experience managing aviation operations in remote or complex environments
Aviation safety, quality, and risk management experience
Involvement in fixed-wing charter or multi-modal logistics planning
Knowledge of RPAS integration
Degree or diploma in aviation, engineering, or safety (or equivalent)
LAME or ATPL license
Certified or trained safety/aviation auditor (ISO 9001)
Certified or trained safety/aviation investigator (ICAM, NTSB)
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
You will play a key role in ensuring a safe and healthy work environment by conducting field inspections, safety audits, and incident investigations. Your efforts will directly support operational leaders in identifying and managing safety risks, helping to eliminate workplace injuries and illnesses.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Monitor field activities and conduct safety audits to identify hazards and ensure compliance.
Deliver hands-on safety coaching and training to site personnel.
Implement safety protocols and procedures tailored to on-site conditions.
Support and contribute to safety programs, including fatality and incident management, injury reduction, and health & wellbeing initiatives.
Assist in executing the site-based Health & Safety plan.
Influence and support frontline leaders in safe work execution.
Coordinate OHS Representative programs and operationalize safety management systems.
Support assurance programs for Health & Safety standards and processes.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Knowledge of industry-recognized health & safety systems, standards, and regulations (e.g., OSHA, MSHA).
Experience with safety investigations, risk assessment, and change management.
Competency in implementing health & safety systems and standards.
Foundational skills in project management, data analysis, and commercial processes (budgets, planning, reporting).
Strong communication, influencing, and collaboration skills.
Self-awareness and a commitment to continuous improvement and team success.
Your Work Environment
You’ll be part of the Safety & Sustainability team, working closely with operational supervisors, H&S peers, and site personnel. The role is field-based on a 21:21 roster, requiring hands-on engagement and collaboration across disciplines to maintain a safe and productive workplace.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, you’ll contribute to a culture that values safety, teamwork, and continuous improvement. You’ll have opportunities to develop your skills, make a meaningful impact, and be part of a diverse and supportive team committed to excellence in health and safety.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 16 December 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!
