jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our underground mining team, this role reports to the Shotcrete Supervisor and is required to ensure that all aspects of shotcrete spraying are carried out in a safe and efficient manner and in accordance with K92 Mining site requirements and procedures
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Operate a shotcrete rig and underground equipment to apply fibrecrete
Inspect ground conditions,
Conduct QA/QC tests, maintain equipment, and support daily mining operations.
Work closely with the Mining shift boss to assess performance and identify improvements to maximise results, reduce risk and minimise wastage of consumables.
Responsible for ongoing communication with supervisors.
Responsible for processing of detailed daily reports to the supervisors and his oncoming shift.
Responsible for housekeeping as per standard.
Maintain work relationship with all working crews during shift hours.
Responsible to safely operate the equipment.
Actively promotes a safe and healthy culture.
Demonstrates personal responsibility for own health and safety whilst setting clear expectations of relevant legal obligations, safe workplace practices and HSE operating practices to others, holding them accountable for their actions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around responsible work area.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must obtain a minimum qualification of Grade 10 or above with experience in operating Shotcrete equipment’s. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Experience in shotcrete spraying
Must have operating certificate.
Ability to work with close supervision.
Must have Underground Mining experience preferred.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
THIS POSITION IS OPEN ONLY TO CANDIDATES WHO HAVE THE RIGHT TO LIVE & WORK IN PNG WITHOUT SPONSORSHIP

Trophy Haus shopping & retail Papua New Guinea’s Home of Genuine Brand in Sports, Fashion & Lifestyle. Largest range of trophies, shields, medals plus expert customization services! We seek a dynamic and experienced Technical Supervisor to join our technical team.
Job Vacancy: Technical Supervisor
Company: Trophy Haus
Location: Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea
Position Overview:
The Technical Supervisor at Trophy Haus is a specialized role combining technical expertise with team leadership. This position requires mastery of engraving equipment, heat press, and sublimation machinery, along with strong design capabilities and customer service excellence. The ideal candidate will support the Technical Manager to manage production workflows, oversee bulk orders, and lead a technical team to deliver exceptional personalized products.

Technical Operation Management
Operate and maintain engravement machine, heat press, and sublimation equipment to the highest standards.
Execute restringing jobs with precision and quality craft man ship.
Create and modify designs using Adobe Illustrator and other design software.
Ensure all equipment is properly calibrated, maintained, and operating efficiently.

Experience managing high-volume and bulk order work flows.
Attention to detail and commitment to quality standards.
Ability to multitask and prioritize in fast-paced environment.

jobs.title: SGSC Geomechanic
jobs.employer_address:
PO Box 842
Port Moresby
NCD 121
Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
Don’t come for an easy career. Stay for a rewarding one.
Santos is a global energy company committed to increasingly cleaner energy and fuels production, with operations across Australia, Papua New Guinea, Timor-Leste and North America.
We are currently PNG’s largest single investor and most active explorer, operating all the country’s producing oil fields and holding an extensive appraisal and exploration portfolio. Our aspirations and strategies reflect our genuine commitment to making a meaningful contribution to the lives of Papua New Guineans.
At Santos, our commitment is to be a global leader in the transition to cleaner energy and clean fuels, by helping the world decarbonise to reach net-zero emissions in an affordable and sustainable way.
Santos is one of Australia’s biggest domestic gas supplier, a leading Asia Pacific LNG supplier and is committed to supplying the critical fuels such as oil and gas in a more sustainable way through decarbonising projects such as the Moomba CCS project.
For more than 65 years, Santos has been working in partnership with local communities, providing local jobs and business opportunities, safely and sustainably developing its natural gas resources, and powering industries and households.
What you’ll do:
The Geomechanic will play a key role in establishing Santos’ PNG National Lead Support Centre in Port Moresby.
You’ll work closely with the Geomechanics Group to provide expert support across a range of studies, including wellbore stability, pore pressure and fracture gradient prediction, subsidence and fracture modelling, seal integrity, sand/fines production, natural fracture characterisation, and fault and cap seal analysis.
Given the scope of the SGSC’s work, the role involves collaboration with teams across Santos’ assets and may require travel to field locations as necessary.
Key Responsibilities
Complete offset well reviews with a focus on geomechanical issues, including wellbore stability, losses, and fracture stimulation challenges.
Contribute to pre-drill and while-drilling assessments of in situ stress, pore pressure, and fracture gradient.
Provide geomechanics support to multidisciplinary studies across all business areas, including conventional and unconventional reservoirs and Carbon Sequestration projects.
Integrate core and image log-scale fracture and fault interpretations with broader seismic interpretation, including analysis of image logs and core.
Supervise rock strength testing of core samples.
Apply Santos standard file management, archiving processes, and procedures to project files for Technical Assistants.
Foster a technical environment that promotes cross-discipline collaboration, generation of new ideas, and technical excellence.
Represent the SGSC, upholding Santos’ values and behavioural expectations with internal and external stakeholders.
Ensure compliance with the Santos Management System (SMS), Delegation of Authority (DOA), and Corporate Governance and Safety requirements.
What you’ll bring:
Essential experience:
Demonstrate some experience in geoscience or engineering roles.
Hold a tertiary qualification in geoscience or a relevant engineering discipline.
Apply a high level of computer literacy in MS Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and Access.
Communicate effectively, both orally and in writing, to liaise with internal Santos stakeholders.
Build and maintain strong working relationships within a culturally diverse workforce.
Work independently with limited direction, meet deadlines, and perform effectively under pressure.
Desirable experience:
Apply knowledge or experience of drilling and subsurface operations.
Utilise a broad range of industry software, such as Wellview, RokDoc, Petrel, or equivalent.
Technical Competencies
Analyse reservoir geomechanics, including in-situ stress, pore pressure, and natural fracturing.
Plan and assess wellbore stability, including mud window calculations and failure mitigation.
Understand and recognise the mechanisms for over and under-pressure and compute basic PPFG plots
Apply laboratory testing to derive rock strength and deformability parameters.
Analyse seal integrity analysis using Fault plane orientation relative to regional stress field (fault seal prediction) and/or top seal integrity using capillary pressure and brittleness/strength indicators
Interpret hydraulic fracture data (Frac, DFIT, XLOT, LOT, FIT) and derive rock mechanics properties.
Analyse pressure data to prepare potentiometric surfaces, water classification, and salinity maps
What you’ll get:
Here, you’ll be amongst high-calibre people and get to work on industry-leading projects. We don’t shy away from solving tough problems at pace. We like it that way. You can expect to be challenged and supported; to learn and grow.
At Santos, we’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive. This means a place that is safe; where you are valued and respected, and your contribution is recognised and appreciated. Join us, and you’ll play a role in this too.
Each of our sites offer access to specific amenities that aim to create the best possible benefits to your health, wellbeing and performance.
What you’re part of:
Everywhere you turn you will be a part of a team who are coming together to contribute to our single uniting purpose - to provide reliable and affordable energy to help create a better world for everyone
And because it’s not only what you do, but how you do it, you will also contribute to improving the living standards of the communities where we operate, building enduring and respectful relationships that serve a generation. It’s about each of us, and all of us – together.
How to Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online recruitment system before
COB Friday 28th November 2025.
A requirement of this role is that you will need to have in place the legal work rights for PNG to apply.
Potential Scams
There are a number of fake adverts that are impersonating Santos Limited, in these instances you will receive an e-mail from a generic e-mail address. We do not make offers without interviews or due diligence taking place. You will know if an advert is genuine if you are directed to the Santos company careers page to apply which is
https://recruitment.santos.com/

Financial Reporting Leadership: Coordinate and lead the financial reporting cycles, including monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting, ensuring timely and accurate consolidation of PNG asset results and commentary.

Quality Assurance: Review outputs from Finance Business Partners to ensure accuracy, completeness, and quality of financial analysis and reporting.

A minimum of 10 years appropriately related work experience.

Experience in recommending and implementing process improvements relating to systems and reporting.

New Porgera Limited (NPL) is a company incorporated in Papua New Guinea and owns the Porgera Gold Mine in Enga Province. The Porgera Gold Mine will employ nearly 3,000 Papua New Guineans at full production, and over the last 30 years of life of the mine it has contributed approximately 10% of Papua New Guinea’s total annual exports
NPL is currently seeking a qualified and experienced individual to join the Capital & Projects team as a
Senior Surveyor.
About the role
Reporting to the Superintendent- Construction Projects, the Senior Surveyor is responsible for leading and managing all surveying activities associated with large-scale capital infrastructure projects. This role involves planning, executing, and overseeing land, construction, and engineering surveys to ensure accurate data collection, alignment, and compliance with project specifications and regulatory standards. The Senior Surveyor collaborates closely with project engineers, planners, and construction teams to support successful project delivery from inception to completion.
In this role, you will.
Lead and coordinate surveying activities for capital projects including topographical surveys, boundary surveys, construction staking, and as-built surveys.
Interpret and analyze project plans, drawings, and specifications to develop accurate survey methodologies and work plans.
Conduct site inspections to assess conditions and resolve surveying challenges in the field.
Manage survey data collection, processing, and quality assurance to ensure high accuracy and reliability.
Prepare detailed survey reports, maps, and documentation for use by engineering and construction teams.
Supervise and mentor junior surveyors and field technicians, ensuring adherence to safety and quality standards.
Coordinate with project stakeholders, including contractors, engineers, architects, and regulatory agencies.
Ensure all surveying activities comply with relevant legal, environmental, and safety regulations.
Utilize advanced surveying equipment such as total stations, GPS/GNSS, drones, and laser scanning technology.
Assist in budget planning and resource allocation for surveying components of capital projects.
Troubleshoot and resolve technical issues related to surveying and measurement.
Work with other seniors, surveyors and contractors to complete projects works on sites outside of the SML
Maintain a high level of health, safety and environmental awareness and comply with all relevant NPL policies & procedures.
About You
To succeed in this role, the ideal candidate will possess the following qualifications and experiences:
Bachelor’s degree in surveying, Geomatics, Civil Engineering, or a related field.
Professional Surveyor certification/licensure preferred (e.g., RPLS, CP Surveyor).
Minimum of 5-7 years of progressive experience in surveying within capital infrastructure or construction projects.
Strong knowledge of surveying principles, techniques, and equipment.
Proficiency in surveying software (e.g., AutoCAD Civil 3D, GIS, Trimble Business Center).
Excellent leadership, communication, and interpersonal skills.
Ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team.
Strong problem-solving skills and attention to detail.
Willingness to work in various site conditions, including challenging terrain and weather.
Valid driver’s license and willingness to travel to project sites as required.
Demonstrated well-developed communication, leadership and technical skills within a multi-disciplined mine team in a medium to large Mining Operation as well as Civil or Community Projects setting
High level understanding of all relevant legislation affecting the employment and safety of persons in the mining industry in PNG
Why New Porgera
In return, you will be joining a world-class mining operation with the opportunity to impact the development and upskilling of our predominantly local workforce, combined with a team keen to learn and absorb knowledge. This offers a unique opportunity to further shape the department and improve plant performance and people knowledge.  You will be joining an operation that safety and lead a team towards best-in-class safety practices whilst contribute to the development of a highly capable national workforce, making a lasting impact on the industry.
Mobilization Requirement
This position is open to
PNG Citizens
Only

jobs.employer_address: P. O Box 789, Port Moresby 121, Papua New Guinea
jobs.description:
About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.
Your Impact
As a Lead People Business Partner, reporting to the Director People, you will play a critical role in shaping workforce strategies, ensuring compliance with labour agreements, and fostering a positive employee experience. Your leadership will directly influence operational success and organizational culture at our Lihir site.
As Part of Our Team, You Will
Provide leadership, coaching and supervision to the People Business Partner team on day to day operational matters
Lead workforce planning and analysis.
Provide advisory support to leaders on all People-related matters.
Execute non-escalated investigations and disciplinary matters in line with standards and procedures.
Manage labour unrest risks and ensure compliance with CBAs.
Support and deliver enterprise led programs and initiatives within the operations by collaborating with other functions within the People Team.
Oversee workplace resources and administrative services.
Foster an inclusive team environment that encourages collaboration and feedback.
Prerequisites for Your Success in This Role
Education:
Bachelor’s degree in Human Resources, Business Administration, or related field.
Experience:
Advanced knowledge in labour relations, disciplinary processes, and project execution.
Skills:
Strong leadership, supervisory of teams and interpersonal skills.
Expertise in workforce planning, HR system and processes, employee relations, and risk management.
Advanced coaching and change management capabilities.
Foundational knowledge of workplace resource administration.
Ability to influence, negotiate, and resolve conflicts effectively.
Ability to collaborate and work collaboratively at all levels of the organisation.
Your Work Environment
This is a residential opportunity offering secure and comfortable family accommodation in a gated community. You’ll enjoy a balanced 5:2 roster that allows you to return home to your family every evening, along with the benefits of tropical island living. Our residential village includes a range of social and recreational facilities such as an on-site gym, basketball court, and a café and deli offering takeaway coffees, snacks, and local and imported groceries, including fresh fruit. Based at Newmont’s Lihir site in PNG, you’ll work closely with site leaders and a team of six Business Partners and three Officers in a dynamic, collaborative environment where adaptability is key.
Why Join Newmont
At Newmont, we value safety, inclusion, and innovation. Joining us means being part of a global leader in mining, where your contributions drive meaningful change and sustainable growth. We offer competitive benefits, career development opportunities, and a culture that prioritizes your well-being.
At Newmont, our commitment to diversity and inclusion ensures that everyone can work to their full potential, free from discrimination, while respecting the cultures, religions, and governance of the regions in which we operate. Guided by our values of Safety, Integrity, Sustainability, Responsibility, and Inclusion, our Lihir team – 90% of which are Papua New Guinean – is dedicated to creating a culturally rich and supportive environment where meaningful, long-term connections can be formed within the industry.
We believe in the strength of our people and the positive impact we can create together. Newmont employees are rewarded with a competitive salary, flexible packaging options, and programs that recognize those who go above and beyond. We know no candidate meets every qualification listed, so if you share our values and feel you can make a meaningful contribution, we encourage you to apply before the closing date: 25 November 2025 – we’d love to hear from you!

Administration Officer - Procurement and Travel
Job Summary
Under the supervision of the Administration Manager and as a member of the Administration Unit, this position is responsible for managing all procurement processes and official travel arrangements for PNG CO and field offices. The role ensures that procurement and travel activities are efficient, compliant, and support the effective implementation of programs.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Procurement:
Review procurement requests for completeness and compliance with policy, prepare purchase orders, and obtain necessary approvals.
Analyze procurement requirements and select appropriate methods based on established policies and best practices.
Maintain the integrity of the competitive process, facilitate vendor debriefings, and protect confidential information.
Maintain and update the procurement policy, ensuring all purchases adhere to it; assist in obtaining donor approvals as needed.
Conduct EPLS/SAM searches for new vendors before issuing purchase orders.
Follow up with vendors for invoices and facilitate timely payments.
Maintain a supplier/vendor database and ensure up-to-date records.
Coordinate with Finance to ensure complete documentation for payments and delivery of goods/services.
Travel Management:
Arrange all official travel (domestic and international) for staff and consultants, including booking flights, hotels, and ground transportation.
Ensure all travel complies with donor and organizational requirements, including obtaining necessary approvals and notifications.
Coordinate with staff and consultants to ensure travel needs are met efficiently and cost-effectively.
Maintain records of travel bookings and expenditures.
Arrange security escorts for staff and consultants as needed.
Inventory and Administration:
Ensure proper custodianship and updating of all office equipment/furniture in the inventory list.
Update asset register for new acquisitions and disposals.
Conduct monthly asset checks for correct branding and facilitate annual physical verification and reporting.
Implement recommendations for disposal of faulty items.
Carry out office improvement plans and ensure the office is orderly and safe.
Ensure workplace health and safety standards are defined and followed.
Perform other duties as assigned by the Administration Manager, Associate Director of Operations or Country Representative.
Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:
Ability to initiate and implement activities with minimal supervision in procurement and travel management.
Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office and Excel.
Good judgment and the ability to deal pleasantly and effectively with people.
Strong team player skills and resourcefulness.
Minimum Requirement Standards:
At least 2–3 years’ experience in procurement, travel management, or office administration.
Ability to initiate tasks and work independently.
Minimum Diploma in office management, administration, or accounting.

Typical office environment: ability to travel domestically and internationally as needed (10-25%).

jobs.title: Cost Controller/Business Analyst
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited operates the Kainantu Gold Mine in the Eastern Highlands Province. Since we launched in 2016, we've grown gold production every year, boosting Papua New Guinea's economy. We take pride in supporting your communities, with nearly 94% of our team members being fellow PNG locals.
Looking ahead, we will significantly increase our gold production in the next three years. This expansion means that K92 is a place for building a stable career, contributing to the community, and being a key part of our success.
About the role
This role is responsible to provide to provide department managers & superintendents with necessary information to be able to control their costs/budgets, month-end financial transaction reviews and to continually improve the business systems and processes within the Department to enhance efficiency, budget compliance and overall cost effectiveness.
Key / Major Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position include.
Track daily expenditure and provide daily, weekly, and monthly cost variance analysis reports to all Sections within the Asset Management Department.
Assist in preparing the Department’s end-of-month and quarterly cost reports. This includes detailed commentary explaining both positive and negative variances to budget.
Review invoicing from Contractors and ensure that POs are approved, receipted, and are accurate and paid in a timely manner.
Assist in the preparation of annual (3 year) operating budgets.
Assist in preparation of CERs.
Assist in sourcing quotations and creating Purchase Requisitions for goods and services.
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you must a bachelor’s degree and/or Graduate Diploma in Business/Business Administration with CPA, CA, CMA or equivalent accounting designation is desirable. You must have a minimum of 5 years experience in a Cost Controller or Business Analyst role – preferably in the mining industry. In addition to this, you will have some or all the following.
Good level of English literacy - sound report writing skills, with use of finance and accounting terminology.
Good level of competency using the MS Office suite (MS Word, MS Excel and MS Power Point).
Familiarity/experience with Pronto ERP – specifically Finance, Supply and Maintenance modules.
Project Management experience – coordinating small projects.
Life at K92
Our core values — Collaboration, Accountability, Respect, Excellence, and Safety — are central to our operations and fundamental to our success. K92 upholds a commitment to equal opportunity, striving to ensure that every individual can reach their highest potential without experiencing discrimination.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
We believe in sharing our success with our employees. In addition to competitive salaries, we offer participation in long- and short-term incentive plans. We also offer savings programs, medical assistance, as well as access to our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.
If you share our values and are looking for your next career step, come join us on this exciting journey. Submit your application through our website today.

jobs.title: Team Lead
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Commercial team, you will undertake all regular purchasing and administrative duties including updating of purchasing records and pricing system. Another demand defined to this role is regular liaison with both local and overseas Suppliers and Service Providers with the prime objective of quality and on-time delivery of goods and services to meet site operational requirements. Moreover, this role involves preparation and processing of purchase orders and relating documents in line with K92 Mining Limited Supply and Procurement guidelines.
Key Accountabilities
Key accountabilities of this position mean you will
Ensure all supplies especially critical items required by end users are sourced and purchased and available for use without delay.
Carry out and monitor all purchasing duties.
Monitor stock levels based on the usage track record so that essential plant, mobile and light vehicle parts are available
Prepare and process purchase orders and supporting documents.
Purchase and issue order in accordance to specification.
Regular liaison with Warehouse and Logistics team to ensure orders are picked up in the shortest possible time.
Source, select and negotiate for the best quote price, terms and deliveries with suppliers/service providers.
Monitor and coordinate delivery of items between suppliers both local and overseas.
Constant liaison with suppliers on supplies and back orders and for logistical arrangements to site in a safe and timely manner.
Update and maintain purchasing records/data.
Maintain regular professional approach with various suppliers and service providers.
Maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance company policy.
Perform all roles and responsibilities that support and reflect the company’s mission and core values
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have the following
A certificate or Diploma in business studies, Accounting or related field preferred but not essential
Five year’s work experience in a warehouse or purchasing role is well regarded
Must be a self-starter, very resourceful and with ability to find solutions.
Good oral and written communication skills.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player
Ability to meet communicated schedules and deadlines.
Strong planning and organizational skills.
Proficient in computer use especially Microsoft suite, especially Excel and Outlook.
Proficient user of Pronto Xi Software is essential.
Mining Industry experience preferred.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

jobs.title: HV Electrical Technician
jobs.description:
Job Type:
Permanent
About us
K92 Mining Limited are the owners the high-grade Kainantu Gold Mine in Eastern Highlands Province. Since commencing operations in 2016, we have delivered consistent production growth. More importantly, we have contributed significantly to the economy of Papua New Guinea, more than 90% of our employees and contractors are from PNG and our local education and skills development initiatives which include scholarships, traineeships and adult literacy programs continue to bring significant benefit the communities in which we operate.
We are now transforming the operation with a new 1.2 mtpa process plant as well as extensive construction and expansion across site that will see us triple the output from our mine by 2027. In addition to our ongoing production success, we have an extensive exploration programme across our highly prospective tenement, making K92 a great place to build a long-term career.
About the role
Joining our Operational Services maintenance team, this role is responsible for monitoring the overall mine site power supply and distribution network including all Permanent Power Station generators and associated controls. In addition, you will maintain of all High Voltage electrical supply equipment and oversee the maintenance of all Permanent Power Station generators and associated controls.
Training of HV Electrical Technicians to effectively monitor and maintain the electrical systems on the mine site, with reference to the electrical components.
Key Accountabilities
Monitor Network supply and communicate with Mining and Processing Operations regarding power supply matters, including changeover of power supplies from PPS to PPL or vice versa, if required.
Prepare High Voltage Switching sheets, understand and follow Safe Operating Procedures related to High Voltage equipment.
Monitor Generators when they are operational and supplying Power to site.
Work with contractors and mechanical staff to maintain Generators so they are in good working order.
Inspect, isolate, and repair electrical malfunctions using various hand and power tools.
Diagnose electrical defects or hazards on systems, appliances and machinery and identify adjustment and repair timely.
Ensure that alarms and emergency electrical systems onsite are always operational.
Conduct regular electrical tests and tagging on equipment, appliances, and machines.
Inspect, test and qualified to apply and remove ‘out-of-service’ or ‘not-to-be operated’ tags to electrical equipment, appliances, and machines.
Direct and train subordinates to install, maintain or repair electrical wiring, equipment and machines.
Respond to routine and emergency calls for repair and service within the mine site area.
Be on call in emergency situations and extreme conditions.
Perform general housekeeping within and around work area.
Ensure and maintain safe work standards and practices in accordance with mine safety regulations for all tasks performed.
Maintain safety work standards in accordance with government regulations and company policy
About You
To be considered for this role, it is essential that you have a
NATTB Trade Certificate
as well a current
electrical license
. You will also need to demonstrate experience in the installation and maintenance of power distribution systems, transformer installations, motor control centres, LVHV transfers, motor starters and controls; and in the maintenance of equipment – electric motors, compressor stations and other electrical equipment.
Experience in High Voltage switching and Power Station Operation and Maintenance
A certified electrician with 5 years’ work experience in a mining environment.
Must be a Tradesman with PPL certification.
Maintain current electrician’s license to meet government regulations.
Ability to train maintenance personnel in all aspects of their trade – particularly in diagnosis and fault finding, quality control, thoroughness and record keeping.
Must be a self-starter, and very resourceful, with the ability to find solutions to problems to ensure the
equipment availability is high.
Good health physical ability is a prerequisite, as is the ability to live in a remote environment with limited facilities.
Flexible, adaptable and be a team player.
Life at K92
K92 is an Equal Opportunity Employer, our commitment is to respect the rights of every individual to work to their highest potential, free from discrimination.  Our values of Collaboration, Accountability, Respect for others, Excellence and Safety are at the core of everything we do, and they are the foundation upon which our success has been built.
Our camp is well managed and provides residents with good, healthy meals made from locally sourced fresh produce as well as internet, cable tv and a gymnasium.
At K92, we want all employees to share in our success, so as well as a competitive salary, employees also participate in our long- and short-term incentive plans, we also provide employees with access to savings incentive programs, medical assistance and the option to salary sacrifice for certain expenses.
In addition to all of this, employees can also access our Wellbeing and employee assistance programs whilst working a friendly roster.

Position:
Logistics and Admin Officer
Full-Time, Fixed-Term position until 30 Sept 2026, with possible extension
Location:
MAG PNG Office, Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea with travel throughout PNG, especially to MAG project locations.
Salary:
The starting monthly salary for this position is 2960 PGK
About MAG:
MAG (Mines Advisory Group) is an international humanitarian organisation based in Manchester, UK, and working in 32 countries. We remove landmines and unexploded ordnance to release safe and productive land for communities, and work to reduce the threat of armed violence by supporting governments to safely manage weapons and ammunition. In 1997, MAG was a co-recipient of the Nobel Peace Prize for our work campaigning for the Anti-Personnel Mine Ban Convention.
About the role:
MAG PNG is currently seeking to recruit a Logistics and Admin Officer to join the team in our Port Moresby office and contribute to our work on reducing armed violence in PNG. The Logistics and Admin Officer is responsible for ensuring that all logistics administrative processes are completed efficiently, including maintaining and controlling equipment, maintaining logistics paperwork and record systems in compliance with Logistics Standard Operating Procedures. Additionally, this role will have some general office administrative responsibilities.
Responsibilities include:
Procurement
Manage day-to-day procurement activities, ensuring compliance with MAG Logistics procedures, policies, and donor requirements.
Assist in preparing and issuing Requests for Quotations (RFQ) and Purchase Orders (PO). Collect supplier quotes in line with MAG procurement policies.
Maintain accurate procurement records and ensure proper documentation and filing.
Liaise with suppliers and service providers to ensure timely and accurate completion of orders.
Cultivate effective supplier relationships to achieve the best possible price, quality, service, and terms for MAG.
Compile and manage a supplier database and establish preferred suppliers.
Regularly review price comparisons and monitor material/item costs.
Prepare and distribute weekly procurement reports to the Security and Access Manager and Country Director (CD), addressing any procurement-related issues.
Asset and Inventory Management
Record all purchases of Capital and Non-Capital Assets, ensuring they are asset tagged
Maintain an up-to-date Asset Register and submit a monthly copy to the Security and Access Manager and CD.
Update the Assets Database to ensure effective asset tracking, including adding newly procured equipment and asset encoding.
Liaise with the Security and Access Manager and CD regarding asset-related matters.
Ensure that all staff return all MAG assets upon departure from the programme.
Perform other tasks assigned by the line manager, which may include aspects of asset management.
Support inventory management of stocks and tool handover/takeover processes.
Monitor product quality, expiry dates, and ensure cleanliness and organization of storage areas.
Issue and record store items accurately; maintain organized and compliant stock documentation.
Distribution:
Collect and dispatch new equipment/supplies as required.
Verify goods for quality, quantity, and compliance with specifications.
Organize transportation of equipment/supplies to areas of operation.
Ensure accurate recording of incoming supplies/equipment on Goods Received Notes.
Office Administration:
Establish and maintain proper and up-to-date filing systems (paper and electronic) for efficient organization of office records, files, and documents.
Handle incoming and outgoing correspondence, emails, and calls.
Schedule and coordinate meetings, appointments, and travel arrangements in coordination with the Security & Access Manager.
Manage office supplies and equipment inventory, and order as needed.
Assist in trip planning and coordination.
Assist in managing travel and immigration matters for MAG staff in the country and visiting staff, including visas, permits, flight reservations, hotel bookings, and transport arrangements.
General Responsibilities:
Work within the framework of MAG’s core values.
Maintain professional conduct in line with MAG’s core values as actions represent MAG.

jobs.description:
PNG's pioneering leader in logistics and property.
Develops staff; invests in PNG's health & education.
Offers stable, rewarding careers with long-term growth.
The Opportunity
This organization is known as a pioneering icon and diversified leader in Papua New Guinea's development, having grown from a single-vessel trading operation into one of the country's largest private employers by diversifying across shipping, transport, property, and hospitality.
This is a perfect opportunity if you are a detail-oriented, proactive professional with a strong background in data analysis and reporting within the logistics, transport, or shipping industry. This role is ideal for those looking to elevate their career by automating reporting tasks, streamlining data processes, and directly impacting business strategy to improve operational efficiency and customer service delivery.
The Role
Your core mission is to drive the organization's success by transforming raw logistics and shipping data into actionable insights that enhance operational efficiency, optimize fleet performance, and drive strategic decision-making. You will be directly responsible for developing and maintaining key reports and dashboards using tools like Power BI and Azure, ensuring data integrity and compliance with regulatory standards, and collaborating with operational and finance teams to streamline reporting processes and contribute to informed management decisions.
Main duties include:
Report Development and Maintenance: Create and maintain reports and dashboards, specifically using tools like Power BI and Azure, including the preparation of monthly Balanced Scorecards.
Data Collection and Validation: Compile and verify data from logistics systems and external sources (like Excel and delivery schedules) to ensure accuracy.
Stakeholder Collaboration: Partner with the four operating companies (OpCos) and finance teams to understand their reporting needs and deliver customised solutions.
Process Optimisation: Identify and implement solutions to automate routine reporting tasks (e.g., daily updates) and streamline data processes to improve responsiveness.
Documentation and Training: Create a repository of data sources, capture operational details (Standard Operating Procedures), and train end-users on reporting functions and data integrity.
Data Integrity and Security: Uphold the accuracy and confidentiality of data, ensuring compliance with both company policies and Papua New Guinea's regulatory standards.
Qualification and Experience:
Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Computer Science, Accounting or Finance.
2-4 years of experience in MIS, reporting, or data analysis, ideally within the logistics, transport, or shipping industry.
Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Excel and strong experience with reporting tools like Power BI or similar platforms. Familiarity with logistics software (Cargowise, TM Master, Cadi) or SQL is a strong advantage.

jobs.description:
Drug Resistant Tuberculosis in PNG and the Western Province TB program.
PNG is one of only 14 countries classified by the WHO as having the triple high burden of TB, MDR-TB, and TB-human immunodeficiency virus (HIV) co-infection. Three hotspot regions have been identified in the country including the Gulf, National Capita District (NCD), and Western Province. In Western province, the problem has been further compounded by high levels of drug-resistant TB, with evidence of primary (person to person) transmission of resistant strains, particularly in Daru of South Fly District.
The Western Province TB program, led by the WPHA, with support from partners has led to commendable success, with an increasing recognition of Daru as a ‘Centre of excellence’ in the programmatic management of DR TB with outstanding treatment outcomes for patients.
We are seeking qualified and experienced professionals for the following position(s):
Position:
Operations Coordinator
Classification:
Full-time, contract
Location:
Daru, Western Province (WP)
Role Purpose
The purpose of the operations Coordinator role is to oversee the day-to-day management of the Daru based logistics support team, lead WP project asset management and to provide support to the WP team. The role will report directly to the Team Leader – Operations and be part of an experienced team of managers, clinicians and public health professionals based in Daru, Port Moresby and Melbourne , providing inputs in WP. The role works to ensure efficient operation of the Burnet Daru office and the timely and efficient delivery of support services to the team.
The Operations Coordinator will be responsible for assisting the Team Leader – Operations to ensure the efficient management and implementation of all operational, logistical, financial, and administrative tasks in line with Burnet Institute PNG policies and practice.

We also provide engineering consulting services for mechanical projects and offer renovation services for commercial and government buildings.
Position Overview:
We are seeking a skilled and experienced
Project Manager
to oversee our OTE Aviation Project. The successful candidate will be responsible for the overall supervision and coordination of site activities, ensuring successful project execution while adhering to safety, quality, and regulatory standards.
Key Responsibilities:
Overall Site Supervision & Coordination:
Act as the primary on-site contact for daily construction activities across multiple disciplines (civil, structural, mechanical, piping, instrumentation, electrical). Ensure alignment of work with project scope and specifications.
Discipline Integration & Multi-Trade Management:
Manage the integration of various trades, ensuring adherence to schedules and quality standards. Provide technical oversight to crews.
Quality Assurance / Control:
Inspect work in progress to verify compliance with project specifications and quality standards. Track non-conformances and facilitate corrective actions.
Health, Safety, Environment & Regulatory Compliance:
Implement safe work practices and ensure compliance with safety regulations. Prepare and enforce Job Safety Analyses (JSA) for high-risk tasks.
Schedule, Cost & Progress Monitoring:
Track daily progress and report on status, identifying risks and proposing mitigation actions.
Resource & Logistics Management:
Supervise site workforce and manage materials and equipment logistics effectively.
Communication & Stakeholder Engagement:
Serve as a communication link between site teams, contractors, clients, and internal functions. Conduct regular site meetings to ensure alignment.
Commissioning, Turnover & Close-Out:
Supervise the handover of constructed scope and support final inspections and close-out reports.
Specific Considerations for a Fuel Loading Facility:
Ensure compliance with hazardous area regulations and oversee construction of containment systems.
Coordinate mechanical piping and instrumentation works, ensuring environmental controls are in place.
Support commissioning activities, ensuring alignment with safety and operational readiness.
Typical Skills & Qualifications:
Proven experience in supervising multi-discipline construction projects, preferably in industrial, energy, or fuel/storage environments.
Strong understanding of civil, structural, mechanical, piping, and electrical/instrumentation scopes.
Excellent leadership, communication, and coordination skills.
Ability to interpret technical drawings and specifications.

About the Burnet Institute
The Burnet Institute is an Australian medical research and public health organisation working to improve the health of vulnerable communities in Australia and globally. In Papua New Guinea, Burnet has operated for nearly two decades, partnering with provincial health authorities and local stakeholders to strengthen health systems, pilot innovations, and conduct research on priority health issues.
About the HEAL-PNG Project
HEAL-PNG is a three-year clinical trial funded by the NHMRC and the Global Alliance for Chronic Diseases (GACD). The project evaluates an innovative model of care that integrates non-communicable disease (NCD) screening and management within existing HIV and TB clinics in
Morobe
and
East New Britain
provinces. The goal is to improve NCD care through enhanced screening, patient education, adherence support via peer counselling, and simplified management protocols.
About the Role
The
Research Health Extension Officer (HEO)
will play a key role in establishing and implementing the HEAL-PNG trial across selected health facilities. Working closely with the Provincial Health Authority (PHA), facility staff, and the HEAL-PNG project team, the HEO will support study coordination, site setup, staff training, and data collection activities.
The position will require initiative, attention to detail, and the ability to build strong working relationships across multiple stakeholders.
Key Responsibilities
Coordinate study activities at participating facilities, ensuring adherence to research protocols and ethical standards.
Facilitate site onboarding, including assessments and staff training in NCD, TB, and HIV management.
Manage data collection, entry, and quality assurance in a confidential and timely manner.
Maintain strong communication with facility and PHA staff, fostering collaboration and problem-solving.
Support logistics for meetings, trainings, and field activities.

Health Extension Officer qualification (Diploma + 1-year residency or Bachelor’s + 2-year residency).
Strong understanding of tuberculosis, HIV, and non-communicable diseases (diabetes, cardiovascular disease, asthma, COPD).

Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, with fluency in English and Tok Pisin.
Strong organisational skills and ability to work both independently and in a team.

Here you’ll make a difference
Save the Children is the world’s largest independent child rights development organisation, making a difference to children’s lives in more than 100 countries. From emergency relief to long-term development, Save the Children secures a child’s right to health, education, and protection. At Save the Children, we attract bright and big-hearted people who are inspired to make a difference. Together, we are fearless in our pursuit of making lasting change for the children and communities who need it most. In Papua New Guinea, Save the Children currently implement programs in the sectors of health, education, child protection, child rights governance and livelihoods. The Child Nutrition and Social Protection Project is an 18-month project implemented from March 2025 to December 2026 in the provinces of East New Britain and Simbu.
Here your skills will be valued
Role Purpose
Reporting to the Provincial Coordinator, the Finance Officer ensures that all expenses, activities, and financial transactions are fully processed, acquitted, and documented in a timely, transparent, and equitable manner – and in accordance with Save the Children, government, and donor policies and requirements and in a transparent and accountable manner. The Finance Officer works with the project teams to ensure that all funds disbursed to respective provinces are fully acquitted and in line with government and donor requirements.
Key Areas of Accountability
Financial Control Framework
Full compliance with the Save the Children’s Pacific Australia Finance Manual and Save the Children in PNG’s Internal Delegation Document.
Mentor and support the team (including Village Health Assistants and Community Development Workers) to process all financial transactions and acquittals in line with policies and donor guidelines.
All breaches of the Save the Children Pacific Finance Manual are promptly recorded and reported.
Monthly Acquittals, Forecasts, and Financial Reports
Support the program team to review all financial transactions and supporting documents to deliver accurate monthly acquittals; ensure copies are kept on file.
Support the team to ensure that all documents and reports are prepared, submitted, and filed in accordance with donor requirements procedures in an orderly and timely manner; ensure copies are kept on file.
Deliver disbursement forecasts in a responsive, timely and quality manner, in accordance with donor requirements.
Address internal and external audit/document review/ donor sampling queries in a timely manner with relevant supporting documentation as relevant.
Financial Risk Management and Compliance
Financial Risk Assessments for projects are updated in a timely manner in collaboration with the donor.
Financial Literacy Training
Provide Financial Literacy Training of Trainers (ToTs) Trainings with support of the Cash Technical Advisor for Village Health Assistants and Community Development Workers, ensuring that they accurately transfer the knowledge to project participants.
Empower with Practical Budgeting Skills: Teach community workers how to guide individuals and families in creating realistic budgets, tracking expenses, and setting financial goals that align with their income and lifestyle.
Demystify Banking and Credit Systems: Provide clear, culturally relevant explanations of savings accounts, loans, interest rates, and credit scores to help communities make informed decisions and avoid predatory financial practices.
Promote Sustainable Financial Behaviours: Equip workers with tools to encourage long-term habits like saving regularly, planning for emergencies, and understanding the value of financial planning for education, health, and retirement.
Bank Accounts, Mibank and Petty Cash
Work with respective program team to ensure an accurate analysis and audit trail of all office bank and petty cash movements.
General
Comply with Save the Children policies and practice with respect to child safeguarding, code of conduct, health and safety, equal opportunities and other relevant policies and procedures.
Embody the Save the Children values in practice of Accountability, Ambition, Collaboration, Creativity, and Integrity. Work according to Save the Children’s mandate and child focus.
Work according to any other duties as assigned by the supervisor.
Child protection and safeguarding requirements
Maintain a child safe environment at the workplace and safeguard children’s rights, acting in the best interests of children at all times.
Maintain compliance with Save the Children’s
Child Safeguarding Policy
,
Code of Conduct
, and PSEAH policies and reporting processes among staff and volunteers.
Act as a role model by demonstrating highest standards of behaviour towards children in private and professional life.
Never abuse the position of trust that comes with being a part of the Save the Children family.
Maintain a safe and positive relationship at all times when working with children and young people.
Respond to any concerns for the safety or wellbeing of a child in a program in accordance with internal reporting processes.
Health, safety, security and risk management
Be a role model for safety and security and comply with all workplace safety policy, procedure, work instructions and training.
Act safely at all times.
Report all incidents, injuries and potential hazards in a timely manner.
Participate in, and contribute to, health and safety awareness and improvements.
Be aware of, and consider, the risks associated with one’s daily work and apply appropriate mitigation measures in line with Save the Children’s policies and procedures.
All roles at Save the Children contribute to our impact for children.
At Save the Children, every role, whether in our programs or support services, plays a vital part in our impact for children. We are committed to creating a positive impact on the lives of children and their communities, and we value the contributions of every team member in achieving this vision.
Person Specification
It takes all types of people to do the challenging work we do. Here are some of the specific skills and experiences you’ll bring in this role:
Skills and Qualifications
Excellent oral and written English communication skills.
Proficient computer literacy: use of Email, Microsoft Word and Excel.
Experience in use of financial management systems software.
Ability to work collaboratively with the program and finance teams, management and community workers.
Minimum of three (3) years’ experience in a similar role, preferably with an NGO.
Diploma in Business Accounting.
Ability to work independently and in multidisciplinary teams.
Willingness to travel to remote areas and adapt to challenging environments.
Fluency in English; knowledge of Tok Pisin or local languages is an asset.

Not Required
Travel:
Frequent travel within the province

Required

jobs.description:
PAPUA NEW GUINEA UNIVERSITY OF TECHNOLOGY
The Papua New Guinea University of Technology is located in the industrial city of Lae, the second largest city in Papua New Guinea.  The city of Lae has an airport with flights to any location in PNG. The University is the only technological university in the country.  It has a main campus and three amalgamated colleges.  The main campus has 14 academic departments including one in Open and Distance Learning (ODL).  It offers undergraduate and graduate programs in engineering, natural and applied sciences, built environment, language and business.  The university has an Information Technology Services department and a Library.
MATHESON LIBRARY
Matheson Library, named after the first Chancellor of the University, which was founded in 1967. It has a current book stock of 130,000 volumes and receives 600 periodical titles. It is the only library in the university serving some 250 academic staff and 3,000 full time students taking a range of degree, diploma and certificate courses in Civil, Electrical, Mechanical, Mining, Communication Engineering, Business Studies, Architecture and Building, Surveying and Land Studies, Mathematics and Computer Sciences, Applied Sciences, Applied Physics, Forestry, Agriculture and Communication and Development Studies.
The library system is automated and it operates 7 days a week with limited operation during weekends. The library seeks to appoint a suitably qualified and highly experienced person to immediately fill the following vacancy.
UNIVERSITY LIBRARIAN
The University Librarian is responsible for the overall management and development of library services, collections, budget and staff.  The University is concerned that it gains access to the information superhighway and its new Librarian will be expected to accelerate this process.
Duties and Responsibilities:
Efficient Information Literacy and Accessibility.
Ensure that Students and Staff have access to library resources effectively and resourcefully and at the same time students and staff are well inducted on the library operations.
2.
Well Maintained Accessibility Resources Center.
All electronic accessibility equipment, books and journals are readily available for staff and students. All library books and journals are acquired on time for students and staff.
3. Academic Success for Students and Staff.
To maintain continuous flow of information between academic departments and students required for research and study.
4.Research Impact
.
Ensuring all PNGUoT research articles and papers are well preserved
5
.Sustain and uphold University’s wellbeing and Identity through effective Clients Service by:
●
Maintaining a decent professional relationship with other libraries in the country and overseas for inter-         library loan purposes.
6.Capacity development of fellow colleagues
Continuously mentoring of library staff skills and knowledge to be able to better serve staff, students and other clients.
7. Actively participate in Policy development for the library.
Qualifications & Experience
A relevant master’s degree and an internationally recognized professional qualification in librarianship.
Required to have experience working in academic or research libraries and operational concepts involved in the delivery of users and bibliographic services and library automation.
Must be able to manage emerging trends in academic libraries especially those resulting from electronic access to information.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, business skills and good interpersonal skills
Conditions of Service

Professor

About Newmont
At Newmont, we’re not just a world-leading gold and metals producer – we’re a team united by our commitment to shaping a more inclusive, sustainable, and responsible mining industry. Joining us means becoming part of a global, diverse workforce where everyone is valued, empowered, and encouraged to grow. Our people are the heart of our success, bringing exceptional skill, integrity, and dedication to everything we do as an organization and we’re dedicated to creating a workplace where everyone can thrive.
About Lihir
Our Lihir Operation, located on the beautiful island of Niolam, approximately 800km north of Papua New Guinea's capital, Port Moresby, is one of the world’s largest gold mines. Set within a geothermically active, extinct volcanic crater, Lihir operates an open-pit mine producing refractory ore, which undergoes pressure oxidation and conventional leaching to recover gold. Our workforce includes both residential and commute rosters, creating a diverse and dynamic team. Lihir offers a range of recreational facilities, including a gym, sports club, restaurant, bar, swimming pool, tennis and squash courts, and a 9-hole golf course. For those who enjoy the outdoors, the Lihir fishing and boating clubs provide access to pristine waters and beaches, while our onsite deli and café serve fresh local and imported produce, barista-made coffee, and freshly baked goods.
We are proud to work closely with the local Lihirian community and value its vibrant culture. Through initiatives like our School to Mine program, we offer meaningful employment, training, and development opportunities for Lihirian men and women, as well as scholarships and vocational apprenticeships. We also partner with the New Ireland Province to ensure economic benefits flow directly to the community, strengthening our commitment to sustainable development and positive local impact.

To safely carry out maintenance and repairs to all equipment associated with the Newmont In-pit fleet as directed by the supervisor. And ensure that all plant and equipment is maintained to Newmont's requirements and meet all safety, availability, and production target KPI’s.
To provide mechanical fitting services on mobile fleet units within an open pit environment
Specific focus is to be on Shovels & Drills.

Ensure personal and team compliance with all company HSE requirements & policies including Fitness for Work.

Ensure documentation, maintenance and service records for equipment are complete and kept up to date

Work constructively within a diverse group of people.

Good verbal and written communication skills.
Self-motivated with the ability to work autonomously from time to time.
High attention to detail with good time management skills.

The
Independent Commission Against Corruption (ICAC)

Organic Law on the ICAC 2020

Executive Director

Lead the Legal Battle Against Corruption

Executive Director, Legal Services Division

complex corruption

Communications & External Affairs Officer

(

jobs.title: PEOPLE, CULTURE & SAFEGUARDING COORDINATOR
jobs.description:
POSITION DESCRIPTION
TITLE
PEOPLE, CULTURE & SAFEGUARDING COORDINATOR
REPORTING TO
OPERATIONS MANAGER
LOCATION
PORT MORESBY
CLASSIFICATION
D2
EMPLOYMENT DETAILS/HOURS
PERMANENT
Introduction
WaterAid’s vision is of a world where everyone has access to safe water and sanitation. Our mission is to transform lives by improving access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) in the world’s poorest communities. WaterAid works with partners to maximise its impacts for policy change/influence.
WaterAid has been operating in Papua New Guinea (PNG) since 2004, working with local partners and the government to increase access to gender sensitive, socially inclusive and climate resilient water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) services. WaterAid PNG’s geographic focus is in the National Capital District, and Central Province in the Southern Region and East Sepik Province.
WaterAid works through supporting local organisations and government authorities to design and demonstrate appropriate and sustainable WASH programs. WaterAid also seeks to influence policy change through government and other key sector actors to secure and protect the right of poor people to safe, affordable water and sanitation services.
Everything we do is shaped by our six values:
Integrity
Respect
Collaboration
Courage
Accountability
Innovation
WaterAid is a child safe organisation. We recognise that we must meet community expectations and the trust placed in our personnel to maintain the highest standards of conduct with children. Therefore, all positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Child Safeguarding Policy and Code of Conduct.
WaterAid is committed to protection from sexual exploitation and abuse in everything we do. The values and standards we uphold are highlighted in our Global Code of Conduct. All positions within WaterAid are required to comply with our Global Code of Conduct.
WaterAid passionately believes everyone in the organisation has a role to play in innovation, encourages curiosity about the world and empowering everyone to take action. We recognise that both big and small changes can have positive impacts on our roles, our team and our mission.
Position Summary
The People, Culture, and Safeguarding Coordinator plays an essential role in promoting safe and positive team culture and operations at WaterAid Papua New Guinea. Reporting to the Operations Manager, this role ensures systems and processes for people management are fit for purpose and supports staff and managers to effectively complete tasks from recruitment, through leave, growth and performance management, and staff exit. They will manage feedback and complaint mechanisms and support the Senior Management Team to make effective decisions in line with both WaterAid Federation and PNG compliance requirements regarding people & HR. As Safeguarding Lead for WaterAid Papua New Guinea, this role will manage safeguarding training and reporting processes and support all staff to meet PSEAH compliance requirements for a safer working environment for staff as well as those we work with through our projects. The People, Culture, and Safeguarding Officer connects with regional and global WaterAid colleagues for training, support, and collaboration.
Key Accountabilities
Systems, Processes, and Staff Engagement
Lead and maintain all people policies, manual, processes and administration in line with current legislation and WaterAid global policies (i.e. recruitment, employment contracts, casuals and consultants contracts, starters, leavers and change processes, org chart, JDs) and standards. Support Managers to deliver these with staff effectively.
Ensure all staff information with Nasfund, IRC, NCSL, Medical Insurance and Police Clearance for starters and continuing staff are update to date.
Manage processing of all work permits, NID, passports and visa for national, regional and global staff as and when required.
Administer the internal web-based People Place HR management system, and support staff and managers to use this effectively.
Manage and continuously improve WaterAid PNG reward ensuring an appropriate mix of pay, benefits and non-pay rewards in line with WaterAid’s reward principles and national legislation. Contribute to reward benchmarking and support managers to communicate to employees about total reward. Coordinate with SMT and Global People Team.
Foster high levels of employee engagement, including staff participation in the Global Employee Engagement surveys (GEES) and line manager capability, coordinating GEES action plans. Organise Staff Days and Induction sessions.
Lead the Country Training and Development Plan and team building activities including Staff Retreats
Collate and accurately analyse people data and metrics for use within the Country Program and organisational wide people reporting requirements.
Engage with the wider Global People team and build connections to other organisations, accessing appropriate learning and resources for the WAPNG team.
Provide support to the SMT and people managers to enhance our people management processes
Embed and role model a strong performance management culture and processes. Advise staff and managers in agreeing appraisal objectives, holding honest conversations, delivering feedback and recognizing success.
Advise Operations Manager and Country Director on issues of under-performance, plan and
implementing performance improvement plans where required.
Ensure new and transitioning employees and volunteers receive a planned, effective and timely induction and exit, and advise managers on their role in delivering this.
Work with the Operations Manager and Country Director to build Manager capability and behaviors.
Provide specialist advice and instruction to SMT and managers on employee relations issues (i.e. disciplinary, grievance, capability, bullying and harassment) in line with CP policy, Global WaterAid policies and legislation, working with legal providers as needed. Inform Organizational Risk Assessment
Give accurate and appropriate advice, training and support to managers to recognize, respect and enable diversity and inclusion.
Advise managers to identify employee learning and career aspirations and agree on effective development plans. Recommend suitable learning methods and develop an annual Country Program learning and development plan, supported by learning initiatives from the global people team.
Support managers in identifying and maximizing potential and drive development through succession planning and individual development planning to meet our skills and capability needs.
Safeguarding Lead
Champion safeguarding principles through people and culture activities
Act as a Safeguarding focal point, receiving safeguarding reports and processing these in line with WaterAid Policy & processes
Revise and maintain policies, processes, and resources related to safeguarding and protection against sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEAH).
Deliver training and information to staff, volunteers, and collaborators in line with policy and standard requirements
Manage internal and external feedback, complaints, and reporting mechanisms
Monitor completion of project risk assessments and application of nominated risk mitigation strategies, report status to Country Director
Qualification, Skills & Attributes (Key Capabilities/Selection Criteria)
Essential
Experience
Minimum of three years’ work experience in a similar role
Experience in designing or providing effective training modules
Excellent communication skills and ability to make clear engaging presentations in English
Good networker adept at establishing and maintaining relationships with colleagues and collaborators.
Knowledge of Papua New Guinea labour law and requirements
Knowledge and skills
Proficient with the use of Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in both English and Tok Pisin.
Excellent time management skills, flexibility, and an ability to prioritise tasks
Education
Completion of a degree course in a relevant area, ideally in human resources or related field.
Personal qualities
An ability to effectively work independently and as a member of a team
A ‘can do’ attitude
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
An ability to manage confidentiality and handle sensitive information
Attention to detail
A commitment to WaterAid’s values and Child safeguarding policies
Physical Environment and Demands
Ergonomic work stations within an open plan office.
Level of contact with children
The position will be required to maintain WaterAid child safeguarding principles and standards at all times.
To Apply:
Please submit an application to
[email protected]
by 14
th
November 2025.
Applications for this position must include a resume and a cover letter addressing the above Qualification, Skills and Selection Criteria.
Applicants must have the right to work in Papua New Guinea

jobs.title: LAE CCTV TECHNICIAN
jobs.description:
Location: Lae, Morobe
CCTV technician - Job Description
CCTV technician is responsible for installing and maintaining closed-circuit television systems. They commonly work with video cameras, monitors, recording devices, networking equipment, and other related hardware to ensure that these systems are functioning properly at all times.
CCTV technician may also be called upon to troubleshoot problems with the system or its components. This might involve anything from replacing broken parts to diagnosing software issues or other technical difficulties.
CCTV Technician Skills Required
Technical skills:
Technical skills are the abilities and knowledge that allow you to perform tasks and complete projects. Technical skills are essential for a CCTV technician as they allow you to install, repair and maintain security systems. Technical skills can include knowledge of electrical systems, computer software and security protocols.
Communication skills:
Communication skills are necessary for a CCTV technician to have, as they must be able to clearly relay information to other technicians, and managers. They must also be able to listen to and understand requests from managers.
Attention to detail:
Attention to detail is the ability to notice small changes in a situation. It’s important for CCTV technicians to notice small changes in a room or area they’ve already inspected. This allows them to identify any new security threats and ensures they’ve thoroughly checked the area.
Problem-solving skills:
Problem-solving skills are essential for CCTV technicians because they often encounter challenges while installing and maintaining security systems. For example, if a camera isn’t working properly, a technician might need to find the source of the problem and fix it. Similarly, if a security system malfunctions, a technician might need to troubleshoot the system and find a solution.
Ability to work independently:
Working independently means that you can complete tasks without the help of others. As a CCTV technician, you may be required to install and repair security systems on your own. This means that you need to have the knowledge and skills necessary to complete the task.
As a CCTV technician at Express Freight Management, you will be responsible for the installation, configuration, and maintenance of our CCTV systems. You will work with our team to ensure that our systems are up-to-date and functioning properly. You may be required to do training or be required to attend training that concerns CCTV systems. You are required to have experience with CCTV systems and networking, as well as a strong understanding of security protocols. You will be required to be detail-oriented and able to work independently.
Duties & Responsibilities
CCTV Roles
Install, maintain, and troubleshoot CCTV systems according to company standards and department specifications.
Perform site surveys to assess department needs and recommend solutions.
Generate system diagrams and documentation for both internal use.
Provide technical support and advice to departments as needed.
Respond to service calls in a timely and professional manner.
Keep up to date with the latest industry developments and technologies.
Maintain and document accurate records of all installed systems.
Always adhere to health and safety guidelines.
Comply with all company policies and procedures.
Installing, maintaining, repairing, and replacing security cameras, computer networks, and other equipment used in video surveillance systems and Information Systems (IT).
Monitoring the operation of security equipment for malfunctions or other problems
Installing and maintaining security equipment such as alarms, access control, or time attendance systems
Structural network cabling and installation
Required Skills and Qualifications
High school diploma or equivalent
2+ years experience in installation, maintenance, and repair of CCTV systems
Working knowledge of CCTV equipment, including cameras, DVRs, and monitors
Ability to read and interpret technical manuals and drawings
Basic computer skills, with aptitude to learn new software and systems
Preferred Skills and Qualifications
4+ years experience in installation, maintenance, and repair of CCTV systems
Strong working knowledge of CCTV equipment, including cameras, DVRs, and monitors
Proficient in configuring CCTV systems
Experience developing and implementing CCTV systems

Location:
LAE, PG
